meta.note: Machine-assisted translation of the Chinese taxonomic prose in _data/*.json. Latin names, authorities, years and measurements are kept verbatim; the pre-existing English abstracts in the source `en` fields are not duplicated here.

/genus/acangaobitermes/.note: Adapted from the English genus-level Description; digestive tract details are omitted, and no species-level measurements are involved.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Noirotitermes; in both the soldier head capsule surface bears a fine granular micro-sculpture and internal granules, the mandibles are piercing-sucking with only 1 extremely reduced marginal tooth, and the worker habitus and digestive tract are also similar; they differ in soldier head shape, frontal tube and pronotum: in this genus the frontal tube is long and conical, the posterior margin of the head lacks the 4 distinct horn-like projections seen in Noirotitermes, and the pronotum is saddle-shaped (exceptional in Noirotitermes). Compared with other genera of Syntermitinae, in this genus the soldier frontal tube is longer than the labrum, the hyaline tip of the labrum is poorly developed, and the mandibles are strongly upturned with only 1 marginal tooth; Macuxitermes also has occipital projections, but they are less distinct in this genus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule subquadrate, the sides almost parallel, each posterolateral corner with 1 very distinct projection; head capsule surface densely covered with fine punctures of similar size, forming a micro-sculpture characteristic of the genus; frontal tube conical, upturned, with a rather wide apical opening surrounded by a white membrane; antennae 14-segmented; mandibles slender, piercing-sucking, the blade strongly incurved and upturned, with 1 very small tooth at the base of the blade, molar plate/molar prominence well developed but without ridges; clypeus much reduced; labrum with a rounded, flat, hyaline tip; postmentum subrectangular, anterolateral margins slightly concave; the antero-outer apical margin of each coxa with an outwardly projecting keel-like process; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Head orange, mandibles rust-coloured, body pale yellow.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule circular; postclypeus inflated; antennae 14-segmented; left mandible apical tooth larger than M1+2, the cutting edge between M1+2 and M3 undulate, M3 distinct and smaller than M1+2, molar tooth distinct, partly hidden by the molar prominence, molar prominence concave, without ridges; right mandible apical tooth larger than the marginal tooth, M1 and M2 distinctly separated, molar plate concave, without ridges; coxa smooth, without projections; body slender, the digestive tract visible through the sternites; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Digestive tract: crop asymmetrical, without a constriction between it and the gizzard; gizzard with 24 folds, 6 primary, 6 secondary, 12 tertiary; columnar band and cushion band about equal in width; Malpighian tubules 2 pairs, arising at the midgut–hindgut junction; P1 oblique to the body axis, more inflated than the midgut; P2 on the left side of the body; P3 slightly constricted between P3a and P3b; dorsal torsion well developed; P4a inflated, folded back in a U shape, P4b tubular.

/genus/acanthotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 13–14). Type species of the genus: Acanthotermes acanthothorax (Sjöstedt). The species list (7 African species) is not included in the description. Note: the dimorphic soldier is the older view of Holmgren 1912 (who described only large and small forms); the keys to Macrotermitinae in Grassé 1937 and Treatise 2013 distinguish a medium soldier as well, and the soldiers of this genus are now regarded as large, medium and small.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldiers are of three sizes — large, medium and small — which is the most conspicuous character of the genus; alate antennae 20–23-segmented, the male with 1–2 more segments than the female, soldier antennae 17–20-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum with spines, lateral margins of the thoracic tergites more or less acute. All known species are from Africa.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broad, nearly circular. Compound eyes medium-sized and protruding; ocelli directed slightly laterally, nearly circular, about one eye diameter from the compound eyes. Frontal gland opening present. Base of the clypeus even longer than half its width, rather narrow, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight, considerably raised, distinctly brighter than the frons; distal part of the clypeus transparent. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type dentition, the first tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than the second. Pronotum with two small tuberculate projections on each side of the midline. Posterior notch of the mesonotum slightly wider than that of the metanotum. Wings transparent, with brown veins at the base and along the anterior margin, membrane weakly reticulate; radius reduced, not extending beyond the wing scale; media of the forewing separate from the wing scale, media of the hindwing arising from the base of the radial sector, slender, branching towards the radial sector and the wing apex; cubitus with a thickened inner vein. Sides of the abdomen with exudatory setae, denser in the female; male with styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major soldier: head narrowing more or less anteriorly, sides parallel, oval to cordate, posterior margin straight to strongly concave. Frontal gland opening distinct, surrounded by a circular area bearing setae, with a spine-like projection in front of the opening; base of the mandibles stout. Base of the clypeus very short, distal part rather large and transparent. Labrum rather wide, distal part trilobed and transparent. Mandibles rather short and stout, more or less strongly curved, each with a more or less sharp large basal tooth; left mandible with an additional 3 to several rather small tuberculate teeth, its base often notched and projecting as a tooth; rest of the right mandible toothless. Postmentum long, narrow, parallel-sided. Anterior margin of the pronotum with two pointed projections on each side of the midline, rather small, anterolateral angles rather sharp; lateral parts of mesonotum and metanotum more or less acute. Legs long, the last tarsomere distinctly longer than the remaining tarsomeres together, slender. Cerci large; styli present but small, or reduced.
Minor soldier: head rather parallel-sided, oval, widest at the level of the antennae; in lateral view both upper and lower surfaces rather convex, the lower especially wrinkled. The frontal gland opening is likewise surrounded by a ring of setae, sometimes raised into a tube, with a distinct spine on its anterior margin. Clypeus rather short, posterior margin convex, anterior margin straight, with a transparent distal part. Labrum pointed, distal part transparent and trilobed. Mandibles narrow, weakly sickle-shaped, the base of the left mandible with tooth marks, the basal tooth weakly developed. Antennae long, 15–20-segmented, segment 2 shorter than segment 3. Postmentum elongate, strongly convex, narrow and parallel-sided. Anterior margin of the pronotum with spines. Cerci large; styli present.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Two forms. Head large, broadly oval, coronal suture distinct, frontal gland opening large and triangular. Base of the clypeus short, much shorter than half its width, raised, distal part large. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles shorter and wider than in the alate, but with the same dentition. Antennae 17–21-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3. Pronotum with stout anterior projections. Legs long, foretrochanter with two stout anterior setae. Cerci large; styli reduced.

/genus/acholotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 139–141. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mandibular apical teeth are long in both castes, and Sands took this as the main character separating Acholotermes from most other genera. Three of the four species are morphologically compact and share much in common; the fourth, A. epius, has a longer mixed segment and a reduced third spur on the fore tibia, resembling certain species of Anenteotermes and Astalotermes, and also clustering with them in numerical classification.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized, head width W 0.70–0.80 mm. Fore tibia slightly to moderately inflated, length/width ratio Ti/Tw 3.91–5.30, with 3 apical spurs, the third usually well developed, small or reduced in only one species. Mandibular apical teeth long to very long, La/Li 0.81–1.07, Ra/Ri 0.97–1.29; left mandible accessory marginal tooth just clear of the molar prominence in surface view or separated by a distinct notch; right mandible with the apex of the 1st marginal tooth distinctly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth, its anterior margin shorter than or equal to the 2nd marginal tooth. Midgut–hindgut junction nearly transverse, to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot (3–4 species), or overlapping up to twice the midgut width and touching the Malpighian tubule knot (4th species). Enteric valve seat distinct but not prominently trilobed, connected by a long neck to the second hindgut pouch, laterally to dorsally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion with scales, the posterior margin of each scale bearing 1 to several minute spines or needles.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 0.84–1.06 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third small to well developed. Mandibular apical teeth long, La/Li 0.68–1.04, Ra/Ri 0.92–1.45; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end level with or slightly clear of the molar prominence edge; right mandible with the apex of the 1st marginal tooth slightly to distinctly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth, its anterior margin equal to or slightly longer than the 2nd marginal tooth. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow to slightly broad at the constriction, M/W 0.25–0.32; transverse suture weak or absent in the type species, present in the other species.

/genus/aciculitermes/.note: The genus-level diagnosis in Emerson 1960 is a single sentence (mandibles without apical points); the remaining characters are taken from that paper's account of the type species (then a monotypic genus); the number of antennal segments of the soldier, the second marginal tooth of the right mandible and the outline of the molar plate were not written into the main text because of the quotation limits of this task. According to the original, the alate was described by John (1925) and Kemner (1931) and Emerson did not examine specimens, so that section is not provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The complete absence of apical points on the soldier mandibles is the primary diagnostic character used by Emerson in 1960 when establishing the genus; the lateral outline of the head from the tip of the nasus to the vertex is almost straight or slightly concave, with only a slight swelling at the base of the nasus; the head is relatively broader than in Subulitermes microsoma. The left mandible index of the worker is 0.73, intermediate between Leucopitermes (0.56) and Subulitermes (1.33).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and frontal projection densely covered with very short microsetae, with a few additional setae on the vertex and at the base of the nasus; head relatively broader than in Subulitermes microsoma; lateral outline of the head from the tip of the nasus to the vertex almost straight or slightly concave, with only a slight swelling at the base of the nasus; mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.73; the apical teeth of both mandibles relatively larger than in Leucopitermes; no notch behind the first marginal tooth of the left mandible; the third marginal tooth of the left mandible rather narrow.

/genus/acidnotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 44–46. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Small body size, together with mandibular morphology, distinguishes it from all other genera. Closely related to Astalotermes, especially A. comis; but the position of the left accessory marginal tooth and the distinctly shorter gut of the worker are both reminiscent of more primitive groups, and numerical classification also separates it widely. Body size overlaps only with Anenteotermes nanus, but the latter differs in the mandibles of both castes, the worker having a long mixed segment and a spinose enteric valve.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Very small, W 0.48–0.57 mm. Fore tibia moderately inflated, Ti/Tw 3.46–3.94, with 3 apical spurs, the third nearly as large as the other two. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.48–0.54, Ra/Ri 0.60–0.68; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end concealed behind the molar prominence in surface view; right mandible proportions as in the alate but with a larger molar plate. Midgut–hindgut junction simple, nearly transverse, without overlap, the midgut short, the Malpighian tubules arising at exactly half its length; first hindgut segment slightly longer than the midgut, slightly inflated, tapering towards the enteric valve; enteric valve seat a simple rim, sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch, lateroventrally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion without spines, scales weak.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very small, W 0.57–0.66 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed, about 2/3 of the other two. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.50–0.56, Ra/Ri 0.62–0.71; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end exactly level with the molar prominence edge; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices in a line, but the 2nd marginal tooth broad and its anterior margin longer than that of the 1st marginal tooth. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.21; transverse suture weak but present.

/genus/acorhinotermes/.note: The original has no separate genus-level Diagnosis section; the generic characters are taken from the generic history in the Introduction and from the first couplet of the subfamily key based on the minor soldier; the rest is the species-level description of A. claritae, marked as species level at each point. The only copy available locally is the publisher's JATS XML (Europe PMC PMC6882922), with no print PDF, so the locator uses section names. An alate is illustrated only for A. subfusciceps, and no alate section was written from it here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The diagnostic character at generic level is the absence of a major soldier, the feature on which Emerson based the removal of the species from Rhinotermes and the erection of this genus; in dorsal view the fontanelle of the minor soldier lies in front of the mandibular lobes (that is, the bases of the mandibular points), which separates it from Dolichorhinotermes and Rhinotermes, in both of which the fontanelle lies at or behind the mandibular lobes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Only the minor soldier is known. In dorsal view the sides of the head are concave, producing a posterior constriction; the vertex bears 10–12 long, erect setae and no microtrichia; antennae 15 or 16 segments, with the formula 2=3<4=5; mandibles reduced, long, straight and sharp; labrum extremely long (hyperelongate), widening towards the apex, which is bilobed, and in lateral view almost in the same plane as the vertex; fontanelle situated at 1/5 of the length from the base of the labrum; pronotum concolorous with the head, bearing 4–8 scattered setae (2–4 on the anterior margin and 2–4 on the dorsum) and no microtrichia; abdominal segments pale yellow, densely hairy at the margins; legs with numerous long and short setae, the fore tibia with stout setae. The mandibular points of the minor soldier of this species are longer than in A. subfusciceps, and the body is relatively smaller.

/genus/acutidentitermes/.note: Of the type species only the soldier and worker are known; the original does not describe the alate. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes but distinguishable in the soldier: head very large, sides slightly convex and nearly parallel; postmentum more bulbous, its lateral margins overlapping and concealing the lateral suture; suture between postclypeus and frons far less distinct; labrum with sharper lateral and median points; anteriorly directed mandibular teeth longer, sharper and more anteriorly directed; anterior lobe of the pronotum larger and longer, the median notch of the anterior margin deeper and wider; fore femur relatively long and slender. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface with only a few rather short setae, none near the fontanelle; postmentum completely hairless, without setae; first 4 abdominal tergites with rather long setae, almost without short hairs, posterior tergites and sternites with additional short hairs. Head very large, sides slightly convex and nearly parallel, fontanelle small. Postmentum more bulbous than in Hoplognathotermes, its posterior lateral margins overlapping, so that in ventral view the outer suture is concealed except near the posterior margin; posterior part of the postmentum without a transverse ridge. Antennae 15-segmented. Suture between postclypeus and frons far less distinct than in Hoplognathotermes. Labrum with sharper lateral and median points. Both mandibles with conspicuous anteriorly directed teeth, but longer, sharper and more anteriorly directed than in Hoplognathotermes; apical outward curvature weaker; the notch on the side at the boundary between apex and base less conspicuous. Anterior lobe of the pronotum larger and longer than in Hoplognathotermes, the median notch of the anterior margin more conspicuous and wider, the posterior margin more concave. Fore coxa simple, the longitudinal ridge obtuse, moderately sharp, straight or slightly convex in section, without coarse spines; fore femur relatively long and slender. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Differs from Hoplognathotermes as follows: the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of both mandibles is sharper; the cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible are proportionally slightly longer; the upper ridge of the molar region of the right mandible is sharper and more concave.

/genus/adaiphrotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 229–231. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Fore tibia with only 2 apical spurs; no other African genus lacks the third apical spur entirely, so this genus is the most easily recognised. The worker gut has a white midgut “ball”, recognisable even without opening the abdomen; the worker abdomen does not rupture. Aderitotermes and Anenteotermes also have a long mixed segment, but the midgut is not inflated distally in those two.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small to medium-sized, W 0.59–0.75 mm. Fore tibia with only 2 apical spurs, hairy, with prominent setae on the posterior margin, inflated, Ti/Tw 3.00–4.00. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.46–0.64, Ra/Ri 0.65–1.10; left mandible accessory marginal tooth clearly clear of the molar prominence proximally; right mandible apical and marginal teeth about equal in length and their apices in a line. Midgut and hindgut overlap to form an elongated mixed segment extending past the Malpighian tubule knot, the midgut distally inflated into a spherical or hemispherical form. First hindgut segment long and inflated, abruptly constricted into a narrow tubular enteric valve; enteric valve seat with 2 or 3 lobes, or a simple rim, sessile or with a short neck, dorsally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion without spines, reticulate or weakly scaly, mostly concentrated proximally.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small to medium-sized, W 0.71–1.01 mm. Fore tibia with only 2 apical spurs. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.43–0.57, Ra/Ri 0.66–0.93; left mandible accessory marginal tooth clearly clear of the molar prominence proximally; right mandible 1st and 2nd marginal teeth about equal in length and in a line with the apical tooth. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.16–0.23; mesonotal suture absent, metanotal suture weak or absent.

/genus/aderitotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 222–223. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is easily recognised by the combination of a prominent fontanelle, a very short, fine, even silvery head pilosity and large size; the only sympatric superficially similar species is Astratotermes prosenus, which is larger and has uneven pilosity. The long mixed segment of the worker distinguishes it from most other genera; Adaiphrotermes shares this feature, but its midgut is inflated distally and that of this genus is not.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, W 0.90–0.99 mm. Fore tibia weakly to scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 4.21–5.31, with 3 apical spurs, the third about half the other two. Mandibular apical teeth rather short to medium-long, La/Li 0.60–0.79, Ra/Ri 0.78–1.00; left mandible accessory marginal tooth separated from the molar prominence by a distinct notch; right mandible 1st marginal tooth apex slightly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth, the marginal tooth anterior margins equal in length. Midgut and hindgut overlap, elongated into a distinct mixed segment about 4–5 times the midgut width at the Malpighian tubule insertion, the proximal hindgut far to the left of the Malpighian tubule knot. Enteric valve seat with 3 prominent equal lobes, regularly arranged, connected by a distinct to very long neck to the second hindgut pouch, entirely dorsal in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion retracted or protruding through the valve opening, not sclerotised, the surface scaly, the valve wall with minute to prominent small spines between and outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Large, W 1.04–1.31 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed, about 2/3 of the other two. Mandibular apical teeth rather short, La/Li 0.54–0.68, Ra/Ri 0.73–1.06; left mandible accessory marginal tooth separated from the molar prominence by a distinct notch; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices about in a line, the 1st and 2nd marginal tooth anterior margins equal in length. Fontanelle round to shortly oval, prominent, markedly paler than the head capsule; head pilosity of short, fine, even silvery felt hairs, with projecting setae. Meso- and metanotal plates rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.28–0.34, transverse suture present.

/genus/adynatotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 102–104. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, separated from Astalotermes mainly by the uniquely developed enteric valve seat; in multivariate similarity analysis close to A. empodius, A. aganus and A. mitis, distinguishable only by several latent vector values. It resembles Acidnotermes in that the left accessory marginal tooth barely emerges from the molar prominence; the worker gut is shorter than in most Astalotermes.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, W 0.85–0.90 mm. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Tw 4.13–4.54, with 3 apical spurs, the third about half the other two. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.53–0.60, Ra/Ri 0.75–0.82; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end level with the molar prominence edge; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices in a line, the marginal tooth anterior margins equal in length. Midgut and hindgut only slightly bent, nearly transverse, to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot. Enteric valve seat with two opposing erect lobes, almost diverticulate, connected by a very short neck to the second hindgut pouch, lateroventrally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion without spines, the surface only weakly reticulate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Large, W 1.14–1.21 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed, nearly as large as the other two. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.51–0.57, Ra/Ri 0.73–0.87; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end exactly level with the molar prominence edge; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices in a line, the marginal tooth anterior margins equal in length. Meso- and metanotal plates rather narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.24–0.28, transverse suture absent.

/genus/afrosubulitermes/.note: Emerson (1960) erected the genus with descriptions of the soldier and worker only; the alate was first described by Sands (1965) and is included in the generic characters. Sands disagreed with Emerson's view that the genus is closely related to Verrucositermes, considering it more likely that the latter arose separately from an ancestor near Eutermellus (p. 154). Emerson recorded a left mandible index of 1.47 for the worker and Sands 1.36–1.39; the samples differ, and the source must be cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands considered this genus the closest to Eutermellus among the Ethiopian genera, and the generic boundary between the two is not as clear-cut as the original description suggested: the main features of the genus are the very small size and greatly reduced pilosity of the alate together with the relatively short nasus of the soldier; it also shares characters of Postsulitermes and appears intermediate between that genus and Eutermellus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Apical tooth of the left mandible distinctly longer than the first marginal tooth, but the distance between them slightly shorter than that between the first and third marginal teeth (left mandible index 0.89–0.94); the cutting edge in front of the third marginal tooth deeply concave, slightly undulate or nearly straight. Postclypeus almost flat, following the contour of the head, 2–3 times as wide as long. The fontanelle appears as a slender narrow ridge, visible only in oblique light on the highly polished head capsule, with a pale elliptical spot in front of it. Compound eyes not projecting from the sides of the head. Head almost hairless, with only paired conspicuous setae on the vertex, between the ocelli, and on the middle and anterior margin of the postclypeus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Nasus slender, cylindrical, tapering to a fine point; reduced mandibles without an apical process; anterior margin of the labrum undulate; antennae 12 segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in the alate, but the apical tooth proportionally longer (left mandible index 1.36–1.39); the cutting edge behind the first left marginal tooth more undulate; the ridge on the right molar plate more pronounced.

/genus/aganotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 135–137. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, somewhat close to Adynatotermes and to some Astalotermes, but easily recognised by the long mandibular apical teeth. Acholotermes also has equally long apical teeth, but in this genus the meso- and metanotal plates are narrower and the ocelli are farther from the compound eyes; the worker enteric valve seat has a shorter neck and a more ventral position. Asagarotermes and Amicotermes also have long apical teeth, but in both the left accessory marginal tooth is clearly clear of the molar prominence, the ocelli are closer to the compound eyes and the postclypeus is more inflated, and the worker enteric valves each have a distinctive structure.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, W 0.86–0.94 mm. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 5.00–5.53, with 3 apical spurs, the third about 1/3 of the other two. Mandibular apical teeth very long, La/Li 0.97–1.00, Ra/Ri 1.25–1.29; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end level with the molar prominence edge; right mandible 1st marginal tooth anterior margin longer than the 2nd. Midgut and hindgut overlap about twice the midgut width or slightly more, the proximal hindgut within the Malpighian tubule knot, to the left. Enteric valve seat with two very weak lobes, connected by a very short neck to the second hindgut pouch, ventrally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion without spines, the surface scaly.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Large, W 1.11–1.23 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed, slightly shorter than the other two. Mandibular apical teeth long, La/Li 0.79–0.83, Ra/Ri 1.11–1.19; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end level with the molar prominence edge; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices in a line, the 1st marginal tooth anterior margin longer than the 2nd. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.21–0.24, transverse suture absent. Ocelli far from the compound eyes.

/genus/agnathotermes/.note: Snyder 1926 described it at subgenus level (as a subgenus of Nasutitermes); this entry treats it at genus level. The original also has statements on the length of the worker postclypeus and on body colour, but because of an OCR word break (Light- colored) they could not be quoted verbatim and were not written into the main text. The alate is not described in the original, so that section is not provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier mandibles lack apical points, the nasus is short and conical; antennae 11–12 segments; the vertex bears only 2–3 long setae in addition to numerous microsetae, the number of long setae being fewer than in Coatitermes. In the worker the cutting edge between the 1+2 marginal tooth and the third marginal tooth of the left mandible is not undulate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without apical points; nasus short, conical; antennae 11–12 segments; vertex with only 2–3 long setae in addition to numerous microsetae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The cutting edge from the 1+2 marginal tooth to the third marginal tooth of the left mandible is not undulate.

/genus/ahamitermes/.note: Established by Mjöberg (1920: 89) for A. nidicola from Queensland, at the time described only from the soldier (the holotype is a single soldier collected from the side of a nest of Coptotermes lacteus); Hill (1942: 308) reduced it to a subgenus of Hamitermes and added subgeneric key characters. The present list treats it as a separate genus. Complete accounts of the worker and alate are not given in the original description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Small, of the Hamitermes type. Soldier mandibles toothless (the original description says “without a median tooth”), which distinguishes it from Hamitermes s. str. (mandibles with well-developed teeth) and Microcerotermes (inner margin of the mandibles largely finely serrate); Hill's (1942: 310) subgeneric key additionally defines this group by “soldier mandibles lacking or with reduced teeth” and “terminal segment of the alate maxillary palp swollen”. Hill (1942: 308) noted that the genus was originally established on species with toothless soldier mandibles, the alate characters being added later from related species. All species live in the nests of Coptotermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head small, longer than wide, with a rounded posterior margin; clypeus small; labrum long and wide, narrowed towards the apex, which is rounded; mandibles short and robust, separated from each other, without a median tooth; antennae very short, 12-segmented; pronotum wide, only its anterior margin slightly ridge-like. Soldier of A. nidicola: body white, head and prothorax pale yellow, mandibles reddish brown; head small, slightly narrowed anteriorly, longer than wide, with a rounded posterior margin; basal segment of the clypeus very short and yellow, the apical segment white; labrum large and wide, narrowed at the sides, rounded apically and hairy; mandibles very short and robust, broad at the base, curved and completely toothless (only the inner side of the left mandible bears two extremely minute, almost invisible “teeth”); antennae pale yellow, segment 2 about half as long and half as wide as segment 1, segment 3 extremely short; pronotum wide, its anterior margin slightly ridge-like, the sides rounded and narrowed towards the base; legs rather short, the femora relatively thick, the tarsi slender. Measurements (A. nidicola, mm): body length including mandibles 4.4, head length including mandibles 1.56, head length excluding mandibles 1.31, head width 0.87, pronotum length 0.29 and width 0.72, abdominal width 1.4.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Terminal segment of the maxillary palp swollen, the alate character by which Hill (1942: 310) separates this group from Hamitermes s. str.; apart from this, the original description gives no complete account of the alate.

/genus/allognathotermes/.note: In the full text available locally (Emerson 1956) this genus has only species-level descriptions and a discussion of its systematic position, with no separate genus-level morphological account; Emerson 1959 also does not treat the genus separately, its generic characters occurring scattered in comparative sentences within the generic characters of Duplidentitermes. Hence only those genus-level comparative features that explicitly concern Allognathotermes are included here, without supplementation or extrapolation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes and Duplidentitermes. The mandibular teeth of the soldier are less conspicuous than in those two, but the left mandible has 2 rather widely separated teeth, apparently homologous with the bidentate teeth of Duplidentitermes; the fore coxal ridge is very similar to that of Duplidentitermes, only slightly more evident because it extends with a slight inward curve; the fore femur is short and stout, as in Duplidentitermes, and clearly different from the slender fore femur of Firmitermes, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes. The second marginal tooth of the right mandible of the alate is reduced to a small mound.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The second marginal tooth of the right mandible is reduced to a small mound, as in Duplidentitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The mandibular teeth are less conspicuous than in Hoplognathotermes and Duplidentitermes, but the left mandible has 2 rather widely separated teeth, apparently homologous with the bidentate teeth of the left mandible of Duplidentitermes. The longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa is very similar to that of Duplidentitermes, only slightly more evident owing to a slightly curved inward extension. The fore femur is short and stout, as in Duplidentitermes, whereas in Firmitermes, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes it is slender.

/genus/allotermes/.note: Adapted from the genus-level account of Krishna (1961); the original is in English and not translated verbatim.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Procryptotermes, but the soldier lacks a ridge between the frons and the vertex and has a club-shaped third antennal segment; the alate lacks an arolium.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Eye diameter about 0.35–0.36 mm, ocelli touching the compound eyes; bases of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible distinctly smaller than the third marginal tooth, their posterior margin about half the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth; pronotum slightly narrower than the head or as wide as the head; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and narrow, sides parallel, anterior part inclined downwards at about 45°; no ridge between the frons and the vertex; a weak angular projection anteroventral to the antennal socket; eyes distinct, pigmented in some species; antennae 10–12-segmented, the third segment dark, heavily sclerotised and long club-shaped; mandibles long, with a distinct basal tubercle, teeth reduced; pronotum as wide as the head, anterior margin broad and deeply concave, sides rounded.

/genus/alyscotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 125–127. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The row of spines on the worker enteric valve inner cushion forms the most conspicuous diagnostic feature of this genus: the spines at positions 3 and 4 are prominent and project through the valve opening, and are usually visible on alcohol-preserved specimens at about 100× magnification. Only Amalotermes has similar spines on the enteric valve, but its worker has a small, brown head and the spines are almost radially symmetrical.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized to very large, W 0.81–1.11 mm. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.28–7.36, with 3 apical spurs, the third usually well developed, sometimes reduced but never vestigial. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.50–0.67, Ra/Ri 0.66–0.87; left mandible accessory marginal tooth separated from the molar prominence by a deep notch; right mandible apical and marginal teeth in a line, the marginal tooth anterior margins nearly equal or the 1st slightly longer. Midgut and hindgut joined obliquely, to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot. Enteric valve seat distinctly bilobed, sometimes with a very weak third lobe, connected by a distinct neck to the second hindgut pouch, dorsally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion unequally developed, positions 1 and 2 retracted, positions 3 and 4 slightly longer and protruding through the valve opening, all spinose, the spines of the middle 1/3 minute, those of the distal 1/3 small to prominent and projecting through the valve opening, especially at positions 3 and 4.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized to large, W 0.90–1.35 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third only slightly smaller than the other two. Mandibular apical teeth rather short, La/Li 0.49–0.66, Ra/Ri 0.67–0.99; left mandible accessory marginal tooth clearly removed from the molar prominence; right mandible apical and marginal tooth apices nearly in a line, the 1st marginal tooth anterior margin distinctly longer than the 2nd. Meso- and metanotal plates moderately to distinctly broad at the constriction, M/W 0.28–0.37, transverse suture present, usually distinct.

/genus/amalotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 47–50. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus with a bizarre combination of characters, possessing features regarded as both primitive and specialised, and difficult to place in any known genus; this conventional conclusion is also confirmed by multivariate analysis. The enteric valve spines are somewhat similar to those of Alyscotermes, but the worker of this genus has a small, brown head and the enteric valve spines are almost radially symmetrical.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 0.74–0.79 mm. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 6.14–6.43, with 3 apical spurs, but the third vestigial, almost disappearing in most specimens. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.41–0.51, Ra/Ri 0.53–0.66; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end concealed behind the molar prominence in surface view; right mandible 1st marginal tooth anterior margin distinctly shorter than the 2nd. Midgut and hindgut overlap up to about twice the midgut width at the Malpighian tubule insertion, extending to half of the Malpighian tubule knot. Enteric valve seat weakly bilobed, connected by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch, laterally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion lobes about equally developed, the distal ends bearing prominent coarse spines projecting through the valve opening.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 0.81–0.90 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, but the third vestigial, almost disappearing in some specimens. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.38–0.48, Ra/Ri 0.56–0.65; left mandible accessory marginal tooth with its proximal end concealed behind the molar prominence; right mandible 1st marginal tooth anterior margin about equal in length to the 2nd, its apex slightly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth. Meso- and metanotal plates rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.25–0.28, transverse suture distinct, usually clear.

/genus/amicotermes/.note: Generic characters in Sands 1972 pp. 152–154. The original gives only body size (head width W, mm), number of fore tibial apical spurs, mandibular tooth ratios, meso- and metanotal constriction (M/W), fontanelle and head pilosity (where present), and gut/enteric valve structure; antennal segment number, pronotal shape and wing venation are not recorded, so no supplementation is made in this entry. Decimal points shown as “*” in the OCR and i/1 confusions have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compound eyes relatively small, W/E about 4.5; all other genera and species are below 4.2, most below 4.0. Fore coxa and remaining legs strongly setose, the tibial apex and femoral base with opposing interlocking setae when folded, the only genus with this feature. Worker enteric valve inner cushion spinose, the valve wall also with a fringe of fine spines.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 0.76 mm. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Tw about 4.3, with 3 apical spurs, the third small, about 1/3 of the other two. Fore coxa and remaining legs strongly setose and spinose, the setae at the tibial apex and femoral base opposing and interlocking when folded. Mandibular apical teeth very long, La/Li 1.09, Ra/Ri 1.33; left mandible accessory marginal tooth just clear of the molar prominence; right mandible 1st marginal tooth apex distinctly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth, the 1st and 2nd marginal tooth anterior margins nearly equal. Midgut and hindgut nearly transverse, slightly bent, to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot. Enteric valve seat distinctly trilobed, the third lobe only slightly smaller than the two outer lobes, connected by a very long neck to the second hindgut pouch, laterally situated in the unopened abdomen; enteric valve inner cushion protruding through the valve opening, position 3 slightly longer than the rest, each bearing numerous irregularly arranged long spines on the posterior 1/3, the remaining surface scaly, most scale margins with small spines or spinules; the valve wall with numerous fine but prominent small spines outside the cushions, and a spine fringe between the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 1.01 mm. Compound eyes relatively small, W/E about 4.5. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third very small, almost vestigial; fore coxa densely setose, the anterior margin slightly spinose. Mandibular apical teeth very long, La/Li 0.99, Ra/Ri 1.36; left mandible accessory marginal tooth just clear of the molar prominence; right mandible 1st marginal tooth apex distinctly behind the line between the apical tooth and the 2nd marginal tooth, the 1st and 2nd marginal tooth anterior margins nearly equal. Meso- and metanotal plates rather narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.28, transverse suture absent.

/genus/amitermes/.note: Based only on the soldier diagnostic couplet in the North American generic key of De Luna et al. 2023 (thin), not a complete set of generic characters.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles curved, usually shorter than head length; mandible bases arising near the anterolateral corners of the head, inner margin smooth.

/genus/amplucrutermes/.note: The generic name means “large foot” (amplus = large, crus = foot). The source describes the worker only and states Imago: Unknown, so no soldier or alate section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the Neotropical soldierless termites (Anoplotermes group) it can be distinguished from all other known genera by the strongly inflated fore tibia and by the structure of the enteric valve: the fore tibia resembles that of Tetimatermes but has a shallower depression and no glandular structure proximally; the enteric valve consists of about 100 scales and about 15 weakly sclerotised apical spines and is likewise diagnostic.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized. Head pale yellow, circular to slightly oval, with about 60 setae in all; fontanelle indistinct; fore tibia strongly inflated, about 3 times as long as wide. The enteric valve is inserted within an extension of the paunch and consists of 6 elongate cushions, each with about 100 scales and about 15 weakly sclerotised spines on the posterior margin.

/genus/ampoulitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (A. wynaadensis Mathur & Thapa), known only from the Periyar reserve in Kerala, India. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus of Nasutitermitinae; soldier head capsule dark brown to chocolate brown, pear-shaped, strongly constricted behind the antennae, posterior margin concave at the middle, nasus long and cylindrical, antennae 12-segmented, mandibles reduced, laterally bluntly pointed; pronotum small, saddle-shaped, with a notch at the middle of the anterior margin. Worker antennae 13–14-segmented, molar plate of left mandible weakly projecting, level with the second marginal tooth.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown to chocolate brown, pear-shaped, strongly constricted behind the antennae, posterior margin concave at the middle; nasus long, cylindrical; antennae 12-segmented, segments short, segment 3 longer and narrower than segment 2; mandibles reduced, laterally bluntly pointed; pronotum small, saddle-shaped, with a notch at the middle of the anterior margin; tibial apical spurs 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; abdomen hairy, with short and long hairs; cerci 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown to brown, subcircular; coronal suture present; frontal plate elongate, white; antennae 13–14-segmented; postclypeus moderately raised, less than half as long as wide; left mandible with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth and first marginal tooth both pointed and nearly equal in length, the angle between them acute; second marginal tooth short, separated from the first marginal tooth by the long posterior margin of the first marginal tooth; molar plate (basal process) weakly projecting, level with the second marginal tooth; right mandible with the apical tooth and first marginal tooth as on the left, second marginal tooth short with a nearly straight posterior margin, molar plate longer than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum saddle-shaped; legs and abdomen as in the soldier.

/genus/anacanthotermes/.note: The monograph does not provide a separate generic diagnosis; the genus-level characters listed above are summarised from its genus-level distribution, the alate and soldier keys and the accounts of the four species. Four species are known from the Indian region (baluchistanicus, macrocephalus, vagans, viarum); the genus comprises 12 species in all.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One of the three genera of Hodotermitinae, distributed from North Africa, Egypt, West Asia, Arabia and Central Asia to western and southern India. Soldier head subquadrate to slightly elongate, the sides nearly parallel, mandibles stout and incurved with distinct marginal teeth, ratio of left mandible length to head length (to mandible base) 0.66–0.76 in viarum and 0.53–0.66 in macrocephalus; posterior third of postmentum sometimes with a distinct “waist”; posterior margin of pronotum deeply concave, weakly concave or not concave at the middle. Alate antennae 24–31-segmented, median part of labrum sometimes raised, distance between compound eye and antennal base 0.05–0.16 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small to medium-sized, body length (excluding wings) 11–15.4 mm. Median part of labrum raised (A. viarum) or straight (A. vagans); antennae 29–31-segmented (baluchistanicus, head width including eyes 3.20–3.42 mm, compound eye diameter 0.63–0.70 mm, pronotum width 2.53–2.90 mm), 26–29-segmented (macrocephalus, mostly 27, Afghan specimens 24; head width 2.70–3.40 mm), 24–27-segmented (vagans); minimum distance between compound eye and antennal base 0.13–0.16 mm (viarum, baluchistanicus) or 0.05–0.08 mm (macrocephalus).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic (major and minor soldiers). Head reddish brown to chestnut brown, subquadrate, slightly elongate, the sides nearly parallel and slightly concave at the middle, covered with moderately long hairs; postclypeus indistinct; coronal suture present; labrum wider than long, hairy throughout, the anterior hairs longer; antennae 23–25-segmented (baluchistanicus); mandibles stout with well-developed marginal teeth, left mandible length 2.71 mm (baluchistanicus major soldier); postmentum long (length 2.91 mm, maximum width 1.02 mm, minimum width 0.87 mm), flat, the sides nearly parallel, the lateral margins of the posterior third weakly concave forming a “waist” (viarum, macrocephalus) or not forming a “waist” (baluchistanicus, vagans); anterior part of pronotum weakly raised and convex, posterior margin deeply concave at the middle (baluchistanicus), weakly concave (viarum, macrocephalus) or not concave (vagans); tarsi 4-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles with 2 marginal teeth, the two marginal teeth far apart on the left mandible and close together on the right mandible.

/genus/anaorotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 184–186. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from Ateuchotermes and Aderitotermes by the dense, irregular head pilosity, which does not form a felt, and from Alyscotermes, Astalotermes and Astratotermes by the oddly shaped, almost triangular fontanelle; Amicotermes has longer apical teeth. The worker enteric valve is unique in structure, and Sands considered no comparison necessary.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, W 0.88 mm. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.89, with 3 apical spurs, the third smaller than the other two but not reduced. Apical tooth of the mandible short, La/Li 0.53, Ra/Ri 0.80; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible has just left the molar prominence; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line joining the apical tooth and the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is slightly shorter than that of the second. Midgut and hindgut overlap, extending to about twice the width of the midgut at the insertion of the Malpighian tubules, close to the right of the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat with 2 rather prominent outer lobes and 1 smaller inner lobe, joined by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch, whose muscle coat is very thick; in the undissected abdomen it lies dorsally. The four enteric valve cushions differ in form: the first is reduced, retracted and not sclerotised, at most with 1–2 minute scales or teeth on its inner face; the second projects slightly through the valve opening and bears 1 or 2 elongated sclerotised spines, the rest being a few minute spines; the third is sclerotised at the apex, hemispherical and evaginated, covered with about 35 stout, long, curved spines; the fourth projects through the valve opening, is sclerotised at the apex and bears 7–8 long outwardly curved spines arranged like a rake.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Large, W 1.11–1.13 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed. Apical tooth of the mandible short, La/Li 0.49–0.51, Ra/Ri 0.75–0.81; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is clear of the molar prominence; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are more or less in line, and the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth are equal in length. Meso- and metanotal plates moderately wide at the constriction, M/W 0.31, transverse sutures present. Fontanelle almost triangular; head pilosity dense and irregular, not forming a felt.

/genus/anenteotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 192–194. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The most important diagnostic character is the mixed segment of the worker gut. Body size varies greatly within the genus (alate W 0.65–1.06 mm), and the width of the meso- and metanotal constriction and the mandibular proportions also span most of the range, so Sands based the genus on the gut rather than on measurements.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Very small to medium-sized, W 0.56–0.84 mm. Fore tibia moderately to scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 3.58–5.00, with 3 apical spurs, the third smaller than the other two, reduced in one species only. Apical tooth of the mandible short to moderately long, La/Li 0.46–0.73, Ra/Ri 0.54–0.89; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible has just left to far clear of the molar prominence; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly to distinctly behind the line joining the apical tooth and the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin equals or is shorter than that of the second, usually shorter. Midgut and hindgut overlap and are prolonged into a distinct mixed segment, the proximal end of the hindgut lying far to the left of the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat weakly bilobed or trilobed, the third lobe usually smaller, sessile or joined by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch; in the undissected abdomen it lies laterally to dorsally. Enteric valve cushions retracted or projecting through the valve opening, sometimes elongate and sclerotised, bearing scales or spines from small to long, the long spines sometimes comb-like.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very small to medium-sized, W 0.65–1.06 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed. Apical tooth of the mandible short to moderately long, La/Li 0.42–0.76, Ra/Ri 0.62–1.00; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to distinctly clear of the molar prominence; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, or the first marginal tooth is set back behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth; the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth may be longer than, equal to or shorter than that of the second. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow to rather wide at the constriction, M/W 0.19–0.31, transverse sutures usually present but not strong.

/genus/angularitermes/.note: The genus was described by Emerson in 1925 as a subgenus of Nasutitermes; that paper describes only the soldier, the alate and the king for the type species and does not describe the worker, so no Worker section is provided. Worker characters are given in Fontes 1987 in a comparison with A. orestes and are species-level material, so they are not included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The nasus of the soldier is very large relative to the head, the most developed nasus known to Emerson among nasute soldier termites; the mandibles have long apical points, the base of the left mandible bears a very small microscopic tooth, and the base of the right mandible is toothless. In the alate the posterior margin of the head is angular behind the eyes in dorsal view.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, constricted behind the antennae, densely covered with setae; antennae 14 segments, segment 3 one and a half times segment 2, segment 4 equal to or slightly longer than segment 3; mandibles with long apical points, the base of the left mandible with a very small microscopic tooth, the base of the right mandible toothless; nasus darker than the head, densely covered with short hairs from the constriction of the head to the apex, very thick and long, with a thick base.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, sparsely covered with long hairs; head oval, its posterior margin angular behind the eyes in dorsal view.

/genus/angulitermes/.note: The book treats numerous species of the Indian region one by one in a dedicated section; the genus is one of the most species-rich in the Indian Termitidae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A large genus of the Oriental region. Soldier small, slender and pale; the anterior margin of the labrum incurved, its anterolateral corners produced into horn-like processes; mandibles slender and rod-like, incurved apically and slightly of the snapping type, as long as or longer than the head; postmentum short and club-shaped; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, the dorsal spurs of the fore tibia extremely small. Worker antennae 14-segmented; alate antennae 15-segmented, the wing membrane bearing stellate and non-stellate microtrichia.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small, brown, densely covered with short and long setae; head nearly circular; frontal plate minute to elongate and slit-like; compound eyes round, medium-sized; ocelli elliptical, far removed from the compound eyes; antennae 15-segmented; postclypeus arched, about half as long as wide; apical tooth of the mandibles larger than the first marginal tooth; posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the left mandible only slightly longer than its anterior margin, the second marginal tooth separated by a notch; anterior and posterior margins of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible subequal in length, the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth incurved; pronotum semicircular or nearly trapezoidal, slightly narrower than the head width including the eyes; tibial spur formula of the fore tibia 3:2:2; wings pale brown, the membranous surface hairy, the anterior and posterior margins with papillae, the membrane with stellate and non-stellate microtrichia; costa thick, running along the anterior margin; radius as thick as the costa, parallel and closely adjacent to it; media weak, with few branches, arising independently in the forewing and from the radius in the hindwing; cubitus with 10–12 branches.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small, slender and pale, sparsely to rather densely hairy; head nearly rectangular, with frontal tubercles; fontanelle situated beneath the frontal tubercles; antennae 14-segmented; anterior margin of the labrum incurved, the anterolateral corners produced into horn-like processes; mandibles slender and rod-like, incurved apically and slightly of the snapping type, as long as or longer than the head; postmentum short and club-shaped; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, the dorsal spurs minute and sometimes indistinct.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small, slender and pale, rather densely hairy; head nearly circular; frontal plate indistinct, with a circular translucent spot; antennae 14-segmented; postclypeus strongly arched, about half as long as wide or slightly more than half; mandibles as in the alate, the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible more strongly incurved; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, the anterior marginal notch weak or absent; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, the dorsal spurs of the fore tibia extremely small, sometimes almost invisible.

/genus/anhangatermes/.note: The original explicitly states 'IMAGO - Unknown', so no Alate section is provided; the original also gives body hairs, a tibial spur formula of 2:2:2 and gut characters, which are omitted from the main text because they are not covered by the quotations used in this section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier head capsule is broadly rounded and the nasus conical-cylindrical, long and slender; the labrum is short and not visible in dorsal view; antennae 13 segments, extending slightly beyond the tip of the nasus; the pronotum is about half as wide as the head. The worker is monomorphic, with a large, rounded, ridge-less molar prominence on the left mandible, and the third marginal tooth of the right mandible is almost lost.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule broad and rounded; nasus conical-cylindrical, long and slender; labrum short, not visible in dorsal view; reduced mandibles without apical points; antennae 13 segments, extending slightly beyond the tip of the nasus; pronotum about half as wide as the head; head almost bare, with only a few setae on the vertex and hairs at the tip of the nasus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monomorphic; head capsule rounded, widest in the anterior part; postclypeus moderately inflated; antennae 14 segments; few setae on the head; apical mandibular teeth well developed, the inner margin concave; the molar prominence of the left mandible large and rounded, without a ridge; the third marginal tooth of the right mandible reduced and almost lost, the molar plate concave.

/genus/anoplotermes/.note: The original explicitly records that soldiers are entirely absent, hence this genus has only the alate and worker sections. This is a Neotropical genus; the African "Anoplotermes" has been separated out, so the African literature (Sands 1972) does not contain the generic characters of this genus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldiers entirely absent. Alate head very broad, usually densely hairy, compound eyes small and prominent, the fontanelle situated far back or at the middle of the head; antennae constantly 15-segmented, segment 3 much shorter; wings dark, hairy and spinose; tibiae with 2 apical spurs. Worker similar to the worker of Eutermes, postclypeus strongly arched, antennae constantly 14-segmented, head mostly pale, fontanelle indistinct.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head very broad, usually densely hairy, compound eyes small and prominent; fontanelle either far back or at the middle of the head; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the compound eyes variable; basal piece of the postclypeus almost always at least half as long as its width (except A. iheringi), usually strongly arched; transverse band longer in the middle than at the sides; mandibles with 1 large apical tooth, slightly elongate; antennae constantly 15-segmented, segment 3 usually far shorter than the adjacent segments; brain large. Pronotum as in Eutermes; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum more or less deeply concave; wings dark, hairy and spinose, venation as in Eutermes; tibiae with 2 apical spurs; abdomen elongate, the sides of the female with glandular hairs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Similar to the worker of Eutermes; postclypeus strongly arched, as long as or even longer than half its width; antennae constantly 14-segmented, segment 3 mostly shorter than the adjacent segments; head mostly pale, fontanelle indistinct.

/genus/apagotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 155–156. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The small size separates it from many genera, including Amicotermes, which is similar in the surface of the worker enteric valve. The alate resembles Astratotermes obstructus, but the latter has a slightly longer postclypeus, wider meso- and metanotal plates, and ocelli closer to the compound eye.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Very small, W 0.58 mm. Fore tibia moderately inflated, Ti/Tw 3.84, with 3 apical spurs, the third about half as long as the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible short, La/Li 0.52, Ra/Ri 0.67; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is level with the edge of the molar prominence; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line joining the apical tooth and the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is shorter than that of the second. Midgut and hindgut are almost transverse, lying to the right of the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat weakly trilobed, the two outer lobes tending to oppose each other but not longer than the third lobe, joined by a distinct and very short neck to the second hindgut pouch; in the undissected abdomen it lies dorsally. Enteric valve cushions project equally through the valve opening, each bearing regularly arranged long spines on its posterior third, the spines below the outermost row slightly spatulate or sword-shaped, the first and third (alternating) cushions bearing slightly fewer spines, the remaining surface with small spines or spinules.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small, W 0.74 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third almost as large as the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible short, La/Li 0.55, Ra/Ri 0.67–0.71; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible has just left the molar prominence; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are almost in line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth being shorter than that of the second, which is curved. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.21, transverse sutures present, the mesonotal one weak. Ocelli close to the compound eye.

/genus/aparatermes/.note: Soldierless. The genus-level description covers only the worker enteric valve and midgut tongue; species counts and distribution data are not used in this batch.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One branch of the Neotropical soldierless Apicotermitinae, defined by a combination of worker enteric valve characters: interpad cuticle without scales, enteric valve seating (EVS) three-lobed — in the 2023 worker key the 14th couplet leads directly to this genus on this combination. The enteric valve armature (EVA) consists of small spines or pointed scales distributed over the central part of each pad, the posterior part of the pads without scales.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Enteric valve seating three-lobed, interpad cuticle bare, without scales; enteric valve with small spines or pointed scales, the pointed scales on the central part of the pads, the posterior part of each pad without scales. Midgut tongue (mixed segment) short, drop-shaped, not spherical or elongate. The junction of P1 and P3 appears as a three-lobed enteric valve seating in dorsal view.

/genus/apicotermes/.note: The original has only the wings of the alate available for description ("Imago: Nur die Flügel sind vorhanden"), so no head or body characters could be recorded. Emerson (1959: 26), in a comparison, separately records that in this genus the setae at the anterior end of the soldier labrum are clustered, which adds one further character.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Of the alate the original makes known only the wings: in the forewing the area between the costa and the radial sector is unusually broad at the base, the radial vein very well developed and giving off 1–2 anterior branches, the media with 6–8 branches, the cubitus with about 14 closely set branches. Soldier head elongate, rectangular, about 1.5 times as long as wide, frons flat and slightly triangularly depressed, fontanelle small, distinct, surrounded by no hairs; mandibles short and very robust; antennae 14-segmented; fore coxa with an anteriorly directed tooth-like process. Worker head very broad, subcircular, pale, basal piece of the postclypeus very large and strongly arched, antennae 15-segmented, fore coxa with a large tooth-like process.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Forewing: the area between the costa and the radial sector is unusually broad at the base; within this area the radial vein is unusually well developed and even gives off 1–2 anterior branches running towards the costa; the base of the radial sector sometimes bears 1 short anterior vein and has a distal posterior branch; the media arises independently from the wing scale and has 6–8 branches; the cubitus has about 14 closely set branches, all reaching the posterior margin of the wing, of which the inner 8–9 are partly concealed; the area between the radial sector and the media is distinctly reticulate. Hindwing: the radial vein is shorter than in the forewing; the media has a thicker anterior accessory vein in the inner 1/3 and gives off 4–5 branches towards the wing apex or the posterior margin; the cubitus has about 16 posterior branches; the rest as in the forewing. Wing surface, especially at the base, dark, finely punctate; forewing 12.5 mm long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head elongate, rectangular, about 1.5 times as long as wide, narrowing only very slightly anteriorly, relatively flat; frons flat, slightly triangularly depressed; fontanelle small but distinct, surrounded by no hairs. Basal piece of the postclypeus not sharply delimited from the frons, the apical piece smaller. Labrum relatively broad, ligulate, with a short, rounded, white, hairy apex. Mandibles short and very robust, the apices curving inwards rather strongly; the left mandible with 3 tooth-like swellings at the apex and in the middle, the outermost largest, situated about the middle of the apical half of the mandible; base large, with a strong basal swelling; the right mandible with 2 weak tooth-like swellings in the middle, the molar angle short and small, with 1 small anteriorly directed rudimentary tooth on the base behind it. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about half of segment 2, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2. Pronotum pale yellow and sclerotised, narrower than the head, shallowly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe large, anterior and posterior margins slightly concave. Dark intestinal contents visible through the abdomen; cerci short, without stylus; fore coxa with an anteriorly directed tooth-like process.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head (very) broad, subcircular, pale; fontanelle plate about at the middle of the head; basal piece of the postclypeus very large, very strongly arched, as long as half its width; first mandibular tooth larger than the second but not large; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 short; anterior lobe of the pronotum very large, saddle-shaped; cerci small, without stylus.

/genus/apilitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 103). The alate section is marked 'unbekannt' in the original, so no 'Alate' section is given; a 'Nymph' section is provided on the basis of the nymph material alone. The worker section in the original consists of a single comparative sentence and is not expanded; this is stated in the text rather than reproducing the provisions for Crenetermes. The Chinese generic name is undetermined (marked '—' in the batch), so the Latin name is used provisionally.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, with the single species Apilitermes longiceps (Sjöst.) from Cameroon; a synonym in part of Eutermes (Sjöstedt) and in part of Termes (Desneux). The alate is unknown and is inferred only from the nymph. The soldier head is long rectangular, the frontal gland opening lying behind the inclined frontal surface on the horizontal part of the head, without surrounding hairs, with a fine groove running forward from the frontal gland opening; the labrum is quadrangular and grooved, with a non-concave anterior margin; the mandibles are long and straight, the apex and the middle continuous as one piece, with a small tooth-like, step-like swelling at the base; antennae of 15 segments. For the worker the original text records only 'the same as Crenetermes'.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long rectangular, fairly convex, anterior margin obliquely truncate. Frontal gland opening behind the posterior edge of the inclined frontal surface, on the horizontal part of the head, small, without surrounding hairs; a fine groove extends forward from it. Clypeus flat, the base small, the clypeal apical piece large. Labrum quadrangular, widening anteriorly, grooved, the anterior margin not concave. Mandibles long, robust and straight, slightly curved towards the apex; dentition as in Crenetermes, but the base of the right mandible smaller; apex and middle joined as one unit, with a separate small tooth-like, step-like swelling at its base, sharply delimited from the base; the apex and middle of the left mandible in particular are finely serrate. Antennae of 15 segments, segment 3 short. Pronotum small, strongly saddle-shaped. Without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original text gives only one comparative sentence: the same as the worker of Crenetermes (»Wie bei Crenetermes.«), without listing further characters, so the provisions for Crenetermes are not reproduced here.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Male nymph with degenerate styli (the original places this under the alate heading; because the adult is unknown, it is judged from the nymph).

/genus/araujotermes/.note: A legible full text of the original description by Fontes 1982 could not be obtained; this entry is based on Constantino's 1999 key to the Brazilian genera (p. 415) and on the intergeneric comparisons in Fontes 1987, and gives only the characters that can be quoted verbatim from the key and from the comparison sentences.
