The shape of the frontal tube (couplet 17 of the key) is not quoted and is therefore not included; alate and gut characters are not quoted from the original, so no such section is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The vertex bears numerous long setae of varying length, by which it is distinguished from Subulitermes, whose vertex has only 0–6 long setae in addition to numerous microsetae; in the worker the cutting edge between the 1+2 marginal tooth and the third marginal tooth of the left mandible is undulate, and the cleft between the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence is distinctly wider than in Atlantitermes and others.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Vertex with numerous long setae of varying length.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The cutting edge from the 1+2 marginal tooth to the third marginal tooth of the left mandible is undulate; the cleft between the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence is distinctly wider.

/genus/archotermopsis/.note: When the original was published the genus was named Termopsis (Heer); the passage on generic characters actually covers the then broad sense of Termopsis (including what is now Zootermopsis); on p. 297 the author states that he had already erected the subgenus Archotermopsis (Desneux 1904, Genera Insectorum XXV, p. 18), and the type species described in the paper is A. wroughtoni, so the generic characters and the species-level description can be assigned to this genus, but it should be noted that some of the features in the generic characters may belong to Termopsis in the broad sense. The generic characters give 27–28 antennal segments, whereas the species-level description gives 24 or 25; the two are inconsistent and must be checked before use.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original gives the generic characters under the name Termopsis: the alate lacks ocelli entirely and the frontal plate is not projecting, which separates it from groups possessing ocelli; the tarsi appear 4-segmented but are actually 5-segmented, segment 2 being only partly separated from segment 1, and a plantula is present between the tarsal claws; the cerci are long and the male styli are well developed; the wings are broad, less than 4 times as long as wide. The soldier is robust, with a large, subrectangular and flattened head, antennae of more than 20 segments, very strong mandibles with teeth on the inner margin, a pronotum narrower than the head and nearly flat, and long cerci and styli. The author subsequently erected the subgenus Archotermopsis on features such as the shape of the compound eye and the remnants of the wing bases, and noted that it differs from the remaining members of Termopsis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Antennae 27–28 segments (the species-level description of the type species, A. wroughtoni, gives 24 or 25 segments, which conflicts with the generic characters and must be checked against specimens); ocelli entirely absent; frontal plate not projecting; compound eyes large, the anterior margin deeply incised and almost kidney-shaped (species level); pronotum nearly flat and narrower than the head; wings less than 4 times as long as wide, the forewing with a subcosta, the radius well developed and giving off several branches that reach the anterior margin, the media near the middle of the wing, the membranous area densely reticulate; tibiae with lateral spines; tarsi appearing 4-segmented but actually 5-segmented, with a plantula between the claws; cerci long and male styli well developed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body robust; head large, subrectangular and flattened, the posterior margin distinctly concave (species level); eyes small or reduced, the species-level description recording them as small, oval and without ommatidia; antennae of more than 20 segments (species level 22–25 segments); mandibles very strong, the inner margin with irregular strong teeth, the apices curved inwards and sharp; pronotum narrower than the head and nearly flat; tarsi without a plantula (the original states that the plantula occurs only in the alate); cerci and styli both long.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original (the species-level description of A. wroughtoni) states that the worker resembles a larva: in the nymphal type the meso- and metathoracic epimera form triangular, leaf-like free processes, as in the soldier, whereas the alate lacks such processes; in some individuals the posterior margins of the meso- and metanota retain scars from broken wing buds, and the head is slightly larger than in the nymph; the original suggests that such individuals perform the worker function.

/genus/armitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 53–54). Armitermes in the original includes the three subgenera Armitermes s. str., Curvitermes and Rhynchotermes, the generic characters being common to all three; the 5 forms of mid-mandibular tooth arrangement in the soldier (numbered 1–5 in the original) have not been translated one by one.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate differs very little from that of Cornitermes, only in the head and body being on average slightly smaller, antennae 14–15 segments; the soldier head is pyriform, drawn anteriorly into a short or long conical frontal tube, the frontal gland opening lies at the apex of the tube, the frontal gland is very large, antennae 13–14 segments, the pronotum is more saddle-shaped than in Cornitermes and the anterior lobe is often shorter. Worker pale, head small. Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into three subgenera, Armitermes s. str., Curvitermes and Rhynchotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Differs very little from the alate of Cornitermes, the head on average smaller and the body also slightly smaller. Compound eyes variable in size; ocelli variable in size and position. Frontal gland opening distinct, small to very large; frons slightly depressed. Base of clypeus strongly arched, as long as or longer than half its width, brighter than the frons, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight. Mandibular first tooth larger than the second or equal to it, in which case the antennae have 14 segments; antennae 14–15 segments, in the former case the third segment much longer than the remaining ones, in the latter shorter than the second. Thorax and wings as in Cornitermes, but the first cubital branch of the wing distinctly stouter than the subsequent ones; wing membrane sometimes weakly punctate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pyriform, drawn anteriorly into a short or long conical frontal tube; frontal gland opening large, at the apex of the frontal tube, frontal gland very large. Transverse band and frons both very small, hidden beneath the 'nose'. Clypeus small, almost indistinguishable from the transverse band. Labrum short and relatively broad. Mandibles often very strongly curved; left base large to very large, often with a sharp molar angle, or with 2 sharp teeth before the molar angle; the middle tooth arrangement is variable, the original describing the number of teeth, their separation or fusion, and the shape of the molar angle in 5 forms. Antennae 13–14 segments. Pronotum usually more saddle-shaped than in Cornitermes, anterior lobe often shorter, otherwise as in that genus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pale. Head small, concolorous with the rest of the body, more or less pentagonal and rounded. Base of clypeus about as long as half its width, strongly arched, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin straight and sharply defined. Mandibular first tooth almost always longer than the second. Antennae 14–15 segments. Pronotum as in the soldier.

/genus/asagarotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 187–189. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate the meso- and metanotal constriction is narrow, and in the key the genus comes nearest to Anenteotermes and to group I of Astalotermes. The length of the apical tooth is comparable with that in Aganotermes and Amicotermes, but in the latter two the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is clear of the molar prominence, the ocelli are closer to the compound eye, and the postclypeus is more inflated. The enteric valve cushions of the worker bear no spines other than a single spiny sclerotised coronal band, a character unique to the genus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, W 0.85–0.88 mm. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Tw 4.40–4.49, with 3 apical spurs, the third about half as long as the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible very long, La/Li 0.96–0.99, Ra/Ri 1.11–1.16; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible has just left the molar prominence; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line joining the apical tooth and the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth being equal in length. Midgut and hindgut overlap by about 1.5 times the width of the midgut at the insertion of the Malpighian tubules, the anterior end of the hindgut lying within the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat almost without lobes, in effect a rim, sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch; in the undissected abdomen it lies laterally. Enteric valve cushions weak, not sclerotised, without spines, each with only a narrow, strongly sclerotised spiny coronal band around its middle.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized, W 1.03–1.10 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third almost as large as the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible rather long, La/Li 0.78–0.80, Ra/Ri 1.09–1.18; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible has just left the molar prominence; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are more or less in line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth being slightly longer than that of the second, almost equal. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.20–0.33, transverse sutures strong. Ocelli rather close to the compound eye; postclypeus rather inflated.

/genus/astalotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 51–54. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands regarded it as a large transitional genus between the primitive and the specialised groups; the generic characters vary very widely, and the alate overlaps several genera, so the limits of the genus rest in part on the gut. In the worker the overlap of midgut and hindgut is short, which distinguishes it from Adaiphrotermes, Anenteotermes and Aderitotermes; the enteric valve cushions are without spines and bear scales on the surface.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small to large, W 0.58–1.08 mm. Fore tibia slender to moderately inflated, Ti/Tw 3.86–5.96, with 3 apical spurs, the third usually distinct, sometimes reduced. Apical tooth of the mandible short to rather long, La/Li 0.43–0.86, Ra/Ri 0.57–1.08; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to distinctly clear of the molar prominence; the marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, or the first marginal tooth is set back, its anterior margin being longer than, equal to or shorter than that of the second. The junction of midgut and hindgut ranges from almost transverse to an overlap of about twice the width of the midgut, the proximal end of the hindgut reaching the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat variable: weakly lobed and sessile, to distinctly bilobed or trilobed and joined by a distinct neck; in the undissected abdomen it lies ventrally to dorsally. Enteric valve cushions without spines, bearing scales on the surface.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small to large, W 0.69–1.33 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third usually only slightly smaller than the other two, sometimes reduced. Apical tooth of the mandible short to rather long, La/Li 0.41–0.79, Ra/Ri 0.55–1.05; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to distinctly clear of the molar prominence; the marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, or the first marginal tooth is set back; the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth may be longer than, equal to or shorter than that of the second. Meso- and metanotal plates narrow to wide at the constriction, M/W 0.20–0.36; mesonotal and metanotal sutures present to absent.

/genus/astratotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 105–108. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Some species are close to Astalotermes, and the only generic character that clearly separates the two is the presence of small spines on the enteric valve cushions. The remaining characters (mandibles of alate and worker, fontanelle, length of the worker gut, development of the mixed segment) vary very widely, and Sands therefore suspected that both genera may be artificial assemblages.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized to very large, W 0.78–1.09 mm. Fore tibia slightly inflated or slender, Ti/Tw 4.54–7.08, with 3 apical spurs, the third distinct and never reduced. Apical tooth of the mandible short to long, La/Li 0.40–0.88, Ra/Ri 0.62–1.10; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to far clear of the molar prominence, or separated by a deep notch; the marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, or the first marginal tooth is set back. The junction of midgut and hindgut ranges from an oblique union to an overlap of about twice the width of the midgut; the proximal end of the hindgut lies to the right of the Malpighian knot and, in the longer ones, may pass half-way into it. Enteric valve seat weakly to strongly bilobed or trilobed, joined by a distinct to very long neck; in the undissected abdomen it lies ventrally to dorsally. Enteric valve cushions scaly, the posterior margin of most scales ending in 1 minute spine, none projecting through the valve opening.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized to very large, W 0.98–1.61 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third only slightly smaller than the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible short to moderately long, La/Li 0.46–0.80, Ra/Ri 0.58–1.07; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to far clear of the molar prominence, or separated by a distinct notch; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are almost in line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth being distinctly longer than that of the second, or nearly equal. Meso- and metanotal plates rather narrow to slightly wide at the constriction, M/W 0.24–0.35, transverse sutures always present, sometimes weak.

/genus/ateuchotermes/.note: Generic characters after Sands 1972 pp. 158–160. The original gives only the body size (head width W, mm), the number of apical spurs of the fore tibia, the mandibular tooth proportions, the constriction of the meso- and metanotal plates (M/W), the fontanelle and the head pilosity (where present), and the structure of the gut and enteric valve; the number of antennal segments, the shape of the pronotum and the wing venation are not recorded, so no such details are supplied here. Decimal points printed as “*” in the OCR and confusions of i with 1 have been normalised to Arabic numerals according to context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve is the most complex in the whole group and also the most easily recognised: the first cushion is elongated and hooks out through the valve opening into the valve seat, its spines touching the wall of the seat, and in one species a sclerotised cup is formed on the seat to receive it. The abdomen is distinctly dehiscent in all species, and Sands suggested that the easily ruptured gut may be an adjunct of the defensive mechanism of abdominal dehiscence.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized to very large, W 0.75–1.10 mm. Fore tibia scarcely inflated or slender, Ti/Tw 4.72–5.90, with 3 apical spurs, the third small or reduced, at most about 1/3 of the other two. Apical tooth of the mandible short to moderately long, La/Li 0.45–0.74, Ra/Ri 0.59–1.01; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is level with the edge of the molar prominence (in one species only) or distinctly clear of it; the marginal teeth of the right mandible are almost in line, or the first marginal tooth is distinctly set back, its anterior margin equalling or distinctly shorter than that of the second. Midgut and hindgut are obliquely joined or slightly longer, lying to the right of the Malpighian knot. Enteric valve seat rather large, weakly bilobed, sessile or joined by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch; in the undissected abdomen it lies dorsally to dorsal-most. Enteric valve cushions all sclerotised and projecting through the valve opening; the first is enlarged, elongated, swollen posteriorly and curved out through the valve opening into the enteric valve seat, its spines being numerous long spines arranged in one to several comb-like or rake-like rows around the margin; the spines of the second, third and fourth are longer and slender, sometimes hooked at the tip and forked, fewer in number than those of the first, and situated at the posterior end of each cushion; the rest of each cushion sometimes bears small spines, or no other spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Medium-sized to large, W 0.90–1.30 mm. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the third well developed, 1/3 of the other two or longer, reduced in one species only. Apical tooth of the mandible short or rather short, La/Li 0.30–0.66, Ra/Ri 0.66–1.01; the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is just to far clear of the molar prominence; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, or the first marginal tooth is slightly set back, its anterior margin equalling or longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotal plates rather narrow to distinctly wide at the constriction, M/W 0.26–0.34; the transverse suture is weak or absent on the mesonotum in most species (distinct in one only), and present or absent on the metanotum.

/genus/atlantitermes/.note: The original was published in Portuguese and this entry follows the terminology of the original (pêlos = hairs, cerdas = setae, naso = nasus, pós-clípeo = postclypeus). The genus-level definition gives only the three passages above (alate, soldier, worker), so no Nymph section is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the head capsule narrows behind the antennal insertions and is bulbous posteriorly, the nasus is conical, and the mandibles lack apical points; the mandibles of the worker and the alate are similar, but in the worker the cutting edge between M1+2 and M3 of the left mandible is distinctly undulate; in the alate the fontanelle is elongate and forked anteriorly, the eyes are large, the distance between each ocellus and its eye is less than the width of the ocellus, and the postclypeus is shorter than half its width.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head sparsely covered with minute hairs, with a few long setae in addition; nasus with numerous short hairs; the dorsal surface of the head narrows behind the antennal insertions and is bulbous posteriorly; nasus conical in both dorsal and lateral view; mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles similar to those of the alate, but the cutting edge between M1+2 and M3 of the left mandible is distinctly undulate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum hairy, with a few long setae in addition; fontanelle elongate, forked anteriorly; eyes large; the distance between each ocellus and its eye is less than the width of the ocellus; postclypeus shorter than half its width.

/genus/australitermes/.note: The genus-level description gives no worker character that can be cited independently, so no Worker section is provided; the width of the alate pronotum, the reduction of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible and the tibial spur formula 2:2:2 were not within the quotation limits of this task and are not written into the main text.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate left mandible index is 1.54, the highest in the Australian Subulitermes lineage (Macrosubulitermes 1.07); the fontanelle is elongate and narrowly oval and not forked at the apex; the length of the postclypeus is greater than half its width. The soldier is monomorphic, the head has a small constriction, and the lateral outline of the pronotum forms an angle close to a right angle between the anterior lobe and the base.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic; head with a small constriction, visible in both dorsal and lateral view; lateral outline of the pronotum forming an angle close to a right angle between the anterior lobe and the base.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Eyes and ocelli large, the distance between the ocellus and the eye suture less than its width, its length 0.15 mm, greater than the 0.12 mm diameter of the antennal fossa; fontanelle elongate and narrowly oval, without a distinct fork at the apex; postclypeus much longer than half its width (length 0.32 mm, width 0.50 mm); antennae 15 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 4, segment 4 longer than segment 2; left mandible index 1.54 (Macrosubulitermes 1.07), the highest in the Australian Subulitermes lineage.

/genus/bandeiratermes/.note: The source records Imago as Unknown; the worker mandibles (apical tooth larger than the marginal teeth, molar region without ridges) and the remaining gut characters are described in the source but not quoted, as quotations are limited to 3 per genus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve (P2) consists of three subequal conical ridges covered with curved spines; P3 is connected to P4 by an isthmus that is inserted subapically.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head elongate, rectangular to subrectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly, lateral and posterior margins slightly convex, posterior corners broadly rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head circular; postclypeus moderately to more strongly inflated; antennae 14 segments.

/genus/basidentitermes/.note: Holmgren (1912) treated it as a subgenus of Mirotermes; the original texts of Silvestri 1914 and Sjöstedt 1924 were not read here, so only key-level characters are given, without measurements, pilosity or numbers of antennal segments.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The anterior part of the soldier head does not cover the bases of the mandibles; Emerson's (1928) key to the Ethiopian soldier termites separates it on this character from Fastigitermes, whose anterior head covers the mandible bases. Few localities are known for this subgenus, so its distribution (Map 20) is difficult to characterise.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles slightly longer than the head capsule, sabre-like; the anterior margin of the labrum forms a convex arc between the two lateral points; the fontanelle opening is circular (Holmgren 1912 key, item B, Taf. IV fig. 10–11).

/genus/baucaliotermes/.note: Type species Subulitermes hainesi Fuller; the genus was erected by Sands to accommodate this monotypic species and is known only from the arid Cape Province of South Africa; it was originally described in Subulitermes and was later placed in Trinervitermes. The description of the alate is based on worn king and queen morphotype specimens. In the source the sex symbols for the fontanelle appear in the scanned OCR as “(^” and “?”, and this entry treats them only as “one form / the other form”, without deciding which is male or female. Sands expected the intergeneric differences to become clearer once fresh alates had been collected; according to his account, the frontal gland at the anterior margin of sternite 5 appears very small in females and is absent in males, whereas in Trinervitermes the gland is clearly visible even when not large.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the sockets of the minute setae on the head capsule (including the nasus) are clearly visible and scattered as pale spots, which is the main distinction from Trinervitermes — the latter has no visible setal sockets in the soldier and its soldiers are dimorphic; in the alate the pilosity is coarser and the sockets more conspicuous, and the distribution of the pale areas of the head likewise disagrees with Trinervitermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Apical tooth of the left mandible subequal in length to the first marginal tooth, the distance between them (specimen worn) slightly less than one-third of the distance between the first and third marginal teeth (left mandible index −0.30); second marginal tooth absent; cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth complete and straight. Postclypeus slightly less than half as long as wide. Fontanelle differing in shape between the sexes: in one form small, pale and irregularly Y-shaped, in the other trapezoidal with the lateral arms arising from the anterior angles and slightly swollen at their ends; in both sexes a smooth shallow depression lies behind the fontanelle, of the same colour as the rest of the head capsule. Pilosity of the head capsule uneven, setal sockets of unequal size, the large ones numerous and conspicuous.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Nasus very slender, cylindrical, at most slightly tapering; reduced mandibles without an apical process; head capsule not constricted; antennae 12–14 segments, usually 14. Sockets of the minute setae clearly visible as pale spots over the whole head capsule, including the nasus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is difficult to distinguish from Bifiditermes; the soldier has a short, truncate head that is strongly frontal-shield-like, and the anterior margin of the pronotum is serrate; it differs from Epicalotermes in the shorter anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Yellowish brown; eyes large, diameter 0.41–0.46 mm, ocelli touching the compound eyes; antennae 12–15-segmented; anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible distinctly longer than the posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth, but not more than 1.5 times as long; molar plate of the right mandible distinctly shorter than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum narrower than the head; wings transparent, with colourless small papillae; media and cubitus with a common stalk beyond the wing suture; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark, short and truncate, anterior part steeply inclined; lateral frontal regions raised into distinct round lobes with a depression between them; the lateral frontal angles near the clypeus project forwards as a horizontal ridge connected with the dorsal margin of the antennal socket; another distinct angular projection anteroventral to the antennal socket; eyes colourless; antennae 11–15-segmented, the third segment subequal to the second or fourth; mandibles short, with a distinct basal tubercle; pronotum narrower than the head or as wide as the head, anterior margin raised, serrate and deeply concave.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Epicalotermes and Bicornitermes; the alate has a shorter anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible than Epicalotermes; the soldier has a thicker head and less strongly curved mandibles than Epicalotermes; the soldier of Bicornitermes has a shorter, more truncate head and short mandibles, and the anterior margin of the pronotum is serrate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Light brown to dark brown; eye diameter 0.37–0.64 mm, ocelli usually touching the compound eyes; antennae 15–20-segmented; anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible distinctly longer than the posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth (not more than 1.5 times as long); molar plate of the right mandible distinctly smaller than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum as wide as the head or slightly wider; wings transparent, slightly iridescent, usually covered with colourless papillae, pigmented in a few species; media and cubitus with a common stalk beyond the wing suture; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and thick, sides straight and parallel; frontal region rugose, concave in the middle, inclined downwards at about 45°; dorsolateral frontal angles slightly raised in some species; eyes large, pigmented or colourless; antennae 10–18-segmented, the third segment longest and club-shaped; mandibles long, the outer margin almost straight, curved near the apex, with a basal tubercle, dentition variable; pronotum transversely arched, anterior margin deeply or broadly concave, sides rounded; femora not inflated.

/genus/biratermes/.note: The source records Imago as Unknown, so no alate section is given; the external morphology of the soldier and worker follows Constantino (1992), and what this revision adds is the mandibular and fore coxal characters shared by the three new genera, together with the gut characters.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the worker of this genus the first-order gizzard cushion (pulvillus I) bears conspicuous spines; among the Syntermitinae, only the workers of Biratermes, Mapinguaritermes and Ibitermes have such conspicuous cushion spines, all other genera lacking them.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: According to the source, the external morphology of the soldier follows the description of Constantino (1992); the source's shared account of the three new genera erected in this revision is: mandibles blade-like and stout, the surface of the fore coxa smooth (by contrast, Embiratermes s.s. has piercing mandibles with a pointed tip and a process on the ventral margin of the fore coxa).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The gizzard has 24 visible folds, of which 6 are first-order, 6 second-order and 12 third-order; the ratio of the width of the columnar band to that of the cushion band is about 1; the first-order (large) cushions bear conspicuous spines.

/genus/bulbitermes/.note: The original has no separate genus-level Diagnosis paragraph; the generic characters are taken from the delimiting sentence for the genus in the Discussion (soldier monomorphic; head capsule with a constriction behind the antennal sockets) and from characters shared by the descriptions of the four species' soldiers and workers; values such as antennal segment numbers and mandibular tooth positions are only the observed ranges for these four species and are not extrapolated to the whole genus; among them, the worker antenna of B. constrictus is given as 14-segmented in the key (Key 1) and as 15-segmented in the species description — the two places in the original disagree, and the text follows the species description. The alates of all four species are recorded in the original as Imago: Unknown, hence no Alate section is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Nasute soldiers, soldiers monomorphic, head capsule with a constriction behind the antennal sockets — this is precisely the character on which Emerson (in Snyder 1949) separated the genus from Nasutitermes, and the condition on which the present paper retains it. Compared with Nasutitermes: in the latter the soldier head capsule has no constriction behind the antennal sockets, the head capsule varies greatly in size and shape, the rostrum is conical to cylindrical, and the antennae are 11–14-segmented. The authors also note that to date the genus has no single absolute diagnostic character, and that in many specimens from the Sunda region the constriction is almost invisible; the genus boundary still rests on a combination of characters (monomorphic soldiers + post-antennal-socket constriction) together with molecular barcodes, rather than on a single diagnostic feature.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head nasute: head capsule subcircular or pyriform in dorsal view, with a constriction of varying strength behind the antennal sockets; posterior margin broadly convex, weakly concave or almost straight in the middle; dorsal outline including the nasus almost straight, the tip of the nasus upturned or downturned. The nasus is usually darker than the anterior part of the head capsule, its tip with 4 setae; setae on the head surface sparse; pronotum and abdominal tergites hairy (microtrichia or short hairs). Mandibular apical process weakly to moderately developed. Antennae 12–14-segmented: the four species recorded have 12, 13 and 14 segments respectively, and mostly 12 with a few 13; the relative length and width of the segments is the main basis for separating species in this paper. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin weakly concave or almost straight in the middle, posterior margin broadly convex or deeply concave in the middle; tibiae pale yellow to yellowish white.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Workers of the four species recorded here: antennae 13–15-segmented (13, 14, 15 and 14 segments respectively in the four species), segment 2 mostly distinctly longer than segments 3 and 4, segment 4 often the shortest. Left mandible apical tooth nearly as long as the 1st marginal tooth or the apical tooth shorter, the 3rd marginal tooth moderately projecting beyond the cutting edge, the 4th marginal tooth almost completely concealed behind the molar process; right mandible 2nd marginal tooth with a nearly straight or weakly concave posterior margin, the inner layer of the molar plate poorly developed, the notch near the proximal end of the molar plate indistinct or only faintly marked.

/genus/caetetermes/.note: The original states 'Imago. Unknown', so no Alate section is provided; the worker characters come from the original's account of the major worker. Constantino's 1999 key gives further characters such as the frontal tube and the number of antennal segments, which are not quoted here and are therefore not written into the main text.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier head is strongly constricted behind the antennae and bulbous posteriorly, the nasus is long and cylindrical and not particularly thickened at its base; the postclypeus is inclined and clearly visible in dorsal view; the mandibles lack apical points and bear a distinct but not sharply delimited thin horny patch at the apex. The worker left mandible index is 0.49, the apical tooth shorter than M1+2, the cutting edge of M1+2 undulate and separated from M3 by a sharp notch; the legs are long but shorter than in the soldier, with a weak swelling on the outer side of the fore coxa (a distinct swelling in the soldier).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule strongly constricted behind the antennae, bulbous posteriorly; nasus long, cylindrical, not particularly thickened at its base; postclypeus inclined, clearly visible in dorsal view; mandibles without apical points, with a distinct but not sharply delimited thin horny patch at the apex.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: (Major worker) postclypeus width/length 3.66–4.89; left mandible index 0.49, apical tooth shorter than M1+2; cutting edge of M1+2 undulate, separated from M3 by a sharp notch; M3 well developed, its posterior margin convex; legs long but shorter than in the soldier, with a weak swelling on the outer side of the fore coxa.

/genus/cahuallitermes/.note: Soldier after the comparative genus characters of Rocha & Cancello (2022) and the genus key of Rocha et al. (2012); of the worker only the left mandible index is known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandibles laminar, with a notch before the first marginal tooth; postmentum finely wrinkled, lateral margins convex; labrum with a well-developed hyaline tip; head rounded. Body relatively large (in the comparison with Acangaobitermes). Distributed in Mexico, Belize and Honduras.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rounded; labrum with a well-developed hyaline tip; lateral margins of the postmentum convex, the surface finely wrinkled. Mandibles laminar, cutting edge relatively straight, marginal teeth well developed, a notch before the first marginal tooth.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.5.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate resembles Glyptotermes; the soldier is distinguished from other genera by a stout spur on the outer side of the apex of the fore tibia, much larger than the other two apical spurs.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; eyes small, diameter 0.29–0.34 mm, ocelli touching the compound eyes in most species; antennae 13–14-segmented; posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible equal in length to the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth, the notch between them lost in most species to form a concave cutting margin; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly longer than the molar plate; pronotum slightly narrower than the head; venation as in Glyptotermes; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark, thick, semicylindrical, distinctly bilobed with a V- or U-shaped depression between the lobes; anterior face of the frons steep, the slope steeper or shallower than vertical, in some species the dorsal margin projecting forwards or concave between the upper margin and the clypeus; in some species the ventrolateral part of the mentum forms an angular projection between the mandibular base and below the antennal socket; eyes distinct or indistinct, colourless; antennae 10–12-segmented, the third segment short and unspecialised; mandibles usually short and broad, with or without a basal tubercle; pronotum narrower than, equal to or wider than the head, anterior margin shallowly angular or distinctly concave; outer side of the proximal end of the fore tibia with a stout spur, much larger than the other two apical spurs.

/genus/capritermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 114–116). In 1912 the genus contained two subgenera (Neocapritermes, Capritermes s. str.), and what is described here are the combined characters at generic level; the lists of subgenera and species are on pp. 115–116 (Old World species: chiasognathus, socialis, capricornis, ceylonicus, foraminifer, incola, medius, minor, nemorosus, etc.). zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name (marked '—' in the batch).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into two clearly delimited subgenera: Neocapritermes (all the American species, plus the African C. alienus v. Rosen) and Capritermes s. str. (Old World species only). The key differences between the two are: in the alate, the size of the first and second teeth, the number of antennal segments, the shape of the posterior margins of meso- and metanotum, and the presence or absence of a radius in the forewing; in the soldier, only the presence or absence of the frontal gland opening — Neocapritermes lacks it, Capritermes s. str. has it; in the worker, whether the anterior margin of the fore coxa is slightly disc-like expanded and the size of the first tooth. Characters common to the genus are: alate antennae 15–17 segments, third segment mostly short, wing membrane dark with spine-like points, media close to the cubitus; soldier head elongate rectangular, flattened and arched, mandibles of Capritermes type, asymmetrically curved, antennae 13–16 segments; worker head more or less pentagonal and rounded, antennae 13–15 segments.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, narrowing anteriorly. Compound eyes relatively small, mostly strongly projecting. Ocelli variable in position, facing laterally. Frontal gland opening depressed. Base of clypeus flatly convex, shorter than half its width. Mandibles in two conditions: either with a large apical tooth (in which case the posterior part of meso- and metanotum is pointed, antennae (14–)15 segments); or with the first two teeth about equal in length (in which case the posterior part of meso- and metanotum is broad, the mesonotum hardly incised, the metanotum broadly incised, antennae 17 segments and the forewing with a radius). Antennae 15–17 segments, third segment mostly short. Wing membrane dark, with small points (spines). Media close to the cubitus. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head slender rectangular, rarely narrowing anteriorly, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening mostly present, exposed on the front of the head; absent in all the American species and in the African C. alienus. Base of clypeus very narrow. Labrum slender: either with the lateral angles projecting and the middle rounded or incised, or trilobed with the lobes very short and rounded. Mandibles of Capritermes type, asymmetrically curved. Antennae 13–16 segments. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head more or less pentagonal and rounded. Base of clypeus strongly arched, slightly shorter than half its width. Shape of the mandibular first tooth as in the alate. Antennae 13–15 segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped.

/genus/caputitermes/.note: There is no soldier section (Neotropical Apicotermitinae lack soldiers); the imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set. The genus-level description is based mainly on the worker body wall and digestive tract. The page numbers of the Acta Amazonica article are taken from the SciELO page 53(3); the genus-level treatment lies around pages 202–204 (not checked page by page).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The primary generic character is worker dimorphism (major worker and minor worker); the junction between the midgut and the first proctodeal segment (P1) is straight, without a mixed segment; the molar plate and molar prominence region bear hairs and scale-like sculpturing; the gizzard is not developed; the inner wall of P1 is densely covered with short, stout spines directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped projection before joining P2. All Neotropical Apicotermitinae lack soldiers.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the ratio of major to minor about 1:2, both forms common. Both forms have a visible fontanelle, the postclypeus slightly inflated, the head covered with fine short setae; the mandibles bear hairs and scale-like sculpturing in the molar plate and molar prominence region, with a shallow concavity on the anterior side of the mandibles; the apical tooth of the left mandible is as large as the first and second marginal teeth together, the apical tooth of the right mandible larger than the first and second marginal teeth together. The major worker has a square head capsule with about 34 setae, distributed mainly on the anterior sides and the posterior region, the head with lateral nodes; the minor worker has a rounded head capsule with about 14 setae, evenly distributed on the sides of the head. The digestive tract of both worker forms is spherical, the structures similar in size and position. The gizzard has no cuticular armature, with 6 primary pulvilli, the surface of the pulvilli scale-like, with minute spines posteriorly; the muscular layer of the enteric valve is thin, with 6 symmetrical cushions; the Malpighian tubules have 4 separate insertion points, without a nodule; the short stout spines of the inner wall of P1 are densest near the midgut and near P2, their tips directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped projection before joining P2. Measurements: species-level (LH, WH, LT, WP, see the species-level description).

/genus/cavitermes/.note: Emerson (1925) described it as a subgenus of Mirotermes; later revisions such as Mathews 1977 were not read here, so only the original description and the characters verifiable in Constantino's (1999) key are given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the frons is ridged along its length and concave anteriorly (whence the genus name); the head shape differs greatly from that of the other subgenera of Mirotermes, but the shape and mode of action of the mandibles remain similar to those of Mirotermes s. str. Constantino's (1999) soldier key diagnoses it by the combination of a broad frontal projection, a concave anterior face, mandibles distinctly longer than the head capsule, and a tibial spur formula of 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head shape very different from that of the other subgenera of Mirotermes; frons ridged and concave anteriorly; mandibles distinctly longer than the head capsule, similar in shape and function to those of Mirotermes s. str.; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

/genus/cephalotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 84–85). Only one species was known, Cephalotermes rectangularis (Sjöst.) (Cameroon, Congo); the alate section is explicitly marked 'Imago (Königin)', i.e. described from the queen; the note on the Malpighian tubules and hindgut glandular plates in the worker section concerns internal anatomy and has been retained faithfully at the end of the worker section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus, with only Cephalotermes rectangularis (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo. The soldier head is rectangular and flattened-cylindrical, eyeless, with antennae of 12 segments; the worker mandibles are of the modified Termes type (Hamitermes type), with antennae of 13 segments; the alate has antennae of 14 segments, segment 1 very large and segment 3 small, wings with spines, and the female without exudate hairs. Holmgren's original description is based on the queen (a dealate individual) and points out that, judging from the size of its head and thorax, the alate itself should be fairly small.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Described from the queen (Königin) in the original. Head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Frons flatly convex, slightly depressed in front of the frontal gland opening. Compound eyes medium-sized, fairly flat; ocelli medium-sized, slightly lateral, separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their larger diameter. Frontal gland opening small and distinct, on the middle of the head. Clypeal base moderately convex, almost as long as half its width, posterior margin fairly strongly convex and anterior margin straight and sharply delimited, brighter than the frons. Labrum wider than long. Mandibular basal segments small; mandibles of the Termes type, the basal tooth of the left mandible weakly developed. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 1 very large, segment 3 small. Pronotum only slightly narrower than the head, head width 0.79 mm, pronotum width 0.7 mm. Posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum with an emargination, the posterior projections blunt and rounded. Forewing scale distinctly longer than the hindwing scale, the wing surface with small spines. Female without exudate hairs; the sides of the queen's abdomen verrucose, seemingly wrinkled, weakly pigmented. Because the abdomen is extremely developed, the queen examined is unusually large.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, flattened-cylindrical. Frons slightly inclined. Eyeless, cranial suture invisible. Frontal gland opening barely discernible, frontal gland very indistinct and small. Clypeus lens-shaped; labrum quadrangular with rounded anterior corners. Mandibles short and robust, the base large; 2 small teeth on each side in the middle; the left mandible with a small tooth at the base, the base of the right mandible mainly rounded. Antennae slender, of 12 segments, segment 3 shorter and narrower than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4. Pronotum rather small, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe rather short. Cerci small, without styli. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small in size. Head oval, fairly thick, flatly convex; frontal gland opening fairly far back. The length of the clypeal base greater than half its width, convex, the posterior margin very strongly arched and sharply delimited, the anterior margin straight. Labrum small, strongly inclined, wider in the middle than at the base. Mandibles of the modified Termes type (Hamitermes type). Antennae of 13 segments, segment 3 far shorter and narrower than segment 2 and distinctly shorter than segment 4. Pronotum short, far narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe almost as long as the posterior part. Cerci short, without styli. Note in the original: Malpighian tubules without a collecting vesicle, hindgut segments I–II without glandular plates.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is closest to Paraneotermes and Comatermes; it differs from Comatermes in lacking long, wavy setae on the head and pronotum; Paraneotermes has a distinct angle in the posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible and lacks an arolium; the soldiers of both have short, strong mandibles, a very weak or absent dorsal frontal projection, and a pronotal anterior margin that is not deeply concave.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; eyes small, about 0.25 mm in diameter, ocelli touching the compound eyes; antennae 13–14-segmented; posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible equal in length to the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth; molar plate of the right mandible subequal to the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum wider than the head, anterior margin concave; radial vein of the forewing usually branched, radial sector with 7–8 branches, the first branch about one-sixth of the wing length from the wing suture; media weakly sclerotised, closer to the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head somewhat frontal-shield-like, narrow, sides parallel; antennal carinae large and distinctly projecting; frons concave, steeply sloping to the clypeus; anterior dorsum with two large swellings or lobes, the space between them evenly arcuate; eyes colourless; antennae 11–14-segmented, the third segment unspecialised and subequal to the second; mandibles long and slender; pronotum as wide as the head, transversely arched, anterior margin raised with a deep angular concavity and a median notch; legs short and stout.

/genus/ceylonitermellus/.note: The alate was not studied by Emerson (the original mentions only Bugnion's 1914 description), so that section is not provided; the only citable soldier character is 'mandibles without apical points', so that section is very short.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier mandibles lack apical points; in the worker (nymph) the 1+2 marginal tooth of the left mandible is exceptionally long, the left mandible index is 0.62, and the third marginal tooth is distinctly smaller than in Leucopitermes; the outline of the molar plate of the right mandible is concave; the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of both mandibles is wider than in any related genus of the Oriental region.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original describes a worker–nymph: the 1+2 marginal tooth of the left mandible is exceptionally long; the left mandible index is 0.62; the third marginal tooth is distinctly smaller than in Leucopitermes; the outline of the molar plate of the right mandible is concave; the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of both mandibles is wider than in any related genus of the Oriental region.

/genus/ceylonitermes/.note: The original (Holmgren 1913, the Ceylonitermes subgenus section) writes Imago unbekannt, so no alate section is given. The text is a Fraktur OCR with many corrupt readings (e.g. Kopf ziemlieh langgestreekt eiförmig, eingesehnürt); anything that cannot be read with certainty is not quoted. The original description also contains body colour and measurements, which fall outside the quotation limit of this entry.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier nasus 2/3 of head length, very narrow, cylindrical and straight; antennae long, 12 segments. Worker clypeus large and inflated, its length half its width; the first two mandibular teeth equal in size; antennae 15 segments.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus 2/3 of head length, very narrow, cylindrical, straight; antennae long, 12 segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Clypeus large, inflated, its length half its width; the first two mandibular teeth equal in size; antennae 15 segments.

/genus/chasitermes/.note: The genus is named after the collector James A. Chase. The source states Imago unknown; there is no soldier, so only the Diagnostic characters and Worker sections are given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The following combination of three characters distinguishes the genus from all other Apicotermitinae genera: the EVA cushions are unsclerotised and rectangular, the EVS has a tubular extension, and the mesenteric tongue projects as a sphere. Only the worker is known at present; the alate is unknown.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule and antennae pale yellow. The EVA cuticle is unsclerotised and forms 6 rectangular cushions, each with about 100 scales; the EVS has a tubular extension.

/genus/coarctotermes/.note: Emerson (1928) treated the genus as a subgenus of Nasutitermes (established by Holmgren, the spelling to be cited as Coarctotermes); the account here is compiled solely from the soldier of his Nasutitermes (Coarctotermes) suffuscus (new species); the alate and the worker were not described. Its distribution spans the Ethiopian and Madagascan regions and, according to the records of the time, it is absent from the Congo Basin rainforest. For the modern genus see Krishna et al. (2013).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head red-yellow-brown, markedly constricted at mid-length, the nasus darker; mandibles with extremely small points, almost indiscernible; nasus and vertex smooth.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head red-yellow-brown, the nasus darker; head markedly constricted at mid-length; vertex with two hairs; antennae 13-segmented (segment 3 longer than segment 2 or segment 4 but less than twice segment 2, unlike N. dorix); mandibles with extremely small points, almost indiscernible; thorax nearly concolorous with the head; legs relatively short for the body. Measurements (mm): head length 1.39–1.47, head width 0.78, pronotum 0.18×0.44, hind tibia 1.10. Much smaller than N. dorix; N. coarctatus has a smaller posterior part of the head behind the constriction and a thicker nasus; N. clepsydra has a black head; N. tenebricus has a longer head and unpointed mandibles.

/genus/coatitermes/.note: The original description (Fontes 1982) could not be obtained in readable full text; soldier characters follow the genus-level comparison of Scheffrahn 2024 and the key of Constantino 1999, worker characters follow Fontes 1987. Constantino 1999's key also contains characters of the frontal tube and head-capsule constriction, which are not cited here and so are not included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier nasus very broadly conical in dorsal view, its basal width more than 1/3 of the maximum head width; vertex with numerous long setae of varying length. The nearest Neotropical group with a broad conical nasus is the larger-bodied Convexitermes and Paraconvexitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus very broadly conical in dorsal view, basal width more than 1/3 of the maximum head width; vertex with numerous long setae of varying length.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Narrow-gap left mandible: the cutting edge from the 1+2 marginal teeth to the 3rd marginal tooth weakly undulate or almost not undulate.

/genus/coendutermes/.note: The original writes Alate. Unknown, so no alate section is given; soldier characters such as the parallel, unconstricted sides of the head capsule and the legs and tibial spurs, as well as the worker left mandible index 0.47 and the details of the molar region, fall outside the quotation limit of this entry and are not written into the text.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head dorsum and sides with many scattered hollow glandular setae, stout, brown, truncate at the tip; apart from the nasus tip the head bears no ordinary setae; nasus conical, slightly curved upwards, pointed at the tip; antennae very long, extending far beyond the nasus tip.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head capsule dorsum and sides with many scattered hollow glandular setae, stout, erect, brown, truncate at the tip; apart from the nasus tip, the head bears no ordinary setae; nasus conical, slightly curved upwards, pointed at the tip; postclypeus weakly inclined, visible in dorsal view; each mandible with a separate process at the tip, but without a developed apical point; antennae very long, extending far beyond the nasus tip.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apparently monotypic; abdominal sclerites pale or colourless, transparent, the gut contents visible through them; no glandular setae; head with a few long setae and many medium-length setae; postclypeus moderately inflated, width/length 2.90–3.25.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus; the alate venation resembles Paraneotermes and Ceratokalotermes, but the head and pronotum bear very long, fine, slightly wavy setae; the soldier differs from Ceratokalotermes in that the latter has two distinct lobes on the anterior dorsum of the head and a raised, deeply concave pronotal anterior margin, and from Paraneotermes in the latter's short, strong mandibles.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; head and pronotum with very long, fine, slightly wavy setae; eyes small, diameter 0.29–0.31 mm, ocelli touching the compound eyes; antennae 14-segmented; posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible equal in length to the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth; pronotum wider than the head; radial sector with 9–10 branches; media less sclerotised than the radial sector, with many cross-veins between it and the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head usually long, sometimes with long-headed and short-headed forms in the same species; head dorsoventrally flattened; frons concave in the middle, anterior part concave, anterior dorsum with two weak swellings; eyes colourless; antennae 13–14-segmented, the third segment unspecialised and equal to the second; mandibles strong, relatively short for the head length; pronotum as wide as the head, anterior margin shallowly and broadly concave; femora inflated.

/genus/compositermes/.note: The generic name derives from Latin compositus (put together, composed of several parts), referring to the ring of more than 15 comb-like spatulae at the S/P3 junction. The source states Imago unknown (only a short-winged nymph is figured), so no alate section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the worker the enteric valve cushions are markedly enlarged, the EVS is a long tube, and the S/P3 junction bears a ring of sclerotised comb-like spatulae (about 15–20); this combination is found in no other termite worker. The alate is unknown.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; fore tibia moderately inflated (length/width ratio 3.98). The enteric valve (P2) consists of 6 slightly irregular oval cushions; at the S/P3 junction there are about 15–20 small comb-like spatulae, visible from outside under the microscope after the abdominal wall has been removed.

/genus/constrictotermes/.note: A subgenus established by Holmgren 1912 under Eutermes and listed as the 14th subgenus in the catalogue, containing cavifrons Holmgren (Suriname), cyphergaster Silvestri and latinotus Holmgren (Ecuador). The 1912 original gives only key entries and the subgeneric catalogue, with no worker characters, so no Worker section is given. The “position in the key” in the Alate section refers to the key branch and is not a complete description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier head capsule is markedly dumbbell-shaped, constricted behind the antennal fossae, the dorsal cephalic outline in front of the depression being only slightly longer than behind it, the nasus relatively short and conical, antennae 14–15-segmented. This combination suffices to separate it from Coarctotermes (nasus long and thick, conical, antennae 12–13(–14)-segmented, the anterior part of the head much longer than the posterior), Tenuirostritermes (nasus slender, cylindrical, antennae 11–13-segmented) and Grallatotermes (nasus short and very broadly conical, the head not dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennae). Alates are distinguished by the broadly oval head, markedly narrowing anteriorly, with a flattened and rounded occiput, together with rather small and strongly protruding compound eyes and a clypeus concolorous with the frons or only slightly paler, from Velocitermes and Tenuirostritermes (head oval, occiput well developed).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, markedly narrowed anteriorly, the occiput flattened and rounded and gently sloping; compound eyes situated on the sides of the head, relatively small and strongly protruding; clypeus shorter than or about equal to half its width, concolorous with the frons or only slightly paler; antennal segments slightly elongate; pronotum relatively large. In the original key, this genus is placed together with Rotunditermes (eyes very large) and Diversitermes (eyes medium-sized) in a branch characterised by “the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd, and the clypeus equal to or slightly shorter than half its width”.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Of the Constrictus group, with a single soldier type. Head capsule dumbbell-shaped, constricted behind the antennal fossae; the dorsal cephalic outline in front of the depression only slightly longer than behind it, the depression itself strong and distinct; nasus relatively short, conical; antennae 14–15-segmented.

/genus/convexitermes/.note: A subgenus established by Holmgren 1912 and listed as the 7th subgenus in the catalogue, containing convexifrons Holmgren (Peru) and nigricornis Holmgren (Peru). The original has no worker characters; the worker clypeal character mentioned in the last sentence of the Soldier section is only a key aid and does not suffice for a Worker section. The Alate and Soldier sections lie in different main key branches and only together form the diagnostic combination of the genus; they must not be taken as a complete description of a single caste.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the key, the alates and soldiers of this genus run in different main branches. In the alate, the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible is distinctly larger than the 2nd, the head is broadly oval and usually narrows anteriorly, and the fontanelle lies far back on the head; the soldiers are small species with no apical part on the mandibles, a short, thick, conical nasus, 11-segmented antennae and a convex frontal profile. On this basis the soldier is distinguished from Occasitermes (nasus long and thick, conical, antennae 13-segmented, frontal profile straight) and Eutermellus (head slightly constricted behind the antennae).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The 1st marginal tooth of the mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd; head broadly oval, usually narrowing anteriorly; fontanelle far back on the head; brain well developed within the head (given as Gehirn stark entwickelt in the original); clypeus about as long as half its width, or shorter but strongly convex, transversely oval and pale yellow.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small species. Mandibles without an apical part (Spitzenteil); nasus short, thick, conical; antennae 11-segmented; frontal profile (Stirnprofil) convex. The key additionally uses the worker clypeus, whose base is about as long as half its width, as an auxiliary character of the branch containing this genus.

/genus/cornicapritermes/.note: The shallowly forked labral apex, the lateral angles of about 60° and the angle of about 150° between them (Emerson 1950) are species-level details and are omitted here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with Paracapritermes, Mirocapritermes and Quasitermes, the soldier mandibles are more strongly asymmetrical and the second marginal tooth of the worker is less distinct; Emerson (1950) regarded Paracapritermes as the most generalised of the four, Mirocapritermes next, Quasitermes next, and Cornicapritermes as the most specialised.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head thick and long, its sides slightly curved; the conical frontal projection points forward, extending far beyond the mandible bases, its apex slightly upturned, with a small tubercle below and before the apex that appears to be the fontanelle opening.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical tooth is distinctly larger than the first marginal tooth; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is reduced or lost; there is a small notch between the third marginal tooth and the fused first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible.

/genus/cornitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 49–50). Cornitermes in the original includes the two subgenera Labiotermes and Cornitermes s. str., the generic characters being common to both; the key to species and subgenera is not included in the description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate relatively large, wings hyaline; antennae 15–17 segments; base of clypeus strongly arched, as long as half its width; mandibular first tooth sometimes larger than the second, third tooth of the left mandible stepped. Soldier head more or less rectangular, frontal gland opening large, at the apex of a long or short frontal tube, antennae 13–15 segments, third segment usually shorter than the second; all tibiae with only 2 apical spurs, styli absent. Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into two subgenera, Labiotermes and Cornitermes s. str.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Relatively large, wings hyaline. Head broadly oval, narrowing anteriorly; compound eyes projecting; ocelli lateral, medium-sized to very large, close to the compound eyes or fairly far from them. Frontal gland opening large and distinct. Base of clypeus as long as half its width, strongly arched, posterior margin strongly convex, anterior margin mostly straight, labrum broader than long. Mandibular first tooth sometimes larger than the second, third tooth of the left mandible stepped, molar region rather well developed. Antennae 15–17 segments, third segment shorter to longer than the second. Pronotum narrower than the head, flat, anterior corners only slightly deflexed; posterior margins of meso- and metanotum broad, more or less broadly rounded. Wings hyaline, only the costa and the radial sector dark and distinct, the remaining veins hyaline and weak; wing membrane rather densely covered with fine hairs; radius reduced, hardly extending beyond the wing scale; radial sector somewhat distant from the anterior margin; media of forewing arising beyond the wing scale, media of hindwing arising at the base of the radial sector, sometimes branching at or before the middle of the wing; cubitus without a thickened basal vein, or only very weakly so. All tibiae with only 2 apical spurs. Cerci short, styli absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head more or less rectangular, rather thick. Frontal gland opening large, at the apex of a long or short frontal tube; the frons in front of the tube slopes gradually towards the mouthparts. Clypeus almost indistinguishable from the transverse band, apex often corneous, always supported by two anteriorly diverging chitinous bands. Labrum either elongate and narrowing anteriorly, or shorter, widest at the middle, apex hyaline. Mandibles stout, sickle-shaped: left mandible with 2 to several incisor teeth, sometimes with a large base; right mandible often with its middle and base fused into a large masticatory part. Antennae 13–15 segments, third segment usually shorter than the second, sometimes equal or longer. Pronotum narrower than the head, weakly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe very large, reaching the neck. Tibiae with 2 apical spurs; cerci short; styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale yellow to white, subcircular to pentagonal and rounded, widest at the level of the antennae, flattened and arched. Clypeus large and arched. Mandibular first tooth either not larger than the second or distinctly larger. Antennae 14–16 segments, mostly 15. Pronotum as in the soldier; meso- and metanotum strongly compressed by the strongly arched abdomen.

/genus/cortaritermes/.note: The original description (Mathews 1977 monograph) could not be obtained in readable full text; this entry rests only on the genus-level key of Constantino 1999, so the range of characters that can be written is narrow; that work gives only soldier key characters and gut characters, hence no worker or alate sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head shape as in figs 83–84, yellowish brown; nasus and vertex densely covered with very short hairs; the first proctodeal segment (P1) forms a distinct intestinal loop in right lateral view (em vista lateral direita); mostly living in damp grassland.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head shape as in figs 83–84, yellowish brown; nasus and vertex with abundant very short hairs.

/genus/crenetermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 101–102). The Chinese generic name is not yet fixed, so zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name in the form of a Chinese common name, pending confirmation at a higher level. Only one species, Crenetermes albotarsalis (Sjöst.), is known, from Cameroon and the Congo; p. 102 is entirely a discussion of systematic relationships with the Mirotermes series and contains no morphological description, so it was not used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, with only Crenetermes albotarsalis (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo; synonyms include Eutermes albotarsalis Sjöst. and Suleitermes Wasm. (an unpublished name) in the literature. Alate head subquadrate, antennae 16 segments with the third short; soldier head rectangular, longer than broad, labrum subquadrate and strongly grooved, mandibles of the same type as Thoracotermes, antennae 15 segments; worker entirely white, head longer than broad, mandibles with a large apical tooth. Holmgren placed the genus in the Mirotermes series, but the soldier mandibles have Termes-type teeth and the frontal gland opening is exposed and not situated beneath a frontal protuberance, differing from all the Mirotermes subgenera and from Thoracotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head width about equal to the length. Compound eyes small, projecting. Ocelli about their own diameter from the compound eyes. Base of clypeus brighter than the frons, very large, slightly longer than half its width (9:8.5), very strongly arched; because the base of the clypeus is expanded, the malar part of the head appears short. Mandibular first tooth large. Antennae 16 segments, third short. The incision of the posterior margin of the mesonotum is broader than that of the metanotum. Wings dark, the membrane with fine dense small spine-like points (»punktiert« in the original). Media of forewing arising independently behind the wing scale. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each. Cerci short. Styli absent. The original adds: a reduced stylus was once observed in a male nymph.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head longer than broad, quadrangular, narrowing slightly anteriorly, rather arched, anterior margin obliquely truncate. Frontal gland opening on the margin of the sloping frons, rather small but densely surrounded by hairs. Base of clypeus completely flat, slightly shorter than half its width. Labrum subquadrate, widening slightly outwards, strongly grooved; anterior margin slightly incised in the middle, the lateral angles only indistinctly acute, directed anteriorly. Mandibles as in Thoracotermes. Antennae 15 segments, third short. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped, small. Tibial spur formula as in the alate. Styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Entirely white. Head longer than broad. Base of clypeus about as long as half its width, strongly arched. Mandibles with a large apical tooth. Antennae 15 segments, third short. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped. Tibial spur formula and condition of the styli as above (styli absent).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier frons flat, clearly different from the other groups of the genus Mirotermes (at that time a broad genus including this group); apart from this it is closest to the subgenus Mirotermes s. str.; mandibles snapping, of the same form as in Mirotermes s. str.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown, broadly oval, densely covered with short hairs and setae; fontanelle slightly deeper than the rest of the head capsule, indistinct; left mandible with 2 large teeth (one pointed, one rounded), right mandible with only 1 pointed tooth; antennal segment 3 extremely short, much shorter than segment 4.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow, covered with short hairs, elongate-subrectangular, the sides nearly parallel, abruptly narrowed in front of the antennal bases; antennae paler than the head, 13-segmented; labrum with 2 points; mandibles brown, slender, apex abruptly curved, base broad with teeth on the inner margin (more marked on the left mandible than on the right); pronotum paler than the head, saddle-shaped.

/genus/cubitermes/.note: Adapted from the English genus-level redescription; measurements and enteric valve typology are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Belonging to Cubitermitinae, with a mixed segment; the second hindgut paunch (P3) of workers, soldiers and alates all bear a caecal projection. Soldier labrum deeply cleft, mandibles sickle-shaped with the inner margin generally smooth, each side with 1 distinct marginal tooth near the molar area; alate antennae mostly 16-segmented, pronotum distinctly wider than long and narrower than the head width including the compound eyes; tibial spur formula 3:2:2 in all castes, with an additional 0:2:0 proximal spines on the mid and hind legs.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule strongly sclerotised, generally dark (C6–C8, old specimens may fade to C4); frontal pore concolorous with the head capsule or 1–5 grades paler; postclypeus C4–C7, usually 1–2 grades paler than the head capsule. Antennae C4–C7, without obvious difference in colour between proximal and distal segments, mostly 16-segmented (about 7% 15-segmented, about 1% 17-segmented). Compound eyes subcircular to short oval; ocelli subcircular to oval, their distance from the compound eye about equal to their own greatest diameter. Labrum bell-shaped, generally wider than long. Left mandible apical tooth longer than the first marginal tooth, marginal teeth 3, the second expressed only as an undulation of the cutting edge between the first and third; molar prominence rounded and blunt dorsally, ending posteriorly in a small pointed process. Right mandible marginal teeth 2, the first with a sharp tip when fresh, the second smaller with a blunt tip; molar tooth with a rounded, blunt labial process on the ventral surface, heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width including the compound eyes, flat to slightly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and slightly raised. Wings hyaline, with a brownish to greyish tinge, the costa darker; R1 completely fused with the costal margin and sclerotised, Rs simple and sclerotised, M not sclerotised, dividing into 2–7 branches near the wing apex, Cu dividing into 7–14 branches reaching the posterior margin. Hindgut caecum small, amorphous, button-shaped.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule generally dark (Cd3–Cd6), with a smooth or rather abrupt transition from the dark frons to the paler posterior part; antennae and labrum usually paler than the head capsule. Mandibles dark (C6–C8), with a ring of abruptly paler colour at the base, mostly concolorous with the frons. Head in dorsal view with the sides mostly subparallel (often slightly narrowed at the posterior 1/3–1/4) or slightly convex, slightly converging forwards to the antennal sockets and then more distinctly converging towards the mandibular bases; in lateral view the upper margin straight to distinctly concave, with or without a frontal projection on the frons.
