Antennae mostly 14.5–15-segmented, rarely 14-segmented (about 12%). Labrum always more or less deeply cleft, length/width ratio variable, the sides straight, slightly concave or harp-shaped, rarely convex; lobe tips rounded, angular or with a white translucent tip; anterior margin concave, circular to V-shaped. Mandibles sickle-shaped, curvature variable, inner margin generally smooth (rarely finely serrate), each side with 1 distinct marginal tooth near the molar tooth, sometimes very small; mandibles generally shorter than or slightly longer than the head length. Pronotum saddle-shaped, width 45%–90% of the head width, anterior margin entire to distinctly notched in the middle. Tibial apical spurs of fore, mid and hind legs 3:2:2, proximal spurs 0:2:0 (the latter sometimes weak). Hindgut caecum small, amorphous or lobed, situated near the middle of the abdomen; enteric valve on the left side, the symmetry of the secondary sexual character may be six-radiate, three-radiate, bilaterally symmetrical or irregular.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3); basal antennal segments pale (C2–C3), distal segments distinctly darker (C4–C5); thorax and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to reddish brown owing to the gut contents. Hindgut P3 with a caecal projection, an important internal character distinguishing it from related genera.

/genus/curvitermes/.note: Soldier after the genus key and comparative genus characters; of the alate only the left mandible index is known. The original description, Holmgren 1912, exists only as a very poor-quality OCR German scan and was not used for the text.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The form of the soldier mandibles is ‘abnormal’: with molar plate, molar prominence and marginal teeth, much resembling the mandibles of the worker of the same name; apical tooth fish-hook-shaped; molar region enlarged, with a posteriorly directed subapical tooth. Frontal tube surface smooth, broadly conical. Alate left mandible index about 2.0 (as in Cyrilliotermes and Paracurvitermes).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Molar region of the mandibles enlarged, with a posteriorly directed subapical tooth; apical tooth fish-hook-shaped; mandibles with molar plate, molar prominence and marginal teeth, similar to the worker mandibles. Frontal tube surface smooth, broadly conical.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible index about 2.0, as in Cyrilliotermes and Paracurvitermes (Armitermes, Embiratermes and Labiotermes 0.7–1.1).

/genus/cylindrotermes/.note: Adapted from the Portuguese genus-level redescription; mandibular tooth positions and interspecific colour variation are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head subrectangular and elongate, labrum usually pentagonal; frontal pore small, situated in the anterior 1/4 of the head, behind the antennal insertions; postmentum narrow and long, about 3/4 of the head length; mandibles symmetrical, curved, each with 1 tooth, the tooth position varying between species, the molar area visible at the base of the mandibles in all species; pronotum in lateral view with the anterior and posterior lobes at nearly 180°, both lobes semicircular; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, mid tibia with 2 spines (1 apical, 1 proximal), hind tibia with 1 apical spine. Alate head circular or slightly elongate, compound eyes hemispherical, medium-sized, not very prominent; ocelli oval to circular, not touching the compound eyes; antennae 11–13-segmented, segment 3 completely or partly divided. Worker head circular, mandibular characters as below.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head subrectangular, elongate; labrum generally pentagonal; frontal pore small, opening in the anterior 1/4 of the head, behind the antennal insertions; postmentum narrow and long, about 3/4 of the head length; mandibles symmetrical, curved, each with 1 tooth, the tooth position varying between species, the molar area visible at the base of the mandibles in all species of this genus; pronotum in lateral view with the angle between the anterior and posterior lobes nearly 180°, both lobes semicircular; tibial spur formula 3:2:2; mid tibia with 2 spines, one at the apex and one proximally at about 1/3 of the total length, hind tibia with 1 apical spine; pilosity varying greatly in density between species. Head capsule yellowish brown, thorax and legs whitish, abdomen transparent; body colour differs little between species.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head circular. Mandibles: apical tooth close in size to the marginal tooth, forming an acute angle with M1+2; left mandible with the cutting edge between M1+2 and M3 straight, M3 smaller than M1+2, the gap between M3 and the molar prominence very narrow, molar prominence with distinct striae; right mandible M2 smaller than M1, molar plate with 5 distinct striae. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Body colour always whitish or slightly yellowish, without differences between species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head circular or slightly elongate in dorsal view, narrow in lateral view; compound eyes hemispherical, medium-sized, not very prominent; ocelli oval to circular, slightly prominent, not touching the compound eyes; antennae 11–13-segmented, segment 3 completely or partly divided; pronotum trapezoidal; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotal plates usually sharper in females than in males; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, mid tibia with 2 spines, hind tibia with 1 apical spine; wings about 1.5 times the body length; head with short hairs and setae, density varying between species, some species also with microtrichia; forewing with sparse short hairs, hindwing with or without; head capsule dark brown, densely covered with pale spots at the bases of the setae and with short hairs, mandibles paler than the head capsule with dark teeth, labrum dark brown, antennae dark brown; head and pronotum with large, variable pale spots, always 2 between the postclypeus and the ocelli, visible in dorsal view; abdominal tergites and sternites paler than the head capsule, both with pale spots at the hair bases, sternites paler at the sides than in the centre; legs pale yellow, paler than the head.

/genus/cyranotermes/.note: Rocha, Carrijo & Cancello 2012 (Zootaxa 3196: 50–57) is the most recent revision of the genus and first described the alate, but only page 1 of its PDF (abstract and introduction) could be obtained through the text proxy and the body of the generic diagnosis was not read, so this entry gives soldier characters only, based on the soldier key of Constantino 1999, and does not supply Alate or Worker sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule narrow, oval, the frontal tube conical and thick at the base; in contrast, Anhangatermes has a very broad, round head capsule and a nearly cylindrical frontal tube that is narrow at the base. This contrast is exactly the position of the genus in the Neotropical soldier key.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule narrow and oval in dorsal view; frontal tube conical, thick at the base. In the key the genus is the counterpart entry to Anhangatermes, which has a very broad, round head capsule and a nearly cylindrical frontal tube narrow at the base.

/genus/cyrilliotermes/.note: Soldier based on the generic key and the comparative generic characters of 2011/2022 (the body text of the genus-level redescription by Constantino & Carvalho 2012 was not provided by Plazi; only the soldier species key was read); for the alate only the left mandible index is known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier frontal tube wrinkled and with irregular transverse ridges, doughnut-shaped at the apex; in most species the frontal tube is long and cylindrical, in C. crassinasus broadly conical. Mandibles “anomalous”, with molar plate, molar prominence and marginal teeth, apical tooth reduced (hook-shaped in Curvitermes). Alate left mandible index about 2.0.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal tube long and cylindrical, its surface wrinkled and with irregular transverse ridges, doughnut-shaped at the apex; mandibles with molar plate, molar prominence and marginal teeth (similar to worker mandibles), apical tooth reduced.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible index about 2.0, as in Curvitermes and Paracurvitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with slender, snapping mandibles, the head bearing a conical cephalic projection (i.e. frontal projection), and with a well-developed large yellow labial gland extending posteriorly deep into the abdomen; the genus is soil-feeding, and the worker enteric valve armature (EVA) is highly diagnostic.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles slender, snapping; in most species the mandibles have marginal teeth (only D. brevicarinatus lacks marginal teeth); the apical hook accounts for about 1/7 of total mandible length (most species) or about 1/3 (D. pantanalis); the shape of the frontal projection (shallow/steep, triangular/narrowly trapezoidal, angle of the posterior margin with the plane of the vertex) is a diagnostic character between species.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Soil-feeding; enteric valve armature highly diagnostic, but without marked intraspecific variation.

/genus/dihoplotermes/.note: Adapted from the English genus-level diagnosis and the description of D. taurus; species-level measurements omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandible base and the region above the condyle each bear 1 anterior marginal spine on either side; mandibles asymmetrical, of the snapping type; labrum asymmetrical; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Worker mandible apical tooth distinctly larger than the first marginal tooth; right mandible without a second marginal tooth; left mandible without a third marginal tooth, the molar tooth separated from the first and second marginal teeth by a small notch. The gut of worker and soldier shares the following features: the columnar band of the gizzard bears 6 primary and secondary folds, the first-order pad (pulvillus) has 1 short spine at its centre; the Malpighian tubule node bears 2 pairs of Malpighian tubules; the enteric valve has 6 pads, 1 of which has a row of longitudinal spines at its distal end.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow, subrectangular, almost the entire surface irregularly scattered with setae of varying length; setae dense at the apex of the frontal projection. Anterior side of the head capsule, near the mandible base, with 1 spine on either side. Anterior part of the head with a prominent projection which, in dorsal view, covers part of the labrum and nearly reaches the lateral margins of the head; the anteroventral margin of the projection is concave above the mandibles and forms a small step in profile, and its margin directly above the antennal sockets bears 2 small projections. Postmentum narrower at the middle, the anterior part slightly wider than the posterior, the posterior margin with 1 spine-like projection visible in profile. Mandibles asymmetrical, dark: proximal 2/3 of the left mandible slightly curved inwards, the distal part slightly wider but narrowing towards the apex, curving sickle-like to the right to form a small notch that receives the right mandible; outer margin of the right mandible nearly straight, narrowing towards the apex, also with a notch that receives the left mandible when closed; apex pointed, slightly curved to the left. Labrum symmetrical, with 7–8 long setae usually arranged in 2 rows, apex slightly curved, anterior margin pointed. Antennae 14-segmented; scape about 3 times as long as segment 2, segments 3–4 equal in length and shorter than segment 5, segments 6–8 equal in length, the remaining segments subequal. Margins of the pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum with long, sparse setae; anterior part of the pronotum with microtrichia. Tergites and sternites of the abdomen covered with long setae. Surface of the fore tibia irregularly scattered with a few long setae. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2; apex of the mid tibia with another spine beside the spur, easily mistaken for the third spur; this tibial spine is present in all castes.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule white, uniformly scattered with setae of varying size except on the anterior margin; fontanelle slightly distinct. Postclypeus slightly inflated, with a few setae; setal density of the labrum similar to that of the clypeus. Antennae 14-segmented, scape longer than segment 2, subsequent segments gradually lengthening. Apical tooth of the left mandible larger than and slightly longer than the first and second marginal teeth combined; inner margin of the apical tooth slightly concave, a small notch between the first and second marginal teeth and the molar tooth; molar prominence distinct, without striae. Apical tooth of the right mandible well developed, longer than the first marginal tooth; second marginal tooth indistinct; molar plate slightly concave, without striae. Anterior part of the pronotum with microtrichia, anterior margins of the pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum with long setae. Abdomen transparent, tergites and sternites densely covered with short setae, posterior part of each sternite with 1 row of long setae. Fore tibia slightly broadened, surface densely covered with setae of varying size. Gut: gizzard small, columnar band with 6 first- and second-order folds, first-order pad with a short spine at its centre; Malpighian tubule node situated on the mesenteric tongue, 2 pairs of Malpighian tubules attached at the same point; enteric valve with 6 pads of varying shape and size, 5 of them with a few short spines at the distal end and 1 with a row of longitudinal spines at the distal end; colon distinctly wider than the midgut.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown, densely covered with short setae mixed with a few long setae; fontanelle distinct, drop-shaped, forming a small depression on the vertex; ocelli small, semicircular, protruding; compound eyes medium-sized, round, protruding. Postclypeus small, yellowish brown, sub-trapezoidal, slightly inflated, surface densely covered with setae of varying size; labrum with many setae, at its widest about as wide as the postclypeus. Apical antennal segment broken off; scape relatively broad, about 3 times as long as segment 2, segment 3 equal in length to segments 4–7, subsequent segments gradually lengthening. Pronotum light brown, covered with setae except at the middle and near the margin below the anterior lobe; slightly narrower than the head; anterior part with microtrichia, median carina weak but visible on the anterior margin. Anterior part of the mesonotum and metanotum dark yellow, posterior part dark brown, the anterior part narrowing posteriorly to the tips of the wing buds and partly covered by them; posterior margin bilobed, the posterior margin of the mesonotum semicircular and of the metanotum V-shaped. Abdominal tergites concolorous with the pronotum, with numerous small setae and a few long setae; sternites light brown at the sides, dark yellow near the midline, posterior margin of each segment with 1 row of long setae. Anterior proximal surface of the fore coxa with small projections; tibia slender.

/genus/disjunctitermes/.note: The imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set; there is no soldier section (soldierless). The genus-level Diagnosis deals mainly with the enteric valve and the tibia, and the genus-level Worker section gives the body wall and digestive tract.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among Neotropical apicotermitines, like Anoplotermes banksi, A. pacificus and Hydrecotermes spp., it has a strongly inflated fore tibia, and an enteric valve without spines and without sclerotisation. It is closest to A. banksi but can be distinguished from it by the accessory (fourth) marginal tooth of the left mandible, the larger enteric valve seating and the more truncate end of P2; Hydrecotermes lacks a spherical mesenteric tongue.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, small. Head capsule pale yellow, covered with about 100 setae of varying length; postclypeus moderately inflated; fontanelle almost indiscernible; antennae 14-segmented. The apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the left mandible are widely separated and both long, clearly projecting beyond the line formed by the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence; above the molar prominence there is another accessory (fourth) marginal tooth, visible in both dorsal and ventral view. The apical tooth of the right mandible is far longer than the first marginal tooth, the third marginal tooth nearly symmetrical. The fore tibia is strongly inflated, about 3 times as long as its greatest width (at the middle). The mesenteric tongue is spherical. P2 enters through a large, stout, trilobed enteric valve seating, two lobes of which are visible through the body wall; the enteric valve consists of 6 slender, inflated pads facing the valve lumen; the posterior end of P2 (including the enteric valve) is truncate and extends about halfway into the seating. Measurements: species-level (Table 2, 12 workers from each of 11 colonies; holotype head width 0.64 mm).

/genus/diversitermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed as the 9th subgenus in the catalogue, containing diversimilis Silvestri (Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia) and castaniceps Holmgren (Brazil). The original contains only key entries and gives no measurements for the three soldier types, so only the number of types and qualitative characters are given above; the original also has no worker characters.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The most conspicuous feature is the trimorphism of the soldier: in the major soldier the nasus is narrow and slender with a weak basal depression; in the medium and minor soldiers the head capsule is more or less dumbbell-shaped constricted; antennae 13-segmented; the legs of the two small soldier types are rather long. In the same group Velocitermes is dimorphic (corresponding to the medium and minor types of this genus) and Trinervitermes is dimorphic or rarely trimorphic but has no apical part on the mandibles; the three fixed soldier types remain the most conspicuous mark of this genus. The alate is distinguished from Rotunditermes (eyes very large) by the medium-sized eyes, the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd, and the clypeus about as long as half its width.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes medium-sized (the original key contrasts them with the very large eyes of Rotunditermes, and that branch additionally records the compound eyes as bulging dorsolaterally on the head and the pronotum as relatively large); the 1st marginal tooth of the mandible about as long as the 2nd; clypeus about as long as half its width, or slightly shorter and strongly convex, transversely oval, pale yellow and sometimes dark; antennal segments with average elongation.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier trimorphic. Major soldier: nasus narrow, basal depression weak. Medium and minor soldiers: head capsule more or less markedly dumbbell-shaped constricted; antennae 13-segmented. The legs of the two small soldier types are rather long.

/genus/diwaitermes/.note: The generic characters are given in three sections, Imago / Soldier / Worker, as in the original; only the type species of the alate is known and it has no morphological description, so that section records only what the original says about this caste and contains no measurements. The original notes that N. orientis is almost certainly a junior synonym of Eutermes kanehirae Oshima, 1914, and the generic characters follow N. orientis; the genus contains three species, D. kanehirae, D. foi and D. castanopsis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Roisin & Pasteels established the genus with Nasutitermes (Subulitermes) orientis from New Guinea as type species, the generic name being taken from the New Melanesian word diwai (wood). The soldier is fully nasute and closely related to Nasutitermes, but the head capsule is not constricted behind the antennal fossae, the soldier is monomorphic, small to medium in size, and the antennae are 11- or 12-segmented. What really separates it from Nasutitermes and Niuginitermes is the worker gut: the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is attached by a broad stalk dorsally and slightly mesally on the midgut, the 4 Malpighian tubules converge where they attach at the midgut–hindgut junction, and the two rings of spines on the enteric valve are asymmetric, with the lower ring of spines projecting into the stomach lumen; the worker is dimorphic. Eleanoritermes from Borneo resembles the genus, but its worker mandibles have a more concave molar region, its enteric valve is placed further forward, only three swellings bear a few small spines, and the colon is longer.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Only the type species is known. The original lists no genus-level morphological characters and only notes that the number of antennal segments may later serve to distinguish the genus from Nasutitermes and Niuginitermes. The original also compares the closely related Nasutitermes liklik: it differs from D. kanehirae in having one more antennal segment in every caste (14 versus 13 in the alate).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Fully nasute, closely related to Nasutitermes. Head capsule not constricted behind the antennal fossae; soldier monomorphic, small to medium in size; antennae 11- or 12-segmented, and when 12-segmented segment 3 is extremely short and incompletely separated from segment 4; head capsule hairy, with many setae of varying length; the points on the mandibles are small and sometimes absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 12- or 13-segmented, and when 13-segmented segment 3 is extremely short and incompletely separated from segment 4. Mandibles very similar to those of Nasutitermes, left mandible index 0.45–0.55. Gut: the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is attached by a broad stalk dorsally and slightly mesally on the rest of the midgut; the 4 Malpighian tubules converge where they attach at the midgut–hindgut junction; the upper ring of spines on the enteric valve is slightly asymmetric, and the lower ring of spines projects into the stomach lumen. Worker dimorphic; the body length distribution of the major worker is unimodal, with no growth and a slight darkening of pigmentation within the same instar.

/genus/dolichorhinotermes/.note: The alate section rests only on the diagnostic statement at generic level (the 3rd flagellar segment shorter than the 1st) and on the account of the fossil species D. apopnus; the original states explicitly that the alate of the extant species is unknown. Page 2 is in two columns and the text layer was reflowed after column-wise cropping; hyphens broken across lines in the quotation (subquad-rate) have been rejoined, with no change to the wording.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate the 3rd flagellar segment is shorter than the 1st flagellar segment; in the major soldier the labrum is distinctly elongate, its apex often reaching the ends of the mandibles, whereas the labrum of Rhinotermes is almost square and much shorter; in the minor soldier the opening of the frontal gland lies on the anterior part of the head but is not borne on a distinct frontal projection, the mandibles are reduced with rounded margins, and in dorsal view the sides of the head are straight or convex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The 3rd flagellar segment is shorter than the 1st flagellar segment. For the extant species D. lanciarius the original records the alate as 'Imago. Unknown.'; the alate of the fossil species D. apopnus: head large, broad and rounded, the anteclypeus projecting forwards as a broad beak-like process, the frontal gland small and situated at the base of the beak, the compound eyes large and protruding, the ocelli large and elongate and not touching the compound eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: posterior part of the head broader, the sides gently rounded and narrowing forwards; left mandible with two coarse teeth, the first just before mid-length and the second slightly behind it, the first distinctly longer than the second; right mandible with two teeth near mid-length, the first shorter than the second; labrum elongate with a rounded apex, without an incision, and with a shallow longitudinal groove dorsally; antennae with at least 14 segments, the 3rd flagellar segment distinctly shorter than the 1st; pronotum saddle-shaped. Minor soldier: sides of the head weakly convex and narrowing forwards, the posterior margin rounded; antennae 16 segments, the 3rd flagellar segment distinctly shorter than the 1st; mandibles reduced to broad fleshy lobes bearing only minute sclerotised points; labrum narrow and long, forked at the apex, the two prongs widely separated.

/genus/drepanotermes/.note: Proposed in the original as a subgenus of HAMITERMES (Untergattung Drepanotermes); the genus diagnosis is given for the soldier and worker, the alate is unknown. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Relatively large in size; alate unknown. Soldier: head rectangular, flatly convex; postclypeus bilobed; labrum oval and slightly pointed; mandibles very long, strongly sickle-curved and slender, with 1 long, obliquely truncate tooth almost at the middle, perpendicular to the inner margin; antennae 17-segmented; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Worker: head large, broadly oval; fontanelle and sagittal suture very conspicuous; postclypeus very large and arched; antennae 18-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Relatively large in size; colour more or less dark. Head rectangular, flatly convex; fontanelle indistinct; pale ocular spots behind the eyes. Postclypeus bilobed. Labrum oval, slightly pointed. Mandibles very long, strongly sickle-curved, slender, with 1 long, obliquely truncate tooth almost at the middle, perpendicular to the inner margin. Antennae 17-segmented, segments elongate; segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, concolorous; remaining tergites slightly paler. Legs long; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: As large as or slightly larger than the soldier, same colour, legs long. Head large, broadly oval; fontanelle very distinct; sagittal suture very distinct, transverse suture indistinct; ocelli vestigial. Pale ocular spots behind the antennae. Postclypeus very large, arched, margins pale; labrum wider than long, pale. Antennae 18-segmented, segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together, segment 3 distinctly longer than segment 4, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 3. Pronotum much narrower than the head. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs.

/genus/duplidentitermes/.note: The original gives the genus diagnosis by comparison with Hoplognathotermes and Allognathotermes. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Hoplognathotermes and Allognathotermes; the soldier differs most conspicuously from the closely related genera in having 1 large bicuspid tooth on each mandible; antennae 13–14-segmented; fore femur short and stout, equally thick at the middle; sharp ridge of the fore coxa with 9–11 conspicuous setae in a row. The alate and the worker mandibles show corresponding features.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Fore coxa with several short hairs and long and short setae on its outline; middle tibia without contrasting outer spines. Fontanelle white, triangular, only slightly smaller than the ocellus. Mandibles broadly similar to those of the worker: apical tooth proportionally larger than in Hoplognathotermes; in the left mandible the distance from the apical point to the first marginal tooth point is greater than that from the first to the third marginal tooth point; cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible undulating; second marginal tooth of the right mandible reduced to a small mound (as in Allognathotermes). Posterior margins of meso- and metanotum deeply concave, the notch angle sharper than a right angle. Fore coxa with a sharp longitudinal ridge, flatly convex in section, the crest of the ridge nearer the base than the middle of the ridge. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, outer spur of the fore tibia short and distinctly reduced. Sc short in both fore- and hindwing, merging with the anterior margin immediately after the basal suture.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head very large, anterior face rather flat; no tuft of hairs near the frontal gland opening; setae at the front end of the large labrum scattered, not in tufts as in Apicotermes; sharp ridge of the fore coxa with 9–11 conspicuous setae in 1 row, curved towards the inner margin and back towards the apex, enclosing a nearly oval flat area in the apical half of the coxa. Inner side of the fore tibia with several weakly specialised spines; middle tibia without contrasting outer spines. Anterior part of the postmentum proportionally larger than in the closely related genera, the narrowest point about 5/6–6/7 of its length from the anterior margin, lateral sutures visible over their whole length. Antennae 13–14-segmented, similar to Allognathotermes (Firmitermes 14-segmented, Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes 15-segmented). Suture between postclypeus and frons visible, but less distinct than in Firmitermes and Hoplognathotermes. Labrum widest at the distinct lateral angles (in Firmitermes the labral lateral margins are convex, in Hoplognathotermes the sides are parallel with obtuse lateral angles, in Acutidentitermes the sides are parallel and slightly concave with a sharper apex, in Allognathotermes the widest point is rounder). Each mandible with 1 large bicuspid tooth, by which it differs conspicuously from all closely related genera. Longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa conspicuous and sharp, gently and evenly convex in section, extending about half the coxa from the apex, more arched and more distinct than in Hoplognathotermes, and very similar to Allognathotermes, only slightly more evident because it extends with a slight inward curve. Fore femur short and stout, sides parallel, equally thick at the middle; fore tibia slightly swollen. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, outer spur of the fore tibia proportionally short (as in Hoplognathotermes).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibular features similar to those of the alate; ridge of the fore coxa more arched and more projecting than in the Hoplognathotermes worker.

/genus/ebogotermes/.note: The genus is named after Ebogo village in Cameroon, near the type locality. The source states Imago. Unknown and Soldier. Unknown, belongs to a soldierless clade, so no soldier or alate section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The largest of the soldierless apicotermitine workers of equatorial Africa; the midgut is looped, the mixed segment well developed, P1 of moderate length, a P3/P4 constriction present and P4 a long tube, on which basis it is placed in the Anoplotermes group.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head, thorax, abdomen and legs all covered with setae of varying length; antennae 14 segments; postclypeus moderately inflated; fore tibia slightly inflated; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/echinotermes/.note: The generic name derives from Latin Echino (spiny), referring to the armature of the enteric valve. The source states Imago: Unknown; there is no soldier, so no alate or soldier section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The crop is unusually large, and the enteric valve consists of 6 spherical comb-like cushions whose ends form spiny spheres; this combination is unique among the genera of Apicotermitinae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head and antennae pale yellow, pronotum pale yellow, legs transparent. Crop very large; EVS trilobed, its smaller lobe not visible in the intact gut; enteric valve with 6 cushions whose ends form spiny spheres at the opening into P3.

/genus/ekueitermes/.note: The imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no "Alate" section is set; there is no soldier section (soldierless). The original also has a Comparison and remarks section, pointing out that the digestive tract is similar to that of Patawatermes and Hirsutitermes, but that the EVS is shorter.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mesenteric tongue of the mixed segment is short and not inflated; P1 is very short; the enteric valve armature (EVA) consists of 6 conical cushions, each covered with 18–25 polygonal scales with fringed margins (4–15 per cushion), the distal end of each cushion with 7–17 sclerotised spines arranged in palmate fashion; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is distinctly differentiated and tubular.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (head length and head width from medium to large). Head capsule pale white to pale yellow, densely covered with evenly spaced long, fine, pale, erect setae interspersed with short hairs; in lateral view the dorsum slightly concave, the antennal segments translucent. Antennae 14-segmented, segment formula 2>3<4<5. Fontanelle distinct, oval, situated behind the brain (visible in preserved specimens); postclypeus strongly inflated. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior and posterior margins with rows of long fine erect setae, the lateral margins with several long setae; the anterior lobe margins of the mesonotum and metanotum also with rows of setae. Abdomen transparent, the tergites and sternites densely covered with setae of varying length. Fore coxa and fore femur with numerous pale fine setae; fore tibia strongly inflated, interspersed with a few long setae and numerous minute dense setae; the tibial spines of all legs weak, indistinct except apically; apical spur formula 2:2:2. The apical tooth of the left mandible is more projecting than M1+2, forming an acute angle with it, the posterior margin of M1+2 slightly concave; M3 less projecting than M1+2, its margin forming an acute angle; molar prominence well developed, not concealing the molar process in dorsal view. The apical tooth of the right mandible is more projecting than M1, M1 small and slightly exceeding M2, a right angle between M1 and M2, the posterior margin of M2 concave, without a ridge. Digestive tract: crop large; mixed segment short and not inflated; midgut short and narrow, gradually widening into a very short, tubular P1 that does not form a ventral loop; EVS well differentiated, tubular; P3 large and inflated, P4 very long and narrow, P5 saccular. Measurements: species-level (Table 1, 17 workers from 3 colonies).

/genus/eleanoritermes/.note: Based only on the comparative diagnosis in Roisin & Pasteels 1996 within their discussion of genera related to Niuginitermes; the original description is in Ahmad 1968 (Bulletin of the Department of Zoology, University of the Panjab 3). The alate is not described.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus (Eleanoritermes borneensis Ahmad, Borneo). Similar to Niuginitermes, but the enteric valve is situated further anteriorly, its 3 swellings bear only a few small spines and are weakly armed; Malpighian tubules inserted close together.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Antennae 11-segmented; mandibles toothless (without points).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 12-segmented; enteric valve situated more anteriorly, the 3 swellings weakly armed, Malpighian tubules inserted close together (see Diagnostic characters).

/genus/embiratermes/.note: Soldier based on the 2022 comparative generic characters and the 2012 generic key; worker based on the description of the enteric valve and midgut tongue; for the alate only the left mandible index is known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandibles of the piercing type, apex acute; marginal tooth at the proximal 1/3 of mandible length, or near the middle or near the base; clypeus not inflated; head in dorsal view elongate, subrectangular, head base usually longer than wide; ventral margin of fore coxa with a process. Worker midgut tongue straight, not reaching the P1 swelling; enteric valve section short and wide, at the mid-point of the abdomen. Alate left mandible index 0.7–1.1.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles of the piercing type, apex acute; marginal tooth at the proximal 1/3 of the mandible, a recognisable marginal tooth (near the middle or near the base); clypeus not inflated. Head capsule in dorsal view elongate, subrectangular; head base usually longer than wide. Ventral margin of fore coxa with a process.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Midgut tongue straight, not reaching the P1 swelling; enteric valve section short and wide, at the mid-point of the abdomen.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.7–1.1, as in Armitermes and Labiotermes.

/genus/emersonitermes/.note: A monotypic genus (E. thekadensis Mathur & Sen-Sarma), endemic to southern India (Kerala). Alate unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus endemic to southern India. Soldier head capsule creamy white and pyriform; nasus reddish brown, slender and conical; mandibles vestigial and without spines; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, without an anterior emargination; each abdominal tergite with 4 long setae; worker antennae 13-segmented, the basal prominence of the left mandible large and projecting beyond the second marginal tooth.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule creamy white, the frontal gland area paler; nasus reddish brown; antennae brown; pronotum yellow; legs and abdomen creamy white. Head capsule pyriform, densely covered with microtrichia mixed with long setae; nasus slender and conical; antennae 14-segmented; mandibles vestigial, without spines; pronotum saddle-shaped, without an anterior emargination; tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; abdomen elongate, each tergite with 4 long setae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule nearly circular, densely hairy; coronal suture not visible; frontal plate elliptical and white; antennae 13-segmented; postclypeus arched, half as long as wide; mandibles with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth; apical tooth of the left mandible pointed, subequal in length to the first marginal tooth; first marginal tooth large, narrow and triangular, with a long posterior margin; second marginal tooth small and far removed; basal prominence large, projecting beyond the second marginal tooth; apical tooth of the right mandible subequal in length to the first marginal tooth; first marginal tooth isosceles-triangular; second marginal tooth short, its posterior margin longer than its anterior margin, the angle between the two marginal teeth obtuse; molar plate longer than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum and legs as in the soldier.

/genus/engelitermes/.note: The genus is monotypic; the original places it in its own Engelitermitinae. The alate is described from a single queen only, and the original also notes that the antennae of the specimen are broken (the segment count can only be given as 'more than 10'). The full text is a PDF without a text layer; it was checked after transcription from page-by-page rendered images.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In overall morphology the soldier most closely resembles the African Cephalotermes and the Neotropical Cylindrotermes, but its gut contains no solid food particles (termed white-gutted in the original), which distinguishes it from both; its soldier is consistently smaller than the mandibulate soldiers of African Termitinae, its size comparable to that of Forficulitermes planifrons (maximum head width 0.63 mm versus 0.65 mm), but the mandible shape is entirely different. The worker mandibles are of the soil/humus-feeding type, whereas those of Cephalotermes and Cylindrotermes workers are wood-feeding: apical tooth broad and widely separated from the first marginal tooth, molar region concave and without ridges (similar to Crenetermes, Eutermellus, Jugositermes and Thoracotermes); it is especially similar to the worker of Forficulitermes in the wide gap between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth and in the well-developed first and fourth hindgut segments. The combination of 'a single spine plus unornamented pad cuticle' in the enteric valve is unique among termite enteric valves; the gizzard structure is simplified compared with most Termitinae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Described from a single physogastric queen only: head brown, bearing several hundred setae of varying length, mostly directed forwards, arising from translucent setal sockets; the median branch of the frontal suture darker than the rest of the head; fontanelle small, circular, situated between the two ocelli; anterolateral part of the head with two crescent-shaped markings anterior to the fontanelle. Pronotum and postclypeus paler than the vertex, with a similar pilosity; postclypeus not inflated. The antennae of the specimen examined are broken but comprise more than 10 segments; segments 3 and 4 almost fused, segment 3 shorter than segment 2, segments 3 and 4 together longer than segment 2. Apical tooth of the mandibles narrower than in the worker. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule nearly rectangular in dorsal view, the lateral margins slightly convergent posteriorly; frontal surface raised near the fontanelle and undulating in lateral view; fontanelle small, almost indiscernible; mandibles stout, with 1 triangular tooth at the base; antennae 12-segmented; anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum congruent, together forming a straight-sided triangle in lateral view; tibial spur formula 2:2:2; abdomen yellowish white, the gut without solid food residues (white-gutted sensu Scheffrahn et al. 2017).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: In dorsal view a large white brain (supraoesophageal ganglion) is visible within the head capsule, anterior to the small diamond-shaped frontal gland; postclypeus slightly inflated in lateral view. Apical tooth of the mandibles broad and prominent; the gap between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the left mandible greater than the distance between the first and the third marginal teeth; molar region concave, without ridges. Antennae 12-segmented; tibial spur formula 2:2:2; fore femur slightly inflated. Gizzard lacking a columnar belt, the pulvillar belt with sclerotised spines, beneath which lie patches of ridge-like scales. Enteric valve composed of 6 smooth, slender pads, each with 1 small spine at its distal end, the pads directed towards the food stream; the enteric valve armature (EVA) has 1 slightly sclerotised pad anterior to the ring, bearing 1–2 stout spines and several small spines. Mixed segment absent. Ileum cylindrical, running along the left side of the abdomen in a long S-shape, narrowing posteriorly and folding forwards to meet P2; P4 broad anteriorly and narrow posteriorly; P5 unusually large in volume (but not in all individuals).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Placed in the Procryptotermes–Cryptotermes branch on mandibular characters; it differs from Kalotermes in the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible being longer than the posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth, the larger body and much smaller eyes, the media and cubitus of the forewing having a common stalk, and the arolium being absent; the soldier has a larger, dorsoventrally flattened head, pigmented eyes, and long, strong mandibles that are strongly curved near the apex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Yellowish brown; eye diameter 0.35–0.55 mm, ocelli always touching the compound eyes; antennae 14–19-segmented; anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible more than 1.5 times the length of the posterior margin of the first and second marginal teeth, the bases of the first and second marginal teeth shorter than the third marginal tooth; molar plate of the right mandible shorter than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum slightly narrower than the head or nearly as wide, anterior margin concave; wings transparent, covered with transparent papillae; media and cubitus with a common stalk beyond the wing suture; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and wide, dorsoventrally flattened, the sides converging anteriorly; genal region concave below the antennal socket; anterior part of the frons gently sloping, beginning about at the middle of the head, concave in the middle; dorsal margin of the antennal socket distinctly raised, appearing as a small tube dorsally; eyes large and pigmented; labrum subrectangular, wider than long, anterior margin convex with a small median projection; antennae 10–13-segmented, the third segment dark, club-shaped and longest; mandibles long and strong, strongly curved towards the apex from near the basal tubercle; pronotum as wide as the head or slightly narrower, transversely arched and subrectangular, anterior margin slightly raised with a deep angular concavity, sides relatively straight; femora not inflated.

/genus/eremotermes/.note: The original records the alate as unknown and gives only the nymph (antennae 14-segmented, head oval, fontanelle very far back, postclypeal basis about half as long as wide, first tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than the second). The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, with technical terms rendered according to standard insect morphology usage.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown (only the nymph known). Soldier: head shaped as in Mirotermes, short-cylindrical, with a distinct, rounded frontal projection, beneath which lies a rather large fontanelle opening; labrum triangular rather than bilobed; mandibles long and rod-like, symmetrical, with 1 sharp tooth at the middle directed inwards and slightly backwards; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, abdomen very thick, nearly spherical, legs short, tibiae with 2 apical spurs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head as in Mirotermes, short-cylindrical, with a distinct, rounded-obtuse frontal projection, beneath which lies a rather large fontanelle opening; head hairy, the hairs denser around the fontanelle; frons descending gently forwards beneath the frontal projection. Fontanelle gland very large, extending posteriorly to the back of the neck. Labrum triangular (not bilobed as in Mirotermes). Mandibles long and rod-like, apex only slightly incurved, symmetrical; with 1 sharp tooth at the middle directed inwards and slightly backwards; mandibular base very long, as long as the rest; the boundary between base and the main body of the mandible marked by a small bend in the outer margin; molar region step-like, quadrangular. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped. Abdomen very thick, almost spherical, its sides bulging out like inflated sacs; legs short; tibiae with 2 apical spurs; cerci short, without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head thick, broadly oval; fontanelle very far back; postclypeal basis with length equal to half its width, rather strongly arched; first mandibular tooth slightly larger than the second; antennae relatively short, with crowded segments, 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped, abdomen rather thick.

/genus/ereymatermes/.note: The original description by Constantino (1991) was not obtained in full; the genus circumscription and the soldier and worker morphology follow Cancello & Cuezzo (2007)'s account of one species of the genus, the worker molar characters follow Cuezzo & Nickle (2011)'s comparative account. The alate is only known to exist, with no morphological description seen, hence no such section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A nasute genus endemic to the Neotropical region. According to later literature, the genus is fairly clearly delimited, its circumscription recognisable from the three castes together: soldier, worker and alate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule oval, slightly constricted behind the antennal bases; nasus long cylindrical, not upturned in lateral view; clypeus extremely reduced; antennae 12 segments; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, narrow-gap and broad-gap, the narrow-gap morph much commoner than the broad-gap; molar region ridges reduced, but the marginal teeth not lost.

/genus/euchilotermes/.note: Only a single key line can be cited for the soldier; Emerson's 1928 genus-level discussion covers only taxonomic history and known species, with no characters of head shape or antennae, so these are not supplied.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier labrum is large and fleshy, and Emerson's (1928) key lists the genus separately on this character alone. For a long time the genus was known only from E. tensus and its varieties; it was described as a new genus by Silvestri in 1914.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The second marginal tooth of the right mandible is lost in the alate–worker; Emerson (1960) noted that this pattern is similar only in Euchilotermes, Ophiotermes, Tuberculitermes and Spinitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier converges with Cryptotermes in having a shield-like frons; the alate wing venation and mandibles resemble Neotermes, but the anterior margin of the forewing scale is nearly straight or slightly convex, whereas it is more convex in Neotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body yellowish brown; eye diameter 0.43 mm, ocelli touching the compound eye; antennae 14–16 segments; mandibles resembling those of Glyptotermes, the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible equal in length to the third marginal tooth, the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly longer than the molar plate; pronotum narrower than the head; anterior margin of the forewing scale nearly straight or slightly convex; radial sector with 5–6 branches, the first branch at about half the wing length; media strongly sclerotised, nearly parallel to and close to the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark brown, frons shield-like, short and thick, the sides rather straight and parallel, slightly constricted at the antennae; frontal region smooth, concave, without sculpture; a sharp circular ridge between the frons and the vertex, anterior part and sides; frontal region projecting forward beyond the mandibular bases; front steep; antennal sockets about 1/3–1/2 of the head length from the anterior margin of the head; eyes present but indistinct, narrow; antennae 11 segments, the third shorter than the second; dorsal surface of the labrum not visible; mandibles short, broad at the base, with a distinct basal tubercle; postmentum short, oval; anterior margin of the pronotum rising abruptly from the posterior, gently arched part, the anterior margin angularly concave and distinctly serrate in dorsal view; femora not swollen.

/genus/eurytermes/.note: In the OCR the later part of the soldier section and the worker section are affected by two-column misalignment; only sentences that can be read continuously have been taken, and gaps are not filled in. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate: head nearly circular, narrowing in a straight line anteriorly, frons rather strongly arched, compound eyes small and strongly projecting, fontanelle distinct and far back (hence the median transverse band rather long); antennae 15-segmented (or 14), segment 3 distinctly shorter than segment 2. Soldier: head thick, rectangular, eyeless, cranial sutures invisible, fontanelle almost indistinct; labrum triangular, mandibles rather short and stout, left mandible with 1 large, strong, anteriorly directed tooth before the midpoint; antennae very fine, 14-segmented. Worker: head oval, length barely exceeding width.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head nearly circular, narrowing in a straight line anteriorly; frons rather strongly arched; compound eyes small, strongly projecting; ocelli small, about their own diameter from the compound eye, inner margin slightly raised. Fontanelle distinct, far back, hence the median transverse band rather long. Postclypeal basis rather arched, length equal to half its width or slightly less, posterior margin rather strongly arcuate. Labrum at the middle barely wider than at the base, without a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type armature, base not very developed. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 much shorter than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4 (or 14-segmented, in which case segment 3 as long as segment 2). Pronotum narrower and smaller than the head, anterior margin straight, only slightly upfolded; meso- and metanotum with only a very narrow triangular emargination; posterior angles pointed, not rounded. Forewing scale only slightly longer than the hindwing scale; wings covered with fine hairs; in the forewing the media arises directly from the wing scale (exceptionally from the radial sector), in the hindwing the media arises from the radial sector; media closer to the radial sector than to the cubitus. Cerci short, without styli. Female densely covered with glandular setae, male also but more sparsely. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Body rather slender.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head thick, rectangular; eyeless; cranial sutures invisible; fontanelle almost indistinct; postclypeus short. Labrum triangular, rather short, without a hyaline apical point. Mandibles rather short and stout; left mandible with 1 large, strong, anteriorly directed tooth before the midpoint, with a trace of a tooth on its basal side; right mandible with 1 slightly obtuse tooth. Antennae very fine, 14-segmented, segment 2 only slightly longer than segment 5. Pronotum barely reaching half the head width, with a large anterior lobe. Cerci short, without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head oval, length barely exceeding width, convex; frons concave above it.

/genus/euscaiotermes/.note: A monotypic genus (E. primus Silvestri), endemic to India; as no specimens were available, the book's account is based on Silvestri's original description and Emerson's notes. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus endemic to India. Soldier head nearly rectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly; antennae 17-segmented (segment 3 shorter than segment 2); labrum triangular with a pointed apex; mandibles robust, incurved apically, the left mandible with a notch behind the apical third, the right mandible toothless; worker antennae 19-segmented, postclypeus one-third as long as wide, mandibles of the same type as in Odontotermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head nearly rectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly; antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2; labrum triangular with a pointed apex; mandibles robust, incurved apically; left mandible with a notch behind the apical third, right mandible toothless; postmentum nearly rectangular; pronotum saddle-shaped, with an anterior notch and a slightly concave posterior margin; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; cerci 2-segmented; with styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head nearly circular, wider than long; fontanelle white, circular and large; antennae 19-segmented; postclypeus arched, one-third as long as wide; mandibles of the same type as in Odontotermes, with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth; pronotum saddle-shaped; legs as in the soldier.

/genus/eutermellus/.note: Sands 1965 provides three sections, Imago, Soldier and Worker, all entered as in the original. The left mandible index of the alate is given in the original as 96–98 (percentage scale) and that of the worker as 1.24–1.62 (ratio scale); the two differ in dimension and have been recorded as they stand without conversion.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands regarded the genus as the least specialised member of the African Paracornitermes group: the mandibles of the alate and worker, the Y-shaped fontanelle typical of some species, the trilobed anterior margin of the soldier labrum and the generally more numerous setae all point to this. It differs from Vernicositermes and Afrosubulitermes in the denser pilosity (and in size). The soldier is monomorphic, with a conical to cylindrical nasus tapering to a fine, distinctly wrinkled point, a trilobed anterior margin of the labrum, 13-segmented antennae, and a head very weakly to moderately constricted behind the antennae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is distinctly longer than the 1st marginal tooth, but the distance between them is slightly shorter than that between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index 96–98); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth is wavy and concave in front of the 3rd marginal tooth, which is nearly equilateral, and a very small subsidiary tooth is visible in the gap between it and the molar prominence. The right mandible has the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth as in the left, the 2nd marginal tooth small but distinct with a concave posterior edge; the surface of the molar plate has no basal concavity and is asymmetric, its posterior edge forming a large rounded wing and its anterior wing smaller, the ridges weak. Postclypeus convex, 1.8–2.5 times as wide as long. Fontanelle variable in shape: Y-shaped, triangular, dumbbell-shaped or nearly absent. The degree to which the compound eyes protrude from the sides of the head ranges from almost none to distinct. The cephalic pilosity is irregular in length, the conspicuous long setae often arranged in symmetrical pairs. The sides of the pronotum converge weakly towards the rounded posterior margin, the pronotum being about two-thirds as long as wide.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. Nasus conical to cylindrical, tapering to a fine point and distinctly wrinkled. Vestigial mandibles with a minute point or with no point at all; anterior margin of the labrum trilobed. Head capsule very weakly to moderately constricted behind the antennae. Antennae 13-segmented. Head and nasus covered with sparse, extremely short fine hairs, longer at the tip of the nasus; in addition, conspicuous longer setae are arranged roughly in two rows, one in front of the constriction (4–10) and one behind it (2–10).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in the alate, but with a proportionally longer apical tooth (left mandible index 1.24–1.62) and a more developed molar region.

/genus/fastigitermes/.note: The genus-level characters are taken only from Emerson's 1928 key and from the comparison in Emerson's 1960 diagnosis of Profastigitermes; the original text of Sjöstedt 1924 was not obtainable.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The anterior part of the soldier head covers the mandible bases, contrary to Basidentitermes (which does not); Emerson (1928) provisionally treated M. jucundus as a subgenus of Mirotermes and agreed with Sjöstedt in erecting Fastigitermes for it.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The swelling of the vertex above the fontanelle opening projects further forward; compared with Profastigitermes, the posterior projection of the postmentum is proportionally much larger and ends in a single, rather sharp backward-directed spine.

/genus/firmitermes/.note: The original gives the provisional assignment '?Firmitermes', and the generic characters of the alate are accordingly conditional; that premise is retained in the rewriting. The original has no genus-level worker description. Rewritten from the English generic characters, not a literal translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closely allied to Hoplognathotermes and shows no genus-level difference in head shape, but the pilosity of the face of the head, the postmentum and the fore coxae is far richer, the postmentum bears transverse wrinkles over its whole length, the labrum is broad and rounded, without lateral angles or apical projections, and the base of the mandibles is short and thick; the alate is described only on the basis of the provisionally assigned 'Eutermes' tripolitanus, whose left mandible has a third marginal tooth proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the Amitermitinae or the Termitinae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The following generic characters presuppose the provisional assignment of 'Eutermes' tripolitanus to this genus. The apical teeth of both mandibles are smaller and finer than in the workers of Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes and lie closer to the first marginal tooth; the angle between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is more acute; the actual lengths of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible are similar to those of Acutidentitermes, but the notch before the third marginal tooth is less sharp and the apical margin of the third marginal tooth is longer (that of Acutidentitermes being distinctly convex and short); the third marginal tooth is proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the Amitermitinae or the Termitinae; beneath the concave ridge between the third marginal tooth and the molar plate of the left mandible there are 2 small projections, with a concave margin between them (Acutidentitermes has only 1 projection beneath the basal molar plate); the first marginal tooth of the right mandible shows traces of a reduced accessory tooth near the angle where it meets the apical tooth; the second marginal tooth is concave on both its anterior and posterior margins, whereas that of Acutidentitermes is convex and blunt with nearly straight margins; the concavity of the upper margin of the basal plate of the right mandible is weaker than in Acutidentitermes. The fore tibiae each bear 3 spurs, the mid and hind tibiae 2 each.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The face, vertex, sides of the head and postmentum bear numerous scattered short hairs and setae, whereas in Hoplognathotermes subterraneus and Acutidentitermes osborni the face bears very few setae and the postmentum is almost hairless. On the fore coxa, the section of the flat-convex apical part shows 3–4 setae, the section of the sharply convex basal part bears a few setae and short hairs, the longitudinal ridge is rounded and blunt, and a few very short hairs are visible when the coxa is rotated. The head shape shows no genus-level difference from Hoplognathotermes, the anterior part being flatter, without marked ridges or tubercles; the fontanelle is small and indistinct. The postmentum is constricted in the middle, its sides fairly concave (slightly deeper than in Hoplognathotermes), and bears a series of indistinct transverse wrinkles over its whole length, whereas H. subterraneus has transverse wrinkles only posteriorly and the postmentum of A. osborni is globular and without transverse wrinkles. The labrum is proportionally as broad as in H. subterraneus but its margin is more rounded, without the lateral angles and apical projection of the latter or of A. osborni. The postclypeus is distinct and the suture between it and the frons is not lost. The base of the mandibles is proportionally short and thick, the outer margin fairly strongly convex, and the junction between the apical and basal parts lacks the angular notch found in Hoplognathotermes or Acutidentitermes; the apical process is shorter and thicker than in either, its outer margin more curved; the tooth base of the type specimen is broken off, so the tooth form cannot be known, but the small notch between the apical margin and the tooth of the right mandible indicates an angle close to that of H. subterraneus and unlike the more acute angle of A. osborni; the tooth-like projection at the base is indistinct or absent. The pronotum is smaller and narrower than in H. subterraneus, its anterior lobe equally large and the median concavity of its anterior margin equally small and shallow; the angle between the anterior lobe and the posterior part in lateral view is less acute than in H. subterraneus, being nearly flat-concave. The fore coxa has no projection, its longitudinal ridge being fairly rounded and blunt, not as sharp and long as in H. subterraneus; the section of the ridge is flat-convex from the trochanteral region to the middle and turns flat-concave towards the basal outer angle. The fore tibiae bear 3 apical spurs, the outer spur extremely short and visible only on careful manipulation; the mid and hind tibiae bear 2 each.

/genus/foraminitermes/.note: The generic characters given by Holmgren (1912) cover the alate only (type species F. tubifrons, Cameroon), and he stated explicitly that its systematic position could not then be determined. The original is in German, and the scanned OCR misspells umlaut letters and individual words (cines/eines, dcutlichen/deutlichen, kegclformigen/kegelförmigen, kiirzer/kürzer, etc.); quotations are reproduced verbatim with corrections noted separately. The external morphology of the soldier and worker is not described at generic level in the full text available, and Sands (1972) compared only the mandibles and gut types, so no separate soldier or worker section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head nearly circular, compound eyes strongly convex with coarse facets, ocelli close to the compound eyes, fontanelle at the apex of a short but distinct conical process (Holmgren suspected a fontanelle gland but left it in doubt because he could not confirm it); clypeal sclerite slightly shorter than half its width, slightly convex, not reaching the mandibular condyles; mandibles resembling those of Mirotermes; antennae 15 segments; anterior lobe of the pronotum large and strongly raised in a saddle shape; both wing pairs with a reduced radial vein; cerci short, without a stylus; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Sands noted that the soldier mandibles of this genus resemble those of Labritermes and that both have a transparent tip to the labrum; in the worker and alate the genus, as an adaptation to geophagy, has an elongated apical tooth and the transverse ridges of the molar plate lost.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head nearly circular; compound eyes strongly convex with coarse facets; ocelli near the compound eyes; fontanelle at the apex of a short but distinct conical process (the source leaves the presence of a fontanelle gland in doubt); clypeal sclerite slightly shorter than half its width, slightly convex, not reaching the mandibular condyles; mandibles resembling those of Mirotermes; antennae 15 segments. Anterior lobe of the pronotum large and strongly raised, saddle-shaped; forewing scale slightly longer and wider than the hindwing scale; wing membrane transparent, slightly iridescent and very finely punctate; both wing pairs with a reduced radial vein; cerci short; no stylus; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier labrum with two lateral pointed corners and a distinctly projecting median lobe, on which basis it is closely related to Basidentitermes, Proboscitermes, Orthotermes, Profastigitermes and Fastigitermes; it is a small, peculiar group split off near Basidentitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head subquadrate in dorsal view, the sides almost straight or slightly convex, frons and vertex flatter than in related groups; frontal gland in a small depression, with two flat longitudinal ridges on each side in front of the opening; anterior margin of labrum with two lateral pointed corners and a distinctly projecting median lobe; mandibles of the biting type, relatively straight and slender, apex not hooked; base of left mandible with a small sharp tooth, followed by a deep, small angular bend ending in a spine-like projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles resembling those of the more primitive groups near Basidentitermes; apical tooth larger than the first marginal tooth; right mandible with a distinct second marginal tooth.

/genus/fulleritermes/.note: The generic diagnosis of Sands 1965 has only two sections, Imago and Soldier, and no worker is described at genus level, so no Worker section is given. The original lists four species, contractus, coatoni, mallyi and tenebricus, and notes that the genus occupies savanna and drier vegetation zones.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Coaton 1962 separated the genus from Coarctotermes on the incision of the cutting edge of the alate left mandible in front of the 3rd marginal tooth; the same feature occurs in Grallatotermes and Leptomyxotermes, but the compound eyes and ocelli of those two genera are much larger, and Grallatotermes has 13–14 ridges on the right molar plate. The molar plate of this genus has 7–9 ridges and a very weak to very strong concavity on the anterior edge near the base, the 1st molar ridge forming a coarse tooth. The soldier is monomorphic or dimorphic, the nasus cylindrical or conical, the head ranging from almost unconstricted to strongly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior lobe usually more than a quarter wider than the anterior part, antennae 12–13-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is as long as the 1st marginal tooth, and the distance from the apical tooth to the 1st marginal tooth is more than one-third of the distance between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index 36–43); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth bears an incision that delimits the 3rd marginal tooth. The right mandible has the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth nearly equal in length, the 1st marginal tooth bearing a small subsidiary tooth at its basal junction near the apical tooth, and the relative lengths of the cutting edges of the 1st and 2nd marginal teeth are variable; the surface of the molar plate has a very weak to very strong concavity on the anterior edge near the base, the posterior edge extending into a rounded wing, the 1st molar ridge forming a coarse tooth, the remaining 7–9 diminishing towards the base. Fontanelle slit-like, distinctly forked anteriorly, usually paler than the head.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic or dimorphic. Nasus cylindrical or conical. Vestigial mandibles with a small to medium-sized point. Head capsule from almost unconstricted to strongly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior lobe usually more than a quarter wider than the anterior part. Antennae 12–13-segmented.

/genus/furculitermes/.note: Emerson 1960 describes the alate, soldier and worker of this genus; only genus-level diagnostic characters are taken here, species-level measurements and pilosity being omitted.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, the surface smooth, with fine sculpturing only around the fontanelle; fontanelle elongate, set in a short, narrow depression on the head surface; vertex gently and evenly convex between the ocelli; compound eyes rather flat, of medium size, their distance from the lower margin of the head slightly less than one third of their diameter.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Labrum large, its two lateral lobes forked and rather narrow, the apex rounded or slightly truncate, projecting beyond the mandibular marginal teeth when extended; the anterior margin of the labrum is deeply concave — the genus name is taken from the forked labrum.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical mandibular teeth are relatively large; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is lost; among related genera this pattern is similar only in Euchilotermes, Ophiotermes, Tuberculitermes and Spinitermes.

/genus/gastrotermes/.note: The generic name is formed from Greek gaster (belly, stomach) and termes, referring to its gut characters. The source does not describe the soldier or alate, so the corresponding sections are left empty.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mixed segment is absent, P1 is very short, and the EVS is large and trilobed, on which basis the genus is placed in the Apicotermes group. It differs from the other genera of the Labidotermes subgroup in that the inner wall of the EVS bears small erect spines and the opening of P3a is lined with stout spines. The alate is unknown; the soldier is unknown (the source records Soldier. Unknown, but may exist).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head, pronotum and abdomen are densely covered with several hundred long to very long hairs.

/genus/genuotermes/.note: The genus-level description covers soldier, worker, alate and digestive tract. Rocha (2013) placed this genus in Termitinae, whereas the batch labels it as Syntermitinae; the two are inconsistent and must be confirmed before merging into the database.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandibles elongate, bent at the proximal 1/3, the inner margin of the distal 2/3 a serrate blade with a basal projecting tooth, molar plate and molar prominence visible at the base; head capsule in dorsal view subrectangular, with a characteristic frontal projection, the opening of the frontal gland at the tip of the head projection, facing forward. Alate compound eyes hemispherical, fontanelle a small slit.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles elongate, bent at the proximal 1/3; inner margin of the distal 2/3 a serrate blade, with a conspicuous projecting tooth at the base; molar plate and molar prominence visible at the base. Head capsule in dorsal view subrectangular, with a characteristic frontal projection (best seen in lateral view); opening of the frontal gland at the tip of the head projection, facing forward. Labrum subrectangular; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule round in dorsal view; fontanelle indistinct; antennae 14–15-segmented; apical tooth of mandibles far more developed than the marginal teeth, the apices of the marginal teeth discernible. Digestive tract: P1 inflated, on the left side of the body, its terminal section forming an elongate loop that reaches the dorsal region and then descends to join P3; gizzard with 24 visible folds in the columnar band (6 first-order, 6 second-order, 12 third-order), the first-order folds with spinous ornamentation; enteric valve composed of three equidistant longitudinal cushions, covered with stout upright spines in a brush-like arrangement.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes hemispherical, elliptical in lateral view, approaching but not touching the ventral margin of the head or the ocelli; fontanelle indistinct, appearing as a small slit on the dorsal surface of the head; pronotum subtrapezoidal, anterolateral corners rounded; posterior margin of mesonotum deeply concave and pointed, that of metanotum shallower and rounded; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/glossotermes/.note: The original is the original description based on a single holotype soldier and records the alate explicitly as unknown, so no alate or worker sections are given. It was then placed in the Rhinotermitidae and is now assigned to the Serritermitidae; the change of classification does not affect the morphological description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original considers this genus closest to Psammotermes (then placed in the Rhinotermitidae), though the relationship is rather distant; when the genus was established only the soldier was known, the alate being unknown. The soldier is characterised by the combination of a nearly square, slightly flattened head, a distinct eye spot behind each antennal socket, an extremely broad labrum, mandibles only slightly hooked, and a large groove at the base of the left mandible that receives the tooth of the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head nearly square and slightly flattened, the sides nearly parallel and slightly convex, reddish brownish yellow; a distinct eye spot behind each antennal socket, smaller than the socket, the ommatidia almost indiscernible; two pale spots above the eye, possibly vestigial ocelli; antennae 13 segments, the terminal segment distinctly narrower than the preceding one, segment 3 about equal to segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 3; postclypeus distinct, about 3 times as wide as long; labrum extremely broad, rounded at the sides, with a thin hyaline margin at the apex; mandibles broad at the base, tapering towards the apex and only slightly hooked, with a notch on the outer margin of each at about 2/9 of its length, dividing it into a basal and an apical part; right mandible with a tooth-like process on the inner margin at 1/3 of the length from the base; left mandible finely serrate on the inner margin behind the apex, with a large groove at the base that receives the tooth of the right mandible; pronotum gently arched, distinctly notched at the anterior margin; tibial apical spurs 2:2:2 on all legs. Measurements of the holotype soldier (mm): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 1.56, head height 0.82, head width 1.10, postclypeus length 0.19 and width 0.57, labrum width 0.57, left mandible length 1.09, pronotum width 0.78, hind tibia length 1.09.

/genus/gnathamitermes/.note: Based only on the soldier diagnostic couplet in the North American generic key of De Luna et al. 2023 (thin), not a complete set of generic characters.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles straight, curved only at the apex, as long as or longer than the head; head width less than 1.4 mm, mandibles relatively narrow, usually longer than head width; mandible bases arising near the anterolateral corners of the head, inner margin smooth.

/genus/grallatotermes/.note: The generic diagnosis of Sands 1965 contains two sections, Imago and Soldier, and no worker is described at genus level, so no Worker section is given. The original places the genus together with Hospitalitermes in a group with the head capsule constricted behind the antennae, and notes that its alate mandibles are unique among the African species. The key of Holmgren 1912 gives a separate description of the soldier (nasus short and very broadly conical, antennae 13-segmented, head not dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennae), which differs in degree from Sands's “nasus thick but only weakly conical, head slightly constricted”; the account above follows the generic diagnosis of Sands.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
