sections.text: Sands regarded its alate mandibles as a unique combination among the African species: the cutting edge of the left mandible has a deep incision between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth, and the right molar plate has 13–14 ridges with no obvious irregularity in surface outline. The incision is shared with Fulleritermes and Leptomyxotermes, but this genus has the most molar ridges (Fulleritermes 7–9, with a concavity on the anterior edge of the molar plate near the base; Leptomyxotermes 6–7, with very large compound eyes and ocelli). The soldier is monomorphic, the nasus thick but only weakly conical, sharply tapering at the tip, the head slightly constricted behind the antennae, and the setae confined to 4 at the tip of the nasus and paired hairs on the postclypeus and vertex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is slightly shorter than the 1st marginal tooth, the distance between them being about one-quarter of that between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index about 25); the 2nd marginal tooth is delimited by a deep incision in front of the 3rd marginal tooth, and the small subsidiary tooth connecting the 3rd marginal tooth with the molar prominence lies, seen from above, behind the gap between the two. In the right mandible the apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth are nearly equal in length, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth is shorter than that of the 2nd and does not overlap the anterior edge of the 2nd marginal tooth (the surface overlap being buried in a smooth, shining fused surface); the outline of the molar plate in surface view shows no obvious irregularity, with 13–14 ridges diminishing posteriorly. Postclypeus short, slightly convex, about one-third as long as wide. Fontanelle pale, slightly T-shaped. Pronotum with an almost non-convex anterior margin. Cephalic pilosity sparse, fine and uniform, with only a few more conspicuous setae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. Nasus thick but only weakly conical, sharply tapering at the tip. Vestigial mandibles with a point. Head capsule slightly constricted behind the antennae; setae only 4 at the tip of the nasus, plus those arranged in pairs on the postclypeus and the two sides of the vertex.

/genus/grigiotermes/.note: Soldierless. Genus characters mainly from the worker gut (P1 and enteric valve), with an additional alate description; the diagnosis also gives the comparison with Patawatermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Worker large (head width over 0.9 mm), foregut P1 extremely broad, the food bolus following a visible serpentine path within it, on which basis it is distinguished from the other South American soldierless genera. Closely related to Patawatermes, but the enteric valve has 6 spiny sclerotised plates.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale yellow, rounded, covered with a variable number of small hairs and 50–100 long setae; fontanelle small, almost invisible; fore tibia slender; the distal half of the abdomen subconical, the gut elongate. Enteric valve within a short extension of the paunch, armature of 6 spiny sclerotised plates; the anterior part of the enteric valve made up of 6 oval pads, each with about 100 scale-like lobules. Midgut junction forming a small spherical knob over the hindgut, slightly prolonged into a short distinct mixed segment; foregut P1 extremely broad.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Sclerotised parts dark brown, covered with thousands of small hairs; head with about 100 scattered long setae; compound eyes and ocelli large; fontanelle small to medium, at the level of the compound eyes; pronotum elongate, covered with dozens of long setae; posterior margins of the meso- and metanota slightly concave, the corners strongly rounded.

/genus/heimitermes/.note: The original explicitly states that the alate is unknown; for the worker only the mandibles and the fore coxa are described at genus level, the rest is reproduced as in the original, without supplementation from related genera (Coxotermes, Duplidentitermes).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown. Soldier head thick and massive, the sides straight, parallel or flatly convex, with a distinct and rather deep pit between the base of the postclypeus and the opening of the frontal gland; postmentum widest behind the bases of the mandibles, constricted posteriorly; mandibles short and stout, the apices slightly hooked, each mandible with 1 small tooth slightly in front of the midpoint; lateral and posterior margins of the pronotum flared, the anterior margin broad and evenly slightly convex, without a median notch; the sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa bears a long and conspicuous nipple-like process; apical spur formula 2:2:2, the outer upper surface of the fore tibia with a white circular spot. Worker with a large mandibular apical tooth, a deep incision between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth on the left mandible, and a small second marginal tooth on the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head thick and massive, with scattered setae, denser on the frons and the sides, a few short hairs near the fontanelle; sides straight, parallel or flatly convex; between the base of the postclypeus and the opening of the frontal gland there is a distinct and rather deep pit; the side of the head is curved in the frontal gland region and slightly bulbously swollen near the vertex. Postmentum widest behind the bases of the mandibles, the sides rounded at the widest point, becoming straight and constricted posteriorly, with a small constriction before the concave posterior margin; the lateral sutures of the postmentum are visible along the whole length except anteriorly. Postclypeus distinct, broadly hexagonal, with a clear suture separating it from the front of the head. Labrum with a white apical area, the sides of the base nearly parallel, usually curved downwards, distinctly shorter than the postclypeus, about 1/3 as wide as the postclypeus. Mandibles short and stout, the apices slightly hooked; each mandible with 1 small tooth slightly in front of the midpoint, and another small tooth at the end of the stout base projecting on the ventral surface, this tooth not continuous with the cutting edge from the apical tooth to the middle tooth but situated in front of the small molar plate, forming a somewhat independent blunt cutting edge. Lateral and posterior margins of the pronotum slightly flared, the anterior margin broad and evenly slightly convex, without a distinct notch or incision, the lateral margins rounded, the middle of the posterior margin concave and depressed. On the sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa there is a very long and conspicuous nipple-like process with a rounded apex; this process is stouter and shorter than in Coxotermes, with a more concave basal face. The middle of the fore femur is as thick as in Coxotermes. Apical spur formula 2:2:2; the outer upper surface of each fore tibia bears a white circular spot, possibly the base of a reduced outer apical spur.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The principal generic characters of the mandibles are: the apical tooth is very large relative to the first marginal tooth; there is a distinct incision between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth on the left mandible; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is small. The sharp longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa bears a conspicuous triangular process, but not so tooth-like as in the soldier.

/genus/heterotermes/.note: The only copy of this paper available locally is the publisher's JATS full-text XML (Europe PMC PMC3264403), with no print PDF, so the locator uses section names rather than page numbers; the jsonl gives the author order as Roisin & Bourguignon, which differs from the order of the contrib elements in the XML (Bourguignon first); the XML is followed here. The worker caste is not described in the original, so no worker section is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus is distinguished from other members of the Rhinotermitinae by the following combination: in the soldier the head is long and narrow, rectangular, the mandibles sabre-shaped with slightly curved apices, the left mandible with one tooth and several serrations at the base and the right mandible without teeth or serrations at the base; in the alate the head is almost oval, the anterior part narrower than the posterior, the ocelli situated at the front of the head, before the compound eyes, the antennae usually 15–19 segments, and the pronotum elongate and narrower than the head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head almost oval, the anterior part narrower than the posterior; fontanelle small, situated in the middle of the head; compound eyes small and flat; ocelli situated at the front of the head, before the eyes; antennae usually 15–19 segments; pronotum elongate and narrower than the head. Species level (H. paradoxus): head slightly elongate, bearing several hundred hairs; pronotum elongate and of medium width; antennae usually 18 segments (occasionally 17); compound eyes flat, with small ocelli in front of the eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and narrow, rectangular; fontanelle small, circular, situated anteriorly; labrum short to medium, about half the length of the mandibles; mandibles sabre-shaped with slightly curved apices; left mandible with one tooth and several serrations at the base; right mandible without teeth or serrations at the base; antennae 13–18 segments. Species level (H. vagus): soldier small, the head elongate with a distinct swelling anteriorly and densely covered with short hairs; labrum elongate with a sharp apex; antennae usually 13 segments; pronotum short and narrow, bearing about 50 hairs; postmentum slightly narrow and hairless; mandibular apices slightly curved.

/genus/hirsutitermes/.note: The genus-level Diagnosis lists only the three characters of the enteric valve and digestive tract; the body-wall characters are given in the genus-level Description. No soldier section (soldierless).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The posterior margin of the enteric valve armature bears several hundred fine spines; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is tubular, trilobed and long; the mesenteric tongue is long but not inflated. It is closest to Longustitermes: the spines of this genus are longer and finer than in that genus, the anterior portion of the cushions pyriform (in the latter more rounded; the original sentence reads "the anterior portion of the cushions is more rounded in the latter than pyriform in the former"); Longustitermes is smaller, with a trilobed rather than tubular EVS.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head capsule forms a very gentle curve in lateral view. Fontanelle distinct, heart-shaped, situated near the imaginary line of the posterior margins of the compound eyes, behind the oval spot (= the median labral muscle). Above the antennal sockets there are two distinct oval spots. Antennae 12-segmented, segment formula 2>3<4≈5. The median suture of the pronotum is distinct, the anterior margin raised.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (body and head size from medium to large). Head capsule pale yellow, densely covered with long hairs and sparse, somewhat larger setae, flat dorsally in lateral view. Antennal segments translucent white; antennae 14-segmented, segment formula 2>3=4<5. Fontanelle circular, distinct but with indistinct margins; postclypeus moderately inflated. Pronotum with very long setae, especially numerous in the middle of the anterior and posterior lobes; the surfaces of the tergites and sternites with short hairs, the posterior margins with long setae. Fore coxa and fore femur with medium-sized spines; fore tibia moderately inflated, densely covered with spines and setae of various sizes. The apical tooth of the left mandible is more projecting than M1+2; the two margins of M3 form an obtuse angle, the apex slightly rounded and directed forwards; the molar process distinct, not concealed by the molar prominence; molar prominence well developed. The apical tooth of the right mandible is far more projecting than M1, M1 small and less projecting than M2, the margin of M2 curved; the molar plate concave, with a few ridges. Digestive tract: mesenteric tongue long but not inflated; EVS rather long and tubular, often with three small but distinct lobes; in dorsal view the junction of P3-a and the seating is visible; the armature has several hundred fine sclerotised spines, distributed from the fourth part of the distal end of the enteric valve. Measurements: species-level (Table 2).

/genus/hirtitermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 1st subgenus, with only Eutermes (Hirtitermes) hirtiventris Holmgren (Sarawak). In the key the alate appears only as “(?Hirtitermes n. subg.)”, appended after the Eutermes s. str. entry, the author himself being in doubt, so no alate section is given; the original text gives no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier of the Constrictus group, with a single soldier morph: nasus large, thick, conical, the depression at the nasus base large; the base of the left mandible with two distinct teeth; pilosity stiff and brown; antennal segments elongate. The contrast with Eutermes s. str. lies precisely here — the latter has the depression at the nasus base small or absent, the mandible base never toothed, the pilosity not stiff, and the antennal segments for the most part normal.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph. Nasus large, thick, conical; the depression at the nasus base conspicuous, the original text noting specifically, among the characters of the group, that the depression is large in this genus; the base of the left mandible with two distinct teeth; head and nasus covered with stiff brown hairs; antennal segments long.

/genus/hodotermes/.note: The generic description follows Sjöstedt 1900 (at that time Hodotermes was a broad genus, including the present Stolotermes and Porotermes as subgenera). Biology after Haviland and Hachmann: living in soil, not shunning light, active outdoors in daylight, often migrating in columns, cutting grass blades into fragments and dragging them into underground passages. Distribution mainly African, also recorded from the East Indies, southern Persia and the Nicobar Islands.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier and worker both with distinct black compound eyes (rare among termites and a striking hallmark of the genus); head capsule without a fontanelle pore. Alate antennae 23–30-segmented, ocelli reduced to a yellow spot beside the eye, pronotum small and nearly heart-shaped, the pulvillus (Haftlappen) absent.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head large and round, the epistome not swollen, compound eyes flattened, not strongly protruding, ocelli represented only by a yellow spot beside the eye; antennae 23–30-segmented, the basal segments very small and spherical, becoming progressively longer outwards; no fontanelle pit; pronotum not rectangular, slightly heart-shaped, saddle-shaped, the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum concave but not forming two sharp projections; the costal area of the forewing with veins, the subcosta crossing the costal area in several branches, the media and submedia of the forewing arising separately from the base of the scale; wing membrane traversed by numerous fine irregular branches; first tarsomere longer than the next two combined; cerci (anal appendages) present in both sexes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Distinct black compound eyes always present. Head large, somewhat round, square or short rectangular, pale to dark yellow-red, without a fontanelle cavity; mandibles shorter than the head, very robust, the inner margin always with distinct teeth (left mandible with more teeth than the right), the apices incurved; labrum short and broad; antennae 27–30-segmented (Wasmann recorded 21–27 segments); pronotum slightly heart-shaped (not transversely rectangular), saddle-shaped, the anterior angles bent downwards, concave and slightly projecting; the meso- and metathorax as wide as the pronotum, rather flat, rectangular, the lateral margins rounded, thin and upturned, wider than the abdomen; the apical tarsomere as long as the remaining segments combined; head and body glossy as if lacquered.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Distinct black compound eyes always present. Head yellow to yellow-red, round; epistome narrow; the first two mandibular teeth small and equal; antennae 24–32-segmented; thorax much narrower than head and abdomen, clearly differentiated from the abdominal segments; the meso- and metathorax widening posteriorly; the apical tarsomere as long as the remaining segments combined.

/genus/homallotermes/.note: Soldier based solely on the Oriental Region generic key of the Pericapritermes group (1 couplet + 1 lead feature); the original description by John (1925) was not obtained in full, hence only a soldier section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the Oriental Region key to soldiers of the Pericapritermes group, this genus stands alone as a couplet (couplet 4) defined by the weakly curved middle of the mandibles; its alternative is “antennae 14-segmented, mandibles stout, middle moderately to strongly curved”, i.e. Mirocapritermes and the following genera.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Antennae 13-segmented; mandibles slender and weak, weakly curved at the middle. Middle of the left mandible moderately twisted, apex acute (or beak-like, hook-like) — this is a lead feature on the key path.

/genus/hoplognathotermes/.note: The alate is explicitly recorded as unknown in the original. Rewritten from the English genus diagnosis, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown. Soldier: head large, sides straight and parallel; frontal gland area flat or slightly concave in section; head surface with only very few short setae near the frontal gland opening, postmentum nearly bare; each mandible with 1 conspicuous, anteriorly directed large marginal tooth situated before the midpoint, the left tooth with a long basal cutting edge; legs and fore coxae longer than in Duplidentitermes; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, middle tibia without dark outer spine.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface with only very few, rather short scattered setae near the frontal gland opening; fore coxa without strong spines, with only a few fine setae not forming a special arrangement; first 4 abdominal tergites with short hairs or setae, posterior tergites and sternites with additional short hairs. Head large, sides straight and parallel; frontal gland area flat or slightly concave in section. Postmentum large, moderately constricted, slightly convex in section. Antennae 15-segmented. Postclypeus distinct, slightly arched; labrum with rounded lateral margins, the sides straight and parallel behind the lateral angles, the apex rounded-obtuse. Each mandible with 1 conspicuous, large, anteriorly directed marginal tooth situated before the midpoint; left tooth with a long basal cutting edge (unlike Firmitermes). Pronotum with a larger anterior lobe, the median notch of the anterior margin shallow and indistinct. Legs longer than in Duplidentitermes; fore coxa also longer, simple, the longitudinal ridge obtuse and unspecialised, straight or flatly convex in section, extending about 1/3–1/2 from the apex towards the base, convex between ridge and inner margin. Femora slender, nearly equally thick at the middle. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, middle tibia without dark outer spine.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apical teeth of both mandibles only slightly larger than the first marginal tooth; cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible long and less undulating (straighter than in Duplidentitermes and other closely related genera of the subfamily); a distinct notch between the first and second marginal teeth and the third marginal tooth; compared with Acutidentitermes, the first marginal teeth of both mandibles less anteriorly directed, the angle between apical tooth and first marginal tooth more obtuse, the cutting edges of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible proportionally slightly shorter.

/genus/hoplotermes/.note: Based only on the soldier diagnostic couplet in the North American generic key of De Luna et al. 2023 (thin), not a complete set of generic characters.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head width greater than 1.8 mm; mandibles stout, shorter than head width; mandible bases arising near the anterolateral corners of the head, inner margin smooth.

/genus/humutermes/.note: The only genus-level measurement is the worker head width 0.49–0.62 mm; the other measurements are species-level. No soldier section (soldierless). Along with Patawatermes and Rubeotermes, this genus comes from the same paper, Bourguignon & Roisin (2016); the three sources are merged into a single record.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mixed segment of the worker is elongate, its inner end inflated into a white spherical mesenteric diverticulum; this character is shared with Anoplotermes sensu stricto and distinguishes the genus from the remaining South American soldierless termite genera. The main difference from Anoplotermes s.s. lies in the enteric valve: the enteric valve of this genus consists of 6 pads, each with 10–20 long spines extending into the paunch (P3); the fontanelle of the alate is larger and more elongate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes and ocelli medium-sized. Fontanelle medium-sized, appearing as an elongate white spot between the two eyes. Pronotum semicircular in dorsal view, with several hundred small setae and several tens of long setae. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum slightly concave, the angles rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Very small to small, head width 0.49–0.62 mm (genus-level measurement). Head capsule white, covered with more than 100 small setae. Fontanelle almost invisible. Fore tibia inflated at the middle. Digestive tract very similar to that of Anoplotermes sensu stricto: the midgut and proctodeum overlap, forming a distinct long mixed segment whose mesenteric part is inflated at its inner end into a white spherical diverticulum. The enteric valve is inserted into the extension of the paunch and consists of 6 sclerotised pads with a well-developed sclerotised armature.

/genus/hydrecotermes/.note: The genus is named after the Hydreco station in French Guiana. The source describes both the worker and the alate; there is no soldier, so no soldier section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Morphologically closest to Grigiotermes and Patawatermes but distinguished from them by the smaller worker and the unclerotised armature of the enteric valve; it differs from other Neotropical soldierless termites in the inflated P1, the short stout abdomen, and the oval, spineless enteric valve cushions.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium-sized, head width 0.6–0.8 mm; gut slightly inflated in the abdomen; head pale yellow and circular, with 50–200 setae but no microtrichia; enteric valve cushions oval, without spines or sclerotised armature.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Sclerotised body parts dark brown, densely covered with several thousand microtrichia; head with only a few long setae; compound eyes and ocelli large; fontanelle fairly large, at the level of the posterior margin of the compound eyes, appearing as a hairless spot.

/genus/hyleotermes/.note: The original transfers Nasutitermes brevipilus to this genus and redescribes it; the generic diagnosis and the descriptions of all castes are on p. 78, the comparative discussion on p. 79.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule oval in dorsal view, with a long cylindrical nasus, without a constriction, without long setae, covered with microscopic hairs; worker slightly dimorphic, the mixed segment very short; enteric valve with 6 pads of unequal size, each pad bearing from a few to several dozen narrow spines set on conical bases. In its small size, pale yellow colour and cylindrical nasus the soldier is closest to Ereymatermes and Subulitermes; among the three, only H. brevipilus, S. constricticeps and S. microsoma have a head capsule without long setae, and the latter two are distinctly smaller (head width about 0.6 mm). The worker enteric valve is diagnostic and differs from that of Ereymatermes and Subulitermes. Distinguished from Nasutitermes s. str.: in the latter the enteric valve armature bears pointed scales trailing posteriorly into scale rows, the molar plate is narrow and straight with well-developed ridges, the apical teeth of the mandibles are short with larger marginal teeth, the mixed segment is very long, and the enteric valve is unsclerotised and bears only minute spines; in addition, female workers of Nasutitermes s. str. are distinctly larger than males.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large, slightly oval; ocelli large, elliptical, about as large as the antennal sockets; postclypeus slightly arched in lateral view, its median line distinct and slightly concave, anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin convex; fontanelle conspicuous, slit-like; frontal suture indistinct; antennae 15-segmented; mandibular tooth pattern similar to that of worker type 2; pronotum trapezoidal in dorsal view, anterior and posterior margins nearly straight; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum deeply and broadly concave, posterolateral corners rounded; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head capsule longer than wide in dorsal view, without a constriction; nasus slender, nearly cylindrical; head capsule, legs and thoracic sclerites densely covered with short, relatively coarse hairs; mandibles with a small but distinct 'point'; antennae 12-segmented; postclypeus not convex in lateral view; labrum wider than long, anterior margin rounded, lateral margins parallel, anterior corners rounded; anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum equally developed, enclosing an obtuse angle; fore coxa conical, without a ridge, its anterior surface without a projection; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the two types similar in size. In type 1 the gap between M3 and the molar region swelling of the left mandible is narrow, the head capsule darker and nearly trapezoidal, the pronotum narrower and the anterior lobe larger than the posterior lobe; in type 2 the gap is wide, the head capsule slightly paler with more convex sides, the pronotum wider with the anterior and posterior lobes nearly equal. In both types the fontanelle lies in the posterior half of the head capsule, is pale and slightly concave in lateral view; postclypeus not inflated; antennae 13-segmented; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. In both types the apical tooth of the left mandible is larger than M1, the posterior margin of the apical tooth slightly concave and forming an acute angle with the anterior margin of M1, the posterior margin of M1 undulating; M3 short but distinct, with a V-shaped gap to the molar region swelling in type 1 and a wide gap in type 2; M4 short, hidden beneath the molar region swelling; molar region swelling concave, with indistinct ridges. Apical tooth of the right mandible larger than M1, M3 reduced with a rounded tip, the posterior margin of M3 concave, the molar plate concave with indistinct ridges, the basal notch distinct but narrower in type 2.

/genus/ibitermes/.note: Soldier based on the 2022/2012 generic characters; worker based on the description of the enteric valve and midgut tongue; for the alate only the left mandible index is known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier postclypeus markedly inflated (except I. tellustris), mandibles without marginal teeth; body relatively large, mandibles straight and large (in Embiratermes the marginal teeth are well developed, in this genus entirely absent). Worker midgut tongue long and twisted, enteric valve section dorsal. Left mandible index 0.9.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Postclypeus markedly inflated (except I. tellustris); mandibles without marginal teeth. Body relatively large, mandibles straight and large.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Midgut tongue long and twisted; enteric valve section dorsal. Left mandible index 0.9.

/genus/indocapritermes/.note: Soldier based on the Oriental Region generic key of the Pericapritermes group (couplets 9–10 and lead features).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Oriental Region key, couplets 9–10: head moderately hairy, frons sloping forward → anterolateral corners of labrum minute and slender, base narrow, anterior lobe of pronotum slightly convex with a weak notch, antennae 14-segmented. Distinguished from Rinacapritermes by the anterolateral corners of the labrum long and stout with a broad base, the anterior lobe of the pronotum strongly convex and without a notch, and antennae 15-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head moderately hairy, frons distinctly sloping forward; anterolateral corners of labrum minute, slender, base narrow; anterior lobe of pronotum slightly convex with a weak notch; antennae 14-segmented. Middle of left mandible strongly twisted, apex blunt.

/genus/inquilinitermes/.note: Inquiline relationships: I. inquilinus shares nests with C. cavifrons, and two other species share nests with C. cyphergaster (Constantino 1999); the original description of Mathews 1977 could not be read, so the full set of genus-level characters is not given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The frontal projection of the soldier is rounded and blunt, the tibial spur formula is 2:2:2, and the genus is found only in nests of Constrictotermes; in Termes the frontal projection is conical and the tibial spur formula is 3:3:2.

/genus/isognathotermes/.note: Adapted from the English genus-level diagnosis and redescription; measurements and details of enteric valve typology omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Belonging to Cubitermitinae; workers, soldiers and alates all possess a mixed segment between the midgut and the hindgut, 4 Malpighian tubules fused at their bases, and a caecum at the second hindgut pouch (P3). The worker enteric valve (EVA) is the most reliable diagnostic character of the genus, comprising the fungifaber type, the finitimus type and an intermediate type between them: in the former the odd-numbered enteric valve pads narrow at the downstream end and bear ridges, the ridges carrying long curved/hooked setae; in the latter the odd-numbered pads are more robust, swollen into a bulb at the downstream end and densely covered with short, stiff, straight setae, the transition between the two being abrupt. Ventral surface of the worker fore coxa ridged, the ridge with 2–7 spines, fore trochanter with 3–8 spines. Soldier head distinctly longer than wide (head length 2.18–3.77 mm, length/width ratio 1.22–1.67), mandibles sickle-shaped and shorter than the head length (0.66–0.92), antennae 14–15-segmented. Alate darkly coloured (C6–C8), antennae 16-segmented, fontanelle small, tibial spur formula 3:2:2 with 2 additional proximal spines on the mid tibia.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule strongly sclerotised, dark (C6–C8, fading to C4 in old specimens); fontanelle concolorous or nearly concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus C5–C7, concolorous with the head capsule or 1–2 grades paler; antennae C4–C6, proximal and distal segments not markedly different. Head large; fontanelle generally a small round or elongate spot. Compound eyes round to short oval (major/minor diameter 1.00–1.25); ocelli round to oval (1.00–1.80). Antennae 16-segmented (only 1 of 278 alates with 17 segments); queens and kings often missing 1–4 segments through wear. Labrum bell-shaped, generally wider than long. Apical tooth of the left mandible longer than the first marginal tooth, marginal teeth 3, the second expressed only as an undulation of the cutting margin between the first and third (lost after wear); dorsal surface of the molar prominence rounded, ending posteriorly in a small pointed projection. Marginal teeth of the right mandible 2, the first sharp when fresh, the second smaller with a blunt apex; molar tooth with a rounded, lip-like ventral projection, heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to slightly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and slightly raised. Ventral surface of the fore coxa ridged. Wings: R1 completely fused with the costal margin and sclerotised; Rs simple and sclerotised; M and Cu unsclerotised or weakly sclerotised, branching into 2–6 and 7–15 branches respectively. Dorsal surface of the abdomen with 10 complete, undivided tergites visible; males with 8 complete sternites visible, females with 6, followed by the subgenital plate and differentiated lateral plates. Hindgut with a mixed segment and a caecum, but the caecum relatively small.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule generally Cd4–Cd6, becoming paler or darker in old specimens (Cf5–Cf7); frontal region often 1–2 grades darker than the posterior part, sometimes giving a distinctly bicoloured head; postmentum concolorous with the head or slightly darker; antennae and labrum 1 grade paler than the head capsule; mandibles dark (C7–C8), with an abruptly paler ring at the base, mostly of the same colour as the frontal region; thorax and legs paler than the head capsule (C3–C5). Head capsule distinctly sclerotised, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides mostly subparallel, narrowing to varying degrees at the posterior 1/3–1/4, the sides slightly convex without obvious narrowing in incipient-colony individuals; posterior margin variable, regularly rounded, or with a short straight/concave section in the middle, or composed of three short straight/concave sections. Upper margin always more or less concave in profile; frons with or without a small frontal projection covering the fontanelle. Posterior half of the postmentum always narrowing to varying degrees in ventral view, the sides of the anterior half ranging from smoothly rounded to angular ear-like lobes. Antennae generally 15-segmented (14.5 segments in about 9%, 14 in about 6%, occasionally 13 in incipient-colony individuals). Labrum always deeply cleft, generally wider than long, the sides harp-shaped in 82% of individuals (convex in 11%, straight in 7%), the lobes subtruncate, finely white or translucent at the apex; anterior margin concave. Mandibles sickle-shaped to subapically hooked, inner margin smooth, each side with 1 distinct but usually very small marginal tooth near the molar tooth; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head, surface smooth and shining; right mandible generally slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, narrower than the head width, anterior and posterior margins generally entire. Ventral surface of the fore coxa ridged. Enteric valve situated in the left posterior part of the abdomen, mostly with triradiate symmetry; odd-numbered enteric valve pads on average 16% longer than the even-numbered ones, generally without ridges or with weak ridges; the pilosity at this site abruptly denser in finitimus-type individuals; secondary enteric valve pads broad at the upstream end and distinctly narrowing downstream.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3), turning grey in old specimens; basal antennal segments pale (C2–C3), distal segments always 1–2 grades darker (C4–C5); thorax and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to reddish brown owing to gut contents. Head capsule weakly sclerotised (except the mandibles); antennae 15-segmented, rarely 14.5 or 14, occasionally 13 in incipient-colony individuals; labrum bell-shaped, generally wider than long. Apical tooth of the left mandible well developed, sharp when fresh; marginal teeth 3, the first well developed, the second weak (visible only as an undulating cutting margin, lost after wear), the third with a blunt apex; dorsal surface of the molar prominence rounded, with a small pointed projection posteriorly. Marginal teeth of the right mandible 2, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller with a blunt apex; molar tooth with a rounded, lip-like ventral projection, heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped. Ventral surface of the fore coxa with a sharp ridge, the ridge with 3–7 spines (only 2 spines in 2 of 400 samples), ventral surface with 0–4 spines; fore trochanter with 5–7 spines; apical tibial spurs of the fore, mid and hind legs 3:2:2, proximal spurs 0:2:0. Enteric valve situated in the left posterior part of the abdomen, always with triradiate symmetry; of the fungifaber type, finitimus type or intermediate type depending on the species (muneris type in I. acristatus); odd-numbered enteric valve pads with generally 13–38 supporting setae on each side; secondary enteric valve pads broad at the upstream end and distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum relatively small, situated near the middle of the abdomen, often with 2–3 lobules, or finger-shaped with the apex sometimes thickened.

/genus/jugositermes/.note: Emerson 1928 established the genus with Jugositermes tuberculatus as type species, describing only the soldier at the time; the alate and the worker were not described; the generic characters are a comparative diagnosis against its close relatives Apicotermes and Allognathotermes, and Emerson pointed out that it differs markedly from all genera then known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier frons steeply inclined (about 45°), with two distinct ridges above the antennal bases, the antennal bases set at one end of a groove; left mandible with a small tooth; both mandibles short and very broad, distinctly broader than in the closely related Apicotermes and Allognathotermes; frontal gland opening present but only dot-like and inconspicuous; labrum extremely small; sides of the head parallel; antennae 15-segmented; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 apical spurs; no pulvillus between the tarsal claws; fore coxa with a large, conspicuous tooth-like process. Type species Jugositermes tuberculatus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head red-yellow-brown, darker anteriorly, a dark longitudinal line running from the middle of the head backwards; head rectangular, sides parallel, posterior margin rounded; the two ridges above the antennal bases distinct, the lower ridge weaker, the antennal bases set at one end of a groove; frons steeply inclined at about 45°; a small wart-like tubercle on each side of the median line of the vertex, visible in profile; head surface sparsely setose, with more setae on the sides below the antennae; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 extremely short, shorter than segment 4, segment 4 shorter than segment 2; labrum very small, ligulate, inconspicuous; mandibles large and broad, proportionally short, the inner marginal teeth of both very short; frontal gland opening only dot-like, slightly in front of the median line; pronotal margins with numerous long setae, the anterior margin also with short hairs; pronotum narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the sides rather straight and narrowing posteriorly, the posterior margin deeply concave with rounded angles, the anterior margin concave, with a longitudinal groove in the middle; fore coxa with a large, conspicuous tooth-like process on its anterior side.

/genus/kemneritermes/.note: Soldier based solely on couplet 1 of the Oriental Region generic key; the original description by Ahmad & Akhtar (1981) was not obtained in full, hence only one character is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the Oriental Region genus-level key to soldiers of the Pericapritermes group, only this genus has a heavily sclerotised frontal ridge and a somewhat “phragmotic” head: it is separated at the first couplet on this basis, all other genera having no frontal ridge and a non-phragmotic head.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head with a heavily sclerotised frontal ridge, head somewhat phragmotic.

/genus/krecekitermes/.note: Apicotermitinae have no soldiers, and the original describes only the alate and the worker; both genus and species characters rest mainly on the digestive tract (mixed segment, enteric valve seating, enteric valve armature). The ZooKeys XML has no in-page pagination markers, so the locator is by section name and no in-page page numbers have been invented.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One of the Neotropical Apicotermitinae with dehiscent organs, a structure shared with Dissimulitermes and Ruptitermes. Distinguished from Dissimulitermes by: enteric valve seating (EVS) trilobed (tubular in the latter), enteric valve armature consisting only of spines, without sclerotised plates (the latter with sclerotised plates). Distinguished from Ruptitermes by: enteric valve armed (enteric valve unarmed in the latter, with R. bandeirai as the only exception, and that species is far larger than this genus, its spines concentrated on only 3 cushion lobes). The genus-level key gives the combination 'enteric valve seating trilobed, fewer than 13 spines on the armed cushions of the enteric valve'. The dehiscent organ fills the haemocoel in front of the crop; the junction between the midgut and P1 is clear, but the mixed segment is short.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dorsal surface of the head capsule concave in lateral view; fontanelle very prominent; postclypeus almost not inflated, its median suture distinct; antennae 14 or 15 segments (segment formula 2>3<4≈5<6).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly concave in lateral view; antennae pale, 13 or 14 segments (2>3<4<5); postclypeus strongly inflated. Apical tooth of the left endognath and M1+2 equally prominent, the edge of M3 forming an obtuse angle, its tip truncate and directed backwards, the raised molar region well developed and projecting, completely concealing the molar lobe process in dorsal view; apical tooth of the right endognath more prominent than M1, M1 well developed, the tip of M2 rounded, projecting and directed backwards, an obtuse angle between M1 and M2. The dehiscent organ is conspicuous in most individuals. The mixed segment of the gut is short, thickened at the midgut tongue; the enteric valve armature consists of 6 cushion lobes with sclerotised, crown-shaped tips bearing spines, located in the posterior part of the cushions.

/genus/krishnacapritermes/.note: Soldier based on couplets 9 and 11 of the Oriental Region generic key (including lead features).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Separated by the “fontanelle transversely wide, fontanelle gland large” from Pericapritermes, Oriencapritermes and Syncapritermes, which have a small, round fontanelle (couplet 11); head sparsely hairy, frons gently sloping (lead feature).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Fontanelle transversely wide, fontanelle gland large; head sparsely hairy, frons gently sloping.

/genus/labiocapritermes/.note: The genus characters are taken directly from the genus-level Diagnosis of the original text and are given separately for the two castes, soldier and worker; the original records the alate of all three known species as Imago: Unknown, so no alate section is provided. The variability of the median arm of the Y-shaped suture of the head capsule and the two spine-like tibial spurs were proposed in the original under Remarks and 'proposed as of generic significance' respectively, and have been incorporated above.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is relatively easy to recognise within the Pericapritermes group by its nearly square head capsule in dorsal view and the absence of frontal processes: the labrum is strongly inflated and asymmetrical left to right, its anterior margin slightly concave, its anterolateral corners either with a very small point or entirely absent; the mandibles are very short, shorter than the head, and extremely asymmetrical left to right — the left mandible is strongly twisted in the middle and its tip bears neither a beak-like process nor a hook, while the right mandible is blade-like with a blunt, non-acuminate tip. Together with the club-shaped postmentum and the strongly saddle-shaped pronotum, this distinguishes it from Pericapritermes and eight other genera. The author additionally proposed a genus-level character: the soldiers of all three known species have two brown, distinct spine-like spurs on the mid tibia.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule subrectangular, without frontal processes; in lateral view the frontal region slopes gently downwards, the fontanelle is small and the fontanelle gland also small. Antennae 14 segments. Labrum asymmetrical and strongly inflated, the lateral margins convex, the anterior margin slightly concave, the anterolateral corners with a very small point (sometimes indistinct). Mandibles strongly asymmetrical and shorter than the head: the left mandible strongly twisted in the middle, its tip without a beak or hook; the right mandible blade-like, distinctly shorter than the left mandible, its tip blunt. Postmentum club-shaped, distinctly constricted at the waist. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, the anterior margin weakly concave, the posterior margin without a notch. The median arm of the Y-shaped suture of the head capsule varies from clear to faint to indistinct within a single species and even within a single colony, and the author therefore did not use it as a species-level character.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule nearly circular in dorsal view; antennae 14 segments. Each mandible with one apical tooth and two marginal teeth, the apical tooth large; posterior margins of the 1st and 2nd marginal teeth of the left mandible long, the 3rd marginal tooth extremely reduced; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible small and projecting, its posterior margin weakly concave; pronotum saddle-shaped. The worker mandibular structure indicates that this genus is a humus/organic-rich soil feeder of feeding group III.

/genus/labiotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 50). The original established it as a subgenus of Cornitermes (Untergattung Labiotermes n. subg.), the generic characters being those of the subgenus, and further subdivided it into two groups (Sektion 1/2); no separate genus-level diagnosis is given in the text, so the 'Diagnostic characters' section is based on the subgeneric characters and the differences between the two groups.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 established Labiotermes as a new subgenus within Cornitermes. The alate has large compound eyes and large ocelli set close against them, antennae of 17 segments, and mandibular tooth 1 larger than tooth 2; the soldier has a relatively short frontal tube, a long labrum with a transparent, sharply delimited tip, antennae of 13–15 segments, and at most 2 teeth in the middle of the left mandible; the worker has antennae of 14–15 (16) segments and mandibular tooth 1 longer than tooth 2. The original text further divides the group into two: one with soldier antennae of 15 segments, the left mandible bearing 2 middle teeth and the basal and middle teeth of the right mandible separate; the other with the alate unknown, soldier antennae of 13 segments, the left mandible without middle teeth and the basal and middle teeth of the right mandible fused.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large; ocelli large, very close to the compound eyes. Antennae of 17 segments. Mandibular tooth 1 larger than tooth 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal tube relatively short. Labrum long, with a sharply delimited transparent tip. Mandibles robust; left mandible with at most 2 teeth in the middle. Antennae of 13–15 segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae of 14–15 (16) segments. Mandibular tooth 1 longer than tooth 2. The original text gives only these two diagnostic features for the worker of this subgenus and does not describe the rest separately (it still falls within the generic characters of Cornitermes).

/genus/labritermes/.note: Krishna & Adams (1982) redescribed the genus and its type species L. buttel-reepeni and added two species, L. emersoni and L. kistneri. The generic alate characters are known only from the description of the type species (original text: 'IMAGO: See the description under Labritermes buttel-reepeni'). The genus was established by Holmgren (1914) and was formerly placed in the Amitermitinae; Noirot & Noirot-Timothée (1969) and Sands (1972) transferred it to the Termitinae on the basis of digestive-tract characters, and Krishna & Adams (1982) confirmed its closest relationship with the African genus Foraminitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head small, cylindrical, height nearly equal to width, the frons inclined towards the postclypeus at about 45°; fontanelle circular, extremely small (diameter about 0.014–0.019 mm); labrum very large and broad (broader than long), asymmetrical, upturned, with a broad hyaline tip in the anterior region and a posteriorly directed posteromedian sclerotised process on the underside; mandibles strongly curved, asymmetrical, the left mandible slightly longer, its inner cutting edge regularly serrate from the tip and ending in four progressively larger teeth, the right mandible more strongly incurved, its dorsal inner edge smooth, with a finely serrate narrow groove; antennae 12-segmented; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Most closely related to the African genus Foraminitermes, the two sharing several synapomorphies such as the hyaline tip of the soldier labrum, the finely serrate left mandible, 1–2 spine-like processes at the base of the molar region of the right mandible, and the structure of the digestive tract, on which grounds Krishna & Adams (1982) transferred the genus from the Amitermitinae to the Termitinae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head small, cylindrical, height nearly equal to width, the frons inclined towards the postclypeus at about 45°; frontal gland extremely small, fontanelle circular, extremely small, about 0.014–0.019 mm in diameter, situated just above the frontal slope; labrum very large and broad, broader than long, asymmetrical, upturned, with a broad hyaline tip in the anterior region and a posteriorly directed posteromedian sclerotised process on the underside. Mandibles strongly curved, asymmetrical: the left mandible slightly longer than the right, its inner cutting edge with clear, regular serrations from the tip, extending about 1/3–1/2 of its length, ending in four progressively larger teeth, the posterior edges of teeth 3 and 4 long, the base of tooth 4 with a small cusp; the right mandible more strongly incurved than the left, its dorsal inner edge smooth, with a narrow groove extending from near the base to the tip, the ventral edge of the groove finely serrate, with 1–2 extremely small spine-like processes at the base. Pronotum saddle-shaped, narrower than the head. Antennae 12-segmented; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Measurements (soldier of the type species L. buttel-reepeni, mm): head length 1.05–1.15, head width 0.58–0.62, head height 0.54–0.59, left mandible 0.58–0.60, right mandible 0.50–0.58.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Left mandible apical tooth short; marginal teeth 1+2 fused, their posterior edge longer than the apical tooth, the cutting edge nearly straight, evenly continuous with the anterior edge of marginal tooth 3 (no distinct angle); mandible index LA/Li 0.28; marginal tooth 4 small, faintly visible from above, almost hidden behind the molar prominence; molar plate with 4–5 grinding ridges. Right mandible: posterior edge of marginal tooth 1 longer than the apical tooth or than the posterior edge of marginal tooth 2, marginal tooth 2 distinct, its posterior edge concave; molar plate with 3–4 grinding ridges. Digestive tract similar to that of Foraminitermes in several respects: crop enlarged, asymmetrical; gizzard not markedly separated from the crop, more strongly sclerotised; midgut very long (about three times the combined length of crop and gizzard); midgut–hindgut junction simple, transverse, without a mixed segment; four Malpighian tubules arising evenly at this junction, running forwards for some distance and then turning back posteriorly, their bases slightly swollen; P1 tubular and narrow proximally (about the same diameter as the midgut), swollen into a sac distally, entering P2 through a toothless conical enteric valve; P2 less swollen than the distal sac of P1, narrowing into a slender tubular colon and ending at the rectum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head yellow to pale yellow-brown, with three pale circular spots between the ocelli forming a triangle; postclypeus, anteclypeus and labrum cream-yellow; antennae pale yellow; pronotum cream-yellow to pale yellow; wing scales brown; wings and legs pale yellow. Head and pronotum densely covered with setae of varying thickness. Head small, oval, posterior margin broadly rounded; Y suture not visible; fontanelle extremely small, almost invisible, not raised; eyes medium-sized; ocelli large, touching the eye margin; postclypeus convex, divided into two halves by a median suture; antennae with 12+ segments, segment 2 equal to segment 4, segment 3 larger than segments 2 and 4; pronotum 0.77–0.81 times the head width, not saddle-shaped, anterior margin slightly concave, the sides broadly rounded, posterior margin distinctly emarginate; coxa without a sclerotised ridge (unlike Foraminitermes); tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Forewing about 5.90 mm long and 1.52 mm wide.

/genus/lacessititermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 18th subgenus, noted for the East Indies, with the species alipes, atrior, breviarticulatus, filicornis, laborator, lacessitiformis, lacessitus, piliferus and others (including new species). The original text has only key entries and no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier nasus relatively narrowly conical, antennae 14-segmented, head often constricted, antennal segment 3 shorter than segment 4; in the same group Longipeditermes has segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4, two soldier morphs and one distinct tooth at the mandible apex, while Hospitalitermes is monomorphic and has no tooth at the mandible apex. Alate clypeus shorter than half its width, only very slightly paler than the frons or concolorous with it, the frons behind the clypeus with a triangular depression, body and wings dark, antennal segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2, fontanelle indistinct and slit-like — distinguished from Hospitalitermes (segment 3 twice as long as segment 2, fontanelle distinct, oval, whitish).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Clypeus shorter than half its width, only (very) slightly paler than the frons or concolorous with it; frons with a triangular depression behind the clypeus; body dark, wings dark; antennal segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2; fontanelle indistinct, slit-like.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus relatively narrowly conical; antennae 14-segmented; head often constricted; antennal segment 3 shorter than segment 4; body mostly dark, legs long.

/genus/leptomyxotermes/.note: The genus name derives from the Greek leptos (slender) and myxa (lamp spout, jug spout). The 1965 generic diagnosis by Sands contains two sections, imago and Soldier, and no worker section. The original text notes that the small tooth connecting the molar prominence with the 3rd marginal tooth is reduced and set back in this genus, whereas it is visible in Fulleritermes and Rhadinotermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands established this genus for the African forest species doriae, which had previously been placed, together with Rhadinotermes, in Coarctotermes. Alate: the cutting edge before the 3rd marginal tooth of the left mandible has a distinct notch, a feature shared with Rhadinotermes and Fulleritermes; but in this genus the compound eyes and ocelli are very large and prominent, the fontanelle is slit-like and does not clearly fork anteriorly, and the molar plate of the right mandible has only 6–7 ridges (7–9 in Fulleritermes, 13–14 in Grallatotermes). Soldier monomorphic with traces of a second morph, nasus columnar, head strongly constricted behind the antennae, antennae 14-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Apical tooth of the left mandible as long as the 1st marginal tooth, the distance from the apical tooth to the 1st marginal tooth half the distance between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth (left mandible index about 50); the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth with a distinct concavity in front of the 3rd marginal tooth. Apical tooth of the right mandible nearly as long as the 1st marginal tooth, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth about as long as that of the 2nd marginal tooth, the latter distinctly concave; surface of the molar plate with a notch on the anterior margin near the base, the posterior margin extended into a rounded wing, the 1st molar ridge tooth-like, the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base. Fontanelle slit-like, not clearly forking anteriorly. Compound eyes and ocelli very large and prominent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph, with traces of a second morph. Nasus columnar. Reduced mandibles with a small point. Head capsule strongly constricted behind the antennae. Antennae 14-segmented.

/genus/leucopitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (leucops). Emerson 1960 described it only from soldier and worker syntypes, without examining alates, hence no such section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.56 (worker); soldier mandibles with or without apical points; the genus that Emerson 1960 regarded as the most primitive in the Oriental Subulitermes branch, possibly allied to the Australian Occasitermes and the Madagascan Malagasitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal process and vertex with very short microchaetae (not as long and dense as in Malagasitermes milloti); abdominal tergites with short hairs and setae (shorter than in Malagasitermes); head outline convex at the sides, the posterior part of the head not as high and broad as in Malagasitermes; a small but distinct constriction on the side of the head behind the antennal base; mandibles with or without apical points; pronotum anterior margin slightly concave, the angle between the anterior and posterior sections of the lateral pronotal outline nearly a right angle.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.56; the apical teeth of both mandibles only slightly larger than the 1st marginal tooth; the angle between the 1st marginal tooth and the apical tooth of the left mandible sharper, the angle at the cutting edge between the 1st marginal tooth and the reduced 2nd marginal tooth distinct, the notch before the 3rd marginal tooth broad and distinct, the 3rd marginal tooth broader; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible distinct, the angle between the 1st and 2nd marginal teeth slightly less than a right angle; molar plate outline of the right mandible nearly straight.

/genus/longipeditermes/.note: Established by Holmgren 1912 and listed in the catalogue as the 16th subgenus, with only Eutermes (Longipeditermes) longipes Haviland (Malacca and Borneo). In the key the alate appears only as “(?Longipeditermes n. subg.)”, appended after the Hospitalitermes entry, the author being in doubt, so no alate section is given; the original text gives no worker diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic, a point specially marked in the key (most other genera of the group being monomorphic); nasus relatively narrowly conical, antennae 14-segmented, head often constricted, mandible apex with only one distinct tooth, antennal segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4. Lacessititermes has segment 3 shorter than segment 4 and is monomorphic; Hospitalitermes is monomorphic and has no tooth at the mandible apex.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic. Nasus relatively narrowly conical; antennae 14-segmented; head often constricted; mandible apex with one distinct tooth; antennal segment 3 equal to or longer than segment 4; legs long.

/genus/longustitermes/.note: Soldierless. In this batch only the 2023 key and comparative accounts were read (the original description, Bourguignon et al. 2010, was not obtained in full), hence only enteric valve and body-size characters are listed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Worker enteric valve seating (EVS) three-lobed, which separates it from Hirsutitermes with a tubular enteric valve seating; the enteric valve armature is a continuous wreath-like structure covering the interpad cuticle, made up of hundreds of tiny thin spines. Body smaller than in Hirsutitermes.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Enteric valve armature (EVA) in a continuous wreath, the spines small and thin, several hundred in number, extending onto the interpad cuticle; enteric valve seating three-lobed. Body relatively small.

/genus/lophotermes/.note: The generic characters are a rediagnosis for the New Guinean group; the original states that the full description is in Miller (1991); alate undescribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with well-developed frontal and lateral tubercles; mandibles generally robust and longer than the head capsule; antennae 14-segmented (rarely 15); labrum usually large; tibial spur formula 3:2:2 or 2:2:2. Worker monomorphic, the left mandible index greater than 1.5 and often greater than 2.0; hindgut P3 divided into a smaller posterior portion and a larger anterior portion.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal tubercles and lateral tubercles both well developed; mandibles robust, longer than the head capsule; antennae 14-segmented, sometimes 15; labrum usually large; tibial spur formula 3:2:2 or 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monomorphic. Left mandible index greater than 1.5, often greater than 2.0; hindgut P3 divided into a small posterior portion and a larger anterior portion.

/genus/macrognathotermes/.note: The generic characters are a rediagnosis for the New Guinean group; the original states that the full description is in Miller (1991); alate undescribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with well-developed frontal tubercles; lateral tubercles usually present, sometimes reduced or absent; mandibles very long and slender; postmentum projecting only slightly below the lower margin of the head capsule; antennae 14-segmented; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Worker monomorphic, the left mandible index greater than 1.5 and often greater than 2.0; enteric valve cushions alternating in size, slightly asymmetrical and densely covered with small spines; hindgut P1 enlarged, P3 divided into posterior and anterior portions of equal size.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal tubercles well developed; lateral tubercles usually present, sometimes reduced or absent; mandibles extremely long and slender; postmentum projecting only slightly below the lower margin of the head capsule; antennae 14-segmented; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monomorphic. Left mandible index greater than 1.5, often greater than 2.0; enteric valve cushions alternating in size and slightly asymmetrical, with numerous small spines; hindgut P1 enlarged, P3 divided into a posterior and an anterior portion, the two nearly equal in size.

/genus/macrosubulitermes/.note: Contains 2 species (greavesi, the type species, and perlevis). The original describes the alate and soldier, without describing the worker mandibles separately, hence no worker section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate left mandible index 1.07 (Subulitermes microsoma 1.29–1.33); soldier head larger than in S. microsoma, the posterior part broader and more spherical, head length/head width ratio 1.49–1.71 (S. microsoma 2.27).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Apical antennal segment pale, basal segment dark; the dark part of the pronotum the same colour as the head (pronotum paler in S. microsoma); tibiae and the distal parts of the femora darker than the middle of the femora; wings darker than in S. microsoma (punctures denser); sternites with dark patches at the sides, pale in the middle; vertex gently raised between the ocelli; head outline strongly arched, the highest point above the ocelli; fontanelle a pale narrow slit, forked anteriorly, shorter than the ocelli; antennae 15 segments, the 3rd slightly longer than the 2nd and 4th and more spherical at the tip; postclypeus length less than half its width (0.20–0.22 × 0.47 mm); left mandible index 1.07; lateral margins of the pronotum drawn back posteriorly; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus base and vertex with 8 setae; frontal process and head sparsely covered with short hairs; abdominal tergite hairs denser, only slightly shorter than the marginal setae; head larger than in S. microsoma, the posterior part broader and more spherical; head length/head width ratio 1.49–1.63 (perlevis) or 1.71 (greavesi); head very slightly constricted, with a lateral ridge behind the nasus base; frontal process nearly cylindrical; antennae 12 segments (perlevis), the 2nd, 3rd and 4th segments nearly equal in length; mandibles without apical points; fore tibia nearly as wide as the femur, slightly swollen; abdomen thick, broad and rounded.

/genus/macuxitermes/.note: Soldier dimorphic, the small soldier known only in M. triceratops; worker based on the addenda of Postle & Scheffrahn (2016) (original description in Cancello & Bandeira 1992).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier dimorphic (small soldier known only in M. triceratops). Major soldier head capsule evenly rounded, or with a dorsal swelling and one anterior projection on each side of the midline, the surface densely covered with microgranules; anterior part of the head narrowed into a stout conical nasus, the tip of the nasus extending far beyond the mandible apices; mandibles strongly incurved, at rest with the apices directed laterally and not upturned, each with a pointed marginal tooth at the middle; antennae 15-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic or not dimorphic. Major soldier head capsule evenly rounded, or with a dorsal swelling and anterior projections on either side of the midline, entirely covered with microgranules; anterior part of the head narrowed into a stout conical nasus, its tip extending far beyond the mandible apices, the apex with a circular fontanelle and without setae; mandibles strongly incurved, at rest with the apices directed laterally and not upturned, each with a pointed marginal tooth at the middle; antennae yellow, 15-segmented (segment I longest, segment III shortest); margins of thoracic tergites with rows of dark short tooth-like spines. Small soldier known only in M. triceratops.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: All three marginal teeth of the mandibles clearly visible, molar plate without ridges; digestive tract completely twisted dorsally, crop small, mixed segment long and inflated (narrow proximally, broadly elliptical distally), P1 very large and plump, P3 relatively small, P4 long, P5 large; enteric valve narrow, located on the left posterior side of the abdomen, with three finger-like cushions, each cushion with two rows of equal-length, regularly arranged long spines.

/genus/malagasitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (milloti). Emerson 1960 described it only from 1 paratype soldier and 2 workers, without examining alates, hence no such section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.66 (worker); closest to the Oriental Leucopitermes rather than to the African genera of that branch (the smallest left mandible index among the African genera is Eutermellus, at 1.12).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal process and vertex with short hairs, few hairs at the nasus base; vertex with a few setae; abdominal tergites and sternites with long dense hairs, the posterior margin of each sclerite with a row of setae about twice the body-hair length; head with a distinct constriction, the posterior part nearly spherical; frontal process conical; antennae 12–13 segments; right mandible with a short pointed apical point, left mandible without an apical point; the angle between the anterior and posterior sections of the lateral pronotal outline less than a right angle.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical teeth of both mandibles relatively larger than the 1st marginal tooth; cutting edge of the 1+2 marginal teeth of the left mandible undulate; a distinct notch retained before the 3rd marginal tooth of the left mandible; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly rounded; left mandible index 0.66.

/genus/mangolditermes/.note: Only the worker and the gut morphology are known; the alate is unknown (original: Imago. Unknown.). The generic characters rest mainly on the enteric valve and the course of P1.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Enteric valve unarmed (as in Hydrecotermes and Rustitermes), but distinguishable from both by P1 being extremely long and S-shaped in left view. Compared with Aparatermes: the midgut tongue elongate (short in the latter), the scales with pointed tips situated on the proximal part of the pads (in the mid-region of the pads in the latter), and the protibia relatively inflated. Compared with Anoplotermes, which likewise has an unarmed enteric valve: the midgut tongue lacks white spherical midgut nodules in ventral view, and the pads are trapezoidal and truncate at the base (spatulate in the latter). Compared with Disjunctitermes: larger (maximum head width >0.75 mm versus <0.7 mm in the latter), pads wider (narrow and slender in the latter), scales distinct only from the middle towards the anterior part (over the whole pad in the latter). Compared with Tonsuritermes: the worker fontanelle is not particularly prominent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Fontanelle oval, its border indistinct; dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly concave in lateral view; antennae pale, 14-segmented (2<3≅4<5). Apical tooth of the left mandible more prominent than M1+2, the apical tooth and M1+2 enclosing a 75° angle, the posterior margin of M1+2 nearly straight and long; molar prominence extremely sharp, conspicuous in dorsal view, nearly as long as M3; molar region swelling small. Apical tooth of the right mandible much more prominent than M1, the tip of M1 very sharp, M2 enclosing an almost 90° angle and directed backwards, a shallow notch between M1 and M2 forming a broad and slightly obtuse angle; molar plate reduced and concave. Crop small; midgut tongue of the mixed segment long but not inflated; P1 extremely long in left view, S-shaped from one side of the crop to P3; enteric valve seating weakly trilobed; enteric valve unarmed, composed of 6 slender, inflated pads, the distal half of each pad bearing distinct fringed pentagonal scales, the proximal end of each pad with about 10–20 minute triangular spines.

/genus/mapinguaritermes/.note: The remaining features of the worker gut (mesenteric tongue, P1, enteric valve with 3 cushions, inverted U of P3b) are described in the source but not quoted, owing to the quotation limit; the source gives no generic description of the alate.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The first-order cushions of the worker gizzard bear well-developed spines, which the source calls a synapomorphy of the genus in the phylogenetic analysis.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head oval in dorsal view; frontal tube conical, nearly parallel to the head base and about four-fifths of its length in lateral view; antennae 14 segments; labrum subpentagonal, with a transparent anterior margin lacking a distinct point; postmentum concave at the sides.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head circular; frontal suture indistinct; fontanelle elliptical and very indistinct; postclypeus slightly inflated; antennae 14 segments.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is very similar to Incisitermes and difficult to distinguish; the soldier differs from Incisitermes in having a ridge between the frons and the vertex, the third antennal segment greatly elongated, and the anterolateral corners of the pronotum serrate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pale yellow; eye diameter 0.46–0.48 mm, ocelli about 0.01 mm from the compound eye; antennae 16 segments; posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible slightly shorter than the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly longer than the molar plate; pronotum slightly narrower than the head; wings transparent; radial sector with 8–9 branches, the first branch at about 1/3 of the wing length; media weak, unsclerotised, lying between the radial sector and the cubitus almost to the wing apex; arolium always absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long, the anterior part inclined downwards at about 40°; a raised ridge between the frons and the vertex, thicker and higher above the antennal bases; eyes distinct, slightly pigmented; antennae 10–11 segments, the first and second dark brown and heavily sclerotised, the third extremely long, club-shaped and dark, about equal to the sum of the following 5–7 segments; mandibles long and slender, toothed, the basal tubercle distinct; pronotum as wide as the head, the anterior margin deeply concave, the anterolateral corners irregularly serrate, the sides evenly rounded, without a median notch; femora slightly swollen.

/genus/mastotermes/.note: The paper is a family-level taxonomic revision; the generic morphology is concentrated in the wing venation, and the original has no sections on soldier or worker morphology, so only diagnostic characters and the alate are given. Two points are easily misattributed: the archidictyon reticulate venation (the original states explicitly that it is shared by the Mastotermitidae and the Hodotermitidae and is not a generic character); and the media joining the radial sector a short distance behind the humeral suture, which is a general feature of termites (the original says 'in nearly all cases'); neither is included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Generic characters at the level of the wing venation: the radial sector of the forewing is strongly fused, with the adjacent upper branches closely spaced; the humeral suture of the forewing is more curved and more convex than in Blattotermes; the hindwing has a well-developed anal lobe, which the original describes as a feature of this genus and its close relatives; the radial sector is compact and the media lies closer to the radial sector and farther from the anterior cubitus, on which basis wing-only specimens can be assigned to this genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The radial sector of the forewing is highly fused, with the adjacent upper branches closely spaced; the humeral suture of the forewing forms a distinct arcuate convexity and is more curved than in Blattotermes; the anal lobe of the hindwing is well developed.

/genus/mimeutermes/.note: Established by Silvestri 1914, type species Mimeutermes giffardii. Sands 1965 records three species and considers that the genus evolved in the West African rain forest. All three sections are taken from the original generic diagnosis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands places this genus in the Paracornitermes group of the Ethiopian region. Alate: apical tooth of the left mandible long, the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth short and slightly concave (left mandible index 2.00–2.23), the gap between the 3rd marginal tooth and the molar plate less than half the width of that cutting edge; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible absent, the molar plate with prominent anterior and posterior rounded wings, tapering towards the apex, without ridges — the absence of ridges makes it easy to distinguish from Fulleritermes, Leptomyxotermes, Grallatotermes and other ridged genera. Soldier monomorphic, nasus thickly conical, joining the tapering base of the head capsule, head in dorsal view not constricted, top-shaped together with the nasus, antennae 12-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible with a long apical tooth, the cutting edge between the 1st and 3rd marginal teeth short and slightly concave (left mandible index 2.00–2.23), the gap between the 3rd marginal tooth and the molar plate less than half the width of that cutting edge. Apical tooth and 1st marginal tooth of the right mandible as in the left mandible, 2nd marginal tooth absent, the posterior cutting edge of the 1st marginal tooth concave, the molar plate with prominent anterior and posterior rounded wings, tapering towards the apex, without ridges. Postclypeus slightly raised, twice as wide as long or a little less. Fontanelle pale, slit-like, slightly forking anteriorly and with a pale spot, or nearly obsolete, only slightly paler than the head. Compound eyes slightly projecting from the sides of the head. Head pilosity variable. Posterior margin of the pronotum rounded, anterior margin concave.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A single morph. Nasus thickly conical, its base joining the taper of the head capsule, fontanelle relatively large. Reduced mandibles pointed or unpointed; anterior margin of the labrum undulate. Head capsule in dorsal view not constricted, top-shaped together with the nasus, sides parallel or rounded posteriorly. Antennae 12-segmented. Head and nasus with only a few conspicuous setae. Tergite hairs sparse, scattered and minute, those of the posterior margin and of the last 2–3 tergites longer; sternite hairs sparse and short, those of the posterior margin about twice as long as the short hairs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in the alate, only the apical tooth proportionally longer (left mandible index 3.32–3.59) and the molar plate of the right mandible larger with more prominent wings.

/genus/mirocapritermes/.note: Soldier based on couplets 3–5 of the Oriental Region generic key.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
