sections.text: Couplet 5: head with a frontal projection, middle of left mandible moderately curved; those without a frontal projection go to other branches such as Pseudocapritermes (apex beak-like). Antennae 14-segmented, mandibles stout (couplet 4).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head with a frontal projection; middle of left mandible moderately curved (apex acute, or beak-like, hook-like); antennae 14-segmented; mandibles stout, middle moderately to strongly curved.

/genus/mucrotermes/.note: Only the soldier and worker characters explicitly given in Emerson's (1960) genus-level diagnosis are included; species-level measurements and pilosity are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: There is no tuft of setae beside the fontanelle opening in the soldier, whereas several related genera have one; the head is relatively short, broad and thick.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In lateral view the vertex forms a sharp hump, with the steeply sloping frons and the vertex respectively above and below it; the fontanelle lies in the middle of the slope, nearer the postclypeus than the vertex.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical teeth of both mandibles are proportionally large; there is no visible angular notch before the third marginal tooth of the left mandible; the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is small but distinct.

/genus/muelleritermes/.note: The source also contains a generic description of the alate (head with a semicircular ridge, antennae 15 segments, fore coxa rough laterally, wing with a stellate micraster) and a description of the minor soldier (head narrower, elongate or oval, distinctly constricted behind the antennae); because quotations are limited to 3 per genus, no alate section is given and the minor soldier text is not quoted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus is distinguished from the other genera of the Nasutitermitinae by its trimorphic soldiers and by the pair of vestigial ocelli on the soldier head; within the subfamily only this genus, Velocitermes and Diversitermes have trimorphic soldiers.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Trimorphic. Major soldier head broad and round, nearly square or slightly oval, without a constriction behind the antennae (M. globiceps), only slightly constricted in a few individuals of M. fritzi; medium soldier head oval or slightly oval.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the minor worker rare; the major worker mandibles are of two forms (called narrow-gap and broad-gap by Fontes, 1987); head circular, antennae 14 segments, postclypeus not inflated, fontanelle indistinct.

/genus/mycterotermes/.note: Sands 1965 explicitly records Imago: Unknown, hence only a soldier section. The original text notes that the genus was established on material from Sia Ding alone, a monotypic genus with a single species; its diagnostic characters share much with the Neotropical Diversitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands established this genus for meringocephalus from Sia Ding, considering it close to Trinervitermes but more primitive, possibly even the ancestor of the latter, its diagnostic characters having much in common with the Neotropical Diversitermes. Soldier dimorphic: the major soldier has a short, columnar nasus and the head very weakly constricted behind the antennae; the minor soldier has a weakly conical nasus and a more evident constriction of the head; the antennae are possibly 13-segmented in the major soldier and 12-segmented in the minor. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: nasus short, columnar, reduced mandibles with a small but distinct point showing traces of the marginal and apical teeth; head capsule very weakly constricted behind the antennae, vertex and nasus with short, conspicuous bristle-like hairs. Minor soldier: identical to the major soldier except for the weakly conical nasus and the more evident constriction of the head capsule behind the antennae. Antennae possibly 13-segmented in the major soldier and 12-segmented in the minor.

/genus/neocapritermes/.note: The original does not give a separate worker diagnosis; the worker mandibles are shown only in Fig. 1 (worker mandibles of N. opacus), so no separate worker section is provided on this page.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Neotropical Termitinae: the soldier has markedly asymmetrical, snapping mandibles, the frons lacks a 'nasus'-like or conical horizontal process and the front has no frontal gland; monotypic; fontanelle circular; head not flattened, the posterior margin evenly rounded (only N. bodkini has a slight median concavity on the posterior margin). Closely related to Planicapritermes; Ahmad (1950) regarded the two as the most primitive groups of Termitinae in respect of the worker–alate mandibles (apical tooth small, posterior margin of the 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible straight), placed in a separate branch before the Capritermes branch.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head usually without a dense pilosity, in a few species with short hairs and a few setae of two sizes; pronotal pilosity rather dense. Fontanelle plate sclerotised, without a visible opening. Ocelli large, not touching the compound eye. Antennae 16 or 17 segments. Mandibles as in Fig. 1: apical tooth of the left mandible small, the posterior margin of the fused 1st+2nd marginal teeth long, the 3rd marginal tooth well developed; posterior margin of the 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible straight. Meso- and metanotal plates deeply and broadly incised. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2 (2:2:2 only in N. bodkini); mid tibia without spines or with 1, 2 to several spines.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic (body size variable). Head usually long, nearly rectangular (distinctly narrowed anteriorly in bodkini, villosus and utiariti); fontanelle small (larger in bodkini), circular, with 1 distinct line running from the fontanelle back to the posterior margin of the head; in a few species the postclypeus is deformed and drawn upwards into a prominent spine-like process. Antennae 15 or 16 segments, segments 5–16 elongated in a few species. Labrum asymmetrical, deflected to the right to accommodate the deformation of the left mandible; anterior margin variable in shape: tongue-shaped, the two sides converging into a bluntly rounded tip, or with two lateral lobules plus 1 median lobule (trilobed). Mandibles asymmetrical: the left mandible rather well developed at the base, with a ridge and a concavity on the outer base in lateral view, moderately or strongly curved about 1/3 from the base, then extending in an undulating manner to the inflated tip, with 1 tooth-like process near the base fitting into the corresponding notch of the right mandible; right mandible straighter and shorter. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe upturned. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2 (2:2:2 in bodkini); mid tibia with or without small outer spines. Fore coxa with a dark sclerotised longitudinal ridge bearing a row of spines.

/genus/ngauratermes/.note: The original authors explicitly record Imago. Unknown., hence no alate section. Soldier and worker characters all come from the genus-level treatment; the comparison with Tenuirostritermes, Diversitermes and Velocitermes is in the Comparisons section of the same work.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A genus living in Amazonian leaf litter, the name taken from the Ticuna ngau'ra (leaf litter). Soldier and worker both dimorphic, the alate still unknown. The original authors note that the genus has many similarities with the group formed by Tenuirostritermes, Diversitermes and Velocitermes, and is especially close to the latter two.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Mandibles with distinct tooth processes; antennae 13 segments; nasus base narrow, nearly cylindrical. Major soldier head capsule broad, slightly constricted behind the antennae, the sides narrowing forwards; minor soldier head capsule narrow and elongate, the constriction behind the antennae pronounced. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, narrow-gap and broad-gap, the two morphs overlapping in body size and not separable into large and small workers; the broad-gap morph at a very low proportion, only 6 of 103 workers in the type series, left mandible index 0.32. Worker antennae 14 segments, the 4th segment very short and unsclerotised; left mandible index 0.35; molar plate broad, concave, ridges weak. P1 a simple tube, without an apical ring; enteric valve conical, curved, posterior in position, inserting into P3 from the left dorsal side, weakly sclerotised, with two rings of spines.

/genus/nitiditermes/.note: All three castes are described by Emerson (1960) for the type species; for the soldier only the verifiable character of the head outline is retained (the OCR of the pilosity part is incomplete).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, smooth and little undulate, with fine sculpturing around the fontanelle; fontanelle elongate, set in a short, narrow depression on the head surface; vertex gently and evenly convex between the ocelli; compound eyes rather flat, of medium size, their distance from the lower margin of the head slightly less than one third of their diameter.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In lateral view the frons forms a bulbous swelling above the depressed fontanelle opening, its anterior part not extending over the mandible bases.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles similar to those of Cubitermes, Procubitermes, Noditermes, Lepidotermes and Mucrotermes; the apical tooth distinctly larger than the first marginal tooth; the distance from the apex of the left mandible to the tip of the first marginal tooth is greater than that from the tip of the first marginal tooth to the tip of the third marginal tooth.

/genus/niuginitermes/.note: A new genus established by Roisin & Pasteels 1996, containing 2 species including N. variratae (type species), endemic to New Guinea.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A genus endemic to New Guinea, containing 2 species. Soldier a small to medium-sized nasute termite resembling Nasutitermes, but with the head capsule not constricted behind the antennae, antennae 12-segmented and mandibles bearing a point; alate antennae 14-segmented, the only constant difference from New Guinean Nasutitermes; worker dimorphic, the gut pattern of diagnostic value.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small to medium-sized, antennae 14-segmented; compared with the alates of New Guinean Nasutitermes, the number of antennal segments (14) appears to be the only constant diagnostic character.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A small to medium-sized nasute termite closely related to Nasutitermes; monomorphic; head capsule not constricted behind the antennae; antennae 12-segmented; mandibles bearing a point; both included species are orange.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic; the body colour of the major worker changes with age; antennae 13-segmented; mandibles very similar to those of Nasutitermes, the left mandible index 0.38–0.53. The gut pattern is diagnostic: the mixed segment is long, and the mesenteric projection lies on the outer side of the gut loop, connected to the rest of the midgut by a broad dorsal stalk; the Malpighian tubules form two pairs, widely separated; the colon is long, passing backwards from the top of the paunch and then forming a three-dimensional S shape through two 180° bends, first forwards and then downwards, followed by a nearly straight section running to the rectum; the enteric valve is oblique and nearly symmetrical, the spinose regions of its upper and lower rings widely separated; the upper ring with 6 regions bearing many small spines; the lower ring with 3 swellings, the spines becoming smaller towards the paunch; the enteric valve armature does not project into the paunch.

/genus/noirotitermes/.note: Alate based on the genus-level supplementary description by Constantino (2012); soldier based on the generic key of Rocha et al. (2012) and the 2022 comparative generic characters (the original text of Cancello & Myles 2000 is an empty shell in Plazi, the body text was not obtained).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Posterior part of soldier head with four conspicuous horn-like projections, the sides convex, the anterior half slightly constricted; head capsule shape highly distinctive, head surface with characteristic microsculpture; mandibles of the piercing type; body relatively small. Alate left mandible index 1.5, antennae 15-segmented, segment order 1>2>6>5=4>3.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Posterior part of the head with four conspicuous horn-like projections, the sides convex, the anterior half slightly constricted; head capsule shape highly distinctive, head surface with characteristic microsculpture; mandibles of the piercing type; body smaller than in congeners.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown, frons with a semicircular pale patch, fontanelle spot elliptical and also pale, ecdysial line pale. Postclypeus markedly inflated, anterior margin straight, posterior margin convex, midline distinct. Compound eyes round, medium-sized; ocelli large and distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles large, left M3 much shorter than M1; left mandible index 1.5. Antennae 15-segmented, segment order 1>2>6>5=4>3. Wing surface microsculpture almost absent, with fine punctures only on the proximal anterior part.

/genus/obtusitermes/.note: The alate of O. monomorphus is recorded in the original as Imago. Unknown.; the alate section rests only on the genus-level comparison of Cuezzo et al. (2017). Constantino & Acioli (2009) state that the soldier mandibles are without points, which contradicts the small points of Scheffrahn et al. (2025); the text follows the latter's original description and the disagreement is recorded here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier monotypic, which is the origin of the genus name. Soldier antennae with fewer than 13 segments. The hindgut structure is unique among the Isoptera: P1 is connected to P3 by a very long tubular P2, P2 bent through about 180°, both ends weakly sclerotised.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic, small; head capsule reddish brown, nasus darker; head capsule pear-shaped in dorsal view, constricted at the anterior 1/3, convex in lateral view behind the antennal fossae; nasus broadly conical, upturned about 10°; antennae 11 segments, segment formula 2<3>4≤5; mandibles with small tooth processes. The number of vertex setae differs between species: O. monomorphus has only 6 long setae, whereas O. panamae and O. formosulus have many scattered long and short setae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; antennae 12 segments; midgut and P1 tubular, the mixed segment absent, P1 with a slightly darker constriction near the middle; left mandible apical tooth as long as the 1st marginal tooth, molar plate ridged; the sclerotised part of the enteric valve very long, tubular, the two rings separated by about 1 mm of smooth cuticle.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Postclypeus slightly arched in lateral view, anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly convex, as in Sandsitermes, Caetetermes, Caribitermes, Cortaritermes and Nasutitermes.

/genus/occasitermes/.note: The original text has only the subgeneric key and no genus-level Diagnosis; the above are the key couplets, and measurements, body colour and worker are all not given. Holmgren (p. 68), on the basis of its long, thick nasus and the alate characters of the Subulitermes group, regards the genus as a relatively primitive member of that group and suggests that it is rather closely related to Tumulitermes. The genus name is given in the original text as a new subgenus (n. subg.).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among Holmgren's subgenera of Eutermes, the soldier is characterised by the combination of mandibles entirely without an apical process, a long and thick nasus, 12-segmented antennae, and a head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets; Eutermellus of the same group has only a weak constriction behind the antennal sockets and can be separated further by head and nasus shape. In the key the alate falls in the Subulitermes group: 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd, fontanelle about at the middle of the head, antennal segments relatively long, pronotum narrow. In his systematic discussion Holmgren points out in particular that the alate belongs to the Subulitermes group while the soldier has a long, thick nasus (similar to that of Rhynchotermes), so he regards the genus as a key member of that branch retaining primitive characters; but what he gives are only key characters, not a complete genus-level description.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, usually narrowing anteriorly; fontanelle about at the middle of the head; antennal segments relatively long; pronotum narrow (Taf. III, Fig. 7). The couplets leading to this genus in the key also include: clypeus usually about as long as half its width, or shorter and rather strongly raised, oval, pale yellow; 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd. Wing surface pilosity and venation are not delimited in the key in the original text, only compared through the plate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without an apical process; the species are small, antennae 11–12-segmented, 12-segmented in this genus; nasus conical, long and thick; frontal profile straight (compared in the key with Taf. III, Fig. 17); head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets.

/genus/occultitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (occultus). The original does not describe the worker mandibles separately, hence no worker section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Left mandible index 0.68 (alate); soldier dimorphic — in all the remaining genera of the Subulitermes branch the soldier is monotypic; soldier mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum densely covered with setae and short hairs; abdominal tergites with short hairs and a few setae at the sides, nearly forming a marginal row; fontanelle distinctly forked anteriorly; postclypeus length much greater than half its width (length 0.22 mm, width 0.32 mm); 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible prominent, the cutting edge of the 1+2 marginal teeth of the left mandible long, the left mandible apical tooth relatively long; left mandible index 0.68; the sides of the pronotum flattened and rounded, not drawn back posteriorly as in Australitermes and Macrosubulitermes; meso- and metanota each with a broad shallow depression; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic; mandibles without apical points.

/genus/ophiotermes/.note: All soldier characters are taken from Emerson's (1928) subgenus discussion; the original text of Sjöstedt 1924 was not seen.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mandibles bend outwards at the middle to form an elbow and then curve slightly inwards towards the apex; Emerson (1928) used this to separate the genus from the remaining subgenera of Mirotermes and from related genera.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The inner margin of each mandible bears a small but conspicuous tooth between the base and the elbow; the apex of the fore tibia has 3 spines, and the apices of the mid and hind tibiae 2 each; the fontanelle opening resembles that of the subgenus Cubitermes; the labrum is bilobed.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The second marginal tooth of the right mandible is lost in the alate–worker; Emerson (1960) noted that this pattern is similar only in Euchilotermes, Ophiotermes, Tuberculitermes and Spinitermes.

/genus/oriencapritermes/.note: Soldier based on couplets 3 and 11–13 of the Oriental Region generic key.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Together with Syncapritermes in couplet 13: this genus has the anterior margin of the labrum deeply concave, about as long as wide, and the base of the anterolateral process pointed; Syncapritermes has the anterior margin shallowly concave, longer than wide, and the base of the anterolateral process unpointed. Left mandible with a well-developed, toothed basal inferior process (couplet 12).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior margin of labrum deeply concave, about as long as wide, base of anterolateral process pointed; left mandible with a well-developed, toothed basal inferior process; labrum long (length ≥ width); fontanelle small, round, fontanelle gland small; middle of left mandible strongly twisted, apex blunt.

/genus/oriensubulitermes/.note: Contains 2 species (inanis, the type species, and inaniformis). The original describes the mandibles of soldiers and worker nymphs, without examining alates, hence no such section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Left mandible index 1.06 (worker–nymph); the 3rd marginal tooth of the left mandible indistinct and the 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible almost completely reduced, which distinguishes it from all other genera of the Oriental Subulitermes branch; soldier mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without apical points.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: (Worker–nymph) left mandible index 1.06; cutting edge of the 1+2 marginal teeth evenly concave, no notch before the 3rd marginal tooth; 2nd marginal tooth of the right mandible almost completely reduced; molar plate outline of the right mandible slightly concave.

/genus/orthognathotermes/.note: Alate unknown; from the nymph the original records 17-segmented antennae, a postclypeal basis slightly shorter than half its width, and a large first mandibular tooth. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten from OCR text, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown (nymph with 17-segmented antennae). Soldier: head rectangular, rather flatly convex, frons flat; frontal prominence and fontanelle both absent; above the antennal socket a rather large, rounded-obtuse, tubercle-like widening of the antennal ridge; labrum short, about as long as wide, lingulate but with the lateral angles projecting slightly rounded-obtusely (weakly trilobed); mandibles symmetrical, with a median tooth at the middle; antennae 15-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, rather flatly convex, frons flat; frontal prominence and fontanelle both absent; above the antennal socket a rather large, rounded-obtuse, tubercle-like widening of the antennal ridge. Labrum short, about as long as wide, lingulate, but with the lateral angles projecting slightly rounded-obtusely (weakly trilobed). Mandibles symmetrical; base very wide, passing forwards over a rather long stretch into the middle of the mandible, with a trace of a tooth at the transition between base and middle; mandible slightly geniculate-bent outwards before the midpoint, the bend forming the median tooth; apex curved inwards; upper surface of the right mandibular apex slightly concave. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Postclypeus about as long as half its width, arched; first mandibular tooth large; antennae 14-segmented.

/genus/ourissotermes/.note: Apicotermitinae, soldier absent; both the alate and the worker are described, the core of the generic diagnosis being the form of the enteric valve armature and the direct insertion of the enteric valve into P3 without a differentiated enteric valve seating.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Enteric valve armature consisting of 6 groups of pectinate spine bundles, each bundle with 4–6 rows of spines: longer spines distally, near P3, decreasing posteriorly, together with smaller dentate spines; the proximal end of the pads (near P1) with 1 small dentate spine; the enteric valve inserting directly into P3, without a differentiated enteric valve seating (EVS). On this basis it is distinguished from Patawatermes (enteric valve seating elongated into a tube, clearly visible externally) and Echinotermes (enteric valve seating trilobed). External gut morphology similar to Hydrecotermes, but the latter has an unarmed enteric valve. The genus name refers to the enteric valve armature resembling a sea urchin (Portuguese ouriço).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head slightly concave above the ocelli; fontanelle very small or indistinct; compound eyes and ocelli nearly circular; antennae 15-segmented (segment formula 2>3<4<5<6); lateral margins of the pronotum elongate and smoothly rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Anterior part of the dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly convex in lateral view; postclypeus strongly inflated; antennae 14-segmented. Apical tooth of the left mandible more prominent than M1+2, the edge of M3 forming an obtuse-angled triangle with a slightly truncate end, molar region swelling well developed, partly concealing the molar prominence; apical tooth of the right mandible more prominent than M1, M2 triangular with an acute angle, its tip prominent but slightly less so than M1. Midgut tongue small, the junction between P1 and the midgut a simple transverse connection; enteric valve seating indistinct; enteric valve armature as in the generic diagnosis (6 groups of pectinate spine bundles, the distal spines long and decreasing posteriorly).

/genus/paracapritermes/.note: Established by Hill 1942 as a subgenus of Mirotermes and raised to genus by Snyder 1949; type species P. primus, distributed in Australia.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier mandibles asymmetrical—the left mandible long, hooked apically and with a prominent tooth-like process at the base, the right mandible short with a distinct basal notch; head with well-developed frontal tubercles, pointed and upturned apically (most developed in P. kraepelinii), the fontanelle opening beneath the frontal tubercles; antennae 14-segmented. Alate with the third marginal tooth of the left mandible well developed and the second marginal tooth of the right mandible weakened, most closely related to Protocapritermes (Ahmad 1950 regarded it as the most primitive member of the Capritermes complex, which Krishna 1968 rejected on the basis of mandibular dentition).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small, dark brown; head densely hairy, with stiff bristles interspersed; frontal plate distinct, narrow and elliptical; compound eyes small; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 the shortest. Apical tooth of the left mandible slightly shorter than the fused first and second marginal teeth, the third marginal tooth well developed; second marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly reduced.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head with well-developed frontal tubercles, pointed and upturned apically; fontanelle situated beneath the frontal tubercles; anterior margin of the labrum nearly straight or slightly angular, in some individuals slightly concave at the middle, the anterolateral corners slightly pointed; mandibles asymmetrical, pointed and hooked apically; left mandible with a prominent tooth-like process at the base, moderately curved at the middle with the outer margin strongly arcuate (P. primus) or slightly curved at the middle (P. kraepelinii); right mandible shorter than the left, with a distinct basal notch; antennae 14-segmented, segment 4 the shortest and segment 3 about equal to segment 2; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, the middle tibia with 1 spine in P. primus and 2 spines in P. kraepelinii.

/genus/paraconvexitermes/.note: The original description, Cancello & Noirot (2003, Annales de la Société Entomologique de France (n.s.) 39: 187–193), was not obtained in full; here only later comparative genus-level accounts could be used, hence no further details.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Nasus conical; antennae 11 segments; differs from Sinqasapatermes in the chaetotaxy and the shape of the soldier head capsule.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Molar region ridges reduced but marginal teeth retained, as in Araujotermes, Atlantitermes, Coatitermes, Convexitermes, Ereymatermes and Subulitermes.

/genus/paracurvitermes/.note: Soldier based on the 2012 generic key and the 2011/2022 comparative generic characters; for the alate only the left mandible index is known.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier relatively small; head capsule relatively wide, round or subquadrate, head base about as long as wide; frontal tube well developed, conical and rather short; mandibles of the piercing type, distinctly curved, longer and less curved than in Acangaobitermes and with triangular teeth, with a conspicuous marginal tooth near the base. Alate left mandible index about 2.0.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule relatively wide, round or subquadrate, head base about as long as wide. Frontal tube well developed, conical, shorter than in Biratermes. Mandibles of the piercing type, distinctly curved; longer and less curved than in Acangaobitermes, with triangular teeth; with a conspicuous marginal tooth near the base.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Left mandible index about 2.0, as in Curvitermes and Cyrilliotermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate has a distinct obtuse-angled bend on the posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible, and the arolium is absent; the soldier, with mandibles short and strong relative to the head length, can be distinguished from Comatermes and Ceratokalotermes (see their respective entries).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark smoky brown; eyes small, about 0.28 mm in diameter, ocelli about 0.02 mm from the compound eye; antennae 14–15 segments; the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible broader at the base than the third marginal tooth, their posterior margins slightly longer than the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth, with an obtuse-angled bend about 1/4 from the apex; molar plate of the right mandible nearly equal in length to the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum slightly wider than the head, the anterior margin broad and shallowly concave; radial sector with 6–7 branches; media paler than the radial sector, weakly sclerotised; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long, dorsoventrally flattened; frons slightly concave along the median line, inclined downwards towards the clypeus at about 35°; eyes colourless; antennae 13–15 segments, the third equal in length to the second; mandibles short and strong relative to the head length, with a basal tubercle; anterior part of the postmentum very broad; pronotum as wide as the head, the anterior margin broadly concave; femora distinctly swollen.

/genus/parvitermes/.note: Established by Emerson 1949 with Nasutitermes brooksi Snyder as type species; redescribed at generic level by Roisin et al. 1996. Originally a West Indian genus, only confirmed from the Central American mainland in 2016.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A small, pale nasute termite. Generic diagnosis rests mainly on the enteric valve (EVA): the spinose ring behind it consists of 3 keel-like pads, each bearing about 7–15 long spines that curve in the direction opposite to the food flow (“against the current”), in both worker and soldier—unique among termite genera except Antillitermes. P1 long and U-shaped (shorter and stouter in P. mexicanus), P2 constricted into a pyriform shape near P3. Compared with its Central American congeners, the soldier head capsule is smaller and paler than in Nasutitermes, the nasus distinctly narrower than in Subulitermes, and the head capsule is not so strongly constricted at the middle as in Tenuirostritermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The narrowest point of the head capsule lies in the posterior third (P. mexicanus) or at the middle (P. mesoamericanus, P. yucatanus); the inclination of the nasus relative to the plane of the vertex is of specific diagnostic value: slightly upturned in mexicanus, coplanar with it or directed downwards in mesoamericanus and yucatanus; in lateral view the apical two-thirds of the nasus is nearly cylindrical in mesoamericanus and conical in yucatanus. EVA as in the worker.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: P1 of the hindgut long and U-shaped; P2 constricted into a pyriform shape near P3; the spinose ring of the EVA consists of 3 keel-like pads, each with 7–15 long spines curving against the direction of the food flow, with or without patches of small conical teeth between the pads; in slide preparations the spines are often embedded in coagulated bacterial masses.

/genus/patawatermes/.note: Genus-level measurements: worker head width 0.69–1.1 mm. Soldierless. The page numbers of the genus-level treatment could not be verified from the Zenodo record (the record gives only the isPartOf full text and the author order), so the locator gives only the genus-level treatment and the author-year.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very similar to Grigiotermes, but clearly distinguishable by the shape of the enteric valve armature of the worker; moreover, although the worker P1 is swollen, it is less so than in Grigiotermes. The same set of morphological criteria (integument, mandibles, digestive tract and enteric valve) also separates the genus from the remaining South American soldierless termite genera.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Sclerotised parts dark brown, densely covered with several thousand minute setae. Head capsule with about 100 sparse long setae. Compound eyes and ocelli large. Fontanelle small to medium-sized, situated at the level of the anterior margin of the compound eyes. Pronotum elongate, with several dozen long setae. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum slightly concave, angles strongly rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Medium to large, head width 0.69–1.1 mm (genus-level measurements). Head capsule pale yellow, rounded, scattered with minute setae and about 100 long setae; fontanelle small, almost indistinct; mandibles and protibia as in figures 5C and 5D of the original. Enteric valve inserted into the tubular extension of the paunch, armature well developed, consisting of 6 circular spiny pads; anterior part of the enteric valve consisting of 6 oval cushions, each composed of about 50–80 scales, with a fringe of spines on the posterior margin. The mesenteron–proctodeum junction forms a small bulb, covered by the proctodeum, slightly elongated into a short, distinct mixed segment; hindgut P1 wide.

/genus/planicapritermes/.note: The original explicitly states Imago: Unknown, so no alate section is given; soldier and worker mandibles after pp. 317–319 and Figs. 45–46. The genus is monotypic (only P. planiceps).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A group of Neotropical Termitinae soldiers with asymmetrical snapping mandibles. Most closely related to Neocapritermes and possibly derived from it: the worker–alate mandibles of the two are completely identical (the alate of this genus is unknown, so the alate cannot be compared); the soldier resembles Neocapritermes, but the head is extremely flattened, the posterior margin trilobed, the antennae 14-segmented (15–16 in the latter), the pronotum far narrower than the head, and the tibial spur formula 2:2:2 (3:2:2 in the latter, only N. bodkini 2:2:2).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and pronotum with moderate setae. Head extremely flattened, the sides convergent anteriorly; posterior margin trilobed, the median lobe not very prominent; fontanelle small and round; frontal gland absent. Labrum asymmetrical, curved around or enveloping the mandibular bases, tongue-shaped, the sides convergent anteriorly to a blunt apex. Mandibles asymmetrical: left mandible strongly curved at mid-length, the base thick, the outer region with ridges and concavities, the anterior region spatulate, the apex blunt, the inner basal region with a tooth-like process fitting into the corresponding notch of the right mandible; right mandible straight. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum far narrower than the head, the anterior lobe very slightly upturned. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2; mid tibia without spines.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in Fig. 46: left mandible with a small apical tooth, a long posterior margin behind the fused 1st+2nd marginal teeth, and a well-developed 3rd marginal tooth; right mandible with a straight posterior margin behind the 2nd marginal tooth and an acute angle between the 1st and 2nd marginal teeth.

/genus/polyspathotermes/.note: The accepted manuscript gives only the worker enteric valve (EVA) as a generic character; there is no generic text for the soldier or alate; the source's Species included lists 8 species (including P. katangensis transferred from Megagnathotermes), and the generic name comes from Greek polys (many) + spathos (spatula). The page numbers of the accepted manuscript (p. 15–16, lines 347–362) differ from those of the published version (Syst. Entomol. 46(1): 224–238).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve of this genus is of two forms: either only the three principal cushions (PC3, PC4, PC5) bear yellow to brown sclerotised spatulate plates at their ends, or all six principal cushions end in sclerotised spatulate plates. The source assigns the genus to clade IV and to the oblectatus and sulcifrons types of Josens & Deligne (2019), and includes the former Megagnathotermes katangensis.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The enteric valve has six principal cushions (PCs); sclerotised spatulate plates occur either only at the ends of PC3, PC4 and PC5 or at the ends of all six principal cushions, and are yellow to brown.

/genus/porotermes/.note: The usable generic characters are concentrated in the key to the genera of the subfamily and the comparison on p. 144; body length, number of antennal segments and pronotal proportions are species-level measurements of P. adamsoni and are marked as species level. The worker section is the original's statement about the caste in the subfamily and is not peculiar to this genus; that qualification must be retained when citing it.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The key to the genera of the subfamily given in the original: an alate without ocelli, without an empodium (the pad between the claws) and with 5-segmented cerci belongs to this genus, whereas one with ocelli, with an empodium and with 2-segmented cerci belongs to Calotermes; a soldier with long, 5-segmented cerci belongs to this genus, and one with short, 2-segmented cerci to Calotermes. The soldier is easily confused with Stolotermes, but the latter is smaller, with a flatter head and body, a small heart-shaped pronotum, and eyes bearing ommatidia.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Ocelli absent; empodium absent; cerci 5-segmented. Species level (P. adamsoni): antennae 15 to 17 segments; body length with wings 14–15 mm, body length 7–8 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Cerci long, 5-segmented. Species level (P. adamsoni): antennae 16 to 18 segments; mandibles stout, the tooth formula the same in the three species; pronotum about 1.5 times as wide as the head.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The subfamily has no true worker caste; the worker function is performed by immature stages of the alate (and possibly of the soldier); the generic characters of this worker-nymph are the same as those of the soldier.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate and the soldier both have a spine on the outer side of the mid tibia near the distal spur, which distinguishes them from Neotermes and other genera; the wing venation resembles Neotermes, but the media is more weakly sclerotised.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Usually dark brown; eyes usually small, 0.25–0.50 mm in diameter; ocelli touching the compound eye or 0.01–0.04 mm from it; antennae 13–19 segments; mandibles resembling those of Kalotermes; pronotum wider than the head; each main vein arising independently at the wing suture; radius branching in some species; radial sector with 7–8 branches, the first branch about 1/5 of the wing length from the wing suture; media more weakly sclerotised than the radial sector and closer to it; cubitus weak, unsclerotised; tibial spur formula 3:3:3; a dark spine on the outer side of the mid tibia, slightly shorter than the distal spur; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long; frons with a median concavity in some species, forming slight lateral swellings, inclined downwards towards the clypeus at about 25–30°; eyes mostly colourless, slightly pigmented in P. pishinensis; antennae 11–18 segments, the third not specialised and not strongly sclerotised, longer or shorter than the fourth; pronotum narrower than, equal to or wider than the head, the anterior margin broadly and shallowly concave or angular; tibial spur formula 3:3:3; an additional spine on the outer side of the mid tibia near the distal spur.

/genus/postsubulitermes/.note: The alate is taken mainly from Sands's generic characters (the mandibles of his queen specimen were not dissected, hence the absence of mandibular characters), and Emerson's original description supplements the pilosity, head shape, pronotum and meso- and metanotal characters. The soldier and worker sections combine Sands and Emerson, without separate annotation where the two agree; the measurements are those of Emerson. Sands considered the genus close to Afrosubulitermes, the evenly rounded margin of the soldier labrum being a further reduction of the trilobed labrum of Eutermellus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Established by Emerson 1960 and supplemented by Sands 1965: the soldier is monomorphic, the nasus slenderly cylindrical, tapering forwards to a fine point, the mandibles without a point, the anterior margin of the labrum evenly rounded, the head capsule hardly constricted behind the antennal fossae and slightly raised at the base of the nasus, the antennae 12-segmented, the setae very few (a pair on the dorsum of the head, one to two pairs at the base of the nasus, a few at its tip); in the alate the postclypeus is moderately arched, twice as wide as long, its anterior margin wavy and convex in the middle, the fontanelle a long Y, the compound eyes not projecting beyond the sides of the head, the pilosity extremely fine and sparse (3 hairs on each eye, 2 pairs on the vertex, 1 pair on the postclypeus), the lateral margins of the pronotum contracted posteriorly, whose length is less than two-thirds of its width; in the worker the apical tooth of the left mandible is much longer than the first marginal tooth (index 2.63), the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire and concave, the gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar process is extremely narrow, the second marginal tooth of the right mandible is missing, and the molar plate has a weak basal concavity, a weak anterior and a strong rounded posterior ridge, and no transverse ridges. Emerson adds: the head is dark brown and the pronotum yellow, in striking contrast; the soldier head is 1.39–1.53 mm long and 0.55–0.60 mm wide, the pronotum 0.34–0.39 mm, the hind tibia 0.71–0.79 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head and postclypeus bear sparse short hairs and several long setae; the pronotum bears several long setae near its lateral and posterior margins and a few short hairs on its surface; the abdominal tergites and sternites both bear numerous long setae or hairs of nearly equal length. The ocelli are large and distinct, separated from the compound eyes by less than half their width, slightly larger than the antennal fossae. The fontanelle is pale brown, elongate, forked at its end, set in a shallow depression on the vertex. The postclypeus is about half as long as wide (0.18 mm × 0.36 mm). The lateral margins of the pronotum are fairly straight and contracted posteriorly, the posterior angles rounded, the posterior margin slightly concave; the posterior angles of the mesonotum are slightly less than a right angle and its median concavity slightly greater than a right angle; the posterior angles of the metanotum are more rounded, about equal to a right angle, and its median concavity greater than that of the mesonotum. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. The antennae of the specimen are broken off.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Setae and short hairs are scattered over the face of the head; there are several hairs at the tip of the frontal projection but no short hairs in the middle or at its base. The pronotum bears a few short hairs, more numerous anteriorly. Each abdominal tergite bears a row of posterior marginal setae and scattered hairs about one-third their length; the setae and hairs of the sternites are both longer than those of the tergites, the hairs about half as long as the setae. The head is oval in dorsal view, the frontal projection slender and slightly tapering forwards, a slight constriction visible behind the antennal fossae (both in dorsal and in lateral view). Antennae 12-segmented. The mandibles are without a point. The anterior margin of the pronotum is very shallowly and indistinctly concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. The head is dark brown and the pronotum yellow, in striking contrast.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical tooth of the mandibles is proportionally longer than in Afrosubulitermes and Verrucositermes; in the left mandible the third marginal tooth is indistinct, the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire and concave, and the gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar process is extremely narrow; in the right mandible the second marginal tooth is missing, the molar plate has a weak concavity near the base, the anterior ridge weak and the posterior ridge strong and rounded, and there are no transverse ridges. Left mandibular index 2.63.

/genus/proboscitermes/.note: Only this line of Emerson's (1928) key was read; the original text of Sjöstedt 1924 was not obtainable, so measurements, mandibles and antennae are not given, and no caste section other than the soldier is provided.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The anterior part of the soldier head extends into a very large and conspicuous nasus, and the sides of the head are rounded; Tuberculitermes also has a large nasus but its head is rectangular, while Orthotermes has no nasus and the sides of its head are straight.

/genus/procapritermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 113). The list of four species is on the same page: atypus n. sp., minutus Hav. and setiger Hav., all from Borneo; the discussion of systematic relationships begins in the lower part of p. 113 (the author states that this genus is in fact formed by slight differentiation from the Protocapritermes subgenus of Mirotermes). zh_name provisionally uses the Latin name (marked '—' in the batch).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, containing 3 species, all from Borneo: Procapritermes atypus (new species), P. minutus (Hav.) and P. setiger (Hav.). The alate has antennae of 14 segments, markedly incrassate towards the apex, the last segment bearing a pointed appendage at its tip; the soldier has a long rectangular head without a frontal projection, the mandibles slender and asymmetric, their curvature of the same type as in Capritermes but very weak, with a sharp, strong tooth above the basal segment; the worker has a rather small, broadly oval head, mandibles with a large apical tooth, and antennae of 14 segments. The original text notes that this genus is in fact a genus formed by slight differentiation from the Protocapritermes subgenus of Mirotermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, narrowed anteriorly. Compound eyes relatively small. Ocelli separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their diameter. Clypeal base shorter than half its width, flatly convex, without a median line. Mandibular tooth 1 large. Antennae of 14 segments, markedly incrassate towards the apex, the last segment with a pointed appendage at its tip. Posterior parts of the meso- and metanotum narrowed, with an emargination at the end. Wing membrane with fine punctures (spines). Media close to the cubitus. Abdomen slender. Without styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head slender, rectangular, without a frontal projection, relatively flat, truncate progressively anteriorly. Frontal gland opening small, fully visible from above, surrounded by sparse hairs (a vestigial hair ring). Clypeal base very narrow, bounded by the large mandibular basal segments. Labrum much longer than wide, either symmetrical or distinctly deflected to the right. Mandibles slender and asymmetric, the outer basal margin of the left mandible fairly strongly concave; their curvature of the same type as in Capritermes, but only very weakly expressed. A sharp, strong tooth above the basal segment. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2 and about as long as segment 4. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head rather small, broadly oval. Clypeal base with a very weakly convex posterior margin and a straight anterior margin, shorter (much shorter) than half its width, fairly strongly convex. Mandibles with a large apical tooth. Antennae of 14 segments. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped.

/genus/procornitermes/.note: The generic redescription follows Cancello (1986), who synonymised Triacitermes with this genus and regarded P. cornutus as a junior synonym of P. lespesii. The original is in Portuguese and the diacritics were lost in the extracted text.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head rectangular or nearly rectangular, slightly or markedly narrowed anteriorly, oval to pyriform; frontal tube slightly conical in dorsal view, of medium length (reaching the postclypeus) or longer (reaching the anteclypeus), rarely reaching the labrum; labrum circular or trifid, often with a white spot in the centre; postmentum straight, narrowed at the base, or widened in its anterior half and then abruptly narrowed; antennae 13–15-segmented, segment 3 or 4 often with traces of annulation; tibial spur formula 2:2:2 or 3:2:2. Alate head oval, fontanelle oval or circular, situated in a flat or depressed area, sometimes projecting; ocelli kidney-shaped or crescent-shaped; forewing 13.30–19.16 mm long and 3.44–5.00 mm wide.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular or nearly rectangular, slightly or markedly narrowed towards the frons, oval or pyriform. Frontal tube slightly conical in dorsal view, of medium length and reaching the postclypeus, or longer and reaching the anteclypeus, rarely reaching the labrum; apex of the frontal tube directed forwards or slightly turned upwards. Labrum circular or trifid, its apex rounded or pointed, a white spot constantly present in the central area. Postmentum straight, either narrowed at the base or widened in the anterior half and then abruptly narrowed. Antennae 13–15-segmented, segment 3 or 4 with traces of annulation. Anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum with or without a notch. Head yellow to orange; labrum and frontal tube may contrast with the head colour or be concolorous with it.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibular morphology is the main diagnostic basis for the genus. In the right mandible A is slightly larger than M1, the anterior margin arcuate and the posterior margin straight; M1 triangular with straight edges; M2 much smaller than M1, running straight from the tip to the molar plate. In the left mandible A is about as large as M1+2, the anterior margin arcuate and the posterior margin straight; M3 is “septum”-like, ending before Prm and running straight; Dm may be visible between M3 and Prm and/or behind it, well developed in all species. The shape and size of the molar plate vary between species; the first stripe (1ª estria) lies behind the apical thickened area and is clearly visible, and the shape of its striped area is a species-level character.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head oval; fontanelle oval or circular, situated in a flat or slightly depressed area, sometimes projecting; Y-shaped suture visible or not. Compound eyes nearly circular, 0.27–0.44 mm in diameter, the distance from the eye to the lower margin of the head 0.07–0.19 mm. Ocelli kidney-shaped or crescent-shaped (in dorsal view), 0.29–0.49 mm from the fontanelle. Labrum circular; antennae 13–15-segmented, segment 3 or 4 sometimes with traces of annulation, the segments subequal in length, or one of segments 2, 3 and 4 shorter. Postclypeus strongly arched, with a distinct median suture; anteclypeus V-shaped at the centre. Posterior lobe of the pronotum with or without a notch; forewing 13.30–19.16 mm long and 3.44–5.00 mm wide, the wing surface covered with very short setae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate resembles Cryptotermes in all respects; the soldier has longer mandibles and a less shield-like frons, and the anterior margin of the pronotum is straight, not serrate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Reddish brown to brown; eyes small, 0.34–0.39 mm in diameter, ocelli touching the compound eye; antennae 16–18 segments; the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible much smaller at the base than the third marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth about 1.5 times the posterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth; molar plate of the right mandible distinctly shorter than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum as wide as or wider than the head; radial sector with 4–5 branches, the first branch at about 1/3 of the wing length; media weak, unsclerotised, lying between the radial sector and the cubitus over the proximal half of the wing, curving towards the radial sector at about the middle of the wing or further back; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long, the sides almost parallel; front inclined downwards towards the clypeus at about 45°; a distinct ridge between the frons and the vertex, with a shallow U-shaped notch in the middle of the ridge in P. fryeri and a few species, the ridge weaker or absent in some species; two pairs of angular processes on the anterior sides of the head: one pair near the lateral margins of the clypeus, in front of the antennal sockets, the other extending forwards and downwards from the lower sides of the mentum; in some species the upper or lower processes are weaker; eyes colourless; antennae 11–16 segments, the third usually long and club-shaped, longer than the second, the third shorter than the second in P. rapae; mandibles 1.28–1.58 mm long, thick at the base, with a tubercle, toothed in most species, toothless in P. fryeri; pronotum as wide as the head, distinctly transversely arched, the anterior margin shallowly or deeply concave; femora not swollen.

/genus/procubitermes/.note: Emerson (1928) treated the genus as a subgenus of Mirotermes (type species Procubitermes arboricola (Sjöstedt)) and provisionally included the groups Noditermes, Unguitermes, Lepidotermes and others that Sjöstedt (1924) had separated. The generic characters given here are compiled from his soldier/worker/alate material of the Congolese Mirotermes (Procubitermes) niapuensis and M. (P.) undulans; for the modern delimitation of the genus and its synonyms see Krishna et al. (2013).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head rectangular, the sides straight and nearly parallel, without sharp gular processes; labrum bifurcate or deeply cleft; each mandible with a small tooth near the base, not evenly curved (the left mandible elbow-shaped, the right evenly curved); antennae 14-segmented. Alate fontanelle slit-like or small and white, antennae 15-segmented, posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with small notches. Similar in many respects to the subgenus Cubitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, yellow to red-yellow, the sides straight and nearly parallel; gula without a sharp process. Labrum bifurcate (in niapuensis the tips are at varying distances apart; in undulans deeply cleft, the tips sharper). Each mandible with a small tooth near the base; in niapuensis the mandibles are slightly elbow-shaped rather than evenly curved, in undulans the left mandible has two elbow bends and the right is evenly curved. Antennae 14-segmented (in niapuensis segment 3 longer than segment 2, segment 2 equal to segment 4; in undulans segment 2 equal to segment 3, segment 4 shorter than segment 3). Pronotal anterior margin slightly or faintly concave. Measurements (mm): niapuensis head length with mandibles 3.26, head width 1.37, antennae 2.20, pronotum 0.31×0.70, hind tibia 1.00, left mandible 1.71; undulans head length with mandibles 3.05, head width 1.10, antennae 2.00, pronotum 0.26×0.67, hind tibia 0.89, left mandible 1.57.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 14-segmented. niapuensis head width 0.94 mm, hind tibia 1.00 mm; undulans head width 0.86 mm, hind tibia 0.72 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: niapuensis: head mid-dark red-brown, fontanelle slit-like and pale; antennae 15-segmented (segment 3 very small, segment 2 equal to segment 4); eyes medium-sized; ocelli 0.14 mm long, oval, facing sideways, 1.10 mm from the eye; postclypeus slightly paler than the head, with a narrow dark median line; pronotum slightly paler, posterior margin deeply concave; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with small sharp notches (angle less than a right angle). Measurements (mm): head length 1.22, head width 1.19, antennae 1.78, eye diameter 0.31, pronotum 0.59×1.05, hind tibia 1.16; posterior length 20.00, abdominal width 3.50. undulans: head yellow-brown, oval; fontanelle small and white, with three muscle-attachment scars in front of it; antennal segment 3 about twice segment 2 or segment 4 (showing signs of subdivision); eyes medium-sized, close to the lower margin; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the eye greater than their width; postclypeus slightly paler, with a faint median line; pronotum slightly paler, posterior margin concave; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum very narrowly concave. Measurements (mm): head length 1.23, head width 1.10, eye diameter 0.38, pronotum 0.57×0.97, hind tibia 1.03; posterior length 19.00, abdominal width 3.00.

/genus/profastigitermes/.note: The original describes only the soldier for this genus, not the worker or the alate, so only a Soldier section is given; for the position of the postmentum and of the vertex hump see Emerson 1960 fig. 15.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Above the fontanelle opening and slightly behind it the vertex forms a rounded hump (the hump of Fastigitermes projects further forward); the postmentum narrows from below and is narrowest at a conspicuous bidentate projection, whereas the corresponding projection in Fastigitermes is a single, sharp backward-directed spine.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head surface is sparsely covered with setae, with a large tuft of long hairs around the fontanelle opening and a few setae near the anterior margin of the labrum and on the anterior margin of the postmentum; the postmentum narrows from below and bears a bidentate projection about a quarter of its length in front of the middle of the posterior margin, with a slightly concave ridge between its two points in anterior view.

/genus/prohamitermes/.note: Published in the original as a new genus (n. g.), with diagnoses for all three castes. The German genus diagnosis is rewritten, not a verbatim translation.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate, soldier and worker all known. Alate: head broadly oval, compound eyes large and flatly convex, not projecting, ocelli level with the frontal surface, fontanelle distinct and rather far back, postclypeal basis far shorter than half its width; antennae 15-segmented. Soldier: head oval, slightly narrowing anteriorly, eyeless, fontanelle very weak, labrum nearly triangular without a hyaline apical point, mandibles sickle-curved with 2 small teeth on each side at the middle, submentum strongly humped at the middle; antennae 14-segmented; fore tibia with 3 spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each. Worker: postclypeal basis lenticular, rather strongly arched, antennae 14-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head (rather) broad, oval, slightly longer than wide; compound eyes rather large, flatly convex, not projecting; ocelli level with the frontal surface (inner margin not raised), distance to the compound eye less than their diameter; fontanelle distinct, rather far back. Postclypeal basis far shorter than half its width, posterior margin only slightly convex, anterior margin straight, nearly flat. Labrum at the middle wider than at the base, without a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type armature, base not excessively projecting. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and as long as segment 4. Pronotum small, saddle very weak, anterior margin straight; emargination of the posterior margin of the mesonotum wider than that of the metanotum; posterior angles rounded. Forewing scale slightly longer than the hindwing scale; wings covered with fine hairs; in the forewing the media arises directly from the wing scale, in the hindwing the media arises from the radial sector. Cerci short, without styli; dealate individual no larger than the soldier; lateral margins of the female abdomen finely and densely longitudinally wrinkled; glandular setae rather sparse in both sexes; apical spur 3 of the tibia reduced.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head oval, slightly narrowing anteriorly, flatly convex, flattening anteriorly towards the labrum; eyeless; cranial sutures invisible. Fontanelle very weak, about the middle of the head; fontanelle gland small. Postclypeus short and flat. Labrum nearly triangular, without a hyaline apical point. Mandibles sickle-curved, sharply pointed, base large, middle rather short, apex long, its base slightly tooth-like widened; each side of the middle with 2 small teeth; each side of the base with 1 small, rather wide molar prominence. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 only slightly longer than segment 2, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 4. Submentum strongly humped (or bullate) at the middle. Pronotum rather small, upfolded in a very strong saddle (almost a right angle), anterior lobe as long as the posterior part; cerci short, without styli. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head oval, widest at the antennae; fontanelle rather far back. Postclypeal basis lenticular, shorter than half its width, rather strongly arched. Toothed inner margin of the left mandible shortened, molar region strongly projecting, roughly as in Hamitermes. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 as long as segment 3 and slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum with a strong saddle, anterior lobe longer than the posterior part.

/genus/promirotermes/.note: Emerson (1928) treated the genus as a subgenus of Mirotermes; the account here is compiled solely from the soldier of his Congolese Mirotermes (Promirotermes) orthoceps (new species, type locality Banana); the generic alate and worker were not described. For the modern genus see Krishna et al. (2013).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head markedly narrowing anteriorly, the sides nearly straight; labral anterior margin concave, ending in two points; mandibles long and slender, black, suited to snapping; antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 very long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow, strongly narrowing anteriorly, the sides nearly straight; antennae 14-segmented (segment 3 very long, about 0.22–0.32 mm, segments 2 and 4 about equal in length); labral anterior margin concave, ending in two points; mandibles long and slender, black, suited to snapping; pronotal anterior margin slightly concave. Measurements (mm): head length with mandibles 3.00–3.10, head width 1.10–1.17, antennae 2.20, pronotum 0.27×0.55, hind tibia 1.27, left mandible 1.77–1.84. Distinguished from M. bellicosi (pronotal anterior margin deeply cleft), M. gracilipes (larger, the sides of the head less straight) and M. holmgreni (frontal prominence more raised, the sides of the head not straight).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate, with the media of the forewing weakly sclerotised and closer to the radial sector, can be distinguished from Incisitermes and Marginitermes; the soldier differs from Marginitermes in that the latter has a much longer third antennal segment, a more distinct frontal ridge, long mandibles and serrate anterolateral corners of the pronotum, and differs from Incisitermes in that the latter has a dorsoventrally flattened head, its front inclined downwards at about 20°, and lacks a frontal ridge.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pale yellow; eyes rather small, 0.39–0.43 mm in diameter, ocelli touching the compound eye; antennae 17–18 segments; the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible slightly shorter at the base than the third marginal tooth; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly longer than the molar plate; pronotum slightly wider than the head; wing membrane transparent; radius of the forewing simple, extending to about half the wing length; radial sector with 4–6 branches, the first branch at about half the wing length; media more weakly sclerotised than the radial sector, parallel to and rather close to the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior part of the head nearly black, fading posteriorly to yellow; sides of the head parallel, the anterior part slightly truncate, inclined downwards towards the clypeus at about 45°; dorsolateral corners of the frons slightly raised; a very weak ridge between the frons and the vertex; the sides above the antennal sockets rough; no angular processes above or below the antennal sockets; eye spots distinct, colourless; antennae 13–14 segments, the third longer than the second or the fourth, club-shaped; mandibles strong, with a distinct basal tubercle; pronotum as wide as the head, the anterior margin slightly raised and deeply concave, the sides and posterior margin rather rounded; femora stout and short.

/genus/protermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 24–26). The original divides the genus into the two subgenera Allodontermes and Protermes s. str.; the alate paragraph describes only the subgenus Allodontermes (end of p. 24–p. 25), the soldier paragraph treats both subgenera together, the two forms of labrum and left mandible being distinguished by figs 7 and 8; the lists of subgenera and species are not included in the description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 divided the genus into the two subgenera Allodontermes and Protermes s. str., 3 species being known at the time, all from Africa. Alate antennae 19 segments; soldier antennae 14–17 segments; worker antennae 16–17 segments. Worker compound eyes either reduced or very distinct and even pigmented; pronotum very small, less than half the head width, anterior lobe upturned. The apex of the labrum and the tooth-like expansion at the apex of the left mandible differ between the two subgenera (shown in figs 7 and 8 of the original).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: This paragraph is headed Allodontermes in the original and reads as follows. Head broadly oval. Compound eyes large, strongly projecting. Ocelli broadly oval, lateral, very close to the compound eyes; spiral in dorsal view, frons flat and depressed. Frontal gland opening small, bright. Base of clypeus bright, rather strongly arched, at least as long as half its width, posterior margin strongly convexly curved, anterior margin straight, the sides reaching the mandibular bases; apex relatively well developed. Labrum longer than broad, narrowing slightly anteriorly, with a narrow transverse chitinous band in the middle. Left mandible with typical Termes-type dentition; right mandible deviating from the Termes type, with a much reduced second tooth, transitional from the Leucotermes type to the Termes type. Antennae 19 segments, third segment shorter than the second and fourth, fourth slightly shorter than the second. Pronotum about as long as half its width, slightly narrower than the head with the mandibles, flat; meso- and metanotum broadly incised. Forewing scale distinctly larger than the hindwing scale, but not reaching the base of the latter. Radius rather weak, soon merging with the anterior wing margin; radial sector reaching the wing apex; media of forewing separate from the wing scale, media of hindwing departing from the base of the radial sector, the media of both wings close to the cubitus and more or less branched towards the apex. Cubitus many-branched, wing membrane hyaline, slightly reticulate. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Cerci short; male with a stylus, female with exudatory hairs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel, both ends very weakly narrowing, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening very indistinct, frontal gland small. Clypeus relatively short, projecting slightly anteriorly, mandibular bases very stout. Labrum in the Allodontermes form (fig. 7) longer, apex sharp and hyaline, in the Protermes form (fig. 8) relatively short, apex rounded. Apex of the left mandible with a tooth-like expansion at its base, with or without a very small tooth tubercle; left mandible with 3 more or less distinct teeth; right mandible with a large tooth before the middle, sometimes with a reduced tooth between this tooth and the apex. Antennae 14–17 segments, second segment longer than the third. Postmentum with parallel sides.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head relatively large, parallel-sided oval, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening indistinct, head sutures not visible. Base of clypeus rather arched, transversely oval, rather large, not quite reaching the mandibular bases. Compound eyes either reduced or very distinct and even pigmented; mandibular bases very large, right mandible with traces of a second tooth. Antennae 16–17 segments, second segment longer than the third, third segment equal to or slightly longer than the fourth. Pronotum small, less than half the head width, with an upturned anterior lobe. At least the fore and mid tibiae with lateral spines, fore tibia with 3 apical spurs. Styli present.

/genus/protocapritermes/.note: The original is a German OCR, and its erroneous forms are kept as they stand (e.g. siehtbar / Vorspriuiges); later revisions were not read here, so only key-level characters are given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The frontal projection is very inconspicuous; the fontanelle is clearly visible from above and is not hidden beneath the frontal projection; the labrum is of more or less equal width, its length distinctly greater than its width; the mandibles are slightly irregularly curved. Holmgren (1912) used these characters to separate it from Mirotermes s. str., in which the frontal projection is distinct and the fontanelle is concealed beneath it.

/genus/protohamitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 77–78). The original explicitly writes 'Soldat unbekannt' (soldier unknown), so only the alate and worker sections are given; the worker section begins on the last line of p. 77 and continues on the first line of p. 78. The original describes a new genus and species, Protohamitermes globiceps n. sp.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus, with only the species globiceps, from Sarawak, Borneo. The left mandible has the Leucotermes-type dentition (4 teeth before the basal segment), on which basis Holmgren placed the genus in the Hamitermes branch and considered its position in that branch fairly primitive. The alate is brown and densely hairy, the wings fairly short and hairy; antennae of 14 segments; worker antennae of 13 segments. Soldier unknown.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brown, densely hairy, the wings fairly short and hairy. Head very strongly broadly convex, slightly depressed around the frontal gland opening. Compound eyes medium-sized, fairly strongly convex; ocelli relatively small, separated from the compound eyes by more than one eye diameter. Frontal gland opening behind the middle of the head, large, dark. Clypeal base very short and flat, without a longitudinal line, the apical piece large. Left mandible with the Leucotermes-type dentition, 4 teeth before the basal segment; right mandible with only 3 anterior teeth, of which the apical is far shorter than the others. Antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 small. Pronotum narrower than the head; the emargination of the posterior margin of the mesonotum wider than that of the metanotum. Forewing scale slightly larger than the hindwing scale; media with 1–2 apical branches, cubitus with 12–18 branches; all veins distinct, the inner 5–7 thickened. Cerci thick and short; without styli; tarsi short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Densely hairy and setose. Head round, sometimes even wider than long, thick, slightly depressed in the middle. Frontal gland opening large, sometimes dark. Clypeal base short and flat. Mandibular basal segments large, mandibles as in the alate. Antennae of 13 segments, fairly thick, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and segment 4 longer than segment 3. Pronotum short, saddle-shaped, the anterior margin not concave. Cerci short and thick, without styli. Tarsi short. Abdomen thick.

/genus/psammotermes/.note: The original publication of the genus (Desneux 1902, Saharan material) is held locally only as a 403 page with no text and cannot be used; all the characters given here come from the genus-level comparison made by Emerson (1950) when describing Glossotermes, cover only the soldier and do not include the alate or the worker; reliability is moderate. The account must not be extended to other castes on this basis.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparison with Glossotermes brings out the soldier characters of this genus: head and body with numerous long hairs; mandibles more curved, both with coarse serrations at mid-length; left mandible without an inner groove at the base, the basal part proportionally larger and the apical part smaller; the suture between the postclypeus and the frons indistinct; labrum large and broad, without a transverse pale band, the apex sharper and without a hyaline margin; postmentum relatively broader at its narrowest point; eye spots indistinct; more antennal segments; anterior margin of the pronotum without lobe-like processes; femora stouter; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. On this basis the original considers the soldier of this genus more primitive in its mandibles, antennae and tibial spur formula.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The soldier bears numerous long hairs all over; mandibles curved, both with coarse serrations at mid-length; left mandible without an inner groove at the base; labrum large and broad, the apex pointed, without a hyaline margin; antennal segments more numerous; anterior margin of the pronotum without lobe-like processes; femora stout; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/genus/pseudacanthotermes/.note: Sjöstedt (1924) split the former genus Acanthotermes, keeping the type species acanthothorax alone in the nominotypical subgenus and assigning most of the other species to Pseudacanthotermes; Emerson (1928) regarded it as a subgenus of Acanthotermes. The generic characters given here are compiled from the major soldier and the alate of the type species Acanthotermes (Pseudacanthotermes) spiniger; Emerson stated that he could not distinguish the subspecies kohli and lujae of spiniger. For the modern delimitation of the genus see Krishna et al. (2013).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The key difference from the nominotypical subgenus Acanthotermes is the absence of outwardly projecting spines on the sides of the mesonotum and metanotum (present in Acanthotermes s. str.). Major soldier with black mandibles, the left mandible coarsely toothed; pronotal anterior margin with two large spines, the sides sharp and converging posteriorly. The genus as a whole thrives in both rainforest and savanna, building large fungus combs in the nest.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head rectangular, red-yellow-brown; antennae 19–21-segmented; labrum broad, with a hyaline tip; mandibles black, the left mandible coarsely toothed; short hairs around the fontanelle, with a spine in front; the sides of the mesonotum and metanotum sharp but without lateral spines; pronotal anterior margin with two large spines, the sides sharp and converging posteriorly. Measurements (mm): head length 3.67–4.00, head width 1.83–2.10, pronotum (including spines) 1.00, pronotum at mid-length 1.67, pronotum width 1.30–1.60, hind tibia 2.00–2.20, left mandible 1.33–1.37.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, mandibles yellow with black tips; antennae 23-segmented (segment 2 longer than segment 3, segments 3 and 4 equal in length); eyes relatively small, their distance from the lower margin equal to their distance from the ocelli; ocelli elongate seen from above, oval seen from the side, their distance from the eye greater than their diameter; labrum yellow; postclypeus yellow, contrasting strongly with the head, with a median line; pronotal anterior margin concave in the middle, the sides straight and converging posteriorly, posterior margin broadly concave; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum broadly concave; wing membrane pale and transparent, the costa, radius and basal veins opaque brown to yellow. Measurements (mm): length with wings 29.00, length without wings 15.00, head length 2.78, head width 2.20–2.30, antennae 3.80, eye diameter 0.53–0.55, pronotum 1.27×2.00–2.20, hind tibia 3.00, left mandible 1.33, forewing 22.00–23.00×5.50; posterior length 52.00, abdominal width 17.00.

/genus/pseudomicrotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 126–127). The lower half of p. 127 is a point-by-point comparison of Pseudomicrotermes and Microtermes together with a discussion of systematic relationships; only the generic-character paragraphs were used here.
