The original work places this genus under the 'Pseudomicrotermes-Reihe'; the Chinese name for the genus was assigned by the batch.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912, with the single species Pseudomicrotermes alboniger (Wasm.) from the Congo; a synonym in part of Mirotermes (Wasmann 1911). Originally placed in Microtermes, it was separated because morphological examination showed only a habit-based resemblance to Microtermes; according to Holmgren's comparative table, the alate of this genus is 'very small', with a very large head far wider than the pronotum, and the soldier head is rectangular and much longer than wide, differing from Microtermes in the relative length of the clypeal base, the length-to-width ratio of the labrum, the mandibular dentition and the wing venation (presence or absence of an accessory vein, reticulation). The soldier labrum is lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide; the mandibles are sabre-shaped and curved, the outer basal margin not concave; antennae of 13–14 segments; cerci unusually long, without styli.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very small in size. Head very large, fairly strongly convex, thick, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Compound eyes medium-sized, flat. Ocelli small, separated from the compound eyes by hardly more than their diameter, facing fully laterally, their inner margin slightly raised. Frontal gland opening far back, with a dark spot in the middle. Transverse band very long. Clypeal base short, much shorter than half its width, slightly convex, posterior margin slightly concave, anterior margin straight. Labrum about as wide as long. Apical tooth of the mandibles slightly swollen. Antennae of 16 segments, incrassate towards the apex. Pronotum rather small, the anterior lobe incurved with a concave anterior margin; posterior margin concave. Posterior parts of the meso- and metanotum slightly pointed, with a rectangular emargination. Forewing scale slightly larger than the hindwing scale. Wing membrane transparent, with extremely fine punctures, without reticulation; veins very indistinct; media close to the cubitus, apparently only very weakly branched (simple?); cubitus with about 10 branches. Abdomen white. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with only 2. The 2nd tarsomere counted from the apex extended into a slender projection. Cerci fairly long. Without styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular with rounded corners, much longer than wide, thick. Frons slightly inclined. Frontal gland opening on the horizontal part of the head, near the edge of the inclined part. Labrum lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide, with a small transparent tip behind which a few setae arise. Mandibles sabre-shaped and curved, the outer basal margin not concave. Left mandible with a bilobed basal tooth and three very small but sharp teeth in the middle; the apex weak, microscopically serrate. Right mandible with two small teeth at the base and only a tooth-like blunt swelling in the middle. Antennae of 13–14 segments, incrassate towards the apex. Pronotum small, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe large with a deeply concave anterior margin. Cerci unusually long. Without styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head broadly oval, longer than wide. Frontal gland opening fairly far back. Clypeal base slightly shorter than half its width, posterior margin fairly strongly convex, anterior margin slightly concave. Mandibles as in the alate. Antennae of 15–16 segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior margin deeply concave. Cerci long. Without styli.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is closely related to Incisitermes and Marginitermes but can be distinguished by its large eyes (0.68–0.71 mm in diameter) and 20–21 antennal segments; the soldier is the largest in the family, with pigmented eyes, a nearly saddle-shaped pronotum and a sclerotised swelling at the base of the postmentum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brown; eyes large, 0.68–0.71 mm in diameter, ocelli touching the compound eye; antennae 20–21 segments; the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible equal in length at the base to the third marginal tooth, their posterior margins equal in length to the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible equal in length to the molar plate; pronotum as wide as the head; subcosta of the forewing long, unbranched; radial sector with 5–6 branches, the first branch at about 1/4 of the wing length; media weak, unsclerotised, lying between the radial sector and the cubitus, branched apically in some specimens; arolium always absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Largest in the family; head very large, the sides rounded; frons inclined gradually downwards from near the middle of the head; a median ridge on each side of the postclypeus, as in Rugitermes; an angular process below and in front of the antennal sockets, near the lateral base of the mandibles; eyes pigmented; antennae 17 segments, the third longer than the second and the fourth; mandibles long and thick, toothed, the basal tubercle distinct; a sclerotised swelling at the base of the postmentum; pronotum wider than the head, slightly saddle-shaped, the anterior margin deeply concave and covering the posterior part of the head, the anterolateral corners raised; mesothorax and metathorax with distinct wing buds; femora swollen.

/genus/quasitermes/.note: Only the verifiable characters in Emerson's (1950) soldier description and comparative diagnosis are given; no genus-level text on the alate or the worker was seen.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The labrum is almost asymmetrical, its lateral points short and sharp; the labrum of Mirocapritermes is more asymmetrical and more deeply forked, and its lateral points are longer and sharper (Emerson 1950).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head elongate and nearly quadrate, its sides parallel and slightly convex; the frontal projection points forward and is not very sharp (the quotation is interrupted here by the original page header); the labrum is longer than wide, its apex shallowly concave or angular; the mandibles are asymmetrical and adapted for snapping, the left mandible slightly undulate and the right slightly curved outwards.

/genus/rhadinotermes/.note: The generic characters are taken from Sands's genus-level Diagnosis; the body colour, indices and measurements are taken from his subsequent description of the species R. coarctatus and have been incorporated and identified as species-level data. The original genus-level diagnosis has only Imago and Soldier sections and no Worker section, so no worker section is given. Sands notes that the genus was separated from Coarctotermes, the soldiers of the two being similar but their phylogenetic positions different.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands placed the genus in the Procornitermes branch; the soldier head capsule is sharply constricted behind the antennal fossae, resembling Fulleritermes, but phylogenetically it is not close to Leptomyxotermes/Grallatotermes, belonging instead to a predominantly Neotropical clade containing Velocitermes, Tenuirostritermes and Diversitermes; its former placement in Coarctotermes was based only on soldier similarity. The soldier is monomorphic, the nasus conical, the mandibles with a small point, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part, the antennae 12-segmented; in the alate the left mandibular index is 0.32–0.36, the second marginal tooth is absent, the right molar plate bears 6–7 transverse ridges diminishing towards the base, the first forming a coarse tooth, and the fontanelle is a very narrow slit, hardly forked anteriorly. The generic name derives from the Greek rhadinos (tapering).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule very dark brown to pitch black, the postclypeus and antennae dark sepia-brown, the wings semitransparent pale brown; the posterior margin of the head behind the compound eyes is almost semicircular; the compound eyes do not protrude and are relatively small for the head capsule (W/E 3.4–3.8), slightly angular-oval; the ocelli are small, oval, separated from the compound eyes by about 1.5 times their own least diameter; the postclypeus is strongly arched, 2.2 times as wide as long, its anterior margin slightly concave; the antennae are 15-segmented, segments II, IV and V nearly equal in length, II thinner, III longer. Mandibles: the apical tooth of the left mandible is equal to or slightly shorter than the first marginal tooth, the distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth being about one-third of the distance between the first and third marginal teeth (index 0.32–0.36), the second marginal tooth is absent, and the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is entire; in the right mandible the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth are nearly equal, and the first marginal tooth bears a small accessory tooth proximally; the molar plate of the right mandible has a weak concavity at the base near the anterior margin, its posterior margin extended into a rounded ridge, the first transverse ridge forming a coarse tooth and the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base; the fontanelle is very narrow, slit-like, hardly forked anteriorly (more pronounced in the female), slightly paler to distinctly paler than the head colour.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. The nasus is conical. The mandibles are reduced, with a small point. The head capsule is sharply constricted behind the antennal fossae, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part. Antennae 12-segmented. Head capsule sepia-brown to pitch black, the nasus black with a reddish apex; the lateral contour of the head is raised and rounded behind the constriction and flatter before it; the nasus is equal to or shorter than the remainder of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal fossae; the nasus cone angle is 10–20°; antennal segment II is short, IV and V longer; setae are confined to 4 at the tip of the nasus, a pair on the dorsum of the head, and a few short curved hairs on the dorsum. Specimen no. 25: head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.17–1.39 mm, head width 0.54–0.66 mm, hind tibia 0.92–1.10 mm.

/genus/rhinotermes/.note: The generic characters are Hill's quotation of Holmgren's definition, given verbatim; the alate, soldier and worker passages all come from that quotation. The Australian species are placed in the subgenus Schedorhinotermes, so most of the species-level material recorded in the paper does not belong to the nominal subgenus of the genus; only generic and subgeneric statements were used here, and species-level characters of the Australian species were not mixed in.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier occurs in two forms, major and minor, both with a forked labrum; the major soldier has very stout and strong mandibles, the left with two strong teeth and the right with one, the bases not finely serrate; the minor soldier has relatively longer, narrower and straighter mandibles with narrower and sharper teeth, or reduced mandibles; the labrum is relatively short and broad in the major soldier and in the minor soldier extends beyond the mandibles, being forked and grooved at the tip, either rather broad or extremely narrow; antennae 14–17 segments; pronotum small, far narrower than the head; styli present. In the alate of the subgenus Rhinotermes s. str. the clypeus is strong and beak-shaped and covers the base of the labrum, the head is relatively large, and in the minor soldier the labrum is forked and the mandibles are reduced.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head almost circular; clypeus more or less strongly arched, with a median longitudinal groove; fontanelle open and relatively wide, situated anteriorly; antennae 20–22 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Occurring in two forms, major and minor, with a forked labrum. Major soldier: mandibles stout and very strong, the left with two strong teeth and the right with one, the mandibular bases without fine teeth; labrum relatively short and broad, forked and grooved at the tip. Minor soldier: mandibles relatively longer, narrower and straighter, with narrower and sharper teeth, or reduced; labrum extending beyond the mandibles, forked and grooved at the tip. Antennae 14–17 segments in both forms; pronotum small, far narrower than the head; styli present.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 16–18 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2; pronotum saddle-shaped.

/genus/rhynchotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, p. 55). In the original, Rhynchotermes is a subgenus of Armitermes (Untergattung), with no separate genus-level description: only three key characters (one each for the alate, soldier and worker) and one species, so each section is very short and does not go beyond what the key provides.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Established by Holmgren 1912 as a subgenus of Armitermes (Rhynchotermes n. subg.), at that time containing only the species nasutissimus (Mato Grosso, Paraguay, Bolivia). The differences from the other subgenera of the genus are given in the key: in the alate mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 are equal in size, the antennae have 14 segments and segment 3 is longer than the adjacent ones; in the soldier the mandibles are fairly robust and very strongly curved, with a quadrangular tooth in the middle, a very well-developed base bearing a sharp molar prominence, the 'nasus' (frontal tube) very long, and each fore coxa with a tooth-like projection; in the worker mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 are equal in length.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 equal in size; antennae of 14 segments, segment 3 longer than the adjacent ones.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles fairly robust, very strongly curved, with a quadrangular tooth in the middle; the base very strongly developed, with a sharp molar prominence. The 'nasus' (frontal tube) very long. Each fore coxa with a tooth-like projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibular tooth 1 and tooth 2 equal in length. The original gives only this single key character for the worker of the subgenus, without further description.

/genus/rinacapritermes/.note: The original records the alate as Not known; both the generic and the specific diagnoses rest on the soldier mandibles, labrum and pronotum, and on the worker mandibles and enteric valve. The two-column PDF extraction contained line misalignments; quotations were checked against the original sentences.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier antennae 15-segmented (14-segmented in Indocapritermes); anterior margin of the labrum nearly straight, with broad-based, stout and long anterolateral processes (labral lateral processes narrow-based, short and slender in the latter). Left mandible slightly longer and more slender relative to head length, its tip not broadly rounded (shorter and stouter in the latter, with a broadly rounded tip); right mandible with a sharp, upwardly directed apical blade (less sharp and nearly straight in the latter). Anterior lobe of the pronotum slightly raised, its anterior margin strongly convex and without a notch (anterior lobe not raised in the latter, anterior margin slightly convex to nearly straight, with a weak median notch); posterior margin nearly straight, not concave (slightly convex in the latter, with a slightly concave end). Worker antennae 14–15-segmented (13–14-segmented in the latter); ventral surface of the left molar plate with a small dentate projection (absent in the latter). The gut lacks Malpighian tubule nodules and P1 is short and tubular, consistent with the Pericapritermes group, hence its placement in that group (although its soldier antennae are 15-segmented rather than the 14-segmented condition usual in the group).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic, small. Head capsule nearly rectangular and broad in dorsal view, the anterolateral corners rounded, without tubercles; frontal surface steeply inclined in lateral view; fontanelle transverse; frontal gland large, the middle arm of the Y-shaped suture distinct only posteriorly. Antennae 15-segmented. Labrum not inflated, asymmetrical, anterior margin nearly straight, with broad-based, stout and long anterolateral processes (spine-like processes). Mandibles asymmetrical and stout: left mandible strongly twisted medially, its tip blunt, without a hook, not beak-like, the basal process sharp; right mandible blade-like, its tip sharp and directed upwards, the middle of the inner margin incurved, the basal half with a deep notch. Postmentum rod-shaped, more than half the head length, narrowed posteriorly into a waist. Pronotum saddle-shaped: anterior lobe raised and smaller than the posterior lobe, anterior margin convex, posterior margin nearly straight, neither margin notched. Mesonotum and metanotum narrower than the pronotum. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2 (dorsal spur of the protibia sometimes indistinct), tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate, cerci short, 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head capsule nearly circular in dorsal view, widest at the antennal bases; fontanellar plate translucent, circular; antennae 14–15-segmented; postclypeus inflated. Apical tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than the first marginal tooth, the posterior margin of the apical tooth concave; second marginal tooth indistinct, third marginal tooth reduced or merely a tooth scar, not separated from the first marginal tooth by a notch; ventral surface of the left molar plate with a small dentate projection; molar plate large, extending to the first marginal tooth. Apical tooth of the right mandible finger-like, larger than the first marginal tooth; posterior margin of the first marginal tooth slightly longer than its anterior margin; second marginal tooth short, its posterior margin incurved; molar plate longer than the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth, without ridges; cockroach notch present. Gut: crop spherical, of large volume; mixed segment present, the two pairs of Malpighian tubules arising together at its base, without Malpighian tubule nodules; P1 short, tubular; enteric valve armature thin, composed of 6 sharply triangular pads, each pad with small spine-like projections distributed over its median longitudinal area, the cuticle between the pads with similar but larger and more widely spaced projections.

/genus/roisinitermes/.note: At genus level only the alate and soldier sections are provided; the original does not treat the worker separately (the species has pseudergates and short-winged nymphs, and the nymphs only have species-level measurement tables), so no "Worker" or "Nymph" sections are set. No measurements are given at genus level; all measurements are species-level (alate Table 1, soldier Table 2).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The only genus in the Kalotermitidae with snapping mandibles: soldier mandibles slender and rod-like, the dentition extremely weak; the alate has no visible ocelli, also unique in the family. In Krishna's (1961) generic key the alate runs to couplet 2 (Epicalotermes) and the soldier to couplet 17 (Allotermes). The soldier mandibles are somewhat similar to the slender, nearly toothless mandibles of Allotermes (especially A. denticulatus), but in this genus the mandibles curve downwards in lateral view, which is unique among kalotermitids with forward-projecting mandibles; although the wing venation and dentition of the alate are very close to those of Epicalotermes, the soldier shares no major character with it.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum pale brownish orange, abdominal tergites paler, concolorous with the legs and labrum; postclypeus nearly transparent. Compound eyes medium-sized and prominent, oval, truncate near the antennal sockets, composed of about 85 ommatidia; ocelli neither pigmented nor with a cuticular projection, completely invisible. Antennae with more than 9 segments, segment formula 1>2=3=4<5 (species-level records 14–17 segments). Pronotum about 2 times as wide as its median length, lateral margins with several long setae and shorter setae. Forewing M and Cu stalked beyond the scale suture, the radial sector (Rs) with 5–6 anterior branches, the subcosta (Sc) closely appressed to the costa and difficult to distinguish; hindwing Rs and Cu stalked behind the suture. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi without an arolium. Anterior margin of the marginal tooth of the left mandible about 1.5 times the combined length of its posterior margin and the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible 1.4 times the length of the molar plate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Eye spots distinct, large and dark brown. Frons in dorsal view bilobed, covered with wrinkled longitudinal ridges, the wrinkles below the frons arranged longitudinally; the ends of the genae with small horn-like processes. Mandibles slender and rod-like, curving downwards in lateral view; dentition extremely weak, the basal swelling sharply projecting forwards.

/genus/roonwalitermes/.note: A monotypic genus (R. wadhwai Bose), endemic to north-eastern India (Meghalaya). Alate unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus endemic to north-eastern India. Soldier dimorphic: major soldier with the head capsule globular, not constricted behind the antennae, abruptly narrowed anteriorly into a long, narrow, cylindrical nasus almost as long as the head, antennae 13-segmented; minor soldier with the head pyriform, antennae 11–12-segmented. Worker antennae 13-segmented, postclypeus only slightly arched (about one-quarter as long as wide).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: head capsule globular, not constricted behind the antennae, entirely covered with microtrichia; the anterior part abruptly narrowed into a long, narrow, cylindrical nasus almost as long as the head; in lateral view the head capsule is slightly incurved at the base of the nasus; antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 long, narrow and clavate, segment 4 the shortest; mandibles vestigial, each with a short spine-like process and without teeth; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; legs slender, tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Minor soldier: head pyriform, not constricted behind the antennae; the anterior part narrowed into a long, narrow nasus, in lateral view with a weak swelling at its base; antennae 11–12-segmented; mandibles vestigial, with short spines; pronotum and legs as in the major soldier.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head nearly circular; fontanelle circular; coronal suture present; antennae 13-segmented, the segments short and broadly rounded; postclypeus weakly arched, about one-quarter as long as wide; mandibles with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth subequal in length to the first marginal tooth and the angle between them narrow; posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the left mandible long and straight, the second marginal tooth short and triangular, the margin between the second marginal tooth and the molar plate strongly incurved, the molar prominence small and pointed; posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible longer than its anterior margin, the second marginal tooth short with a long, straight posterior margin, the molar plate about 1.25 times the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth; pronotum and legs as in the soldier.

/genus/rotunditermes/.note: The original text has only key couplets and plates, with no genus-level Diagnosis; there are no measurements, no body colour and no worker description. Holmgren places this genus and Diversitermes in the same branch, the two being distinguished by compound eye size, the compound eyes of this genus being “sehr gross”.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with very large compound eyes distinctly projecting from the sides of the head (Taf. III, Fig. 10), clypeus about as long as half its width or slightly shorter and often dark, 1st tooth of the left mandible about as long as the 2nd; soldier with a more or less distinct apical process on the mandibles, head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets, nasus short and cylindrical, head capsule in frontal view perfectly circular (Taf. III, Fig. 15). The short cylindrical nasus together with the perfectly circular head capsule makes the soldier easy to distinguish from Tumulitermes, which has a longer nasus and an oval head, and from Subulitermes, whose mandibles lack an apical process; the alate is distinguished from Diversitermes (medium-sized compound eyes) by its exceptionally large compound eyes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: 1st tooth of the left mandible about as long as the 2nd; clypeus about as long as half its width or slightly shorter, often dark; compound eyes large to very large, projecting dorsally from the sides of the head; pronotum relatively large. Head shape and wing surface pilosity are not further delimited in the key in the original text, only compared through the plate (Taf. III, Fig. 10).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles with a more or less distinct apical process; head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets; nasus short, cylindrical; head capsule perfectly circular (Tafel III, Fig. 15).

/genus/rounditermes/.note: The original describes only the soldier: the holotype is a soldier, the paratypes comprising 29 soldiers and 3 workers, but the workers were not described, and there are no alates, so only the Diagnostic characters and Soldier sections are given. The specimens were collected in a small marsh on a granite outcrop at pk 15 on the Kourou–Sinnamary road, French Guiana, the nest being built over a 30 cm diameter tree stump, together with about 10 Dynastidae larvae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distinguished from the closely allied Cortaritermes as follows: the soldier antennae are constantly 14-segmented, the head capsule longer and broader, the hind tibia relatively longer, the face of the head lacking microtrichia, the nasus more conical and shorter. The original twice emphasises that the head capsule is circular and as long as wide and is unconstricted behind the level of the antennal fossae, on which basis it can be distinguished from the various species of Cortaritermes, which have a narrower head capsule and a more slender, elongate nasus; the generic name is taken from the circular shape of the soldier head capsule.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (1) Head dark brown, circular, as long as wide, unconstricted behind the level of the antennae; (2) nasus conical, slightly upturned; (3) a few long hairs on the face of the head, mainly around the base of the nasus; (4) 4–5 long hairs and several small hairs at the tip of the nasus, a few hairs at its base; (5) mandibles slender and weak, small, reduced, but with a distinct sharp point; (6) antennae nearly concolorous with the head, constantly 14-segmented; segment 1 longer than the rest, segment 2 shorter than the rest, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 5, segments 3 and 4 about equal in length; (7) pronotum pale brown, its anterior margin raised and notched, with about 7 long erect setae and a few fine hairs posteriorly; the pronotum broadly rounded at its anterior and posterior margins, concave in the middle and depressed on both sides; (8) abdominal tergites yellowish brown, with several hairs on the posterior margin; (9) sternites yellow, with numerous long hairs on the posterior margin; (10) legs yellow, slender, the tibiae and femora bearing rows of long hairs and spines; (11) means for specimen no. 10: body length 5.20 mm, head length including nasus 1.99 mm, head width 1.55 mm, nasus length 0.72 mm, pronotum length 0.40 mm, antennal length 1.97 mm, hind tibia 1.77 mm, hind tibia about 0.9 times the head length.

/genus/rubeotermes/.note: The genus-level account contains two sections, worker and alate; soldierless. The genus name refers to its turning red in alcohol (rubeo-, red); the Chinese name is taken from 'red'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Workers turn red in alcohol; the forecoxa bears several long, stout spines as large as the tibial spurs — on this basis they can be distinguished from all South American soldierless termites.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes and ocelli medium-sized. Fontanelle very small. Pronotum semicircular in dorsal view, with several hundred setae. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum rather concave, angles rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, head width about 1 mm. White in life, turning red in alcohol. Head capsule densely covered with many small setae; fontanelle very small. Forecoxa with several spines as large as the tibial spurs; protibia slightly swollen. The connection between the mesenteron and the proctodeum is truncated, devoid of a mixed segment (original: Mesenteron and proctodeum connection truncated, devoid of mixed segment); enteric valve inserted into a trilobed enteric-valve seating.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate can be distinguished from other genera of the family by the media of the forewing, which is short, sclerotised and joins the radial sector close to the wing suture, and by the absence of the media in the hindwing; the soldier resembles Neotermes, but the third antennal segment is club-shaped and always longer than the second, and there is a distinct ridge anteromesally to the antennal sockets.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Usually dark brown, the pronotum pale yellow in some species; eyes small, 0.29–0.43 mm in diameter, ocelli not touching the compound eye, 0.04–0.07 mm from it; antennae 15–20 segments; mandibles resembling those of Kalotermes; pronotum wider than the head; wing membrane densely covered with small verrucose pigment papillae; each main vein arising independently at the wing suture; radius simple; radial sector with 7–8 branches; media strongly sclerotised, joining the radial sector at 1/5–1/10 of the wing length from the wing suture and curving upwards shortly after the suture; cubitus weak; media absent in the hindwing; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long and narrow, the sides parallel; median concavity only slightly bilobed; dorsal antennal ridges extending towards the middle and forming a distinct ridge anteriorly; eyes colourless; antennae 12–18 segments, the third always longer than the second, club-shaped; mandibles short and thick, the outer margin evenly rounded, with or without a basal tubercle; pronotum narrower than, equal to or wider than the head, the anterior margin shallowly concave or angular; legs not swollen.

/genus/ruptitermes/.note: Soldierless. The genus-level redescription covers the worker, alate and gut; the abdominal dehiscent glands are an autapomorphy of the genus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The anterior abdomen of the worker bears a pair of well-developed spherical dehiscent glands, which may occupy 1/3 of the abdominal volume and are usually white masses, hence easy to recognise; the glands are an autapomorphy of the genus, absent in all other termite genera. The alate is larger than most Neotropical Apicotermitinae, and is distinguished from Aparatermes by the postclypeus not being depressed at both ends of the midline.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head short, broad and rounded in dorsal view, densely covered with short hairs and scattered setae; fontanelle oval to circular, usually distinct; compound eyes relatively small, ocelli round or oval, at least their diameter away from the compound eye; postclypeus small to large, moderately to strongly inflated, depressed at both ends of the midline, the midline distinct but incomplete, disappearing near the anterior and posterior margins; antennae 15 segments; each tibia with 2 spurs; wing surface evenly covered with irregular micro-scales with 2–4 arms; female larger than male.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker monotypic (a few species noted otherwise). Head broad and rounded, usually strongly sclerotised, dark; fontanelle oval to circular, variable in size and colour, usually distinct; postclypeus inflated or flattened. Apical tooth of the left mandible (A) shorter than the first marginal tooth (M1), a notch always present between M1 and M3; molar plate of the right mandible concave, without ridges. Antennae 14 segments; fore tibia with 1–2 rows of irregular spiny setae, in most species the fore coxa with a curved or oval row of spines. The pair of spherical dehiscent glands in the anterior abdomen may reach 1/3 of the abdominal volume. Gut: crop mostly very small, gizzard unarmed, mixed segment short to very short, P1 a long tube; enteric valve bilaterally symmetrical, with 6 unclerotised reticulate ridges, in most species without spines; enteric valve armature (EVA) absent, only R. bandeirai excepted.

/genus/rustitermes/.note: Apicotermitinae, soldier absent. The original generic diagnosis listed only enteric valve characters; the morphology of the alate and worker is given in the Description section; the genus is also distinguished by 'two rows of stout setae on the inner edge of the protibia'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Enteric valve with 6 slightly asymmetrical pads, each pad forming a central pouch whose scales are smaller than those between the pads; each pad with about 60–80 scales, broad at the base and narrow at the tip; posterior part of the pads truncate, with 35–50 rectangular scales arranged from the middle towards the tip and becoming progressively denser. Distinguished from Hydrecotermes, which has a similar gut coiling, by the worker protibia bearing stout setae on its inner edge (absent in the latter). Distinguished from Aparatermes, which may have a similar enteric valve and gut, by: the cuticle between the pads bearing cubic scales (absent in the latter); the enteric valve seating not trilobed (trilobed in the latter); the enteric valve lacking small spines or pointed scales (present in the latter); the posterior part of the pads bearing scales (without scales posteriorly in the latter).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The fontanelle is indistinct in both sexes, the fontanellar region concave, a median spot faintly indicated. Apical tooth of the left mandible slightly larger than M1+2, M3 triangular with an obtuse lateral margin, anterior molar process indistinct, molar prominence not concealed by the molar region swelling. Head capsule with short and sparse setae, dark brown; the frontal markings slightly paler than the rest of the head capsule, their boundary indistinct. Pronotum subhexagonal, anterior margin straight and without a median notch, lateral margins very straight and distinct, the surface sparsely covered with setae and short hairs. Tergites and sternites with short hairs. Fore coxa with 4–5 conspicuous long setae; inner surface of the protibia with 2 rows of 6–7 stout setae each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; fontanelle small and round; postclypeus slightly inflated; head capsule with medium and long setae. Apical tooth of the left mandible more prominent than M1+2, M3 triangular with a right or acute lateral margin, molar prominence not concealed by the molar region swelling. Long setae of the pronotum concentrated along the margins of the anterior and posterior lobes; tergites and sternites densely covered with long setae, mostly directed backwards or upwards. Fore coxa with 4–5 stout setae; inner surface of the fore femur with long setae; protibia moderately inflated, its inner surface with 2 rows of 6–7 stout setae each. Enteric valve unarmed, with 6 pyriform pads of slightly different sizes, the pads composed of relatively large fringed polygonal scales; the cuticle between the pads consisting of larger fringed cubic scales, closely packed near P3.

/genus/sandsitermes/.note: No genus-level measurements are given; the measurements are species-level; the distinction of the two worker types is placed in the genus-level Description. The original uses 'Imago' (for the alate) rather than the word alate.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate the dorsal surface of the head is slightly raised in front of the fontanelle, at the position of the ocelli; postclypeus slightly arched, anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly convex; molar region of the right mandible distinctly concave, with faint ridges and a distinct basal pit. In the soldier the nasus is long and conical, but there is no apparent uniquely distinct morphological character (the original explicitly states no apparent uniquely distinct morphological character). In the worker the molar region of the mandibles is concave without well-developed ridges; P1 of the gut forms a separate loop before joining the paunch (P3); the enteric valve (P2) is weakly sclerotised, arranged in two rings, with minute conical spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule oval in dorsal view; frontal region between the ocelli not concave; in lateral view the dorsal surface of the head is slightly raised in front of the fontanelle, at the position of the ocelli. Compound eyes oval, large, their distance to the lower margin of the head smaller than to the ocelli. Ocelli oval in dorsal view, large (smaller than the antennal sockets), situated in the anterior half of the compound eyes, their distance from the compound eyes smaller than the width of an ocellus. Fontanelle paler than the head, lying in a shallow depression, Y-shaped, with a short anterior arm and a small transparent circle above the arms. Postclypeus slightly arched in lateral view, slightly concave along the midline in dorsal view; anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly convex. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum wider than the head (excluding eyes), sub-trapezoidal, anterior margin raised, anterolateral angles rounded, lateral margins concave and narrowing posteriorly, posterior margin rounded and not concave. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum deeply concave, posterolateral angles pointed. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule oval to round in dorsal view, not constricted, posterior margin not concave; in lateral view the vertex is slightly raised at the base of the nasus, with a shallow depression behind. Nasus conical, shorter than the head capsule, not directed upwards; postclypeus slightly convex in lateral view. Labrum wider than long, anterior margin rounded, lateral margins parallel, anterolateral angles rounded. Mandibles with a distinct 'point'. Antennae 13-segmented. Anterior lobe of the pronotum less developed than the posterior lobe, the angle between them about 90°. Forecoxa conical, without a keel on the anterior face. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Abdominal sclerites well sclerotised, tergites imbricate.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule trapezoidal in all workers; fontanelle distinct, situated at the middle of the head capsule, slightly concave; postclypeus swollen; antennae 14-segmented; anterior margin of the pronotum rounded, not concave; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Workers dimorphic, distinguished by head-capsule pigmentation, mandible morphology and the shape and size of the tergites: type 2 is less numerous than type 1 in all samples studied, head capsule brownish yellow, with a depression anteriorly followed by a swelling; outer margin of the mandibles with a distinct concavity in front of the apical tooth, apical tooth larger, the gap between M3 and the molar prominence wider on the left, molar plate narrower; anterior lobe of the pronotum more developed than the posterior lobe. Within type 1 the head-capsule size appears to vary, but the number of individuals is insufficient for measurement.

/genus/scheffrahnitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (only Scheffrahnitermes ubuntu), without soldiers. Holotype (worker, MZUSP 18093) collected at UHE Jirau, Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil. Distribution: Colombia (Llanos) + Brazil (Amazonia, Cerrado, Atlantic coastal forest, Caatinga). Alate described from females (female larger than male).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus (Scheffrahnitermes ubuntu), without soldiers (subfamily Apicotermitinae). The enteric valve seating (EVS) is unique: internally it bears two sclerotised spiny plates of unequal size (spines directed towards P3), with spines also between the plates, while externally it forms a small pouch at the P1–P3 junction (the larger plate is inserted into the pouch); workers turn red after preservation in alcohol. Distinguished from Grigiotermes, Dissimulitermes and Humutermes: in the latter three the sclerotised plates lie within the enteric valve (EV) and there is one per each of the six valves, whereas in this genus they lie within the enteric valve seating; distinguished from the closely related species of Ruptitermes: in the latter the enteric valve seating forms three small pouches, whereas this genus has only one; it shares with Rubeotermes and Tonsuritermes the 'turning red in alcohol', but differs in body shape, gut coiling and mixed segment, and this genus lacks spines on the fore tibia/fore coxa (Tonsuritermes has spines on the fore tibia, Rubeotermes on the fore coxa).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Female larger than male. Fontanelle prominent, subcircular, medium-sized spot distinct; compound eyes circular, ocelli oval, the distance to the compound eye less than its diameter. Left mandible apical tooth equal in size to M1+2, M3 triangular with a sharp edge, a gap between M3 and the distinct premolar prominence; right mandible apical tooth nearly equal to M1, M2 triangular with a sharp edge. Head capsule circular in dorsal view, densely covered with short hairs and short, medium and long setae; dark brown, paler around the antennae. Antennae 15-segmented (formula 2>3<4=5). Postclypeus slightly inflated, slightly paler than the head capsule, median suture distinct. Labrum covered with short hairs and setae. Pronotum sub-trapezoidal, shorter than the head, anterior margin straight with a median incision, median suture distinct, densely covered with hairs of different sizes and setae. Fore tibia long and slender, not inflated, with a few short stout setae on the inner surface. Wings three times the length of the abdomen; veins brown, membrane transparent, slightly brownish; forewing and hindwing with short marginal hairs (except on the basal third of the posterior margin).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule and thorax turning from pale yellow to deep red/brown after preservation in alcohol. Head slightly convex in lateral view, circular in dorsal view, scattered with setae and short and medium hairs. Postclypeus inflated, often with a pair of setae at the top. Fontanelle large and prominent. Antennae 12–14-segmented (formula 2>3=4<5), pale at the base and gradually darker towards the apex. Left mandible apical tooth equal in size to M1+2, M3 triangular with a sharp edge, a gap between M3 and the premolar prominence; right mandible apical tooth nearly equal to M1, M2 triangular with a sharp edge. Anterior lobe and posterior margin of the pronotum with long setae and short hairs. Fore tibia moderately inflated, with short hairs and 5–6 long stout setae. Crop spherical, inflated when full; cardiac valve long, inserted at the apex of the midgut; a small white spherical nodule on the ventral surface at the junction of the mixed segment and P1; P1 of uniform width, widened and folded, appearing as a mirror-image C in ventral view; enteric valve (EV) with six columnar pads, each pad with a short spine at its base, covered with small scales (sub-trapezoidal in the centre, sub-rectangular at the edges), the small spines at the scale edges directed towards P3; enteric valve seating (EVS) short, forming a small pouch, with two asymmetrical sclerotised plates inside, spines directed towards P3, spines also between the plates, the larger plate aligned with the pouch; P3 connected to P4 by a narrow isthmus on the left side of the body; P4 making a U-shaped turn after the mixed segment, entering the inflated P5 dorsally at its end. Measurements (mm, n=30, six nests): head width 0.63–0.73 (0.68), head length 0.78–0.90 (0.83), fore tibia width 0.09–0.13 (0.11), fore tibia length 0.36–0.49 (0.45), tibial index 0.74–0.87 (0.82).

/genus/schievitermes/.note: The genus-level Description is divided into Imago (queen only)/Soldier/Worker, and the Diagnosis likewise has two parts, Soldier (compared with the Neotropical snappers) and Worker (wood-feeding mandibles and gut). The bibliographic data conflict: the Pensoft page gives the citation as ZooKeys 1125: 103–124, whereas the fpage/lpage in the XML are 103–114; this batch follows the latter.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the Neotropical snappers, the soldier is distinguished from Termes, Inquilinitermes, Cavitermes, Palmitermes, Dihoplotermes and Cornicapritermes by the absence of a frontal projection; Planicapritermes has a flattened head capsule and strongly asymmetrical mandibles; it differs from Crepititermes in the stouter mandibles, which show a slight but distinct asymmetry, and in the bulbous third antennal segment; the species of Neocapritermes are all larger (head width >1 mm), with 15–16 antennal segments (13 in this genus), and the mandibular asymmetry is always stronger. The worker mandibles are of the wood-feeding type, with a short gap between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth and well-developed molar ridges; the digestive tract resembles that of Planicapritermes, but the bilobed tip of the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is characteristic of this genus; Neocapritermes also has two mesenteric lobes, but its mixed segment is shorter and the lobes are larger and farther apart. The differentiation of the P3 cuticle is intermediate between Neocapritermes (long spines and filaments) and Planicapritermes (minute spines).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: At genus level only a single queen is known (only known from a single queen); the original gives no separate genus-level description but refers to the species-level description. Nothing is added here.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule subquadrate with rounded angles, about twice as long as wide, with about 100 setae. Mandibles about as long as the head capsule, rather stout, of the snapping type; right mandible nearly straight, only slightly incurved; left mandible slightly but distinctly curved: outer margin slightly concave at the base, convex in the middle, concave again where it contacts the right mandible, incurved at the tip. Tips of both mandibles hooked, turned inwards by about 60°. Antennae 13-segmented, the last segment extending beyond the tip of the left mandible; third segment distinctly bulbous, as wide as the first segment and wider than the remaining segments. Labrum nearly parallel-sided, anterior margin wavy with a convex middle, bearing a few long setae, anterolateral angles rounded. Frons without a projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule white, with numerous setae. Mandibles of the wood-feeding type: in the left mandible the A–M1+2 gap is about half the M1+2–M3 gap; M3 distinct, the premolar tooth (sensu Deligne 1999) blade-like, molar ridges well developed. Right mandible: A–M1 gap short, M2 distinct, molar ridges well developed. Crop moderately developed; gizzard of the broad type, the cuticular armature restricted to small comb-like scales on the pulvilli. Mixed segment long, mesenteric tongue bilobed at its tip. P1 slightly swollen, narrowing posteriorly into P2. Enteric valve (P2) funnel-shaped, conical at the end of P1, forming a narrow tube where it meets P3; the armature consists of two rings of spines: the proximal ring lies on the conical part of P2 and consists of 3 oval cushions alternating with slender cushions, all bearing small triangular spines; the distal ring lies in the narrow tubular part and consists of 6 cushions of alternating length bearing fine, curved spines. P3 large, its wall bearing many small spines, longer on the rounded posterior part near the P2 opening, short and often comb-like on the anterior part where it narrows towards P4.

/genus/serritermes/.note: The family is monotypic, and the generic characters are given on p. 3: 'Diagnostic Characters. The same as those of the family Serritermitidae.', so the family-level diagnosis serves here as the generic diagnosis. The alate, soldier and worker accounts are adapted from the descriptions on pp. 3–4, 6–8 and 8 respectively; measurements are omitted to avoid confusion with species-level data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus is monotypic within the Serritermitidae, and its generic characters are the same as those of the family: in the alate, worker and nymph the apical tooth of the mandible is proportionally elongate and sharp, separated by a broadly curved inner margin from a marginal tooth near the ridged molar plate, which distinguishes it from all other Termitidae; in the soldier the apical parts of both mandibles are long and rather straight, with numerous coarse serrations on the inner margin behind the apex; the pronotum is narrow and long, with both the anterior and posterior margins distinctly bilobed and a deep notch in the middle of each.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head oval, medium light brown to yellow; fontanelle set in a small depression, white, of medium size, reduced and forked; compound eyes of medium size and circular, about 1/4 of their diameter from the lower margin of the head; ocelli situated between the compound eyes and the frons, smaller than the compound eyes; antennae 13 or 14 segments; postclypeus large, its length slightly less than half its width, with a median longitudinal line; pronotum about half as long as wide, slightly concave at the anterior margin, the sides rounded and narrowed posteriorly; each tibia with 2 apical spurs; tarsi 4-segmented; arolium absent; cerci 2-segmented; styli absent in both sexes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The sides of the head are nearly straight and narrow forwards, the head broader than long (to the anteclypeus); the outer margin of each mandible is concave at the base, nearly straight in the middle and convex apically; the apices of both mandibles are almost unhooked, and the inner margin of the apical 1/3 bears numerous coarse serrations, with no molar ridges at the base; the serrations of the left mandible reach almost to the base, and before the base there is a blunt process and a small tooth-like process of about 60°; behind the 3–4 coarse serrations at the apex of the right mandible there are about 6 smaller serrations; postclypeus short with a concave anterior margin; labrum longer than wide with a bluntly pointed apex; pronotum elongate, deeply notched at the anterior and posterior margins into two lobes; each tibia with 2 apical spurs; tarsi 4-segmented, segment 4 longer than the remaining segments together; styli absent; cerci 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 13 segments; the mandibles are the most specialised known among termites, with the apical part proportionally elongate and sharp and the marginal teeth reduced to one.

/genus/silvestritermes/.note: The worker gut (gizzard with 24 folds, mesenteric tongue, spindle-shaped P1, enteric valve with 6 cushions) and the generic description of the alate are given in the source but no sections are provided for them, as quotations are limited to 3 per genus; the text extracted from the 2012 PDF retains the original line-break hyphens (e.g. “extend- ing”), and quotations are copied verbatim.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier differs from Armitermes in lacking a row of short stout spines along the margins of the pro-, meso- and metanotal plates.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head circular in dorsal view, or with rounded lateral margins and angular posterior corners; frontal tube conical, projecting beyond the labrum in dorsal view.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head circular, frontal suture indistinct; fontanelle elliptical but very indistinct (except in S. lanei); postclypeus and labrum as in the alate; antennae 13 or 14 segments.

/genus/sinqasapatermes/.note: The imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no Alate section is provided. The genus-level Diagnosis lists only enteric characters; the integumental characters of the soldier and worker are given in the genus-level Description; no genus-level measurements are given, the measurements being species-level.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The distal margin of the enteric valve (P2) is not folded into the paunch (P3) but bends towards the ileum (P1), i.e. against the direction of food flow; the armature consists of a ring of 6 subequal, nearly triangular ridges, the surface of each densely covered with short spines; the armature lies on the outer surface of the cone, facing the inner wall of P1; the enteric-valve seating is trilobed and separated from the rest of P3; P3 is further subdivided.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule constricted behind the antennal bases in dorsal view, greatest width behind the constriction, at the middle of the posterior lobe; in lateral view the vertex is almost straight to the base of the nasus, the base of the nasus weakly concave. Nasus narrow, conical (dorsal view), about as long as the head capsule, slightly upturned in lateral view. Mandibles reduced, without a 'point'. Postclypeus moderately arched in lateral view. Labrum wider than long, anterolateral angles rounded. Antennae 11-segmented. Pronotum shallowly saddle-shaped, anterior margin rounded and not concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule trapezoidal in dorsal view, greatest width at the mandibular bases; fontanelle area concave, situated in the posterior third of the head capsule. Postclypeus short, moderately swollen, midline weak. Antennae 12-segmented. Pronotum shallowly saddle-shaped, anterior margin rounded and not concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Apical tooth of the left mandible as large as M1+2 or slightly more prominent, posterior margin of the apical tooth weakly concave or truncate; posterior margin of the apical tooth forming a right or acute angle with the anterior margin of M1+2; posterior margin of M1+2 straight or slightly curved; third marginal tooth reduced to a vestigial segment; molar tooth visible in the V-shaped gap, but its tip hidden by the molar prominence; ridges of the molar prominence extremely weak. Right mandible: apical tooth slightly more prominent than the first marginal tooth, second marginal tooth invisible or reduced to a minute projection; molar plate concave, ridges extremely weak; basal pit distinct. Digestive tract: the gut forms a short, wide coil in the body; crop large; gizzard with thick musculature; mesenteron passing along the right side of the body, not reaching the midline in ventral view; mesenteron–proctodeum junction circular, without a mixed segment; bases of the Malpighian tubules slightly swollen into ampullae, paired and adjacent, attached to the inner face of the junction by a common base; P1 tubular, shorter than the mesenteron; P2 situated below P1, conical, its distal margin bent against the food flow as described under the diagnostic characters; P2 coaxial with P3; enteric-valve seating trilobed, separated from the rest of P3 by a constriction; distal end of P3 very prominent in dorsal view, joining P4 on the left side; isthmus distinct.

/genus/sphaerotermes/.note: Type species Sphaerotermes sphaerothorax (Sjöstedt). The account here is compiled from the generic and type-species descriptions of Emerson (1928) (the alate from a king and queen collected by H. Kohl at Stanleyville). For the modern genus see Krishna et al. (2013).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head rectangular with rounded corners, only slightly narrower anteriorly, red-yellow, covered with short hairs; left mandible with a much stronger bend than the right, with several serrations and one blunt tooth near the base; fontanelle central on the head, small and indiscernible. Alate antennal segment 3 very small, segment 4 about equal to segment 2, styli absent in both sexes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, with rounded corners, only slightly narrower anteriorly, red-yellow, covered with short hairs; antennae 13-segmented (segment 3 smaller than segment 2, segment 2 equal to segment 4); labrum rounded on both sides, with hyaline points; left mandible with a much stronger bend than the right, with several serrations and one blunt tooth near the base; right mandible inner edge smooth; fontanelle central on the head, small and indiscernible; pronotal anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin faintly concave. Measurements (mm): head length 1.79–1.83, head width 0.96–1.00, antennae 1.03–1.10, pronotum 0.33–0.37×0.57–0.60, hind tibia 0.61–0.67, left mandible 0.61.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 13-segmented; head width 0.95 mm, hind tibia 0.67 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale brownish yellow, oval; fontanelle a small pale circular dot; head covered with short hairs and a few long bristles; antennal segment 3 very small, segment 4 about equal to segment 2; eyes medium-sized, round, not very close to the lower margin; ocelli large, very close to the eyes; labrum pale, rather transparent; postclypeus concolorous with the head, with a median line, about half as long as broad; pronotum pale yellow, slightly paler than the head, the sides rounded, anterior and posterior margins concave, covered with short hairs and long bristles; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum broadly concave; legs pale yellow, each tibia with two apical spurs; abdominal tergites pale yellow; styli absent in both sexes. Measurements (mm): head length 1.27–1.28, head width 1.13–1.20, eye diameter 0.30–0.31, pronotum 0.60×0.97–1.07, hind tibia 1.20–1.23, left mandible 0.57; posterior length 26.00, abdominal width 5.00.

/genus/spinitermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 108–109). The 1912 work treats Spinitermes as a subgenus of Mirotermes and gives only one line of key characters, with no separate generic diagnosis, so this entry has no 'Alate' or 'Worker' section. Editorial note: the first line of the species list on p. 109 is misprinted in the original as »Miroteermes« (a repeated letter); judging from the other lines on the same page and the key on p. 108 it should be »Mirotermes«; the quotation is retained as printed and the point is explained separately here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1912 treated it as a subgenus of Mirotermes (Mirotermes (Spinitermes)) and noted that it occurs 'only in South America', containing 4 species: brevicornutus (Desn.) Silv. (Mato Grosso, Paraguay), gracilis Holmgr. (Peru), nigrostomus Holmgr. (Bolivia) and trispinosus (Bates) Wasm. (Cuiabá, Amazon). The original gives only one line of characters in a key to the subgenera of the genus and provides no separate description; the alate and worker are not dealt with in that work. The soldier is recognised by the following combination: frontal projection large and projecting, with a distinct tubercle or projection on each side; posterior margin of the head without tooth-like projections; labrum wider than long; mandibles far shorter than the head, fairly robust, slightly sabre-shaped and curved.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: From the key to the subgenera: frontal projection large and projecting, with a distinct tubercle or projection on each side. Posterior margin of the head without tooth-like projections. Labrum wider than long. Mandibles far shorter than the head, fairly robust, slightly sabre-shaped and curved (plate IV, fig. 7). The adjacent subgenus Tuberculitermes in the same key differs in having a nearly tooth-like projection on each side of the posterior margin of the head, a labrum far longer than wide, and mandibles as long as the head and straight, with the apex hooked back.

/genus/spiralitermes/.note: Monotypic genus (type species Spiralitermes jurupari Almeida-Azevedo & Azevedo, 2026). Soldierless; the generic characters are based entirely on the external morphology and digestive tract of the worker; the original text notes that the alate is unknown (Imago: Unknown) and that its exact phylogenetic position cannot be inferred without molecular data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldierless. The worker first proctodeal segment (P1) is extremely long, coiled into a spiral at the end of the abdomen, completing a full turn along the body axis before entering the third proctodeal segment (P3) on the right side (ventral view); the enteric valve seat is not lobed, funnel-shaped; the enteric valve bears no spines, but the proximal central region of each of the six symmetrical lobes bears spines directed towards P1 — this feature of spines directed towards P1 distinguishes it from Mangolditermes and Tucupitermes, which also have spineless enteric valves.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: External morphology: head capsule pale yellow, scattered with sparse short hairs; fontanelle distinct, oval, white; postclypeus slightly swollen, with only a few short hairs; labrum convex, more coarsely setose than the head capsule; antennae 13-segmented (segment 1 > segment 2, segment 3 shorter than the remaining segments). Left mandible apical tooth slightly shorter than M1+2, with a deep notch between M1+2 and M3 typical of the Neotropical soldierless subfamily, M3 tooth indistinct, the molar prominence completely hidden by the molar ridge, its process about as long as M1+2; right mandible apical tooth longer than M1, an open angle between M1 and M2, M2 tooth triangular, molar plate concave, without grinding ridges. Thorax pale yellow, the margins of the pro-, meso- and metanotum each with a row of long hairs; tibiae and femora slender, of uniform width; the anterior surface of the fore coxa with extremely long fine hairs. Abdomen semi-transparent, tergites and sternites densely covered with short hairs, mostly directed posteriorly. Digestive tract: crop enlarged, about 1/4 of the abdominal length; gizzard reduced; proventricular valves subterminal; midgut uniform, slightly wider than P1; midgut tongue long, about 1/3 of the midgut length; P1 extremely long, visible on all four faces, distinctly S-shaped in left lateral view, forming a complete ring ventrally, entering P3 on a distinct enteric valve seat (not lobed, funnel-shaped); enteric valve without spines, with six symmetrical lobes, the proximal central region of each lobe bearing spines directed towards P1, the spines smaller the further they are from the lobe tip; P3 spherical in ventral view, connected to P4 through a distinct isthmus, forming an inverted U-shaped dorsal loop; P4 smaller in diameter than the midgut, making a short U-turn. Measurements (worker, mm, n=30, means in parentheses): head width 0.68–0.90 (0.80), head length 0.75–0.85 (0.83), hind tibia length 0.73–0.85 (0.78), pronotum width 0.43–0.48 (0.46), fore tibia width/length ratio 0.24–0.36 (0.30).

/genus/stolotermes/.note: The original title is “DIAGNOSIS OF THE SUBFAMILY STOLOTERMITINAE AND THE GENUS STOLOTERMES”. The genus was monotypic at the time, so the generic characters were written together with the subfamily characters, and this qualification must be retained when citing them. The worker caste was not described in the original, so no Worker section is given. Another paper, Hill (1926, Proc. Roy. Soc. Victoria 38: 192–214), also records this genus, but it was not used to supplement the account here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original diagnosis was given for the subfamily and the genus combined (the genus was monotypic at the time, so the generic characters were the subfamily characters). Its most conspicuous feature is the degeneration of the ocelli; the mandibular pattern is clearly homologous with that of Archotermopsis, being intermediate in type between Archotermopsis and Hodotermopsis. Alates lack a fontanelle and an arolium, and the postclypeus is extremely short and fused with the frons; soldiers lack a frontal gland, the fore and mid tibiae bear 2–3 apical spurs and the hind tibia 2, and both sexes have a pair of styli.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head, pronotum, wing scales and abdomen covered with fairly long hairs, the head less densely so; no fontanelle; epicranial suture present; ocelli degenerate; compound eyes medium-sized, oval, with a rather straight anterior margin, separated from the lower margin of the head by slightly more than half their length; postclypeus extremely short and fused with the frons, the boundary being a depression with no visible suture, about 5 times as wide as long; anteclypeus short, transparent; labrum tongue-shaped, with a rather straight apex; antennae 15–17-segmented; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth and a molar plate, the anterior part of the 1st marginal tooth bearing a small subsidiary tooth near its base; left mandible with 3 subequal marginal teeth, the 3rd separated from the other two by a wide-angled notch; pronotum much narrower than the head, rather flat, with a shallow longitudinal median depression and a shallow lateral depression on each side of the anterior margin, together forming a Y-shaped depression, the anterior margin evenly concave, the lateral margins slightly rounded, the posterior margin wider and slightly concave; tibial apical spurs 3:3:2 or 2:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented; no arolium; cerci 4–5-segmented; female without styli, the male styli reaching near the abdominal apex.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, thorax and abdomen sparsely covered with hairs and longer setae; head proportionally large, elongate or oval, flat or rather flat, the anterior part evenly continuous with the vertex; epicranial suture present; no frontal gland; anterior part of the postmentum wide, its narrowest point less than half its greatest width; mandibles proportionally large, the left with 3 marginal teeth, 4 notches and a molar plate, the right with 2 marginal teeth, 3 notches and a molar plate, the 2nd marginal tooth with a long cutting edge bearing a point at each end; eyes distinct; antennae 14–18-segmented; labrum broadly tongue-shaped, the anterior margin straight or curved; postclypeus fused with the frons but the sutural depression still present; pronotum narrower than the head; tarsi 4-segmented, no arolium; femora swollen; fore and mid tibiae with 2–3 apical spurs, hind tibia with 2; both sexes with a pair of styli; cerci 4–5-segmented.

/genus/subulitermes/.note: The original text has only key couplets; Holmgren (p. 68) discusses the question of the primitiveness of this genus, regards the narrow cylindrical nasus as a derived character, and places the genus at the end of the branch (“Gipfel” being occupied by Subulitermes). No measurements, body colour or worker description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with an oval head, fontanelle near the middle of the head, brain very well developed (Taf. III, Fig. 9), 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd; soldier with mandibles entirely without an apical process, nasus narrowly cylindrical, antennae mostly 12-segmented, frontal profile almost straight, head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets. Holmgren states explicitly that precisely because the nasus of this genus is cylindrical and extremely narrow, Subulitermes cannot be regarded as the primitive type of the branch; it and Convexitermes both depart from it through their slender body and well-developed brain, except that the latter still retains a thick nasus. The systematic discussion also states that the whole Subulitermes branch has a large clypeus and places this genus at the end of that branch.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head oval; fontanelle about at the middle of the head; brain (Gehirn) very well developed; clypeus about as long as half its width, or shorter and strongly raised, oval, pale yellow; 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd; antennal segments relatively long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles without an apical process; the species are small, antennae 11–12-segmented, usually 12-segmented; nasus cylindrical, narrow; frontal profile almost straight; head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets.

/genus/synacanthotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of the archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 21–22). The original treated this genus as a partial synonym of Eutermes, containing only Synacanthotermes heterodon (Sjöst.) from Cameroon; the alate was unknown at the time, hence only the soldier and worker sections; the alate is now known (Krishna et al. 2013 merged the alate described as angolensis into trilobatus).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is now known (the alate of trilobatus is the former angolensis, described by Weidner 1956). The antennae of both soldier and worker have 15 segments, segment 2 longer than segment 3; the soldier is eyeless, the frontal gland opening and frontal gland perhaps absent, the sides of the head parallel and flatly convex; the pronotum is small, less than half the head width, and weakly saddle-shaped. Holmgren recognised only one species (heterodon, Cameroon) and placed it among the fungus-growing termites.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head elongate, sides parallel, slightly narrowed anteriorly from the antennal sockets, flatly convex, eyeless. Cranial suture invisible; frontal gland opening and frontal gland perhaps absent. Frons flat, antennal carinae distinct. Clypeus short: the anterior margin of the base completely straight, bounded at the sides by the large mandibular basal segments; the apical piece fairly short and transparent. Labrum large and wide, narrowed at the base, with a trilobed transparent tip. Mandibles slightly geniculate near the middle, weakly curved, the apex fairly long; the left mandible with 3 teeth from the middle to the base, tooth 1 the largest, the base of the apex often with a slight notch; the right mandible with only one large step-like tooth at the base. Antennae of 15 segments, segment 2 longer than segment 3. Postmentum rectangular, elongate. Pronotum small, far narrower than the head, weakly saddle-shaped. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the fore and mid tibiae with several shorter lateral spines in addition. Cerci relatively large and thick, styli degenerate.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: In two forms. Head large, relatively flat, oval with parallel sides. Frontal gland opening very indistinct, cranial suture invisible. Clypeus slightly convex, the base shorter than half its width, posterior margin fairly strongly convex and anterior margin slightly concave, the apical piece fairly large and transparent, the mandibular basal segments fairly large. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous band. Left mandible with the Termes-type dentition, tooth 2 larger than tooth 1; right mandible with a degenerate tooth 2, tooth 3 larger than tooth 1, the inner margin as in Leucotermes. Antennae of 15 segments, segment 2 larger than segments 3 and 4. Pronotum saddle-shaped, both anterior and posterior margins concave, less than half the head width. Cerci relatively large and thick, styli present.

/genus/syncapritermes/.note: Soldier based on couplets 11–13 of the Oriental Region generic key.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Together with Oriencapritermes in couplet 13, distinguished by the anterior margin of the labrum shallowly concave, longer than wide, and the base of the anterolateral process unpointed; left mandible with a well-developed, toothed basal inferior process (couplet 12). Fontanelle small, round, fontanelle gland small.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior margin of labrum shallowly concave, longer than wide, base of anterolateral process unpointed; left mandible with a well-developed, toothed basal inferior process; labrum long; fontanelle small, round, fontanelle gland small.

/genus/synhamitermes/.note: Proposed in the original as a subgenus of HAMITERMES (Untergattung Synhamitermes), and the diagnosis is very brief (4 characters for the soldier, 2 for the worker); reproduced here as given, without adding anything the original does not state.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate unknown. Soldier: head rectangular, longer than wide; mandibles short, with 1 posteriorly directed tooth; postclypeus simple, not bilobed; fontanelle indistinct; antennae 13–14-segmented. Worker: postclypeus large, antennae 13–14-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, longer than wide; mandibles short, with 1 posteriorly directed tooth; postclypeus simple, not bilobed; fontanelle indistinct; antennae 13–14-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Postclypeus large; antennae 13–14-segmented.

/genus/syntermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 46–47). The original lists 9 South American species (bolivianus, brasiliensis, chaquimagenses, dirus, grandis, molestus, obtusus, peruvianus, Silvestrii); the species list is not included in the description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier monotypic, antennae 19–20 segments, the segments long and elongate; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe large, anterior corners produced, often spine-like. Alate antennae 20–21 segments, labrum broader than long, without a transverse band, frontal gland opening large, circular to oval, ocelli far from the compound eyes; cerci short, styli absent. All the species listed by Holmgren 1912 are from South America.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval. Frontal gland opening large, circular to oval. Compound eyes relatively small, strongly projecting; ocelli very far from the compound eyes. Base of clypeus about as long as half its width, more or less strongly arched, apex hyaline. Labrum broader than long, without a transverse band. Mandibles with Termes-type dentition. Antennae 20–21 segments, rather long. Pronotum broad, shorter than half its width, anterior corners often acute; posterior margins of meso- and metanotum weakly arcuate. Wings long, hyaline, costa brown; radius very short; media of forewing arising beyond the wing scale, media of hindwing arising at the base of the radial sector, weakly branched; cubitus many-branched. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with only 2. Cerci short, styli absent. Female abdomen without exudatory hairs, longitudinally finely wrinkled.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head large and rather broad, narrowing anteriorly, flattened and arched. Frontal gland opening and frontal gland present, opening at the apex of a very short frontal tube; frons depressed. Clypeus very short. Labrum short and broad, apex trilobed, the median lobe usually hyaline. Mandibles stout, rather strongly curved; left mandible with the base of the apex slightly expanded, then abruptly narrowing, often with a very strong tooth beyond the apex, with 2 smaller teeth inside this tooth and usually a stout basal tooth; right mandible with a slightly nodular basal tooth. Antennal segments long and elongate, 19–20 in total. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, anterior lobe large, anterior corners produced, often spine-like; meso- and metanotum either with spine-like elongated anterior corners or with angular sides. Legs long; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with only 2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Two forms. Head pentagonal, rounded, widest at the level of the antennae. Frontal gland opening large, circular; head sutures visible. Base of clypeus almost as long as half its width, arched, apex relatively small and hyaline. Labrum broader than long, without a transverse band. Mandibles of Termes type. Antennae long, 19–20 segments. Pronotum saddle-shaped, with a large anterior lobe; lateral angles of the thoracic nota with or without lateral spines. Legs long; tibial spurs and cerci as in the soldier.

/genus/tarditermes/.note: The alate and soldier combine Emerson's original description with Sands's generic characters; the two give different values for the left mandibular index (2.91 and 3.17), which are cited side by side here without averaging. Sands's worker section contains only one sentence comparing the mandibles, and the worker section here is written accordingly, without extrapolation. Emerson recorded that the genus moves extremely slowly, whence its name; its nests occur in earth passages on the outside of nests of Acanthotermes acanthothorax.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate the apical tooth of the left mandible is extremely long (Emerson gives the index as 2.91, Sands as 3.17, the two accounts disagreeing), the second marginal tooth is absent, the molar plate has no transverse ridges, the postclypeus is 2.1 times as wide as long, the fontanelle is a pale round spot, the compound eyes project slightly beyond the sides of the head, and the pronotum is nearly semicircular; the soldier is monomorphic, the nasus long and thick, conical, reaching the large fontanelle at its tip, the mandibles without a point, the anterior margin of the labrum wavy, the head capsule unconstricted, broadly rectangular with rounded corners in dorsal view and wider than long up to the base of the nasus, the antennae 13-segmented, setae present only at the tip of the nasus and as scattered microtrichia; in the worker the molar plate has a weak concavity near the base, the anterior and posterior rounded ridges more marked (index 3.23). Sands notes that its alate is larger than all nasute allied genera except the Neotropical Angularitermes, and that its closest relative is Mimeutermes; the generic name derives from its extremely sluggish movement.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head, postclypeus and pronotum bear fairly dense short hairs, though not forming a felt; several setae occur on the margins of the head, postclypeus and pronotum. The wing membrane is densely covered with short hairs, longer than on the wings of most termites.
