Each abdominal tergite is densely covered with short hairs and bears a row of posterior marginal setae, each about three times the length of the short hairs; the pilosity of the sternites is denser and slightly longer than that of the tergites. The head is broad, the sides nearly parallel near the compound eyes; the compound eyes are large and convex, separated from the lower margin of the head by about one-seventh to one-tenth of their diameter; the ocelli are fairly large, smaller than the antennal fossae, separated from the compound eyes by slightly less than their width; the fontanelle is a small pale round spot in the middle of the head; the postclypeus bears a dark median line and is slightly more than twice as wide as long; the antennae are 14–15-segmented. The apical tooth of each mandible is extremely long and the cutting edge behind the first marginal tooth reduced; the left mandibular index is 2.91; the right mandible has no second marginal tooth. The pronotum is large, slightly narrower than the head, its lateral margins rounded and its posterior margin slightly concave; the median angle of the mesonotum is rounded, about 130°; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Measurements: head width 1.28–1.35 mm, diameter of compound eye 0.41–0.42 mm, forewing 10.15–11.48 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head and frontal projection bear microtrichia visible only in good light; there are no setae except near the tip of the frontal projection; the pronotum bears a few short hairs and no setae. The head is fairly large and broad, the conical frontal projection thick at its base; the head capsule is unconstricted. Antennae 13-segmented, segments 2 and 3 about equal in length, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 3. The mandibles are without a point. The pronotum is fairly broad, its anterior margin not concave or only very shallowly so, the anterior region fairly large. Head length 2.41–2.65 mm, width 1.25–1.49 mm, hind tibia 1.12–1.19 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The mandibles are as in the alate, except that the molar plate of the right mandible has a weak concavity near the base and the anterior and posterior rounded ridges are more marked; left mandibular index 3.23.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is unknown; the wing-bud venation and mandibles of the nymph indicate a close relationship with Incisitermes, Marginitermes and Allotermes; the soldier can be distinguished from these genera by the two distinct swellings on the frons, with a concavity between them, and by the serrate anterior margin of the pronotum.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frons shield-like; anterior part dark, with sculpture; front steep; frons with two well-developed swellings separated by a broad concavity; no angular processes above or below the antennal sockets; antennal ridges slightly raised and rounded; a very weak ridge between the frons and the vertex, not as sharp as in Procryptotermes; eyes distinct, colourless; antennae 10–11 segments, the third broader and longer than the second; mandibles slender, the basal tubercle distinct; pronotum as wide as the head, the anterior margin raised and covering the posterior part of the head, deeply concave, undulating and serrate; femora not swollen.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Mandibles resembling those of Cryptotermes; the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible smaller at the base than the third marginal tooth; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth of the right mandible distinctly longer than the molar plate; media of the forewing bud weak, unsclerotised, lying between the radial sector and the cubitus almost to the wing apex.

/genus/tenuirostritermes/.note: In the alate key of the original text the couplet assigned to this genus (between Velocitermes and Constrictotermes) is missing entirely from the OCR text, only the genus name surviving, so no alate section is given; the systematic discussion on p. 71 gives its relationships with Velocitermes and Constrictotermes, which have been written into the diagnostic characters. The worker is represented in the key by only a single proportion of the basal part of the anteclypeus, which does not amount to a description, so no worker section is given either.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier of a single morph, mandibles with an apical process, head capsule dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennal sockets, nasus narrowly cylindrical, antennae 11–12-segmented, the outline of the sides of the head far longer before the depression than behind it (Tafel III, Fig. 26). It differs from Constrictotermes in that the outline of the sides of the head before the depression is far longer than behind it (in the latter only slightly longer), and from Cephalotermes in that the nasus is narrow and not a long, thick cone. Holmgren considers this genus an intermediate link in the transition from Velocitermes to Constrictotermes: its soldier corresponds to the major soldier of Velocitermes (that is, the medium soldier of Diversitermes), and the small soldier has disappeared.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles with an apical process; a single soldier morph; nasus conical to cylindrical, never very broad; antennae 11–12-segmented; head capsule dumbbell-shaped constricted behind the antennal sockets; the outline of the sides of the head far longer before the depression than behind it; nasus narrowly cylindrical.

/genus/termes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 28–29). Important: Termes in the original is a genus in the broad sense, divided into the subgenera Macrotermes and Termes s. str., distinguished by the alate pronotum (large and wide in Macrotermes / narrower and shorter in Termes s. str.) and by the shape of the soldier head (markedly narrowing anteriorly in Macrotermes / nearly parallel-sided in Termes s. str.), while the workers do not differ. The 'large and small forms' in the original genus diagnosis, 'Soldat: 2 Grössen' for the soldier and 'Arbeiter: Zwei Grössen' for the worker, are characters of Macrotermes and other fungus-growing genera and do not belong to Termes s. str.; in modern Termes both soldiers and workers are monotypic (after Krishna et al. 2013, Treatise on the Isoptera, where all 24 extant species are described with monotypic soldiers/workers and no major and minor soldiers; Huang Fusheng et al. 2000, Fauna Sinica — Isoptera: dimorphic soldiers occur in Macrotermes and Microtermes, dimorphic workers in Macrotermes). This entry has been corrected according to the modern narrow Termes s. str.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Termes in Holmgren 1912 is a genus in the broad sense, containing two subgenera, Macrotermes and Termes s. str., distinguished by the size of the pronotum of the alate: in Macrotermes the pronotum is large and wide, in Termes s. str. it is narrower and shorter (s. str. is the present-day Termes). Note: the 'large and small forms' of soldiers and workers in the broad genus are a character of Macrotermes, whereas in the narrow Termes s. str. (the present-day Termes) both soldiers and workers are monotypic. Diagnostic characters of Termes s. str.: soldier mandibles sickle-shaped, the base of the left mandible with three notches and a distinct basal tooth; alate antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2; protibia with 3 apical spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval. Compound eyes usually slightly protruding, or strongly protruding. Frontal gland opening distinct, slightly raised; frontal gland plate present. Ocelli more or less separated from the compound eyes, rather large, inner margin slightly raised, hence directed somewhat laterally. Clypeus about as long as half its width; base raised, posterior margin convex, anterior margin straight, distal part usually relatively small. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles with the Termes-type dentition. Antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2. Pronotum narrower and shorter. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum with a rather weak arcuate invagination. Radius extending slightly beyond the wing scale; media of the forewing separate from the wing scale, media of the hindwing arising from the base of the radial sector. Protibia with 3 apical spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each. Cerci short; styli present, very small to reduced. Lateral membranes of the queen's abdomen without exudatory setae, wrinkled.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Sides of the head nearly parallel; frontal gland opening and frontal gland always present, compound eyes always indicated by a bright spot. Frons flat, its posterior part bounded by two shallow grooves leading to the frontal gland opening. Base of the clypeus rather narrow, rectangular, its posterior boundary indistinct; distal part very short, transparent. Labrum widest at or in front of the middle, with a well-developed transparent distal part. Mandibles of variable length, sickle-shaped; base of the left mandible with three notches and a distinct basal tooth, the right mandible toothless apart from the basal tooth. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2. Postmentum narrow, rectangular, narrowest at the middle. Pronotum narrower than the head width, anterior part slightly strongly upturned, anterior and posterior margins more or less distinctly concave. Protibia with 3 apical spurs, meso- and metatibia with 2 each. Cerci 2-segmented; styli small to reduced.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head indistinctly pentagonal, bluntly rounded; frontal gland opening very distinct, circular, white. Compound eyes appearing as a distinct bright spot behind the antennae. Base of the clypeus short, relatively strongly raised, distal part large and transparent. Labrum longer than wide, with a chitinous transverse band. Mandibles of the Termes type. Antennae 17–20-segmented, segment 3 of variable size. Pronotum saddle-shaped, much narrower than the head. Legs, cerci and styli as in the soldier.

/genus/termitogeton/.note: Only the publisher's JATS full-text XML of this paper (Europe PMC PMC3264403) is available on this machine, with no print PDF, so section names are used as locators; the author order in the jsonl is the reverse of that in the XML, and the XML is followed here. The character “wings without a media and a radius” is cited in the original from Krishna (1970) and is not a new observation of that paper, so the chain of provenance has been retained as it stands.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alates densely hairy, the posterior part of the head larger than the anterior, the fontanelle extremely narrow and situated at the middle of the head, compound eyes small, antennae 10–15-segmented, pronotum very small, about half the width of the head, wings lacking a media and a radius; soldiers densely hairy, the head characteristically heart-shaped and dorsoventrally flattened, antennae 13–15-segmented, labrum nearly triangular, mandibles elongate and without marginal teeth, pronotum half the width of the head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body densely hairy throughout; posterior part of the head larger than the anterior; fontanelle extremely narrow, situated at the middle of the head; compound eyes small; antennae 10–15-segmented; pronotum very small, about half the width of the head; wings without a media and a radius. Species level (T. planus): body very small, covered with small hairs; head narrow in front and wide behind, heart-shaped; compound eyes large; ocelli situated in front of the compound eyes; antennae usually 9–15-segmented; pronotum about half the width of the head, with a small projection in the middle of the anterior margin.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body densely hairy throughout; head characteristically heart-shaped, dorsoventrally flattened; antennae usually 13–15-segmented; labrum nearly triangular; mandibles elongate, without marginal teeth; pronotum half the width of the head. Species level (T. planus): labrum elongate with a pointed apex, narrow at the base, widest in the apical 1/3; antennae 11–15-segmented; pronotum half the width of the head, projecting forward in the middle of the anterior margin; mandibles short, without marginal teeth, slightly curved apically.

/genus/ternicubitermes/.note: The accepted manuscript gives only the worker enteric valve (EVA) as a genus-level character; there is no genus-level text for the soldier or the alate. The original Species included lists 13 species; the genus name comes from Latin terni (three) + cubus (cube). The page numbers of the accepted manuscript (p. 16–17, lines 364–376) differ from those of the published version (Syst. Entomol. 46(1): 224–238).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve of this genus is of the basic type (basic EVA), the primary cushions being spindle-shaped or roughly rectangular. The original places the genus in clade V, corresponding to the muneris and bilobatodes types of Josens & Deligne (2019).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Enteric valve of the basic type; primary cushions spindle-shaped or roughly rectangular.

/genus/tetimatermes/.note: Soldierless. Only a single character from the 2023 worker key was read (the scoop-shaped excavation of the fore tibia); the original description, Fontes 1986, was not obtained in full, hence only a worker section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the 2023 key to Neotropical soldierless workers, the genus stands alone as a couplet (the 2nd) on ‘fore tibia with a long scoop-shaped excavation’ and does not branch further; the remaining characters overlap with related genera.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Fore tibia with a long ‘scoop-shaped’ excavation (scooped out excavation, see Fontes 1986).

/genus/thoracotermes/.note: Description after the original text of Holmgren 1912 (page images of archive.org item biostor-184513, pp. 98–99). The original records only one species, Thoracotermes macrothorax (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo; the record of the styli in the alate is explicitly attributed to Wasmann 1911, and that source has been retained.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, with only Thoracotermes macrothorax (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and the Congo. In Holmgren's generic key it is distinguished from related genera by 'styli present' together with 'pronotum very broad, rather flat, yellow'. Alate antennae 16 segments, thickening towards the apex, the third and fourth segments small; soldier head quadrangular, frontal gland opening large and upright, surrounded by a ring of hairs, labrum ligulate, antennae 15 segments; worker antennae also 15 segments, mandibular first tooth much larger than the second.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, broader than long. Frontal gland opening elongate, deeply depressed. Compound eyes very large, strongly projecting; ocelli about their own diameter from the compound eyes. Antennae long, 16 segments, thickening towards the apex, the third and fourth segments small. Mandibular first tooth longer than the teeth behind it. Base of clypeus shorter than half its width, strongly arched. Pronotum semilunar, as broad as the head without the compound eyes. Hindwing dark, the venation very different from that of the forewing: the media of the forewing trifurcate in the apical third; the hindwing with two additional cross-veins, the first stronger, running obliquely backwards in the middle of the wing and joining the media, the second arising from the radial sector in the apical quarter of the wing, running towards the wing apex and rejoining the radial sector, thus enclosing a long elliptical area. The cubitus is similar in both wings, with 11–12 branches. The stylus of the male is the only appendage (according to Wasmann 1911).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head quadrangular, the angles rounded, longer than broad, narrowing slightly anteriorly, highly arched, anterior margin truncate. Frontal gland opening large, vertical, surrounded by a ring of hairs. Base of clypeus flat, with a white apex. Labrum ligulate, longer than broad, anterior margin bluntly pointed, with a broad longitudinal groove or channel, the anterior part covered with setae. Mandibles with typical Termes-type teeth. Antennae 15 segments, third small. Pronotum short and very broad, darker in colour than the rest of the body. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each. Cerci short. Styli present, though small.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head broadly oval, widest at the antennal insertions. Base of clypeus large, strongly arched, about as long as half its width. Labrum broader than long. Mandibular first tooth much larger than the second. Antennae 15 segments, third segment as long as broad. Pronotum small. Cerci short. Styli present.

/genus/tiunatermes/.note: The original records the alate as Unknown. The specific epithet: ti = nose (Tupi), una = dark. The printed page numbers differ from the PDF page order by 357 (PDF p. 2 = printed p. 359); locators are given according to the printed page numbers.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier shares with Anhangatermes and Cyranotermes 13-segmented antennae, a head length including the nasus greater than 1.90 mm, a relatively long nasus and sparse setae on the head capsule; with Anhangatermes it further shares a broad head that is wider than long, mandibles with a distinct outer margin, and numerous short hairs at the tip of the nasus. It differs from Anhangatermes in: the nasus conical (cylindrical in the latter); the anterior surface of the fore coxa without a projection (with one in the latter); the abdominal sclerites strongly sclerotised and the tergites imbricate (sclerites unsclerotised in the latter, the gut coiling visible through them, tergites not imbricate). The generic key (supplemented by Constantino 2002) leads to this genus by 'nasus conical; fore coxa without a projection; abdominal sclerites sclerotised; tergites imbricate'.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head capsule broad in dorsal view, without a constriction; nasus conical, broad at the base; mandibles with a distinct outer margin, not forming a clear 'point'; antennae 13-segmented; postclypeus slightly convex in lateral view; labrum wider than long, anterior margin rounded, lateral margins parallel, anterior corners rounded; anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum equally developed, enclosing a 90° angle; fore coxa conical, without a ridge, its anterior surface without a projection; tibial spur formula 2:2:2; abdominal sclerites strongly sclerotised, tergites imbricate, intersegmental membranes not visible.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule nearly trapezoidal in dorsal view, posterior margin rounded; fontanelle oval, situated in the posterior 1/3 of the head capsule; the surface of the head capsule not depressed at the fontanelle (in the same plane in lateral view); postclypeus distinctly curved in lateral view; antennae 14-segmented; anterior lobe of the pronotum more developed than the posterior lobe, its anterior margin rounded, not concave; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Apical tooth of the mandibles sharp and more prominent than the first marginal tooth, the posterior margin of the apical tooth slightly concave and forming an acute angle with the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth; in the left mandible M1+2 distinct, its posterior margin straight or slightly undulating, M3 greatly reduced, the tip of the molar tooth visible or faintly visible beneath the molar region swelling, the molar region swelling concave and without definite ridges; in the right mandible the first marginal tooth distinct, the second marginal tooth absent, the molar plate concave and without definite ridges, the basal notch distinct. Gut: crop more developed than the gizzard, the cuticle of the crop with pectinate scales; gizzard with a fully sclerotised hexaradiate armature, the pulvillar belt more developed than the columnar belt, pulvillus I well developed with long needle-like spines on its surface, pulvillus II reduced and smooth; mixed segment short, the midgut tongue outside the midgut arc and not constricted proximally; enteric valve (P2) lying beneath P1 and coaxial with P3, its armature an asymmetrical ring of alternating long and short pads, the surface of the long pads sparsely set with small, nearly triangular spines (larger on the posterior margin), that of the short pads with small spines, larger on the median and terminal surfaces, all spines curved in the direction of the food stream; enteric valve seating monolobed or trilobed.

/genus/tonsuritermes/.note: The genus is soldierless; the worker enteric valve (P2 spineless, with 6 symmetrical cushions and 3–5 small triangular spines proximally) is described in the source but not quoted, owing to the quotation limit.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the worker and alate the fontanelle is very large, occupying from one-quarter to three-quarters of the head width in dorsal view; the inner surface of the fore tibia bears two rows of spine-like setae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic or dimorphic; head flattened in lateral view and circular in dorsal view; fontanelle margin distinct, depressed into the vertex, occupying one-quarter to three-quarters of the head width; antennae 14 segments; postclypeus moderately to strongly inflated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head trapezoidal in dorsal view, flattened in lateral view; between the postclypeus and the ocelli, above the antennal insertions, are two frontal spots larger than the ocelli; between the two frontal spots and the fontanelle are two further, smaller triangular spots.

/genus/triangularitermes/.note: The original description of Mathews (1977) is unavailable; the above is the genus-level comparative account of Constantino & Acioli (2009) citing Mathews (1977), not the text of the original description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier monotypic; similar to the major soldier of Ngauratermes in body size, colour, head-capsule shape, 13-segmented antennae and mandibles with distinct tooth processes, and occurring in the same area.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; nasus more conical; legs and antennae longer; short hairs on the head capsule sparse.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mixed segment longer; Malpighian tubules attached in a group at the same point; the posterior end of P1 forming a short loop dorsally; the two rings of enteric valve spines of similar length.

/genus/triclavitermes/.note: The source records Imago as Unknown, and the genus is soldierless, so only the Diagnostic characters and Worker sections are given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve seating (EVS) forms a distinct ring at the insertion of the enteric valve (EV), followed by a short section of P3; the ventral surface of the mesenteric tongue bears a white spherical mesenteric nodule; the enteric valve has three hemispherical sclerotised plates.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head pale yellow, sparsely covered with setae of the same colour; head slightly convex in lateral view, postclypeal region inflated, fontanelle not visible; antennae 14 segments, relative lengths of the segments 2>3=4<5; gizzard indistinct, without spines, with 4 first-order cushions whose surfaces bear comb-like scales.

/genus/trinervitermes/.note: The generic characters are taken from Sands's genus-level Diagnosis (comprising the Imago and Soldier sections), with no species-level characters mixed in; the original gives no genus-level worker description. Sands adds that the genus feeds mainly on grasses and leaves and is found only in savanna and grassland zones, and describes it as the most difficult genus in the subfamily and indeed in the Isoptera. The character 'antennae 15–16 segments and pronotum broad in large species' among the alates comes from the key of Holmgren (1912: p. 60) and complements Sands's generic characters.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the alate, the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is about as long as the second (rather than distinctly longer), the left mandibular index is 0.29–0.41, the second marginal tooth is absent, and the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is straight; the cutting edge behind the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is distinctly longer than that behind the second marginal tooth; the surface contour of the right molar plate shows no marked irregularity, bearing 5–9 transverse ridges, the first much larger than the rest and blunt-toothed in form, the posterior ridges weaker. The postclypeus is about equal to or slightly more than half as long as wide; the fontanelle is pale, slit-like, forked anteriorly into an almost triangular shape, the two arms enlarged or tapering at their ends; the cephalic pilosity is uniformly fine and dense, the hair pits regular in size, interspersed with a few larger pits; in large species the antennae have 15–16 segments and the pronotum is broad. The soldier is dimorphic in most species, showing traces of a major/minor differentiation or an almost continuous series; the nasus is cylindrical to broadly conical, the apical process of the mandibles is usually lost, the head capsule is not at all constricted behind the antennal fossae and bears no conspicuous setae except on the nasus (major soldier; the head capsule of the minor soldier is often constricted). It is distinguished from Nasutitermes by the longer mandibular cutting edges of the alate and by the structure of the right molar plate; its closest relative is the monomorphic-soldier genus Baucaliotermes. Sands described it as the most difficult genus in the subfamily and indeed in the Isoptera.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is equal to or slightly shorter than the first marginal tooth, the distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth being slightly less to slightly more than one-third of the distance between the first and third marginal teeth (left mandibular index 0.29–0.41); the second marginal tooth is absent; the cutting edge between the first and third marginal teeth is straight; the apical and first marginal teeth of the right mandible are as in the left, and the cutting edge behind the first marginal tooth is distinctly longer than that behind the second marginal tooth; the surface contour of the molar plate shows no marked irregularity, bearing 5–9 transverse ridges, the first much larger than the rest and blunt-toothed in form, the more posterior ridges weaker. The postclypeus is slightly less to slightly more than half as long as wide. The fontanelle is pale, slit-like, forked anteriorly into a nearly triangular shape, the two arms enlarged or tapering at their ends. The cephalic pilosity is fairly uniform and fine, arising from small hair pits of regular size, with a few larger pits scattered among them.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic in most species, with traces of a major/minor differentiation, or in some colonies and local populations almost completely continuous. The nasus is cylindrical to broadly conical. The apical process of the mandibles is usually lost. The head capsule is not at all constricted behind the antennal fossae and bears no conspicuous setae except on the nasus (major soldier; the head capsule of the minor soldier is often constricted).

/genus/tuberculitermes/.note: The soldier is taken from item ee of Holmgren's (1912) key and from Emerson's (1928) key; for the worker there is only the comparative statement in Emerson (1960).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The anterior part of the soldier head extends into a large and conspicuous nasus, and the head is rectangular; the sides of the head are rounded in Proboscitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Each side of the posterior margin of the head bears a nearly tooth-like process; the labrum is much longer than wide; the mandibles are as long as the head capsule, straight, and hooked at the apex.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The second marginal tooth of the right mandible is lost in the alate–worker; Emerson (1960) noted that this pattern is similar only in Euchilotermes, Ophiotermes, Tuberculitermes and Spinitermes.

/genus/tucupitermes/.note: At genus level, 'Genus Diagnosis' and 'Genus Description' are given separately; the imago is recorded as Unknown in the original, so no Alate section is provided; soldierless. No genus-level measurements are given; the measurements are species-level.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Cutting edge of the left mandible twice as long as the distance from the apical tooth to M1+2; stomodeal valve twice as long as the crop; Malpighian ampullae well developed, visible in both right ventral and dorsal views; mesenteric tongue long and slightly bulbous, reaching the midline of the abdomen; the connection between P1 and P3 is not visible in any view, only a small bilobed seating being visible. The largest species currently known in the subfamily (the title itself calls it the largest Apicotermitinae).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule dark yellow, with dark longitudinal muscle marks converging towards the vertex; fontanelle white, convex, drop-shaped. Head capsule with few setae of unequal size, none in the posterior region; postclypeus small, slightly swollen, with setae as large as those of the head capsule; labrum convex, longer than the postclypeus and clypeus together, setae rather stout. Antennae 13-segmented, I<II, III shorter than the remaining segments. Mandibles stout: apical tooth of the left mandible shorter than M1+2; the distance from the apical tooth to M1+2 relatively short, the cutting edge twice as long as this distance; the notch between M1+2 and M3 distinct and far from M1+2; M3 pointed, at a short distance from the molar prominence; molar prominence conical, with grooved sculpture and basal scales. Right mandible: apical tooth slightly smaller than M1, first marginal tooth distinctly larger than the others; posterior margin of M1 wider than the molar prominence; angle between M1 and M2 130°; M2 conical; molar plate concave, without a groove, with grooved sculpture and basal scales. Thorax pale yellow; pronotum wider than half the head width, margins with numerous setae; lateral and posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum with setae. Tibiae paler than femora, anterior surface with numerous irregular spines; anterior face of the forecoxa with a row of distinct spine-like setae. Abdomen semi-transparent, tergites and sternites covered with many setae of unequal size. Digestive tract: crop small, immediately behind the thorax; gizzard reduced, without armature, with 6 first-order pulvilli; stomodeal valve very long; mesenteron with 4 well-developed, slender Malpighian ampullae; P1 long; P2 asymmetrical, trilobed; P3 bulbous, connected to P4 by an arched isthmus. Measurements: species-level (Table 1, 20 workers).

/genus/tumulitermes/.note: The original text gives key couplets; the systematic discussion on p. 68 adds that the group as a whole has a large clypeus, that Tumulitermes comes closest to Eutermes s. str. in body structure, and that its soldier apical process, though weak, is present, so it is regarded as the connecting link. No measurements, body colour or worker description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with the 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd, head broadly oval and often narrow anteriorly, fontanelle near the middle of the head, antennal segments rather long, pronotum broad, wing surface punctate and sparsely hairy (Taf. III, Fig. 12); soldier with an apical process on the mandibles (weak but certainly present in T. tumuli and T. apiocephalus), head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets, nasus relatively long and narrow, conical to cylindrical, head oval (Taf. III, Fig. 13). Distinguished from Subulitermes by the presence or absence of the soldier apical process, and from Rotunditermes by nasus and head shape. Holmgren considers that in general body structure the genus differs very little from Eutermes s. str. and is the link connecting the group to Eutermes s. str.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head broadly oval, usually narrowing anteriorly; fontanelle about at the middle of the head; antennal segments relatively long; pronotum broad; wing surface punctate and sparsely hairy (Tafel III, Fig. 12). 1st tooth of the left mandible distinctly larger than the 2nd; clypeus about as long as half its width, or shorter and strongly raised, oval, pale yellow.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles with a more or less distinct apical process; head capsule not constricted behind the antennal sockets; nasus relatively long and narrow, conical to cylindrical; head oval (Tafel III, Fig. 13).

/genus/uncitermes/.note: The alate is described at generic level but no section is provided for it owing to the quotation limit; the soldier has only one vertical sharp-edged tooth per mandible and an indistinct molar region and lacks a process on the fore coxa, and the worker abdomen is oval and semitransparent; these details are found in the source's “Soldier” and “Worker” sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier mandibles are hook-like, there is no row of short stout spines along the margins of the pro-, meso- and metanotal plates, and the fore coxa lacks a keel-like process and coarse setae; on these characters it can be distinguished from Armitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head circular in dorsal view; frontal tube conical, as long as the head base and forming an angle of nearly 45° with it in lateral view; antennae 15 segments; labrum rounded, with a transparent anterior margin lacking a distinct point; postmentum subrectangular.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; head circular; frontal suture indistinct; fontanelle elliptical and indistinct; antennae 15 segments.

/genus/vaninitermes/.note: Of the alate the source knows only V. ignotus and gives no generic description, so no alate section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve (P2) consists of three subequal ridges covered with fine curved spines; P3 and P4 are connected by an isthmus inserted subapically.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head subrectangular, the convexity of the lateral and posterior margins varying, posterior corners rounded; nasus conical, medium-sized.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head circular; postclypeus short and inflated; antennae 13 or 14 segments.

/genus/velocitermes/.note: The original text has only key couplets; the systematic discussion on p. 71 gives the evolutionary explanation outlined above. Sands (1965: 651–666) places Velocitermes together with Tenuirostritermes and Diversitermes in a predominantly Neotropical branch, and points out that Fulleritermes and Rhadinotermes, although their soldier head capsule is constricted, belong to that branch and not to the Leptomyxotermes branch. No measurements, body colour or worker description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with compound eyes at the sides of the head, relatively small but strongly projecting, clypeus mostly concolorous with the frons or only slightly paler, head mostly oval with a well-developed occiput, antennal segments more or less elongate, 1st tooth of the left mandible about as long as the 2nd; soldier with two size classes (corresponding to the medium and small soldiers of Diversitermes), mandibles with an apical process, antennae 14-segmented, legs long. Holmgren considers the genus undoubtedly closely related to Diversitermes, very probably derived from an originally trimorphic subgenus whose largest soldier morph has been lost, while the alate has a more elongate head, smaller and more projecting compound eyes, and has shifted in life history to diurnal habits, migrating and storing food by means of its long legs. Sands (1965) places this genus together with Tenuirostritermes and Diversitermes in a predominantly Neotropical branch.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: 1st tooth of the left mandible about as long as the 2nd; clypeus about as long as half its width or slightly shorter, often dark, mostly the same colour as the frons or only slightly paler; compound eyes at the sides of the head, relatively small, strongly projecting; head mostly oval, occiput well developed; antennal segments more or less elongate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Two size classes of soldier, corresponding respectively to the medium and small soldiers of Diversitermes; mandibles with an apical process; antennae 14-segmented; legs long (Tafel III, Fig. 27 a, b). Here the key additionally uses the basal part of the worker anteclypeus being about as long as half its width as an auxiliary condition, but the original text gives no worker description.

/genus/verrucositermes/.note: The alate is known only from the single morphotype king, whose mandibles were not dissected, so Sands described the worker mandibles instead (p. 156); Emerson additionally recorded the head as round-oval, the compound eyes proportionally large, the ocelli about two-thirds of an eye width from the compound eyes, and the tibial spur formula 2:2:2 (p. 4). Sands regarded this highly distinctive soldier caste as the chief generic character and noted that the nasus and its base in Eutermellus and Mimeutermes show a similar tendency to roughening, though far less pronounced than in this genus (p. 157). Sands further pointed out that the “worker mandible” figured by Emerson (1960) was in fact a specimen of Orthotermes depressifrons (Termitinae) mixed in, so the worker account follows Sands.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Emerson pointed out that the numerous conspicuous tubercles on the soldier head capsule and antennae are unique among the known nasute termites and, judging from their structure and position, are probably olfactory sensilla.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Postclypeus moderately convex, 2–5 times as wide as long, anterior margin concave and undulate; fontanelle a pale stripe, narrowing and slightly depressed posteriorly; compound eyes slightly projecting beyond the sides of the head, with a notched margin; pilosity fine, dense and uniform, with a few coarser setae intermixed; pronotum narrowing posteriorly at the sides, less than two-thirds as long as wide.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Nasus slender, cylindrical, tapering to a fine point; reduced mandibles without an apical process but angular in outline; anterior margin of the labrum undulate. Head capsule strongly inflated at the base of the nasus and sharply constricted at the middle, densely covered with irregular small tubercles, densest at the base of the nasus and on the anterior lobe. Antennae 12–13 segments, segments III–IX or X each with 3 tubercles on the inner side.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apical tooth of the left mandible longer than the first marginal tooth, the distance between them greater than that between the first and third marginal teeth (left mandible index 1.36); the cutting edge in front of the third marginal tooth with a notch; the gap between the third marginal tooth and the molar prominence slightly wider than that notch, the small tooth between them barely visible.

/genus/zootermopsis/.note: Based only on the soldier diagnostic couplet in the North American generic key of De Luna et al. 2023 (thin), not a complete set of generic characters.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large mandibulate soldier; antennae with more than 20 segments; cerci conspicuous in all castes.

/family/hodotermopsidae/.biology: This group inhabits moist forests, boring into damp logs, fallen timber and stumps, and also damages living trees and the timber of cottages and old buildings; hence the name dampwood termites. Primary and secondary forests suffer especially heavily. Their galleries have no connection with the soil, and they live a concealed, wood-dwelling life.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Hodotermitidae)
/family/hodotermopsidae/.diagnosis: The grass termites recorded in the book belong to one of the more primitive branches of the Isoptera. No caste has a fontanelle; the pronotum is flat and narrower than the head; the first tarsomere of the hind leg is cleft only on its ventral surface and remains a single segment dorsally, so that the tarsus appears five-segmented in ventral view but only four-segmented in dorsal view; the cerci consist of four to eight segments; the alate lacks ocelli and has antennae of fifteen to twenty-seven segments; the soldier's tibiae bear two to four apical spurs. The transformed caste (the soldier) approaches the primitive type in head shape, mandibular teeth and the number of antennal and cercal segments; caste differentiation is not pronounced, and many ancestral characters are retained.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.distribution: The book records only one genus and one species as extant in China, found in subtropical montane and hilly forests; the precise localities and hosts are given on the species page for this genus.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.soldier: The soldier of the single genus recorded for China has a broad, flattened, nearly circular head capsule, with the posterior and lateral margins both rounded; the antennae are many-segmented, up to twenty-four segments; the compound eyes are distinct; the mandibles are robust and strongly curved, with very well developed mandibular teeth, the left mandible bearing four marginal teeth and the right three. The pronotum is flat and slightly narrower than the head; the hind tibia bears two lateral spurs in addition to four apical spurs, whereas the fore and mid tibiae have no lateral spurs; the cerci have four to six segments.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work follows the system of Snyder and Emerson, placing the subfamily Termopsinae within the family Hodotermitidae (noting that the subfamily had been proposed for elevation to the family Termopsidae). This subfamily was later generally raised to the separate family Hodotermopsidae; this site follows the current system, so what is presented on this page is in fact the part of the original work's Hodotermitidae that concerns the Chinese species.

/family/kalotermitidae/.biology: In all groups of this family both nesting and feeding are confined to wood, and the galleries do not connect with the soil; seasoned timber, standing dead trees, structural timber and stored wooden articles may all be attacked. Because the colonies are small and concealed, they are often noticed only after the wood has been hollowed out; there are comparatively many records of damage to old buildings and old furniture in southern and coastal China.
/family/kalotermitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Kalotermitidae)
/family/kalotermitidae/.diagnosis: This family is a medium-sized, wood-dwelling primitive group, commonly called drywood termites. No caste has a fontanelle; the pronotum is flat, about as wide as the head or slightly wider; the tarsi are four-segmented and the tibiae bear two to four apical spurs; the cerci have only two segments. The soldier retains pale eye spots behind the antennae; the alate has ocelli, the forewing scale is much larger than the hindwing scale and overlies its base, the radial sector is well developed and branches several times, and the subcosta is weak. The family has no worker caste; feeding and brood care are carried out by the nymphs.
/family/kalotermitidae/.distribution: The book records five genera from China (Cryptotermes, Kalotermes, Incisitermes, Glyptotermes and Neotermes); the number of genera and species included here under the current classification has been slightly adjusted; see the list below.

/family/rhinotermitidae/.biology: Most species of this family are both soil- and wood-dwelling, and the nest may be built underground, in tree trunks or within objects on the ground; colony structure is comparatively complex. They feed on living trees, dead wood and structural timber, and can also damage leather, plastics, cable sheathing and even metal articles; several genera are major cosmopolitan pests, causing particularly severe damage to houses, bridges, utility poles and telecommunications installations.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Rhinotermitidae)
/family/rhinotermitidae/.diagnosis: The head bears a fontanelle, the most conspicuous feature of the family; the antennae have thirteen to twenty-five segments; the pronotum is flat and narrower than the head; the tarsi are four-segmented, with no arolium beneath the claws; the cerci have two segments. The alate and worker have three marginal teeth on the left mandible and two on the right, the first marginal tooth bearing a subsidiary tooth; the alate has ocelli, the forewing scale is larger than the hindwing scale and the two overlap, and the wing membrane bears cross-veins forming a network.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.distribution: The family is species-rich and widely distributed, with the Oriental region as its centre of distribution and differentiation; some genera extend into the Neotropical, tropical and Australasian regions, and some species have established populations in the drier parts of the Northern Hemisphere. It occurs throughout China, north and south.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work's Rhinotermitidae includes groups that have since been separated or synonymised: the genus Stylotermes is now usually placed in a family of its own, Stylotermitidae; the genus Tsaitermes has been sunk into Reticulitermes; and several species of Coptotermes have also been revised. This site follows the current system, so this page does not correspond genus by genus to the chapter in the original work.

/family/termitidae/.biology: All members of this family are soil-dwelling, nesting underground, in earthen mounds, in tree trunks or inside buildings. Groups such as the Macrotermitinae cultivate fungus combs in the nest to break down wood; they are important decomposers in tropical and subtropical ecosystems and at the same time major pests of crops, forest trees and buildings.
/family/termitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Termitidae)
/family/termitidae/.diagnosis: The largest family in the Isoptera, comprising about three-quarters of all species; its members are soil-dwelling higher termites, nesting mostly underground or within earthen mounds. The book divides it into five subfamilies: the Termitinae, the Amitermitinae, the Macrotermitinae, the Nasutitermitinae, and the Apicotermitinae established separately by Grasse and Noirot in 1954. Soldiers and workers are often markedly polymorphic, and a few groups lack soldiers. The soldier's pronotum is narrower than the head, its anterior margin upturned and saddle-shaped; a fontanelle is present; the cerci have one to two segments and the tarsi three to four. The alate has only one or two marginal teeth on the left mandible; the forewing and hindwing scales are separate, the forewing scale slightly larger; the radial vein is reduced or lost; the postclypeus is large and convex, and the fontanelle is prominent.
/family/termitidae/.distribution: The family is most flourishing in the tropics and subtropics; southern China is rich in species, and it is distributed throughout the provinces and regions south of the Yangtze River, being especially concentrated in the mountains of South China and the Southwest.
/family/termitidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work adopts the five-subfamily system and leaves within this family such groups as the genus Indotermes, which have since been proposed for separate family rank; this site follows the current system, so this page is an adapted account of the general characters of the original work's Termitidae, and the placement of individual genera follows the list.

/genus/ahmaditermes/.alate: In the alate, the apical tooth of the left mandible is almost as long as the first and second marginal teeth together, and the cutting edge between the marginal teeth is undulating. Antennae 15-segmented. The media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, while that of the hindwing arises from the base of the radial sector. These mandibular and wing-venation characters agree with those seen in the worker; only the number of antennal segments is greater.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Ahmaditermes section of the original book)
/genus/ahmaditermes/.diagnosis: In the soldier the head lacks a nasus and is broadly pear-shaped; the head surface is scattered with fine hairs; the head is constricted behind the antennal sockets, the sides strongly convex near the base, the posterior margin concave at the middle; the mandibles are short and blunt, without pointed tips; the mandibular body is robust; monomorphic or dimorphic; antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed in southern China, mostly in tropical and subtropical forest areas.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.soldier: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic. Head surface scattered with fine hairs. Head without a nasus, broadly pear-shaped in outline, narrowed behind the antennal sockets, the sides distinctly swollen near the base, the posterior margin concave inwards at the middle. Mandibles short and blunt, not forming pointed tips at the apex, the mandibular body robust. Antennae 12–13-segmented. The head capsule is widest between the swellings near the base.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.worker: In the worker the apical tooth of the left mandible is almost as long as the first and second marginal teeth together, and the cutting edge between the two marginal teeth is undulating rather than straight. Its mandibular tooth pattern agrees with that of the alate; only the body form and the development of the wings differ.

/genus/ancistrotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Ancistrotermes section of the original book)
/genus/ancistrotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dimorphic, predominantly yellow in colour; head nearly circular, widest at the middle; the anterior portion of the mandibles slender and curved; the inner margin with only minute denticles at mid-length; labrum ligulate with a bluntly rounded apex; antennae 15- or 16-segmented; pronotum distinctly narrower than the head width.
/genus/ancistrotermes/.distribution: Oriental and Afrotropical regions; distributed in tropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/ancistrotermes/.soldier: Soldier of two forms, major and minor. In the major soldier the head capsule is yellow to deep yellow, the mandibles reddish brown, the labrum pale yellow, the antennae milky white, and the pronotum, abdomen and legs pale yellow. Long hairs are scattered over the head, the labrum bears a pair of apical hairs, and several long hairs are arranged in longitudinal rows on each side. The head is nearly circular to oval, widest at the middle, the middle or anterior part humped in lateral view. Labrum ligulate with a bluntly rounded apex; the anterior portion of the mandibles slender and curved, the inner margin with or without a minute denticle at mid-length. Postmentum raised, projecting in a broad arc at the middle. When the antennae are 15-segmented the third segment is the shortest; when 16-segmented the fourth is the shortest. The pronotum is narrower than the head, its anterior and posterior margins both concave at the middle. The minor soldier is paler in colour and smaller in size, its parts otherwise similar to those of the major soldier.

/genus/arcotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Arcotermes section of the original book)
/genus/arcotermes/.diagnosis: In the soldier the head bears only scattered short hairs; head pear-shaped; distinctly narrowed behind the antennal sockets, widest near the posterior margin; posterior margin rounded, scarcely concave at the middle; nasus a slender tube; mandibles short and small, blunt, without pointed tips; antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/arcotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a component of tropical and subtropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/arcotermes/.soldier: Soldier with sparse pilosity on the head. Head pear-shaped, the lateral margins markedly narrowed behind the antennal sockets, widening again only from there backwards to near the posterior margin, widest near the posterior margin; posterior margin arcuate, not or scarcely concave at the middle. Nasus tubular. Mandibles without pointed tips. Antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/arcotermes/.worker: Worker with a large and conspicuous fontanelle situated near the middle of the vertex; the cutting edge between the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible is not straight but undulating, and the undulation is gentle, an easily observed character of the worker of this genus.

/genus/coptotermes/.alate: Alate with a broad, oval head capsule; postclypeus very short, its surface flat. Antennae 18–25-segmented. Pronotum flattened, narrower than the head capsule. Forewing scale larger than the hindwing scale and overlapping it; venation with a very faint reticulate pattern, the wing surface hairy; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, that of the hindwing from the base of the radial sector, the media and cubitus very close together. Fontanelle situated at the centre of the head.
/genus/coptotermes/.biology: Species of this genus mainly attack timber components in buildings and cause the greatest losses of any termite group in the provinces of southern China; buried plastic cables and amenity trees are also frequently damaged. They are important pests worldwide. The species are morphologically very similar and often difficult to identify, and individuals of different colony ages in the same nest differ greatly in colour and size.
/genus/coptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Coptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/coptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with an oval head, distinctly narrowed anteriorly; fontanelle a large opening, situated at the front of the head and projecting forwards as a short tube; mandibles slender and curved, the inner margin smooth and toothless apart from the serrate notch at the base; antennae 13–17-segmented.
/genus/coptotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed throughout the provinces of southern China, with the greatest number of species in the South China area.
/genus/coptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with an oval head, markedly narrowed anteriorly. Fontanelle large, situated at the front of the head, extending outwards as a short tube with the opening directed forwards. Mandibles slender and curved, the tooth row entirely absent apart from the serrate notch retained at the base, the inner margin smooth. Antennae 13–17-segmented. Labrum an acute ligula. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head capsule.

/genus/cryptotermes/.alate: Alate head pale yellow, yellowish brown, reddish brown or dark brown in colour, pilosity sparse to moderate, posterior margin evenly rounded, coronal suture usually visible. Compound eyes small, round or nearly round; ocelli oval, touching or close to the compound eyes. Antennae 12–18-segmented. Postclypeus slightly trapezoidal, its anterior margin either convex or concave; labrum transverse. Left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right with two. Pronotum narrower than the head capsule, in a few species slightly exceeding the width of the head including the compound eyes. Tibiae with three apical spurs, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/cryptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Cryptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/cryptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a short, thick head capsule, the front part almost black; frontal and genal regions each extending into a pair of horn-like processes; vertex and frontal area often irregularly wrinkled; antennae 11–15-segmented; postclypeus nearly trapezoidal; tarsi 4-segmented; cerci 2-segmented.
/genus/cryptotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; species of this genus are recorded from all provinces of southern China.
/genus/cryptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with a short, thick head, dark brown with the front part almost black; in some species the vertex, frontal area and sides are coarsely wrinkled, and a thick transverse frontal ridge often lies between vertex and frontal area, with or without a V-shaped notch at its centre. Two pairs of horn-like processes at the front of the head: the upper pair, above and in front of the antennal sockets, arises from the lateral margin of the postclypeus and is termed the frontal horn; the lower pair, below and in front of the antennal sockets, is formed by prolongation of the genae and is termed the genal horn, its shape varying with the species. Frontal surface mostly concave; compound eyes generally visible, unpigmented. Antennae 11–15-segmented, clypeus slightly trapezoidal, labrum nearly triangular or ligulate. Mandibles short, the outer margin convex at the middle, the posterior part of the postmentum broad. Pronotum about as wide as the head capsule, its anterior margin deeply concave, mostly wavy or dentate. Legs short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented, cerci 2-segmented.

/genus/cucurbitermes/.alate: Dealate head with long and short hairs interspersed with setae, the pronotum with rather many setae. Head nearly circular; fontanelle large and elongate-oval, not forked anteriorly, with a longitudinal line running from it to the posterior margin; postclypeus raised, with another longitudinal line at its centre; compound eyes large, elliptical and convex outwards, ocelli oval and slightly convex. Apical tooth of the left mandible as long as the first marginal tooth, the cutting edge between the two teeth nearly straight. Antennae 15-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum nearly straight, the posterior margin slightly concave at the middle. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Cucurbitermes section of the original book)
/genus/cucurbitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic; head almost bare, the nasus with only a few hairs at its apex, constricted like a gourd at the base of the nasus and at the antennal sockets; nasus a slender tube; mandibles blunt and convex, without pointed tips; antennae 13–14-segmented; anterior half of the pronotum upright.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a subtropical element, recorded from southern and south-eastern China.
/genus/cucurbitermes/.soldier: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic. Head almost bare, with only a few hairs at the apex of the nasus, the thoracic tergites hairless. Excluding the nasus, the head is about as long as wide, or slightly wider than long; constricted like a gourd at the base of the nasus and at the antennal sockets, strongly convex behind the antennal sockets, the sides rounded, the posterior margin rather flat; nasus slender and tubular. Mandibles blunt and convex, without pointed tips. Antennae 13–14-segmented. The anterior half of the pronotum stands upright, at about a right angle to the posterior half. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/dicuspiditermes/.alate: Alate with a broad oval head capsule, slightly narrowed anteriorly, densely covered with long and short hairs. Fontanelle generally slender, slit-like; compound eyes elliptical; ocelli oval and separate from the compound eyes. Postclypeus raised. Apical tooth of the left mandible short, slightly larger than or almost equal to the first marginal tooth, which in turn is larger than the second; the posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible long. Antennae 14–15-segmented.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Dicuspiditermes section of the original book)
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a rectangular head, the anterior part raised; an anterolateral process below each antennal socket; mandibles asymmetrical, the left twisted into a hook, the right straight as a blade; lateral corners of the labrum projecting forwards like needles; antennae 14-segmented; pronotum saddle-shaped.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed in tropical and subtropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/dicuspiditermes/.soldier: Soldier with a rectangular head capsule, the anterior part raised, with an anterolateral horn-like process on each side below the antennal sockets. Mandibles asymmetrical: the left twisted, its apex curved inwards into a hook; the right straighter, blade-like. Anterior margin of the labrum deeply concave, the lateral corners slender as needles and projecting far forwards. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped, its width far less than the head width.

/genus/euhamitermes/.biology: Euhamitermes live underground beside grass roots and feed on decaying plant material; colonies are small and mostly lack soldiers, so identification is quite difficult. The species of this genus are rather secretive in their activity, and specimens often have to be obtained by digging.
/genus/euhamitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Euhamitermes section of the original book)
/genus/euhamitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule between rectangular and square; mandibles stout and short, strongly curved like hooks, with a small tooth at the middle of the inner margin; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; soldiers are not easily collected.
/genus/euhamitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; 24 species are known worldwide, 13 in China, with Yunnan accounting for about half of the national total.
/genus/euhamitermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule intermediate between rectangular and square. Mandibles stout and short, strongly curved like hooks, with a small tooth at the middle of the inner margin. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped. Spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Because colonies are small and often lack soldiers, specimens are not easily obtained.

/genus/globitermes/.alate: Alate rather small; head capsule thick and slightly convex; compound eyes very small; fontanelle distinct. Postclypeus wider than the frons, its surface rather flat, less than half as long as wide; labrum wider than long; antennae 15–16-segmented. Pronotum more than half as long as wide. Forewing scale slightly longer than the hindwing scale, the wing surface densely covered with fine punctures; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, that of the hindwing branches from the radial sector close to the cubitus. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
/genus/globitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Globitermes section of the original book)
/genus/globitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a short, thick, nearly circular head capsule; mandibles slender with hooked apices, each mandible with a sharp tooth at the middle of the inner margin; labrum bluntly rounded anteriorly; antennae at most 15-segmented; alate with very small compound eyes, the media of the forewing arising independently at the humeral suture.
/genus/globitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a component of tropical and subtropical forests, recorded from southern China.
/genus/globitermes/.soldier: Soldier with a short, thick head capsule, nearly circular in outline, yellow in colour. Mandibles slender, the anterior portion curved into a hook, each mandible with a sharp marginal tooth at the middle of the inner margin. Labrum oval, bluntly rounded without a point at the apex. Antennae with no more than 15 segments. Postmentum distinctly raised upwards at the middle. Pronotum narrower than the head, slightly convex anteriorly and at the middle.

/genus/glyptotermes/.alate: The alate largely resembles that of Kalotermes, differing in that the media of the wing is straight and closely appressed to the radial sector, and neither media nor radius branches. Antennae 12–15-segmented, spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented; the structure of the legs and wings is similar to that of Kalotermes.
/genus/glyptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Glyptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/glyptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with an elongate head capsule, the vertex often raised above the rest and forming twin peaks; mandibles short and stout, much shorter relative to head length than in Neotermes; antennae short, mostly 10–12-segmented; labrum square; tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/glyptotermes/.distribution: Recorded from the Oriental, Australian, Neotropical and Afrotropical regions.
/genus/glyptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with an elongate head capsule, the vertex usually higher than the rest of the head, forming twin peaks. Frontal surface either sloping or steep; in some species the frontal wrinkles are coarse and deep, in others smooth or with punctate sculpture. Antennae short, mostly 10–12-segmented. Mandibles short and stout, much shorter relative to head length than in Neotermes, with several distinct marginal teeth, the basal ridge of the mandible prominent or flat. Pronotum flattened and broad. Labrum mostly square. Femora not thickened. Spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented.

/genus/hodotermopsis/.biology: Hodotermopsis mainly attacks primary and secondary forest, boring into living standing trees and also feeding on stumps, and in severe cases invading dwellings and historic buildings. It mostly inhabits moist forest and feeds on timber containing moisture, hence the name dampwood termite.
/genus/hodotermopsis/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Hodotermopsis section of the original book)
/genus/hodotermopsis/.diagnosis: Soldier with a broad, flat, nearly circular head capsule, the posterior and lateral margins arcuate; antennae up to 24-segmented; compound eyes distinct; mandibles stout and strongly curved, the left with four marginal teeth, the right with three; pronotum flat, slightly narrower than the head.
/genus/hodotermopsis/.soldier: Soldier with a broad, flat head, nearly circular in outline, the posterior and lateral margins arcuate. Antennae with many segments, up to 24; compound eyes clearly visible. Mandibles strong, strongly curved, the tooth row well developed, the left mandible with four marginal teeth, the right with three. Pronotum flat, slightly narrower than the head capsule, its anterior margin slightly concave. The hind tibia bears two lateral spines in addition to the four apical spurs, while the fore and mid tibiae lack lateral spines. Cerci 4–6-segmented.

/genus/hospitalitermes/.alate: Alate dark in both body and wings. Head broadly oval; postclypeus less than half as long as wide; frons triangularly depressed behind the postclypeus. Forewing and hindwing scales similar in size; radius absent; media closely appressed to the cubitus. Antennae 15-segmented, the third segment about twice as long as the second.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Hospitalitermes section of the original book)
/genus/hospitalitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dark in colour; nasus slender, deeply concave where it meets the head; mandibles reduced while the pointed tips are very long; antennae 14-segmented with the third segment not shorter than the fourth; anterior part of the pronotum raised; legs very long; alate entirely dark.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a group of tropical rainforest and monsoon forest, recorded from southern China.
/genus/hospitalitermes/.soldier: Soldier mostly dark in colour. Head with a rather slender nasus, markedly concave where the nasus meets the head capsule. Mandibles much reduced, only a very small mandibular base remaining, but the pointed tips very long, their surface smooth and toothless. Antennae 14-segmented, the third segment equal to or slightly longer than the fourth. Anterior part of the pronotum raised. Legs very long, their segments slender.

/genus/hypotermes/.alate: Alate head reddish brown; anteclypeus white, postclypeus pale yellowish brown, antennae brown; the pronotum slightly darker in colour than the head and bearing a T-shaped mark, each of the two anterior lateral corners with a ring-shaped spot resembling an ocellus. Head and postclypeus densely covered with short hairs, interspersed with sparse long hairs. Head outline semicircular; fontanelle small and round; compound eyes not very regularly rounded, protruding slightly outwards; ocelli broadly oval. Postclypeus about half as long as wide, the median longitudinal line clear; labrum arcuate; anteclypeus trapezoidal; antennae with nineteen segments. Pronotum narrower than the head, half-moon shaped in outline; its anterior margin roughly straight, the median notch very shallow, and the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle.
/genus/hypotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Hypotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/hypotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly, body colour pale yellowish brown; labrum arcuate, slightly longer than wide; the middle of the left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right mandible with serrated small teeth before the base; antennae with fifteen to sixteen segments.
/genus/hypotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; in China the species occur in western and southern Yunnan.
/genus/hypotermes/.soldier: Soldier head pale yellowish brown to brown, paler anteriorly; pronotum yellow, antennae brown, labrum pale brown, mandibles pale reddish brown. Head surface sparsely haired; the anterior half of the labrum with several long hairs around its margin, the anterior margin of the postmentum also with long hairs, long hairs scattered over the pronotum. Head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Labrum arcuate, slightly longer than wide. Mandibles slender and incurved, the middle of the left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right mandible with serrated small teeth before the base. Postmentum arcuate, the two sides slightly straight. Antennae with fifteen to sixteen segments, occasionally seventeen. Anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum both slightly concave in the middle.

/genus/incisitermes/.alate: Alate body colour mostly pale brown, some species dark brown. Compound eyes round and large, ocelli close against the compound eyes, the two almost touching. Antennae with thirteen to twenty segments. Left and right mandibles each with two marginal teeth. Pronotum usually slightly wider than the head, or as wide as the head. Wing membrane transparent, without nodular structures, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, most species with an arolium between the claws.
/genus/incisitermes/.biology: Incisitermes colonies are small and simply built, tolerate drought and are readily spread by human transport, so they deserve attention in quarantine. Incisitermes minor was introduced into China in the late 1940s and formerly damaged large buildings in Nanjing, Shanghai, Ningbo and elsewhere; after control the Nanjing population has not been seen for many years.
/genus/incisitermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Incisitermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/incisitermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule flattened, rectangular, the two sides parallel, the frontal slope very small; antennae with ten to seventeen segments, the third longest and club-shaped; pronotum as wide as or slightly wider than the head, its anterior margin deeply concave, tibial spur formula 3:3:3.
/genus/incisitermes/.distribution: Nearctic, Neotropical and Oriental Regions; in China only Incisitermes minor is known, introduced from abroad.
/genus/incisitermes/.soldier: Soldier head flattened, rectangular, the two lateral margins parallel to each other, the frontal surface sloping very gently. Mandibles stout. Antennae with ten to seventeen segments, the third longest, club-shaped and heavily sclerotised. Pronotum as wide as or slightly wider than the head capsule, its anterior margin deeply concave. Femora stout, tibial spur formula 3:3:3.

/genus/indotermes/.alate: Alate head nearly circular, ocelli and compound eyes both small, postclypeus markedly raised, its length equal to or slightly less than half its width, the posterior margin arcuately curved, fontanelle distinct and situated posteriorly, antennae with fifteen segments. Wing membrane brown, the media of the forewing arising from the radial sector and closely adjacent to the cubitus. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave in the middle, the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum each with a narrow, pointed triangular notch. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi three-segmented.
/genus/indotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Indotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/indotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head capsule stout and broadly cylindrical, the lateral margins nearly parallel, each mandible with one marginal tooth, postmentum broad, short and flat; alate with small ocelli and compound eyes, fontanelle posterior, the media of the forewing arising from the radial sector, tarsi with only three tarsomeres.
/genus/indotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; a tropical and subtropical element, recorded in southern China.
/genus/indotermes/.soldier: Soldier head capsule broadly cylindrical, very stout, the lateral margins nearly parallel, broadly rounded posteriorly. Body colour mainly yellowish brown, mandibles of the same colour but reddish brown to almost black apically, labrum and antennae pale. Head densely covered with fine hairs, thorax and abdomen with intermingled long and short hairs. Mandibles strong, each with one marginal tooth; labrum short and small, its margin transparent; antennae with fourteen segments; postmentum flat, broad and short. Pronotum extremely narrow and short, the anterior lobe semicircular and erect, less than half the width of the head. Tarsi three-segmented.

/genus/kalotermes/.alate: Alate head slightly convex, the lateral margins parallel, the posterior margin broadly arcuate, outline nearly quadrilateral. Postclypeus extremely short, not divided into two lobes. The posterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is fused with the second marginal tooth and longer than the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth. Antennae with sixteen to nineteen segments, ocelli slightly separated from the compound eyes. Pronotum broad and flat, the notch of the anterior margin broadly arcuate, the two sides slightly parallel and symmetrical, the posterior margin broad, the median notch shallow and wide. The anterior margin of the forewing scale projecting, longer than or equal to the pronotum and much larger than the hindwing scale. Rs divided into several branches. The media of the forewing not sclerotised, arising within the wing scale of Cu and running between Rs and Cu. Legs very short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, with an arolium, cerci indistinct.
/genus/kalotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Kalotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/kalotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier head large, rectangular, the two sides rather flat; mandibles stout, longer than half the head length, the inner margin with many teeth of unequal size; antennae with thirteen to eighteen segments, the third swollen; tibial spur formula 3:3:3.
/genus/kalotermes/.distribution: Oriental Region; species of this genus are recorded from every province and autonomous region of southern China.
/genus/kalotermes/.soldier: Soldier head large, rectangular, the two sides rather flat, the dorsal margin straight in lateral view. Frons slightly projecting, sloping towards the clypeus. Mandibles stout and somewhat elongate, longer than half the head length, the inner margin bearing many teeth of unequal size. Antennae with thirteen to eighteen segments, the third distinctly enlarged. Pale eye spots visible behind the antennal sockets. Postmentum somewhat elongate, the waist at the middle or slightly behind it, the widest part with the two sides nearly parallel in the anterior two-thirds, slightly concave in the middle. Pronotum broad and flat, the median notch of the anterior margin wide and shallow, the two sides nearly parallel, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Femora thick, legs short, with three tibial spurs, formula 3:3:3.

/genus/macrotermes/.alate: Alate head broadly oval, fontanelle distinct and slightly raised, ocelli fairly large. Postclypeus convex, about half as long as wide, the posterior margin arcuate and the anterior margin straight. Antennae with nineteen segments, the third longer than the second. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum form shallow arcuate incisions. Radius projecting slightly beyond the wing scale; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, the media of the hindwing mostly from the base of the radial sector. The lateral walls of the queen's abdomen without dense coloured dots.
/genus/macrotermes/.book_ref: (generic description in the original book's section on Macrotermes, reorganised and rewritten)
/genus/macrotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier usually of two sizes, major and minor, or of three, major, medium and minor; the two sides of the head parallel or narrowed anteriorly, frons flat, fontanelle punctiform; mandibles curved like sickles, the base of the left mandible with several notches and a distinct basal tooth; antennae with seventeen segments.
/genus/macrotermes/.distribution: Oriental and Afrotropical Regions; recorded from every province and autonomous region of southern China.
/genus/macrotermes/.soldier: Soldier usually of two sizes, major and minor, some species also with a medium size, three in all. The two sides of the head parallel, or narrowed anteriorly. Frons flat, fontanelle punctiform. Labrum widest at the middle, with a small transparent patch at the apex. Mandibles curved like sickles; the base of the left mandible with several notches and one distinct basal tooth, no other teeth besides the basal one; the right mandible likewise toothed only at the base. Antennae with seventeen segments, the third often longer than the second. Pronotum saddle-shaped, both its anterior and posterior margins notched.

/genus/microcerotermes/.alate: Alate head capsule oval, the lateral margins straight; compound eyes not large, protruding outwards. Ocelli small, slightly separated from the compound eyes. The frontal gland opening is often difficult to see. Postclypeus slightly raised, lower than the frons, its anterior margin straight. Antennae with thirteen to fourteen segments.
